# LeanBridge work tracker

All 1725 LMFDB knowls (snapshot of 28 October 2026) by status against Mathlib ccbef15 and Tau Ceti 5a01f5f (LeanBridge's pins) and their latest main, as of 24 November 2026. 1420 are in the blueprint. Mathlib and Tau Ceti declarations link to their Tau Ceti Review page.

## Nothing to formalise (306)

Site, search, display and data knowls, history and placeholders: nothing mathematical to formalise.

## Formalised in Mathlib (219)

Every notion the knowl defines is in Mathlib (at the pin or on its latest main).

- `af` [L-functions]: `ArithmeticFunction`
- `af.multiplicative` [L-functions]: `ArithmeticFunction.IsMultiplicative`
- `ag.affine_space` [Background › Algebraic geometry]: `AlgebraicGeometry.AffineSpace`, `AlgebraicGeometry.AffineSpace.homOverEquiv`, `AlgebraicGeometry.AffineSpace.coord`
- `ag.base_field` [Background › Algebraic geometry]: `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Over`
- `ag.dimension` [Background › Algebraic geometry]: `topologicalKrullDim`, `TopologicalSpace.IrreducibleCloseds`
- `ag.irreducible` [Background › Algebraic geometry]: `IrreducibleSpace`, `AlgebraicGeometry.GeometricallyIrreducible`
- `ag.projective_space` [Background › Algebraic geometry]: `Projectivization`
- `alg.binary_operation` [Background › Ring theory]: the function type S → S → S itself, the operation argument of Lean core's Std.Associative, Std.Commutative and Std.LawfulIdentity (linked for the alg.binary_operation.* sub-knowls); Mul (Lean core, Init.Prelude, shipped with Mathlib) is the class of one written *
- `alg.binary_operation.associative` [Background › Ring theory]: `Std.Associative`, `Semigroup`
- `alg.binary_operation.commutative` [Background › Ring theory]: `Std.Commutative`, `CommMagma`
- `alg.binary_operation.identity` [Background › Ring theory]: `Std.LawfulIdentity`, `MulOneClass`, `MulOneClass.ext`
- `alg.binary_operation.inverse` [Background › Ring theory]: `Invertible`
- `alg.matrix.skew_symmetric` [Background › Ring theory]: LieAlgebra.Orthogonal.so n R with LieAlgebra.Orthogonal.mem_so (A ∈ so n R ↔ Aᵀ = -A) (Mathlib)
- `alg.symmetric_bilinear_form` [Background › Ring theory]: `LinearMap.BilinForm`, `LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm`

- `portrait.ec.nf` [Varieties › Elliptic curves]: Round AI (AI2), reviewed. Formalised by existing declarations; no new file. The text, sentence by sentence. (1) 'the plot displayed consists of the graphs of the real points of $E$ with respect to each real embedding of $K$' says what the picture shows; it states no fact and defines nothing. For each real embedding s of K the LMFDB plots the real affine points of the stored Weierstrass model with the coefficients s(a_i) (lmfdb/ecnf/WebEllipticCurve.py, EC_nf_plot), and it shows no plot when the signature has no real place. These objects exist in Mathlib (WeierstrassCurve.map along s, WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Equation over R); the knowl claims nothing about them. (2) 'Complex embeddings of $K$ are ignored, so for example there is no plot shown when $K$ is a totally complex field such as an imaginary quadratic field': a display rule, the linked definition of totally complex (nf.totally_imaginary, no real embedding: Mathlib's NumberField.IsTotallyComplex with NumberField.IsTotallyComplex.complexEmbedding_not_isReal, NumberField.IsTotallyComplex.nrRealPlaces_eq_zero and NumberField.InfinitePlace.card_real_embeddings, the number of real embeddings is the number of real places), and one stated fact, the example: an imaginary quadratic field is totally complex. Tau Ceti's NumberField.isTotallyComplex_of_minpoly_eq_X_sq_sub_C_of_neg (pinned module TauCeti.NumberTheory.NumberField.Quadratic.InfinitePlace, docstring 'An imaginary quadratic field is totally complex') states it: a number field containing an algebraic integer theta with minpoly Z theta = X^2 - d and d < 0, in particular Q(sqrt d), is totally complex. It rests on NumberField.isTotallyComplex_of_sq_ratCast_of_neg (TauCeti.NumberTheory.NumberField.InfinitePlace.Basic): any field with x^2 = r for a negative rational r is totally complex, which covers every presentation of an imaginary quadratic field. Non-vacuous: Tau Ceti applies it to Q(i), Q(sqrt -5) and Q(sqrt -21). (3) 'The plots are produced using SageMath ...': provenance and display. The audit (N4) proposed 'To be formalised' with 'no lemma states it'; it missed the Tau Ceti lemma, so the category is Formalised in Tau Ceti (with Mathlib). No text error. Review: the six declarations exist at the pins in the modules recorded, with the meanings stated; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

Formalised in LeanBridge, building on Mathlib and Tau Ceti.

- `af.bernoulli_numbers` [L-functions]: The gap is closed: radius_bernoulliSeries proves that the power series sum B_n T^n / n! over C (bernoulliSeries, the formal multilinear series whose coefficients are those of Mathlib's bernoulliPowerSeries C) has radius of convergence exactly 2 pi. From Mathlib's hasSum_zeta_nat, |B_2k| / (2k)! = 2 zeta(2k) / (2 pi)^(2k) for k >= 1, with 1 <= zeta(2k) <= zeta(2) = pi^2/6 <= 2 (bounds proved from the series), while B_1 = -1/2 and B_n = 0 for odd n >= 3; so |B_n / n!| r^n <= 4 for r < 2 pi (le_radius_of_bound) and it is unbounded for r > 2 pi (contradicting norm_mul_pow_le_of_lt_radius). The rest is Mathlib: bernoulli (rational, B_1 = -1/2, the knowl's convention) and the formal identity bernoulliPowerSeries * (exp - 1) = X, i.e. T / (e^T - 1) = sum B_n T^n / n!.

The depth: in an ultrametric space the diameter of a nonempty bounded set is the least radius of a closed disc containing it (IsUltrametricDist.isLeast_diam), and the new extended-real depth padicClusterValDepth is -log_p of it, ∞ for a single root; the relative depth padicClusterRelValDepth is the difference with the parent's depth (∞ for a single root), and the depth for the top cluster (isPadicCluster_rootSet). Automorphisms are those of X over K (g2c.aut_grp). The affine line with x -> zeta x is no longer an instance (A^1/H = A^1 is not P^1). Concrete instance: over a field with a primitive cube root of unity zeta, P^1 is cyclic trigonal (x -> zeta x, fixed field K(x^3), quotient isomorphic to P^1 through Tau Ceti's anti-equivalence and the committed regular quotient), in particular over F_7; for this, P^1_K is proved geometrically integral, hence an algebraic curve (ProjectiveLineCurve.lean). - `ag.fq.point_counts` [Background › Algebraic geometry]: The gap is closed: finite_pointOver proves that a scheme X of finite type over a finite field K (LocallyOfFiniteType and QuasiCompact structure map; a variety over F_q in particular) has finitely many L-points X.PointOver K L (morphisms Spec L -> X over Spec K) for every finite extension L of K, so X(F_q) (L = K) and X(F_{q^n}) are finite and Nat.card counts them without its junk value. Proof: X is compact, so finitely many charts of its affine open cover cover it; a morphism from the spectrum of a field factors through a chart containing its image point (IsOpenImmersion.lift), where it is the Spec of a ring map R_j -> L (Spec.preimage); R_j is finitely generated over K (LocallyOfFiniteType through HasRingHomProperty.Spec_iff), hence over Z as K is finite, and there are finitely many ring maps from a finitely generated ring to the finite ring L (finite_ringHom_of_finiteType_int).
- `ag.geom_component` [Background › Algebraic geometry]: Both gaps are closed. geometricComponents K X is the set of irreducible components of X_Kbar = X x_K Spec(AlgebraicClosure K) (geometricBaseChangeScheme, the scheme underlying LeanBridge's geometricBaseChange). The parenthetical fact: for X smooth and of finite type over K (Smooth and QuasiCompact structure map), geometricComponents_eq_range_connectedComponent proves that they are exactly the connected components of X_Kbar; the general theorem irreducibleComponents_eq_range_connectedComponent (a Noetherian scheme smooth over a field) uses that connected components of a Noetherian space are open (Tau Ceti's local connectedness) and that a connected scheme smooth over a field is irreducible (Tau Ceti's Smooth.irreducibleSpace_of_connectedSpace). They are finitely many (finite_geometricComponents: X_Kbar is Noetherian). The Galois action: geometricGaloisPerm is a group homomorphism from Gal(Kbar/K) (Mathlib's Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K, by definition Kbar ≃ₐ[K] Kbar) to the permutations of the geometric components, sigma acting by preimage under the automorphism id x Spec(sigma) of the fibre product (geometricGaloisMap, a homeomorphism geometricGaloisHomeomorph with inverse that of sigma^-1); a MulAction instance follows.

A finite set of closed points of a curve lies in an affine open (weak approximation for a function regular on the set, a conductor at the non-normal points, then Mathlib's Zariski main theorem and prime avoidance), which gives a cover by two H-stable affine opens; the quotient is the pushout of their invariant quotients, shown to be a separated geometrically integral curve of finite type. Tau Ceti main's Quotient/FiniteGroup/Relative.lean does not cover this: it needs an H-invariant affine morphism to a base, which it does not construct. The criterion is now proved: not_isUnramifiedIn_artinField_iff_exists / _iff_forall: p is ramified exactly when the inertia group in Gal(Q^/Q) of some, equivalently of every, prime of Q^ (a prime of the ring of algebraic integers O Q^ = integralClosure Z Q^, as in LeanBridge's GaloisRep) above p is not contained in ker rho. Core: Ideal.map_inertia_restrictNormalHom, restriction Gal(K^/K) -> Gal(L/K) maps the inertia group of a prime P of O K^ onto that of P cap O L, for every field K of characteristic 0 and finite Galois L in K^; it is Ideal.map_inertia_of_surjective_of_profinite (new, Mathlib's map_inertia_of_surjective with the finite kernel replaced by the profinite Gal(K^/L), using Mathlib's profinite transitivity and residue-automorphism surjectivity) with Gal(K^/L) acting continuously on the discrete O K^ with invariants O L; then Tau Ceti's isUnramifiedIn_iff_forall_inertia_eq_bot over the base Z. The reading with primes of K and inertia in Gal(K/Q) is isUnramifiedIn_artinField_iff_forall_comap (its negation). Every sentence is captured; no text error; nothing unproved.

- `av.fq.singular_dimensions` [Varieties › Abelian varieties over 𝔽_q]: Round AM (AM4_etale_orders). The whole blocker of tracker v60c is closed ('for fractional ideals of orders in etale Q-algebras, I/PI finite-dimensional over the finite field R/P, dim = 1 iff I_P principal, invertible iff locally principal at every prime, not locally principal at P implies P singular, and R Gorenstein and (I:I) = R implies I invertible'). Setting, the LMFDB's: R an order in an etale Q-algebra K (R : Subalgebra Z K whose additive group is a lattice, toSubmodule R finitely generated and spanning K over Q, Mathlib's Submodule.IsLattice, the LeanBridge convention of ConductorInvertible and OrderIndex; [Algebra.Etale Q K] where needed); a fractional R-ideal is I : FractionalIdeal R^0 K with a non-zero-divisor of K (hI : exists x in I, x in K^0): K is the total ring of fractions of R (new instance IsFractionRing R K) and R is Noetherian (new instance), so these are exactly the LMFDB's finitely generated R-submodules of K containing a non-zero-divisor (FractionalIdeal.fg_coe_of_isNoetherianRing, and Mathlib's isFractional_of_fg for the converse). Claims: (1) R/P is finite for every maximal ideal P (Subalgebra.finite_quotient_of_isLattice: P contains a nonzero integer n and R/P is a finitely generated group killed by n), a field (Ideal.Quotient.field), and I/PI is finite-dimensional over it (FractionalIdeal.finite_quotient_smul_top_of_isLattice). (2) dim_{R/P} I/PI = 1 iff the localisation I_P is a principal R_P-submodule, with Mathlib's Submodule.localized (FractionalIdeal.residueFinrank_eq_one_iff_isPrincipal_localized; for any localisations, Submodule.isLocallyPrincipalAt_iff_isPrincipal_localized'; by Nakayama, Submodule.residueFinrank_eq_one_iff). (3) I invertible iff I_P principal for every maximal ideal P (FractionalIdeal.isUnit_iff_forall_isPrincipal_localized), and also for every prime ideal (isUnit_iff_forall_isPrime_isPrincipal_localized): locally principal at P gives x in I, y in (R : I) with xy in R minus P, so I(R : I) lies in no maximal ideal. (4) If I_P is not principal then P is a singular prime (FractionalIdeal.mem_singularPrimes_of_not_isPrincipal_localized): a maximal ideal not containing the conductor is invertible (the committed Subalgebra.isUnit_of_not_relativeConductor_le), and at an invertible maximal ideal every fractional ideal is locally principal (FractionalIdeal.isLocallyPrincipalAt_of_isUnit_coeIdeal: else (R : I) is contained in P(R : I), against Nakayama). (5) R Gorenstein (Subalgebra.IsGorenstein, Cohen-Macaulay type 1, the definition of ag.cohen_macaulay_type) and (I : I) = R imply I invertible (Subalgebra.IsGorenstein.isUnit_of_div_self_eq_one), through trace duality on etale algebras, new here: the trace form of a reduced finite-dimensional algebra over a field of characteristic 0 is nondegenerate (traceForm_nondegenerate_of_isReduced: some xy is a nonzero idempotent, the trace of a nonzero projection), so the trace dual of a fractional ideal is one and I^tt = I (Subalgebra.traceDualSubmodule_traceDualSubmodule), (I : I) = (I I^t)^t (div_self_eq_traceDualSubmodule_mul), Tr(R) in Z (trace_mem_range_of_isLattice), CM type 1 implies R^t invertible (IsGorenstein.isUnit_traceDualFractionalIdeal), and (I : I) = R gives I I^t = R^t. (6) 'we record the dimensions ... over the singular primes' is a database remark; the recorded number is Submodule.residueFinrank. Readings, both the LMFDB's own: 'prime of R' is a maximal ideal ('A maximal ideal, or prime' in av.fq.singular_primes; R/P must be a finite field), the criterion (3) holding for all primes too; 'singular prime' is LeanBridge's Subalgebra.singularPrimes, maximal ideals containing the conductor (R : O_K), O_K = integralClosure Z K as for av.fq.conductor and av.endomorphism_ring_conductor (round ZZ4's review: that O_K is also the product of the rings of integers is av.fq.order's own claim). Under the literal 'divides' of av.fq.singular_primes (its recorded text error, 'divides' -> 'contains'), claim (4) would fail for R = Z[9i] (no singular prime, but Z[i] is not locally principal at (3, 9i)); with the recorded correction it is proved, so no new text error here. Non-vacuity (scratch NonVacuity.lean, NonVacuityPi.lean): Z in Q (lattice instance, Etale Q Q, the fractional ideal 1, Z Gorenstein via traceDualFractionalIdeal = 1, every main theorem instantiated) and the non-field Z^2 in Q^2 = Fin 2 -> Q (lattice instance, Etale instance, the main theorems instantiated). Checks: lake build of the four modules, #lint clean (14 + 12 + 1 + 30 declarations), #print axioms only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; no sorry, native_decide or maxHeartbeats; all new names checked absent from Mathlib, Tau Ceti and LeanBridge (other AM clusters' untracked files included). 896 lines in four files. Review (AM4_etale_orders, 2026-11-17, review/AM4_etale_orders.md): formalised, confirmed; every sentence of the live text checked against the declarations. The setting is the LMFDB's: Algebra.Etale Q K is a finite product of number fields (Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod), IsLattice Q is av.fq.order's 'free of maximal rank' (round ZZ4's precedent), and the fractional ideals are Marseglia's (finitely generated, with a non-zero-divisor). 'Prime' = maximal ideal is av.fq.singular_primes's own wording ('A maximal ideal, or prime'); claim 4 holds with the recorded 'divides' -> 'contains' and fails under 'divides' (Z[9i]: f = 9Z[i], P = (3, 9i) does not divide it as (f : P) = P and P^2 = 9Z + 27Z[i] misses 9i, while Z[i]/PZ[i] = F_9 has dimension 2); O_K = integralClosure Z K as for av.fq.conductor and av.fq.index_of_order (av.fq.order's own claim). Non-vacuity in the non-field Z^2 in Q^2 with every hypothesis met, Gorenstein included (its trace dual is Z^2, the trace being x_0 + x_1: review scratch NonVacuityPi.lean); the theorems also apply to any order of the LMFDB's Q[F] = h.EtaleAlgebra (Probe2.lean). Claim 4's antecedent holds only at singular primes, e.g. Z[i] over Z[9i] at (3, 9i) (by hand). Instances: correct and Prop-valued, no loop; nine downstream files re-elaborated with them in scope give the same messages in comparable times; they fire for a variable K but not on Fin n -> Q or AdjoinRoot (whose Z-algebra instance is not Ring.toIntAlgebra), where they apply by name (now said in SingularDimension's module docstring). Review changes: instance Module.Finite Z R for orders (replacing four copies of one have), a private helper for a twice-written unit proof, Submodule.finite_quotient_smul_top (replacing a twice-written block), recurring binders hoisted (N, u, P, l, and the I of the trace-dual lemmas in a section), names with two namespace components, header packing, redundant haves; signature change: residueFinrank_eq_one_iff_isPrincipal_localized now takes P before hI. Judgement point put to the user, who ruled formalised on 2026-11-17: 'Gorenstein' is Cohen-Macaulay type 1 by the formula of ag.cohen_macaulay_type, proved equivalent to R^t invertible and to the (I : I) = R criterion for every order in an etale Q-algebra; only ag.cohen_macaulay_type's canonical-module definition of the type is unformalised. 877 lines in four files after the review.

- `av.semiabelian_variety` [Varieties › Miscellaneous]: A semiabelian variety over K is a commutative group object G of Over (Spec K), of finite type and geometrically integral (a group variety; smoothness is proved as an instance), with a flat surjective homomorphism to a Tau Ceti abelian variety whose kernel (Tau Ceti's kernel in Grp (Over (Spec K))) is a torus: isomorphic to Mathlib's hopfSpec of a finite-type Hopf algebra with Tau Ceti's torusCommHopfAlgProperty (split over an algebraic closure: the general, not necessarily split, torus). Not vacuous: every abelian variety is one, with kernel the rank-0 split torus (proved, via the zero object hopfSpec K).
- `av.weak_equivalence_class` [Varieties › Miscellaneous]: The gap is closed: FractionalIdeal.WeaklyEquivalent.div_self_eq proves (I : I) = (J : J), as R-submodules (I : Submodule R K) / I of K, for weakly equivalent fractional ideals I, J of an order R (Submodule.IsLattice: finitely generated, spanning K over Q) of any Q-algebra K, in particular an étale one. The proof is local and elementwise, without localising K: for x in (I : I) and y in J, an isomorphism I_p = J_p at a maximal ideal p, the equation n(x i) = (nx) i with nx in R for a positive integer n, and cancellation of the unit n of K give s(xy) in J for some s outside p; as this holds at every maximal ideal, xy is in J. The definition of weak equivalence ('locally isomorphic', 'same genus') is the existing WeaklyEquivalent. No text error found.

- `character.dirichlet.values` [Representations › Dirichlet characters]: Round AI (AI2), reviewed. Formalised, with a text correction (fixable text, ruling of 2026-11-11). The knowl is one sentence about a Dirichlet character chi of modulus q > 1 (Mathlib's DirichletCharacter C q, a MulChar on ZMod q; the LMFDB's function Z -> C is n -> chi (n : ZMod q)). (1) 'Complete information ... is contained in the list of values (chi(1), ..., chi(q))': DirichletCharacter.eq_iff_forall_mem_Icc, chi = psi iff chi n = psi n for every n in [1, q] (every residue class has a representative in [1, q]), for every q >= 1, the modulus 1 of the LMFDB included. (2) chi(1) = 1: Mathlib's MulChar.map_one. (3) chi(q) = 0 for q > 1: DirichletCharacter.apply_modulus (false at q = 1, where chi(1) = 1, which is why the knowl takes q > 1). (4) 'each of which is a root of unity e(r) := exp(2 pi i r), for some rational number r': false as written for the zero values (chi(q) = 0, which the knowl's own list shows, and chi(n) = 0 whenever gcd(n, q) > 1, Mathlib's MulChar.map_nonunit). Corrected text, old 'each of which is a root of unity', new 'each of which is either $0$ or a root of unity' (the old string occurs once in the live text). Proved: DirichletCharacter.apply_eq_zero_or_exists_rat_apply_eq_exp (every value chi a, a : ZMod q, q >= 1, is 0 or exp(2 pi i r) for some r : Q), from DirichletCharacter.exists_rat_apply_eq_exp (the value at a unit u is exp(2 pi i r), r = i / |(Z/qZ)^x|, from Mathlib's MulChar.apply_mem_rootsOfUnity and Complex.mem_rootsOfUnity). The LMFDB's table itself shows the values at -1 and at the first integers prime to q only (lmfdb/characters/web_character.py, Gelts), all roots of unity; the storage and display are a convention. Also a pure typo, recorded: '$e(r) := \exp({2 \pi i r}$)' closes the math mode before ')'. Review: statements and proofs checked, the modulus q = 1 included (scratch Probe.lean); no statement changed (the variable q hoisted to the file level). lake build through the guard; #lint (15 linters) clean; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; the six public names are new in Mathlib, Tau Ceti and LeanBridge (dup_decls: 0 clashes).
- `character.dirichlet.values_on_gens` [Representations › Dirichlet characters]: Round AI (AI2), reviewed. Formalised. (1) 'A Dirichlet character of modulus q is determined (via multiplicativity) by the values chi(g_1), ..., chi(g_r) it takes on any list of generators g_1, ..., g_r for the group (Z/qZ)^x': DirichletCharacter.eq_iff_forall_apply_eq_of_closure_eq_top, for any family g : iota -> (ZMod q)^x with Subgroup.closure (Set.range g) = top, chi = psi iff chi (g i) = psi (g i) for every i (through Mathlib's MonoidHom.eq_of_eqOn_dense on the unit homomorphisms and MulChar.ext); any modulus q, any index type (iota = Fin r for a list). (2) 'the values chi(g_i) are roots of unity e(r) := exp(2 pi i r), where r is a rational number': DirichletCharacter.exists_rat_apply_eq_exp (the value at any unit is exp(2 pi i r) for some r : Q; every q >= 1). (3) 'The generators g_i can each be specified as integers in the interval [1, q-1]': every unit is the class of an integer in [1, q - 1] when q > 1: ZMod.val_mem_Icc_of_isUnit (the least nonnegative representative a.val of a unit a lies in [1, q - 1]) with Mathlib's ZMod.natCast_zmod_val ((a.val : ZMod q) = a). The range q > 1 is implicit, as it is explicit in character.dirichlet.values: at q = 1 the interval [1, 0] is empty. In the LMFDB's setting this never arises: the page shows values on generators only for q > 2 (lmfdb/characters/templates/Character.html), the generators being Sage's unit generators of Z/qZ (lmfdb/characters/TinyConrey.py), an empty list for q = 1 and q = 2. No text error. Review: statements and proofs checked (scratch Probe.lean: q = 1 with the empty family, q = 3); no statement changed. Checks as for character.dirichlet.values (same file).
- `character.hecke` [Representations › Dirichlet characters]: Formalised on the user's ruling of 2026-11-11 ("Something that has a different but fixable definition isn't partial. Something that is strictly weaker is partial."): corrected. As written the condition is not the intended one: ℂˣ being divisible, such a χ_∞ exists iff χ((q)) = 1 for the rational q ≡ 1 mod* 𝔪, with no continuity. So for K = ℚ it admits only even Dirichlet characters (α = 1 − 2N forces χ((2N − 1)) = ψ(−1) = 1), and in general it excludes |N(·)|^s while admitting non-Hecke characters. LeanBridge's IsIdealHeckeCharacter takes the standard condition (a product of continuous characters of the infinite completions), and isIdealHeckeCharacter_iff is proved for that corrected definition. The wording is in the LMFDB issues.

The analytic rank of a newform f is Tau Ceti's Newform.analyticRank, the order of the continuation ModularForm.L of sum A_n n^{-s} at k/2; it is the analytic rank of the AnalyticLFunction of f (analyticRank_analyticLFunction, LMFDB lfunction.analytic_rank). For a self-dual newform (Tau Ceti's IsSelfDual, real coefficients, LMFDB cmf.selfdual) the AnalyticLFunction has real coefficients, so AD's sign_eq_neg_one_pow_analyticRank_of_selfDual gives the sign of the functional equation epsilon = i^k lambda_N(f) = (-1)^r, r the analytic rank (IsSelfDual.rootNumber_eq_neg_one_pow_analyticRank): the sign determines the parity. The conjecture on embeddings, its verification in the LMFDB and the provable correctness of the stored ranks are conjectures and database remarks, not claims. Non-vacuous: deltaNewform has trivial nebentypus, hence is self-dual.

Tau Ceti's GeometricEnd (over the separable closure) embeds into it, so its geometric CM gives non-integer elements over every field (HasGeometricCM.exists_notMem_range_intCast; concrete instance y² = x³ - x over ℚ), and it is isomorphic to it over perfect fields (geometricEndEquivAlgClosure). IsogenyGraph has one arrow from c to c' per prime ℓ for which some ℓ-isogeny exists, so distinct ℓ-isogenies between the same vertices give one edge, and loops from prime-degree endomorphisms are included. 'The edges are the isogenies of prime degree' cannot be meant literally (φ and −φ would be two edges), and the two natural readings differ under CM over the base field. On y² = x³ − x over ℚ(i), 2 + i and 2 − i are 5-endomorphisms with different kernels, not related by automorphisms: two 5-loops when edges are isogenies up to isomorphism, one here. The wording is in the LMFDB issues.

But the knowl's notion is that of an isogeny class over any field: its link ec.isogeny_class is 'over a field K' (finite over number fields, and over finite fields too), ec.isogeny discusses characteristic p, and only the second paragraph ('In the LMFDB, ...') concerns the database's curves over number fields. So the knowl states the symmetry and the attained minimum for every field, while both are proved only in characteristic zero (isSymm_isogenyMatrix and isLeast_isogenyMatrix take CharZero); in characteristic p both are true but unproved. Under the rulings (a restricted range; when in doubt, partial) the knowl stays partial; if the user rules that it concerns the LMFDB's curves over number fields, it is formalised with these decls. The label order of the second paragraph is read as the database's presentation, as in round ZX2. Blocked by: the symmetry and the existence of cyclic isogenies in positive characteristic (the dual of a cyclic isogeny is cyclic there too; a non-cyclic geometric kernel contains E[ℓ] for some ℓ ≠ p, since the p-part of E(K̄) is cyclic, and the factor through [ℓ] must descend along a separable closure, Tau Ceti's descent being for Galois extensions). Not closed by this either: ec.isogeny's decomposition 'every isogeny is a cyclic isogeny composed with [m]'. - `gg.galois_group` [Groups › Galois groups]: The converse is proved: for a transitive G <= Sym(X), X finite and nonempty (and for G <= S_n, n >= 1), there are a field K and an irreducible separable polynomial f over K of degree |X| with a labelling e of its roots in its splitting field by X such that the image of Polynomial.Gal f in Sym(roots), transported by e, is exactly G. K is the fixed field of G acting on L = Q(x_i) by renaming, f = minpoly K x_{i0}; its roots in L are the Galois conjugates g x_{i0} = x_{g i0}, all the x_i by transitivity; every automorphism of L/K is some g (Artin), acting as x_i -> x_{g i}, and Gal.restrict is onto Gal(f); the result is moved to the splitting field through the Galois-equivariant rootsEquivRoots (the general statement for a finite nonempty X is Subgroup.exists_galActionHom_range_eq, in the same file). The rest of the knowl is at the pins: the embedding (galActionHom_injective, with card_rootSet_eq_natDegree for the n roots), transitivity (galAction_isPretransitive) and conjugacy of the images under relabelling (Tau Ceti's Equiv.map_permCongrHom_eq_map_conj). - `gl2.profinite` [Background › Ring theory]: The gap is closed. gl2ZModLimit is the inverse limit of the finite groups GL2(Z/nZ), n in N+, ordered by divisibility along the reduction maps (the compatible families in their product, with the topology induced by the discrete topologies); it is closed in the product (isClosed_gl2ZModLimit), hence compact and totally disconnected, so a profinite group (gl2ZModLimitProfiniteGrp). gl2ZHatContinuousMulEquiv is an isomorphism of topological groups GL2(Z^) = lim GL2(Z/nZ), Z^ being Tau Ceti's topological ring of profinite integers Additive zHat (the inverse limit of the rings Z/nZ: existsUnique_forall_toZMod_eq, with continuity detected by the reductions): reduction modulo every n is continuous and bijective (gl2ZHatToLimit_bijective: injective since a profinite integer is determined by its reductions, surjective since the entries of a compatible family of matrices and of their inverses are compatible), and GL2(Z^) is compact, so it is a homeomorphism. The definition and the equivalence with inverse limits of finite discrete groups are Mathlib's (ProfiniteGrp, isoLimittoFiniteQuotientFunctor, and limits of finite groups being profinite). Every sentence is captured; no text error; nothing unproved.
- `gl2.split_cartan` [Background › Ring theory]: The gap is closed over every field F, so for F_p: IsSplitCartanSubgroup.exists_map_conj_eq proves that every split Cartan subgroup is conjugate to the whole diagonal torus, and isSplitCartanSubgroup_iff that the split Cartan subgroups are exactly the conjugates of the diagonal torus. Key step cartanSubgroup_eq_diagonalTorus_of_le: a Cartan subgroup made of diagonal matrices is the torus (over F_2 the torus is trivial; otherwise, with c != 0, 1 in F, some translate a + t, t in {0, 1, c}, of an element a of A outside F is a unit because the determinant of multiplication by a + t is a monic quadratic in t, its matrix is diagonal with distinct entries, and every invertible diagonal matrix is then the matrix of a unit alpha + beta u); a conjugate Cartan subgroup is the Cartan subgroup of the same algebra in another basis (cartanSubgroup_map_conj, CartanConjugate.lean). The isomorphism of the torus with F_p^x x F_p^x is diagonalTorusMulEquivProd; Cs is the diagonal torus (isSplitCartanSubgroup_diagonalTorus) and Cs.a.b is labelCsAB, its minimal (a, b) being Sutherland's convention (CanonicalParamsOf, which agrees with the script on Cs). Every sentence is captured; no text error; nothing unproved.

- `group.complete` [Groups › Abstract groups]: Round AG. Both recorded gaps are closed. (1) Baer's theorem, Group.isComplete_iff_forall_exists_isComplement': G is complete iff for every group H of the universe of G and every injective f : G →* H with normal image, f.range has a normal complement. The forward direction holds for H in any universe, with the centralizer of f.range as the normal complement (Group.IsComplete.isComplement'_centralizer_range); the converse only needs groups of G's own universe, the strongest form. The new part is the centre half (center_eq_bot_of_forall_exists_isComplement'): a central z is identified with the central commutator c = (0,0,1) = [(1,0,0),(0,1,0)], of infinite order, of Tau Ceti's Heisenberg group H(Z) in the central product (G x H(Z))/<(z, c^-1)>, in which G is normal; a retraction onto G along a normal complement sends H(Z), which centralizes G, into Z(G), hence the commutator c, which equals z, to 1. The automorphism half (surjective_conj_of_forall_exists_isComplement') applies the existing holomorph argument (G ⋊ Aut(G), in G's universe). (2) S_n is complete for n != 2, 6 (Equiv.Perm.isComplete, for every finite type, with Nat.card): Z(S_n) = 1 for n >= 3 (center_eq_bot), S_0 and S_1 are trivial, and every automorphism is inner for n != 6 (surjective_conj_of_card_ne_six; the shared theorem also used for nf.sextic_twin): an automorphism keeps centralizer orders, and 2^k k! (n-2k)! = 2 (n-2)! forces k = 1 unless (n, k) = (6, 3), so transpositions go to transpositions (isSwap_mulAut_apply); an automorphism sending transpositions to transpositions is conjugation by x -> phi(a x)(z) (mem_range_conj_of_forall_isSwap; for n <= 2 every automorphism is the identity). The second condition is the recorded LMFDB error ('inner automorphism group' should read 'automorphism group'; G -> Inn(G) is always onto with kernel Z(G)), a fixable text under the ruling of 2026-11-11; corrected, it is the definition IsComplete (MulAut.conj bijective). Review (AG2): formalised, confirmed; every sentence of the corrected text is proved, and the centraliser-order count, the small cases and Baer's centre half were checked by hand. The forward direction now states its witness, the centralizer (it was IsComplete.exists_normal_isComplement'), as the house rule on existentials asks; the class docstring of Group.IsComplete in committed GroupTheory/Complete.lean, which still says that Baer's converse is not proved for the centre, is stale (recorded in review/AG2_symmetric.md). Axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

(1) 'a unique identifier for each Gassmann class: we count the intersection of H with each G-conjugacy class': LeanBridge's Subgroup.IsGassmannEquivalent is exactly equality of these counts (the definition of group.gassmann_equivalence). 'For an odd prime p, the unique non-abelian group of order p^3 and exponent p': He_p has exponent p for odd p (exponent_zmod) and every non-abelian group of order p^3 and exponent p is isomorphic to He_p (nonempty_mulEquiv_of_exponent_eq, any prime). No error in the text. Review (AG5, 2026-11-13): formalised, confirmed. The matrix isomorphism sends (x, y, z) to [[1, x, z], [0, 1, y], [0, 0, 1]] in Tau Ceti's upperUnitriangularGroup (Fin 3) R (upper triangular with diagonal 1, a subgroup of GL_3): the knowl's display with a = x, b = z, c = y, and the coordinate product z + z' + x y' is the matrix product. ModularPCubedGroup p is the modular group C_{p^2} x| C_p with the generator acting by v -> (1 + p) v (inr_mul_inl_mul_inv), non-abelian of order p^3 with an element of order p^2 for every prime p, hence not isomorphic to He_p (exponent p) for odd p. The K of exists_forall_iff_nonempty_mulEquiv satisfies the left-hand side itself (take H = K), so the theorem says exactly that He_p and K are the two non-abelian groups of order p^3 up to isomorphism. The LMFDB's He family takes primes p > 2 (lmfdb/groups/abstract/main.py, valid_params); every prime is covered. - `group.linear` [Groups › Abstract groups]: Round AG (AG1). Closes the round-AF blocker, on the user's ruling of 2026-11-12 that 'often simple or almost simple' needs PGL(n, q) almost simple. New: (1) IsAlmostSimple.of_centralizer_eq_bot: a group with a simple normal subgroup N of trivial centraliser is almost simple in LeanBridge's sense (IsAlmostSimple, LMFDB group.almost_simple: an embedding G -> Aut(N) by conjugation, MulAut.conjNormal, whose image contains Inn(N); N is non-abelian since an abelian N would lie in its own centraliser). (2) The image of PSL(n, F) under Mathlib's injective Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup.toPGL is normal in PGL(n, F) (an instance; it is the image of ker det, range_toPGL) and has trivial centraliser, for every field F and every n (Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup.centralizer_range_toPGL): if the class of g commutes with that of a transvection t, then t g = u g t for a scalar u; comparing the column of g on which t acts trivially gives u = 1 (Matrix.TransvectionStruct.eq_one_of_mul_mul_scalar_eq), so g commutes with every transvection and is scalar (Mathlib's mem_range_scalar_of_commute_transvectionStruct). (3) Hence PGL(n, F) is almost simple whenever PSL(n, F) is simple (Matrix.ProjGenLinGroup.isAlmostSimple_of_isSimpleGroup), so for n >= 3 and every field, and for n = 2 when |F| >= 4 (isAlmostSimple_fin; the bound is on Nat.card F, so for n = 2 the field is finite; over F_q this covers every PGL(n, q), n >= 2, other than PGL(2, 2) and PGL(2, 3)). (4) 'Often simple' for PGL itself: over a finite field PGL(n, q) is simple exactly when gcd(n, q - 1) = 1, in the same range (isSimpleGroup_fin_iff; general form isSimpleGroup_iff_coprime, for any finite F and index type with PSL simple): the image of PSL is a nontrivial normal subgroup, the whole group exactly when every unit is an n-th power (Mathlib's toPGL_surj_iff), which for the cyclic group F_q^x of order q - 1 holds exactly when gcd(n, q - 1) = 1 (Nat.Coprime.pow_left_bijective and, conversely, Cauchy's theorem: Nat.Coprime.of_forall_exists_pow_eq). With round AF's results (PGL(n, K) = GL/scalars is the group of linear automorphisms of P^{n-1}(K), recorded off-by-one; PSL(n, F) simple, Jordan-Dickson) every sentence of the knowl is proved: 'these groups are finite' by instances (GL(n, q): Mathlib; PGL(n, q): Tau Ceti's Matrix.ProjGenLinGroup.instFinite; their subgroups), 'often simple or almost simple' by PGL(n, q) itself, a projective linear group (almost simple for n >= 3 or q >= 4, simple iff gcd(n, q - 1) = 1), and by PSL(n, q), now a normal subgroup of PGL(n, q) (Mathlib's toPGL_injective, this file's normality and centraliser). The final clause 'and so they play an important role in the classification of finite simple groups' is a remark, not a statement. Supporting declarations not linked (limit of eight): Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup.centralizer_range_toPGL, Matrix.ProjGenLinGroup.isAlmostSimple_of_isSimpleGroup, Matrix.ProjGenLinGroup.isSimpleGroup_iff_coprime, IsAlmostSimple.of_centralizer_eq_bot, Mathlib's Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup.toPGL_injective and AF's Matrix.ProjGenLinGroup.toPermHom_injective. Text: the recorded off-by-one ('projective (n-1)-space') stands; AF's proposed rewording of 'often simple or almost simple' is no longer needed (the sentence is true as written, read as the families above). Review (AG1): formalised, confirmed. IsAlmostSimple is the LMFDB's definition (group.almost_simple: S <= G <= Aut(S) for a non-abelian simple S, as an embedding G -> Aut(S) whose image contains Inn(S)); the edge cases are excluded exactly (n = 1: PGL(1, q) is trivial; PGL(2, 2) and PGL(2, 3) have no non-abelian simple normal subgroup) and checked on PGL(3, 2) (simple) and PGL(2, 5) (almost simple, not simple). The user's ruling is met by PGL(n, q) itself, which is trivially a closed subgroup of PGL(n, q), so the closedness of the image of PSL(n, q) (true over a finite field, not formalised) is not needed; PSL(n, q) now sits inside PGL(n, q) as a normal subgroup with trivial centraliser, the point round AF raised. The closing clause 'and so they play an important role in the classification of finite simple groups' draws a consequence and states no theorem beyond the simplicity results; the classification itself is not invoked. Review changes: proofs use Mathlib's le_centralizer_iff_isMulCommutative and MulAut.conjNormal_val instead of hand-made copies; the repeated cancellation in eq_one_of_mul_mul_scalar_eq is one local lemma; layout, a hoisted n, and docstrings that no longer assert PGL(2, 2) = S3, PGL(2, 3) = S4 or the quotient PGL/PSL, which are not proved.

- `group.metabelian` [Groups › Abstract groups]: Round AJ (AJ7). The last gaps of AD2 ('p-groups of p-rank one are metabelian; p-rank is not defined; no IsExtraspecial definition') are closed, without the classification of these groups as cyclic or generalised quaternion. Group.pRank p G (MetabelianPRankOne) is the largest n such that G has an elementary abelian subgroup of order p^n (an abelian subgroup all of whose elements satisfy h^p = 1), the rank the knowl means (not group.rank's minimal number of generators). IsPGroup.isMetabelian_of_pRank_le_one: a finite p-group of p-rank at most one (in particular of p-rank one) is metabelian. Route: a maximal abelian normal subgroup A of a finite p-group contains its centraliser (IsPGroup.centralizer_le_of_maximal: otherwise the image of C_G(A) in the nilpotent G/A is a nontrivial normal subgroup, which meets the centre in some xA != 1, and the preimage of <xA> is abelian, normal and strictly larger); in a p-group of p-rank <= 1 every abelian subgroup is cyclic (IsPGroup.isCyclic_of_pRank_le_one: exponent = order, by induction on the exponent p^k through the p^(k-1)-power map, whose image is elementary abelian, so of order <= p); so A is cyclic, Aut(A) is abelian (IsCyclic.mulAutMulEquiv), every commutator acts trivially on A and lies in C_G(A) = A (IsPGroup.isMetabelian_of_forall_normal_isCyclic). Non-vacuity: Group.pRank_multiplicative_zmod (C_p has p-rank one); QuaternionGroup.pRank_two (every dicyclic group has 2-rank one, its only element of order 2 being a n) with QuaternionGroup.isPGroup_two_pow (QuaternionGroup (2^k), the generalised quaternion groups, are 2-groups). Extraspecial groups (ExtraspecialMetabelian): IsExtraspecial p G (a p-group whose centre has order p and equals both the commutator and the Frattini subgroup), IsExtraspecial.isMetabelian (the commutator subgroup is central), example TauCeti.HeisenbergGroup.isExtraspecial_zmod (the Heisenberg group over F_p; through IsPGroup.frattini_eq_closure_sup_commutator, the Frattini subgroup of a finite p-group is generated by the p-th powers and the commutators, from Tau Ceti's pro-p Frattini description). Every sentence is now proved: the definition, the extension equivalence, solvability and the abelian case (instances in Metabelian.lean), dihedral, quaternion (dicyclic), metacyclic, extraspecial groups and p-groups of p-rank one, and C_2^3 metabelian but not metacyclic. Also linkable if the cap allows: the definitions Group.pRank and IsExtraspecial, isMetabelian_of_commutator_le_center. Text: the recorded correction 'and groups of $p$-rank one.' -> 'and $p$-groups of $p$-rank one.' (A_5 has 3-rank one) is a fixable text (ruling of 2026-11-11); the typo 'metacylic' is recorded too. Overlap with Tau Ceti main: main has TauCeti.HeisenbergGroup.commutator_eq_zAxis (Heisenberg/Basic.lean), absent at the pin; ExtraspecialMetabelian proves it as a private auxiliary, to be replaced at the bump. Review (AJ7): formalised, confirmed. Group.pRank is the standard p-rank (largest rank of an elementary abelian p-subgroup), the one of the recorded correction; the LMFDB has no group p-rank (its source has only av.fq.p_rank), and a p-group of rank one in the sense of group.rank is cyclic, so that reading is covered too. IsExtraspecial is the standard definition (Z(P) = P' = Phi(P) of order p; the LMFDB has no group.extraspecial knowl), met by the Heisenberg group over F_p (D_4 for p = 2). Every sentence of the knowl has its declaration (table in review/AJ7_small.md).

- `group.monomial` [Groups › Abstract groups]: Round AJ (AJ2). Every mathematical statement of the knowl is proved for IsMGroup (finite G : Type; every simple W : FDRep ℂ G is isomorphic to Ind_H^G of a linear character χ : H →* ℂˣ). (1) 'Such a group is always solvable': Taketa's theorem IsMGroup.isSolvable (Isaacs, Character Theory, 5.12): by induction on n the n-th derived subgroup acts trivially on every irreducible representation of degree at most n; for W ≅ Ind_H^G χ of degree n + 1 = [G : H], the augmentation subrepresentation of ℂ[G/H] (Tau Ceti) has degree n, so G⁽ⁿ⁾ fixes every coset and lies in H, and G⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾ ≤ [H, H] ≤ ker χ together with its conjugates. (2) 'monomial groups include all supersolvable groups and solvable A-groups': IsMGroup.of_isSupersolvable (Huppert) and IsMGroup.of_isSolvable_of_isAGroup (Isaacs 6.23), both cases of IsMGroup.of_isSupersolvable_quotient (Isaacs 6.22: a normal solvable A-subgroup N with G/N supersolvable). The proof extends Tau Ceti's nilpotent case (FDRep.exists_character_eq_indClassFun_of_isNilpotent): for W not induced from a proper subgroup, every normal subgroup acting through commuting operators acts centrally (Clifford correspondence at the inertia group, Tau Ceti's exists_simple_liesOver_inertia_nonempty_iso_indFDRep and commute_of_inertia_eq_top); going up the derived series of N each term acts through a quotient that is nilpotent of class at most 2 and an A-group, hence abelian (IsAGroup.commutatorElement_mem_of_forall_commutatorElement_mem); and a proper centrally acting Z with G/Z supersolvable would give x ∉ Z with ⟨x⟩Z normal and acting through commuting operators. No extension of characters is needed. (3) The three non-implications, on LMFDB groups: A₄ is a solvable A-group (cube-free order 12, IsAGroup.of_forall_not_pow_three_dvd_card), hence monomial (alternatingGroup.isMGroup_fin_four), but not supersolvable (alternatingGroup.not_isSupersolvable_fin_four, by decide +kernel: no nontrivial cyclic normal subgroup): not_forall_isSupersolvable_of_isMGroup and not_forall_isSupersolvable_of_isSolvable_of_isAGroup; SL(2, 3) is solvable (Burnside's pᵃqᵇ theorem, Tau Ceti) but not monomial (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.not_isMGroup_fin_two_zmod_three: 7 conjugacy classes, from the 168 commuting pairs, so the squares of the seven irreducible degrees sum to 24 and one degree is 2; SL(2, 3) is generated by squares, so it has no subgroup of index 2; and in an M-group every irreducible degree is the index of a subgroup, IsMGroup.exists_index_eq_characterDegree): not_forall_isMGroup_of_isSolvable. 'A purely group-theoretic description of monomial groups is not known' is a remark on the literature, not a mathematical statement. Axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only (the finite checks use decide +kernel).

Formalised, with the recorded corrections (fixable text, ruling of 2026-11-11): the classes are those of nondegenerate forms (Mathlib's QuadraticMap.Nondegenerate, valid in every characteristic; the proofs only use a trivial radical), and the knowl's 'one equivalence class' in odd dimension is read as one similarity class. P (equivalent_parabolicForm_or_equivalent_smul_parabolicForm), and P, nu . P are not isometric, since they take the value 1 a different number of times, 2A + (q - 2)B against qB with A != B the numbers of zeros and of solutions of H = 1 for the hyperbolic part (not_equivalent_smul_parabolicForm). The blocker, the classification of nondegenerate quadratic forms over finite fields, is proved for every finite field F, both parities of q: odd dimension 2m+1, every nondegenerate Q has c . Q isometric to the parabolic form z^2 + x1 y1 + ... + xm ym for a unit c (exists_equivalent_smul_parabolicForm); even dimension 2m+2, every nondegenerate Q is isometric to the hyperbolic form (+) or to the elliptic form (-) (equivalent_hyperbolicForm_or_equivalent_ellipticForm), and no scalar multiple of the hyperbolic form is isometric to the elliptic one (not_equivalent_smul_hyperbolicForm_ellipticForm), so there are exactly two classes, for isometry and for similarity alike; every anisotropic plane is isometric to x^2 + xy + zeta y^2, so GO^- does not depend on zeta (equivalent_anisotropicPlane). Groups: similar forms have isomorphic O, SO, PGO, PSO (orthogonalGroupEquivOfSMul and its SO/PGO/PSO companions, by conjugation, which preserves the scalars), so GO(2m+1,q), SO, PGO, PSO are unique up to isomorphism (nonempty_orthogonalGroup_mulEquiv_parabolicForm and the specialOrthogonalGroup/projectiveOrthogonalGroup/projectiveSpecialOrthogonalGroup versions), and in even dimension every nondegenerate form has the groups of the + or the - form (nonempty_*_mulEquiv_hyperbolicForm_or_ellipticForm). The definitions (O, SO, PGO, PSO, the table, the standard forms QuadraticForm.parabolicForm, hyperbolicForm, ellipticForm) are round R3's. Range: the statements cover n = 2m+1 >= 1 and n = 2m+2 >= 2, the LMFDB's orthogonal groups; for n = 0 there is one class, a case the LMFDB does not use. No new error. Review (AG5, 2026-11-13): formalised, confirmed. - `group.perfect` [Groups › Abstract groups]: Round AD (AD5_psl25). The only gap left by AD1, SL(2,5)/{±1} ≅ A5 behind 'SL(2,5) = C2.A5' (group.name: A.B is an extension with normal subgroup A and quotient B; no splitting is claimed), is proved in PSL2ZModFive.lean: the centre of SL(2,5) is {±1} (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.center_two_zmod_five), of order 2 (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.card_center_two_zmod_five), and PSL(2,5) = SL(2,5)/centre ≃* alternatingGroup (Fin 5) (twoZModFiveEquivAlternatingGroup). Route: Tau Ceti's A5 ≅ Δ(2,3,5) (TauCeti.TriangleGroup.equivIcosahedral). The classes of S = [[0,-1],[1,0]], T = [[0,-1],[1,1]], U = [[1,0],[1,1]] satisfy the relations x², y³, z⁵, zyx (S² = T³ = UTS = -1 and U⁵ = 1, by decide on 2x2 matrices over ZMod 5), giving Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup.icosahedralHom : Δ(2,3,5) →* PSL(2,5). It is injective as Δ(2,3,5) is simple and S ≠ ±1, and bijective as both groups have order 60 (|SL(2,5)| = 120 by Matrix.card_SL_field). No native_decide, no maxHeartbeats. With AD1 every sentence is proved: perfect iff no nontrivial abelian or soluble quotient (all groups), iff no nontrivial cyclic quotient for finite groups (the recorded correction; Q is the counterexample, Group.subsingleton_of_surjective_rat); non-abelian simple and quasisimple groups are perfect (IsSimpleGroup.isQuasisimple and the class field IsQuasisimple.isPerfect, LeanBridge.ForMathlib.GroupTheory.SpecificGroups.Quasisimple); SL(2,5) is perfect, and every composition series of it has a factor of order 2 (Group.exists_card_factor_eq_two_SL_two_five), the centre C2 of C2.A5. Reviewed (review/AI7_finishing.md): formalised, confirmed. The knowl's one mathematical statement is the parenthesis '(Here p is the largest prime less than 2^128.)' for p = 340282366920938463463374607431768211297. Proved as written: Nat.isGreatest_prime_lt_two_pow_128, IsGreatest {q | q.Prime and q < 2^128} p, for the literal p of the knowl (the same 39 digits); its first half is Nat.prime_two_pow_128_sub_159, p is prime. Not linked, being no statements of the knowl: Nat.two_pow_128_sub_159 (2^128 - 159 = p, by rfl) and Mathlib's lucas_primality. Route: p is prime by lucas_primality with the witness 5 and p - 1 = 2^5 * 3 * 10253 * 29333 * 4454477 * 42113237 * 62826870453001 (5^(p-1) = 1 and 5^((p-1)/q) != 1 in ZMod p for each prime factor q); the factor 62826870453001 is certified the same way (witness 11, 62826870453000 = 2^3 * 3 * 5^3 * 73 * 13147 * 21821), the smaller factors by norm_num; each of the 158 numbers n with p < n < 2^128 fails Fermat's test to the base 2 (2^(n-1) != 1 in ZMod n; interval_cases, then one reduce_mod_char per case), so none is prime. The modular powers are evaluated by reduce_mod_char and the final comparisons by decide, in the kernel: no native_decide, and the axioms of every declaration of the module, the private ones included, are propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound (no Lean.ofReduceBool, no Lean.trustCompiler). The review re-checked the certificate independently in Python (both factorisations, the Lucas conditions, the small prime factors by trial division, and that none of the 158 numbers passes Fermat's test to the base 2). The module builds in 8.3 s (lake build; about 14 s with the imports loaded), so it can run in CI. Reading, the audit's, both authors' and the review's: the generator a_j = a_0 b^j mod p with its constants a_0 = 123 and b, and the product-replacement procedure for group elements (the (k+5)-tuple, 20 rounds, 'picking random subscripts i and j according to our pseudo-random sequence of integers') are the database's algorithm for its labels, a convention like that of the sibling group.division_computing_labels, which the audit of 2026-11-13 left under 'Nothing to formalise'; the knowl states no fact about them (no period: b is not a primitive root modulo p, its order is (p - 1)/2; no property of the group elements), and it does not say how the indices i and j are read off the integers, so the text does not determine the procedure. No text error (p is 2^128 - 159, prime, and the largest prime below 2^128). Names: digits for large numerals as in Mathlib's isCarmichael_561, isCarmichael_1105, ofJ_1728_of_two_ne_zero and four_mul_arctan_inv_5_sub_arctan_inv_239 (and Tau Ceti's j_eq_1728_iff), and two_pow for 2^_ as in Mathlib's Nat.two_pow_pos. Changes by the review: the private helper (a prime dividing a power of a product of primes is one of them) is now one application of Mathlib's mem_list_primes_of_dvd_prod; the binder n is a variable; the identity 2^128 - 159 = p is proved by rfl. Defined the stronger notion Group.IsQGroup (every complex representation is realized over ℚ, via LeanBridge's FDRep.IsRealizedOver with the bottom subfield ℚ ⊆ ℂ), proved it implies rationality and holds for the trivial group (Group.isQGroup_unit, so it is not vacuous), and proved Q₈ = QuaternionGroup 2 rational (QuaternionGroup.isRational_two) but not a ℚ-group (QuaternionGroup.not_isQGroup_two): its 2-dimensional representation a 1 ↦ diag(i, -i), xa 0 ↦ !![0, -1; 1, 0] (QuaternionGroup.twoDimHom, built from the dicyclic presentation) is not realized over ℚ, since the rational matrices of a 1 and xa 0 would satisfy tr A = tr B = tr AB = 0, tr A² = tr B² = -2, impossible over an ordered field (Matrix.false_of_trace_quaternion). The sentence 'It is an unsolved problem to determine what cyclic groups of order p can be composition factors of rational groups' reports the state of the literature and makes no mathematical claim to prove.

Every sentence is proved, for finite G (the LMFDB's abstract groups; G : Type, as Mathlib's groupHomology over Z requires; K and C in any universe). Closes the whole tracker v60c blocker ('Schur's theory of stem extensions of a finite group G (|K| <= |M(G)|, so |C| is bounded; K = M(G) when |C| is maximal; Schur covers unique up to isoclinism, and up to isomorphism for perfect G)'), with M(G) = H_2(G, Z) = groupHomology (Rep.trivial Z G Z) 2, the definition of group.schur_multiplier. Nothing from Tau Ceti's main is used (its MonoidHom.CentralCover, universal central extensions of perfect groups, has no link to H_2(G, Z) and is not needed). Definition: the committed GroupExtension.IsStem and Subgroup.IsStem (K <= Z(C) cap C'). Text error already recorded, fixable (lmfdb-knowl-edits.md, section group.stem_extension): Old '{{KNOWL('group.commutator_subgroup', 'commutator')}} of $G$' New '{{KNOWL('group.commutator_subgroup', 'commutator')}} of $C$' (the center too is that of C). Route. (1) CentralExtension.lean, for any group G: for pi : C ->* G with central kernel N and a section sigma, the factor set alpha(g, h) = sigma(g) sigma(h) sigma(gh)^-1 in Z(C) (MonoidHom.centralFactorSet) pairs with the inhomogeneous 2-chains of the trivial representation Z of G and kills the boundaries (cocycle identity), giving theta : H_2(G, Z) -> Z(C) (MonoidHom.H2ToCenter). Its image is exactly N cap C' (MonoidHom.mem_range_H2ToCenter_iff): it lies in C' because the image of a cycle in C^ab is that of its boundary under [g] -> sigma(g) C'; conversely, if z in N cap C' were not in the image, a Q/Z-valued character chi of Z(C) killing the image but not z (Mathlib's CharacterModule) makes chi o alpha vanish on the 2-cycles, so it factors through the boundary map and extends to the 1-chains (Q/Z injective, CharacterModule.dual_surjective_of_injective): chi(alpha(g, h)) = b(g) + b(h) - b(gh); then c -> chi(c sigma(pi c)^-1) + b(pi c) is a homomorphism C -> Q/Z extending chi, which kills C', so chi(z) = 0, a contradiction. Hence N cap C' is a quotient of H_2(G, Z) (MonoidHom.surjective_H2ToKerInfCommutator). (2) SchurCover.lean: the 1-boundaries are a free Z-module (Tau Ceti's Submodule.free_of_isPrincipalIdealRing, any rank), so the 2-cycles are a retract of the 2-chains; extending Z_2 -> H_2 gives a normalised 2-cocycle with values in H_2(G, Z) (SchurCover.factorSet, a Tau Ceti FactorSet for the trivial action) whose extension SchurCover G has theta = the inclusion of H_2(G, Z), so SchurCover.extension : 1 -> H_2(G, Z) -> SchurCover G -> G -> 1 is a stem extension (SchurCover.isStem_extension, any G). For finite G its centre has finite index, so its commutator subgroup is finite by Schur's theorem (Mathlib's instance for finitely many commutators; the commutator set is finite through Group.centralCommutatorMap) and H_2(G, Z) is finite (SchurCover.finite_H2). (3) MaximalStem.lean. 'For fixed G, the size of C is bounded': GroupExtension.IsStem.nat_card_le, |C| <= |G| |H_2(G, Z)| for every stem extension, C being finite (GroupExtension.IsStem.finite, so no junk value), the bound attained by the Schur cover (SchurCover.nat_card). 'For any extension with C of maximal size, the kernel K is isomorphic to the Schur multiplier': GroupExtension.IsMaximalStem (a stem extension with |C'| <= |C| for every stem extension 1 -> K' -> C' -> G -> 1, K', C' : Type), equivalent to |K| = |H_2(G, Z)| (GroupExtension.isMaximalStem_iff); then the homomorphism H_2(G, Z) -> K of GroupExtension.IsStem.H2ToKernel is bijective (GroupExtension.IsMaximalStem.bijective_H2ToKernel); maximal ones exist (SchurCover.isMaximalStem_extension). 'In general, C is only determined up to isoclinism in such an extension': GroupExtension.IsMaximalStem.isIsoclinic (the fibre product P of C_1 and C_2 over G is a central extension of G, |ker cap P'| <= |H_2(G, Z)| = |K_1| by MonoidHom.nat_card_ker_inf_commutator_le, and the first projection maps ker cap P' onto K_1 <= C_1', so the kernel of P -> C_1 meets P' trivially and round AL's Group.isIsoclinic_of_surjective applies; likewise for C_2), and the 'only': GroupExtension.not_forall_nonempty_mulEquiv_of_isMaximalStem (KleinFour.lean: D_4 and Q_8 are the middle groups of stem extensions of maximal size of C_2 x C_2, DihedralGroup.isMaximalStem_reduceModTwoExtension and QuaternionGroup.isMaximalStem_reduceModTwoExtension, not isomorphic by the committed DihedralGroup.isEmpty_mulEquiv_quaternionGroup; maximality from |H_2(C_2 x C_2, Z)| = 2, nat_card_H2_kleinFour, whose upper bound is MonoidHom.nat_card_ker_le_two: the kernel of a stem extension of C_2 x C_2 is C' <= <[x, y]> with [x, y]^2 = [x^2, y] = 1, applied to the Schur cover). 'but if G is perfect then C is determined up to isomorphism': GroupExtension.IsMaximalStem.nonempty_mulEquiv (C_1 and C_2 are perfect, GroupExtension.IsStem.isPerfect, and both projections map P' isomorphically onto them). Checks: lake build of the four modules, #lint 0 errors, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, every multi-lemma simp list checked by single deletion, no name clash in the three trees or Tau Ceti main. Lean: 1048 new lines in four files (CentralExtension 238, SchurCover 236, MaximalStem 333, KleinFour 241). Also linkable: GroupExtension.IsStem.finite, GroupExtension.isMaximalStem_iff, SchurCover.isMaximalStem_extension, SchurCover.nat_card, GroupExtension.IsStem.isPerfect, DihedralGroup.isMaximalStem_reduceModTwoExtension, QuaternionGroup.isMaximalStem_reduceModTwoExtension, MonoidHom.nat_card_ker_inf_commutator_le. Review (AM5_schur review, 2026-11-17): formalised, confirmed, links unchanged. IsMaximalStem is the knowl's 'C of maximal size' among the stem extensions of G; it compares only the stem extensions with K', C' : Type, which loses nothing for finite G (a maximal one bounds the stem extensions in every universe, and maximality among those of any one universe implies IsMaximalStem: both checked in the review's Probe.lean; the docstring now says so). 'the order of a stem group divides the order of every other group in its isoclinism class': Group.IsStemGroup.nat_card_dvd (an isoclinism maps Z(G) cap G' onto Z(H) cap H', Group.Isoclinism.centerInfCommutatorEquiv, so |S| = |S/Z(S)| |Z(S) cap S'| divides |H| = |H/Z(H)| |Z(H)|). Not through a junk value in the LMFDB's finite setting: a stem group isoclinic to a finite group is finite (Group.IsStemGroup.finite_of_isIsoclinic, which uses the divisibility with |H| > 0), and for groups of every cardinality the divisibility holds in cardinal arithmetic (Group.IsStemGroup.lift_mk_dvd). (1) Huppert's criterion: Group.isSupersolvable_of_forall_isCoatom_index_prime (a finite group all of whose maximal subgroups have prime index is supersolvable) and, with the committed IsSupersolvable.index_prime_of_isCoatom, Group.isSupersolvable_iff_forall_isCoatom_index_prime (the knowl's 'a group is supersolvable if and only if each of its maximal subgroups has prime index'). Proof (SupersolvablePrimeIndex.lean, 568 lines): the property passes to quotients (index_prime_quotient_of_forall_isCoatom, through Mathlib's Subgroup.isCoatom_comap_of_surjective); the Sylow subgroups for the largest prime p are normal (normal_sylow_of_forall_isCoatom_index_prime: Sylow counting in G and in a maximal subgroup over the normalizer gives q = 1 mod p); with a Schur-Zassenhaus complement H of P, H acts on V = P/Phi(P) (RankFrattini's F_p-structure, the conjugation representation through Tau Ceti's MulAut.mapQuotient), and every maximal subrepresentation has index p (card_eq_mul_card_of_isCoatom, through relIndex_prime_of_forall_isCoatom: the preimage W gives the maximal subgroup W H of index [P : W]); Maschke (Mathlib's IsSemisimpleRepresentation) makes the atoms lines, so commutators and (p-1)-th powers act trivially on V (Representation.commutatorElement_eq_one_of_forall_isCoatom, pow_card_sub_one_eq_one_of_forall_isCoatom), hence centralize P by Burnside's theorem (IsPGroup.commute_of_forall_conjNormal_eq, from Tau Ceti's IsPGroup.isPGroup_ker_mapQuotient_frattini); then H has a common eigenvector on the elements of order p of the centre of P (Representation.exists_ne_zero_forall_apply_eq_smul, with Module.End.exists_ne_zero_apply_eq_smul_of_pow_eq_one via the minimal polynomial dividing X^p - X), which gives a normal subgroup of order p inside P (exists_ne_one_normal_zpowers_of_forall_commute, exists_ne_one_normal_zpowers_of_forall_isCoatom), and induction on |G| finishes. (2) 'The smallest solvable groups that are not supersolvable are A4, S4, SL2(F3) and C2 x A4': Group.isSolvable_and_not_isSupersolvable_iff (a finite group of order at most 24 is solvable and not supersolvable iff it is isomorphic to alternatingGroup (Fin 4), Perm (Fin 4), SL(2, ZMod 3) or Multiplicative (ZMod 2) x alternatingGroup (Fin 4); the orders are 12, 24, 24, 24, so every other solvable non-supersolvable group has order above 24), with Group.nonempty_mulEquiv_of_not_isSupersolvable and Group.isSupersolvable_of_card_lt_twelve (A4 is the smallest); the four are pairwise non-isomorphic (alternatingGroup.isEmpty_mulEquiv_perm_fin_four, alternatingGroup.isEmpty_mulEquiv_specialLinearGroup_fin_two_zmod_three, alternatingGroup.isEmpty_mulEquiv_prod_alternatingGroup_fin_four, Equiv.Perm.isEmpty_mulEquiv_specialLinearGroup_fin_two_zmod_three, Equiv.Perm.isEmpty_mulEquiv_prod_alternatingGroup_fin_four, Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.isEmpty_mulEquiv_prod_alternatingGroup_fin_four: they have 4, 10, 2 and 8 solutions of g^2 = 1, compared through the committed MulEquiv.card_sq_eq_one). Proof (SupersolvableSmallOrder.lean, 758 lines): prime powers and products of two primes are supersolvable; orders 18 and 20 by a normal Sylow subgroup (order 18 through exists_ne_one_normal_zpowers_of_forall_commute of part (1)); for orders 12 and 24 a normal Sylow 3-subgroup gives supersolvability, otherwise there are four Sylow 3-subgroups and G acts on them (sylowThreePermHom) with a kernel of order prime to 3 dividing |G|/4: order 12 gives A4 (Perm.eq_alternatingGroup_of_index_eq_two), order 24 gives S4 (kernel 1) or a central extension of A4 by C2 (kernel {1, z}), identified with SL(2, 3) or C2 x A4 by lifting generators of A4 to elements satisfying the relations of a polycyclic presentation (relatorsTwentyFour, with LeanBridge's card_presentedGroup_le), the concrete groups being checked by decide +kernel (relations, generation, and that every nontrivial normal subgroup meets the relevant elements, so the induced homomorphism is injective; PolycyclicPresentation.nonempty_mulEquiv_of_twentyFour). The solvability and non-supersolvability of the four groups (AJ2) are restated through the iff. All other sentences were proved in rounds T1 and AJ2 (record AJ2_monomial_groups.json): the definition with strict inclusions (Group.IsSupersolvable, isSupersolvable_iff_exists_strictMono), supersolvable implies solvable and not conversely (IsSupersolvable.isSolvable, not_forall_isSupersolvable_of_isSolvable), monomial (IsMGroup.of_isSupersolvable), finite abelian, nilpotent, metacyclic, Z-groups and squarefree order (isSupersolvable_of_isMulCommutative, IsNilpotent.isSupersolvable, IsMetacyclic.isSupersolvable, IsZGroup.isSupersolvable, isSupersolvable_of_squarefree_card), subgroups and quotients but not extensions (IsSupersolvable.subgroup, IsSupersolvable.quotient, not_forall_isSupersolvable_of_isSupersolvable_quotient), not every supersolvable group is nilpotent or metacyclic (not_forall_isNilpotent_of_isSupersolvable, not_forall_isMetacyclic_of_isSupersolvable); the two LMFDB search links illustrate these and are not mathematical claims. - `hecke_algebra.definition` [Modular forms › Miscellaneous] (#36): The R-Hecke algebra of an R-module with Hecke operators as Algebra.adjoin R of the operators in End_R(M) (commutative for commuting operators, finite over a noetherian R for finite M), instantiated over ℂ on M_k(Γ₁(N)) and S_k(Γ₁(N)) (all T_n, including U_p, and the diamonds; finite-dimensional), on M_k(N, χ) and S_k(N, χ) (classical T_n of the Γ₀(N) Hecke ring; commutative), and over every commutative ring R (ℚ, finite fields, ℤ) on the modular symbols 𝕄_w(Γ₁(N); R), equal over ℤ to Tau Ceti's heckeTAlgebra. Tau Ceti's T_n on Γ₁(N) is the single double coset Γ₁(N) diag(1, n) Γ₁(N), which differs from the classical T_n when p² ∣ n for a prime p ∤ N (T(1, p²) = T_{p²} - p^{k-2}⟨p⟩), so the diamonds are included as generators and the algebra is the classical ℂ[T_n, ⟨d⟩]. Spaces of forms are taken over ℂ only, as they carry no ℚ-structure in the pinned libraries.

Level: isLevel_level, if Γ contains Γ_𝔟(𝔑) of SL(𝒪_F ⊕ 𝔟) for a nonzero 𝔑, then level 𝔟 (sl 𝔟) Γ is its level (IsLevel: nonzero, contained, and dividing every nonzero 𝔐 with Γ_𝔟(𝔐) ≤ Γ): the family has a maximal element by noetherianity, the greatest as it is closed under sums. Formalised on the recorded corrected text (lmfdb-knowl-edits.md: 'If the ideals 𝔑 with Γ_𝔟(𝔑) ⊆ Γ have a least element for divisibility (as they always do when Γ ⊆ SL(Z_F ⊕ 𝔟)), it is called the level'; the wording 'The largest such 𝔑, that is, the least for divisibility, is called the level; it exists for the congruence subgroups of SL(Z_F ⊕ b)' of the AC7 and AF5 reports paraphrases it, with the same content), on the ruling of 2026-11-11 (fixable text is not partial). In GL⁺(𝒪_F ⊕ 𝔟) a least ideal need not exist (counterexample over Q(√2) in CongruenceSubgroup.lean's docstring, not formalised; the corrected text claims nothing there); in the LMFDB's setting, the groups Γ₀(𝔑)_𝔟 of GL⁺, the level exists and is 𝔑 (level_gammaZero, round ZZ). Hypotheses instantiated (F = Q, 𝔟 = 1, 𝔑 = ⊤, Γ = Γ₀); no sorry, no new axioms; #lint clean. In a real inner product space it is LeanBridge's ZLattice.IsArithmetic (isArithmeticLattice_innerₗ_iff). The forms need not be symmetric or nondegenerate for any of this. If cB makes L^# a primitive integral lattice, so does -cB (its values are the negatives, with the same scale ideal), so the rescaling is unique only up to sign. - `lattice.genus` [Groups › Lattices]: The gap is closed: LinearMap.BilinForm.genus B L hL is the knowl's genus on the real space V, the set of lattices M on V (finitely generated, discrete, spanning V over R; Submodule.IsDiscreteLattice) with M_p = Z_p ⊗ M isometric to L_p for every prime p, each with the Z_p-bilinear extension of its integral form (LinearMap.BilinForm.integralForm, B restricted to the lattice). It ranges over all lattices on the real space V, not only those in the rational span of L (the sweep's example sigma(Z^2), sigma a rotation by 1 radian, is such a lattice; that example is not formalised). Was partial (11-06 sweep, tracker v63, hard): the n <= 4 theorem and the non-uniqueness. (1) IsMinkowskiReduced.integralNorm_eq_successiveMinimum and gramMatrix_apply_self_eq_successiveMinimum: for a positive semidefinite integral lattice of rank <= 4 (the LMFDB's lattices are positive definite) and every Minkowski-reduced basis e, gramMatrix e i i is the i-th successive minimum (van der Waerden). Tau Ceti's IsMinkowskiReduced is the knowl's definition (b_i of least norm among the i-th vectors of the bases agreeing with b before i, i.e. among the vectors with which b_0..b_{i-1} extend to a basis). Proof checked: Tau Ceti's lambda_i <= beta(e_i, e_i); conversely a vector y of norm <= lambda_i outside the span of e_0..e_{i-1}, m >= i its last nonzero coordinate c: c = +-1 extends e_0..e_{m-1} to a basis; |c| >= 2 rounds the coefficients of y/c, each step costing at most beta(e_j, e_j)/4, and m <= 3 gives beta(y, y) >= 4 beta(a, a) >= beta(e_m, e_m). The bound n <= 4 is needed: Z^5 + Z(1/2,...,1/2) with the form 4x.y (halfGlueLattice 4) has successive minima 4,4,4,4,4 but every reduced basis has diagonal 4,4,4,4,5 (computed). (2) Non-uniqueness: the simple roots of A_3 and their partial sums are reduced bases (bases of minimal vectors, isMinkowskiReduced_of_forall_integralNorm_eq_minimum, isMinkowskiReduced_typeASimpleRootBasis, isMinkowskiReduced_typeAThreePartialSumBasis), with Gram matrices the Cartan matrix and (2,1,1;1,2,1;1,1,2) = T^t C T for T upper unitriangular (gramMatrix_typeAThreePartialSumBasis, gramMatrix_typeAThreePartialSumBasis_ne); rechecked by hand, and no signed permutation of a basis relates them (computed). (3) The rest of the knowl: gramMatrix with gramMatrix_apply and isSymm_gramMatrix (the symmetric matrix [B(w_i, w_j)]), map_gramMatrix (every Z-basis of L extends to a Q-basis of V, in which the Gram matrix of V is that of L; it replaces the record's rationalBasis, which concerns only the chosen basis), Mathlib's LinearMap.BilinForm.toMatrix and isSymm_toMatrix_iff_isSymm (the Gram matrix of a basis of V), gramMatrix_unitLatticeBasis (Z^3), gramMatrix_eq_transpose_mul_gramMatrix_mul (A = T^t G T for a form-preserving map); the database and search sentences are not mathematics. Convention: the successive minima are norms B(v, v), as in Tau Ceti and in reduction theory, and as the LMFDB's own minimum (lattice.minimum, formalised reading 'length' as norm); lattice.successive_minima, which lattice.gram does not link, measures them as lengths through the unit ball, whose squares these are (t K meets L in the vectors of norm <= t^2, so lambda_i^2 is the least bound for i independent vectors of norm <= it). Text: 'For an integral lattice L, the minimal vectors of L come in pairs: if v is a minimal vector, then so is -v. A minimal vector is normalized if its first nonzero component is positive.' The definition: IsNormalized b x, for a Z-basis b of L indexed by a linearly ordered type: exists i, every coordinate b.repr x j with j < i vanishes and b.repr x i > 0, the knowl's 'first nonzero component is positive'. Reading: the components are the coordinates in the basis of the Gram matrix in which the LMFDB stores the lattice, indexed by Fin n (its pages list the normalized minimal vectors as integer coordinate vectors, lmfdb/lattice/main.py). Justification of the definition: isNormalized_neg_iff (well-ordered index type): for x != 0, -x is normalized iff x is not (isNormalized_iff_pos_toLex: normalized means positive in the lexicographic order of the coordinates), so each pair has exactly one normalized vector; kissingNumber_eq_two_mul_ncard: for a positive definite lattice the kissing number is twice the number of normalized minimal vectors (the LMFDB's code uses kissing/2 for their number). - `lattice.perfect` [Groups › Lattices]: Round AJ (AJ4): every stated fact of the knowl is proved for ZLattice.IsPerfect (L a Z-submodule of EuclideanSpace R iota, with no further hypothesis: IsPerfect.discreteTopology and IsPerfect.isZLattice show a perfect submodule is a lattice, discrete and of full rank). Core lemma IsPerfect.eq_zero_of_apply_self_eq_zero: a symmetric bilinear form B on R^n with B(x, x) = 0 at the minimal vectors of a perfect lattice is zero (pair the matrix A of B with the x x^T by the trace form: trace(A^T A) = 0, so A = 0). (1) Well-rounded in the knowl's own sense (lattice.well_rounded: S(L) spans a sublattice of finite index): IsPerfect.relIndex_span_minimalVectors_ne_zero, from the committed IsPerfect.span_minimalVectors and the general ZLattice.relIndex_span_minimalVectors_ne_zero (ranks). (2) Arithmetic: IsPerfect.isArithmetic (ZLattice.IsArithmetic) and IsPerfect.exists_isIntegralLattice_isSimilarLattice (similar to a finitely generated discrete integral lattice of R^n, the knowl lattice.arithmetic's definition, through round ZY's isArithmeticLattice_iff). Route: IsPerfect.inner_mem_span_minimum_sq, every inner product of L is a rational multiple of the minimal norm m: for Q-linear f : R -> Q with f(m) = 0 (Mathlib's Submodule.exists_le_ker_of_notMem), the form with Gram matrix f(<b_i, b_j>) in a Z-basis of L vanishes at the minimal vectors, hence is zero; then a common denominator over the basis. (3) Determined by its minimal vectors (Voronoi): IsPerfect.eq_of_apply_self_eq (a symmetric bilinear form is determined by its values B(x, x) at S(L): the Gram matrix is the unique solution of a^T A a = m), IsPerfect.inner_map_eq (a linear map scaling the norms of the minimal vectors by c is a similitude of ratio c), IsPerfect.inner_map_eq_of_mapsTo (an isometry when the minima agree) and IsPerfect.isSimilarLattice_of_mapsTo (a lattice M = psi(L), psi linear bijective with psi(S(L)) contained in S(M), is similar to L; the Gram matrix of M in psi(b) is (m(M)/m(L))^2 times that of L in b). (4) Voronoi's finiteness: finite_quotient_perfectSimilaritySetoid (the quotient of {L // IsPerfect L} by similarity, perfectSimilaritySetoid on round ZY's IsSimilarLattice, is finite for every n, n >= 2 included) and exists_finite_forall_isPerfect_exists_isSimilarLattice (finitely many perfect lattices meet every class). Route, with no volumes or Hermite constant: a basis b of R^n inside S(L) (IsPerfect.exists_basis_mem_minimalVectors); exists_nsmul_eq_sum_zsmul, from Tau Ceti's TauCeti.simultaneous_dirichlet (pin): if w in L is a real combination of k vectors of L of norm <= m then q w is an integral combination of them for some 1 <= q <= (k+1)^k (the difference has norm < m); hence the coordinates of L in b have denominators dividing K!, K = coordBound n = (n+1)^n, and the minimal vectors have coordinates of absolute value <= K (the same lemma for b_i and the family y, b_j, j != i); so the coordinate sets of S(L) and of L in [0,1)^n lie in the finite set coordBox n and determine L and S(L), and two perfect lattices with the same data are similar by (3). Non-vacuity: isPerfect_hexagonalLattice (the hexagonal lattice of R^2, minimum_hexagonalLattice = 1). Text: 'is uniquely determined by its minimal vectors' is false as a statement about subsets of R^n (D_12 and D_12^+, also D_10 and D_10^+, are distinct non-similar perfect lattices with the same minimal vectors: the glue vectors of D_n^+ have norm n/4 > 2) and is proved in the classical reading (3); old and new strings in review/AJ4_lattices.author-report.md, a judgement point for the user (reading versus text correction). Verified: lake build of the three modules through the guard, #lint clean, #print axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. New import: TauCeti.NumberTheory.DiophantineApproximation.Dirichlet (at the pin). Review (AJ4): formalised confirmed. Every sentence checked against the LMFDB's definitions: well-rounded is lattice.well_rounded's finite index, arithmetic is lattice.arithmetic's 'similar to an integral lattice' (finitely generated, discrete, integral, in R^n), similarity classes are those of IsSimilarLattice (lattice.similarity), and Voronoi's finiteness is proved for every n with no hypothesis beyond Fintype (TauCeti.simultaneous_dirichlet has none either). 'Uniquely determined by its minimal vectors' is a fixable text, not a genuine doubt: the literal reading (as subsets of R^n) is false (D_12 and D_12^+, both perfect, same minimal vectors, minimum 2, determinants 4 and 1; D_12 and D_10 perfect checked by the rank 78, resp. 55, of the x x^T), and the classical one (Voronoi's definition of a perfect form: determined by its minimum and the coordinates of its minimal vectors) is proved, up to similarity and, for equal minima, up to isometry; text error recorded in review/AJ4_lattices.md. Reading of the last sentence, decided by the review: for every rank n >= 5 (resp. n >= 10) there is a positive definite integral lattice of rank n that is well-rounded but not generated by its minimal vectors (resp. generated by them with no basis of them). The sentence states where the conditions differ, not that they agree below rank 5 or 10; its probable source (Boettcher, Fukshansky, Garcia, Maharaj, Needell, Lattices from tight equiangular frames, arXiv:1607.05350, section 2) says 'strictly stronger than the first when rk >= 5' and 'an even stronger condition (at least when rk >= 10)'. The agreement in lower rank (Martinet; Martinet and Schurmann) is not stated and not formalised. (1) halfGlueLattice m = Z^{m+1} + Z(1/2,...,1/2) with the form 4 x.y (scaled D_{m+1}^*), Gram matrix halfGlueGram in the basis e_1..e_m, h: finrank_halfGlueLattice (m + 1), isPosDef_halfGlueLattice, minimum_halfGlueLattice (4 for m >= 4), isWellRounded_halfGlueLattice, not_isGeneratedByMinimalVectors_halfGlueLattice (the minimal vectors +-e_1..+-e_{m+1} span Z^{m+1}, of index 2). (2) martinetSchurmannLattice k: the Z-span of x = c/5, c = (4,4,4,2,2,2,3,3,3,3), e_1..e_10 with Gram matrix msGram (the symmetrisation over S3 x S3 x S4 of Martinet and Schurmann's example, IJNT 8 (2012), section 8) and k orthogonal f_l of norm 72: finrank_martinetSchurmannLattice (10 + k), isPosDef, minimum 72, mem_minimalVectors_martinetSchurmannLattice_iff (exactly +-x, +-e_i, +-f_l, via msT_eq_of_msQuad_le: t^T G t <= 1800 only at t = 0, +-c, +-5 e_i), isGeneratedByMinimalVectors_martinetSchurmannLattice, not_isStronglyWellRounded_martinetSchurmannLattice (for each of the 11 + k pairs a sublattice containing the other pairs, so a basis of 10 + k minimal vectors cannot exist). Recomputed independently by the review (scratch/AO2_lattices-review/examples.py, exact LLL and Fincke-Pohst): half-glue n = 5..10 (minimum 4, 2n minimal vectors +-e_i, their span of index 2; n = 4 is generated by its 24 minimal vectors), Martinet-Schurmann k = 0, 1, 2 (x.e_i = 12, x.x = 72, minimum 72, exactly 22, 24, 26 minimal vectors as stated, next norm 78, their span of index 1, the maximal minors of the 11 + k pairs in 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, never 1). About 1450 lines.
