- `lf.defining_polynomial` [Fields › Local fields]: The gap of round ZZ is closed: every finite extension K of ℚ_p has a monic defining polynomial f ∈ ℤ[x] (exists_monic_nonempty_isAdjoinRoot: Nonempty (IsAdjoinRoot K (f.map ℤ → ℚ_p)), so f is irreducible over ℚ_p and K = ℚ_p(a) for a root a, by LeanBridge's IsAdjoinRoot.nonempty_iff, the defining-polynomial notion linked for nf.defining_polynomial), hence also one in ℤ_p[x] (exists_monic_nonempty_isAdjoinRoot_padicInt). Route, avoiding Hensel: the minimal polynomial of a primitive element a, embedded in ℚ̄_p (Mathlib's PadicAlgCl with the spectral norm), is approximated by a monic g ∈ ℚ[x] of the same degree (ℚ dense in ℚ_p); by Mathlib's continuity of roots g has a root β closer to a than every other conjugate, so a ∈ ℚ_p(β) by Mathlib's Krasner lemma (IsKrasner.of_completeSpace), and ℚ_p(β) = ℚ_p(a) by degrees (exists_ratPolynomial_adjoin_simple_eq, following Mathlib's proof of IsAlgClosed.of_denseRange); clearing denominators (IsLocalization.integerNormalization, integralNormalization) gives a monic f ∈ ℤ[x] with root d·b generating K and of degree [K : ℚ_p], hence its minimal polynomial. Applies to ℚ_[2] over itself (checked). Review (AA2): outcome changed to formalised. Every mathematical sentence is proved: the definition, 'can be chosen to be monic with coefficients in ℤ_p' and 'by Krasner's lemma, we can further take f(x) ∈ ℤ[x]', the last being the only gap the sweep of 2026-11-06 recorded. The numbered list ('The LMFDB uses the following conventions for choosing defining polynomials') is a remark about the database, which the ruling of 2026-11-06 excludes, and neither of the author's two reasons counts: the unfixed storage choice ('When it is feasible to compute, we use the Conway polynomial') says which polynomial is stored, not what a defining polynomial is; and that a monic lift of a polynomial irreducible mod p defines the unramified extension of that degree is not stated anywhere in the knowl, only presupposed by the storage rule ('needs to be irreducible modulo p' cannot be a mathematical claim: x² − p²u defines the unramified ℚ_p(√u) for odd p and is x² mod p). That presupposition is unproved; it is closable from the pins (Mathlib's Monic.irreducible_of_irreducible_map and Gauss's lemma, Tau Ceti's isUnramified_of_adjoin_eq_top_of_isUnit_aeval_derivative and eq_unramifiedExtension_finrank) but not quickly (transports between ℤ_[p] and 𝒪[ℚ_[p]] and their residue fields, about 100 lines). Of the other conventions, Conway polynomials exist in LeanBridge (FiniteField.conwayPolynomial), every extension has a generator with Eisenstein-form minimal polynomial (exists_adjoin_eq_top_isEisensteinForm_minpoly, round ZZ), and Monge's reduction is in MongeReductionLoop (exists_mem_mongeSemicanonicalPolynomials). No text error found.

Family level (ExtensionFamilyPolygon.lean), for every extension E inside K-bar with Herbrand invariant I at the residue characteristic of K (hE : I.IsInvariantOf K E, hp : ringChar k_K = p), which by AI6's mk_mem_family_iff is every extension whose class lies in the family I/K: IsInvariantOf.lowerConvexEnvelope_minpoly (for every uniformiser pi of E, with minimal polynomial phi over O_{K_f}, K_f the unramified extension of degree f inside E, the lower convex hull of the points (n, v_E(rho_n)) of rho(x) = pi^(-e) phi(pi x + pi) is ramificationPolygon I: the ramification polygon is the same for all the extensions of the family and all their uniformisers), IsInvariantOf.map_visibleRams_eq_map_neg_unitSlope (the rams of E, Deligne's lower breaks visibleRams E, are with their multiplicities the negatives of the slopes of ramificationPolygon I between the consecutive powers of p; through AI6's IsInvariantOf.visibleRams_eq, unchanged by AI6's review) and, added by the review as the knowl's sentence itself, IsInvariantOf.setOf_neg_unitSlope_ne_zero (the set of nonzero slopes of the reflected polygon of I is the set of rams of E). (1) Necessity of compatibility. IsAdmissible.isCompatible (HerbrandInvariantCompatibility.lean): a Herbrand invariant admissible for e0 (the committed IsAdmissible, Monge's conditions at the vertices of the ramification polygon) is compatible with e0 in the sense of the committed IsCompatible, i.e. every distinct ram b = b_i, of multiplicity d = d_i with c = d_1 + ... + d_{i-1} smaller rams (ramCountLT), is geometric ((p^d - 1) b integer, prime to p, b < p^(c+1) eps e0 / (p - 1)) or arithmetic (d = 1, b = p^(c+1) eps e0 / (p - 1)). Proof: the rams equal to b are the r_j with c < j <= c + d (ram_lt_iff_le_ramCountLT, ram_le_iff_le_ramCountLT_add_ramMultiplicity), c and c + d are vertices; e m_{c+d} - e m_c = p^(w-c-d) (p^d - 1) b (mul_mean_add_sub_mul_mean); at a vertex k, e m_k = p^(w-k) B for a natural B (IsAdmissible.exists_mul_mean_eq), and B is prime to p unless r_k^* = e0 (IsAdmissible.exists_mul_mean_eq_of_smallRam_ne, from the A-point of index k); so (p^d - 1) b = A - p^d B is an integer (IsAdmissible.den_pow_ramMultiplicity_sub_one_mul), prime to p when r_{c+1}^* < e0 (the small rams r_{c+1}^* = p^(d-1) r_{c+d}^* decrease along the block), and when r_{c+1}^* = e0 a block with d >= 2 would make A divisible by p (geometric sum), so d = 1; r_{c+1}^* <= e0 (Monge's Lemma 2, committed) translates into the two bounds. Then for extensions: IsInvariantOf.isAdmissible (ExtensionFamilyCompatibility.lean; the invariant of every extension E inside K-bar of a p-adic field K, I at the residue characteristic of K, is admissible for v_K(p), through the committed isAdmissible_of_isInvariantOf over K_f, v_{K_f}(p) = v_K(p) as K_f/K is unramified), IsInvariantOf.isCompatible (compatible with v_K(p)), IsInvariantOf.den_pow_ramMultiplicity_sub_one_mul ((p^{d_i} - 1) b_i is an integer, positive as b_i > 0: the knowl's '∈ N'), and for a finite extension K of Q_p, addVal_natCast_eq_absoluteRamificationIndex (v_K(p) = e_K, Tau Ceti's absoluteRamificationIndex) and IsInvariantOf.isCompatibleWith (the knowl's 'K is compatible with I'); isCompatibleWith_iff_of_eq ('depends only on e_K', also true by definition). Non-vacuity (scratch AJ6_local_fields/CheckCompat.lean and ProbePolygon.lean): every finite E inside K-bar has the invariant visibleHerbrandInvariant E (committed isInvariantOf_visibleHerbrandInvariant), which is therefore compatible; for (2)_1^1 (Q_2(sqrt 2), committed dyadicSqrtTwo) the ram 2 is arithmetic for e_K = 1 and the invariant is admissible for 1. (2) The three representations. The Herbrand invariant of L/K is visibleHerbrandInvariant (rams = Deligne's lower breaks, eps, f; committed); its Swan slopes computed from the rams are Deligne's upper breaks of L/K (committed isInvariantOf_visibleHerbrandInvariant), which is the reading of the user's ruling of 2026-11-13 (Swan slopes = Deligne's upper breaks, the convex-hull identification being lf.slopes's own gap); its means are the means of the invariant (ruling of 2026-11-13 on round AI for lf.family_invariants: the means of an extension are those of its Herbrand invariant, the slope polygon being lf.means's own gap). Conventions s_0 = r_0 = m_0 = 0: swanSlope 0 = 0 (empty sum), ram_zero, mean_zero (committed). e = eps p^w with p not dividing eps: ε_mul_pow_w_visibleHerbrandInvariant and the structure's not_dvd_ε (committed). (4) The slope polygon: meanPoints (the points (e', e'm') of the subextensions L'/K_f of L/K_f, e' = [L' : K_f] and m' the mean of L'/K_f, through Mathlib's IntermediateField.relfinrank and intermediateMean); meanPolygon (S, round AJ's lowerConvexHull of these points); meanPolygonFunction (h); meanPolygon_eq (S is the graph of h on [1, e]). (5) The means: polygonMean (m_k = h(eps p^k)/(eps p^k)); polygonMean_eq_mean (for k <= w, m_k is the mean sum_(j<=k) (p - 1) r_j/(eps p^j) of the Herbrand invariant (r_1, ..., r_w)_eps^f of L/K, so the points (eps p^k, eps p^k m_k) lie on S); polygonMean_zero (h(eps)/eps = 0, so the convention m_0 = 0 agrees with the polygon); extensionMean_eq_polygonMean (m = m_w). (6) sort_hullWildSwanSlopes_eq: the Swan slopes s_1 <= ... <= s_w of lf.slopes (hullWildSwanSlopes, read off the hull of the points (n_E, c_E)) are (p m_k - m_(k-1))/(p - 1), that is (p - 1) s_k = p m_k - m_(k-1) for 1 <= k <= w. Route: lf.slopes's vertex theorem (LowerHullVertices), applied to the subgroups H <= J <= H G_0 of the Galois group of the Galois closure M of L, H = Gal(M/L). K_f is the fixed field of H G_0 (fixingSubgroup_unramifiedExtension). The subextension fixed by J has e' = [H G_0 : J] and e'm' = c(J)/f - e' + 1 (relfinrank_mul_intermediateMean). The vertices are the points of the H G_t, with slopes phi_(M/K)(t) (isLowerHullVertices_subgroupMeanPoints), on the lines x -> x phi_(M/K)(t) - phi_(M/L)(t) (subgroupMeanOrdinate_sub_mul). The Herbrand function of the invariant puts eps p^k on the segment with r_k <= phi_(M/L)(t) <= r_(k+1), which gives h(eps p^k) = eps p^k s_k - r_k = eps p^k m_k. No text error: the knowl's 'Swan slopes [s_1,...,s_w]' are the wild ones, as in lf.slopes's corrected sentence. Overlap with Tau Ceti's main, found after the fact and not used: main's IntermediateField.unramifiedExtension_inertiaDegree_le and IntermediateField.inf_maximalUnramifiedExtension state K_f <= L and L meet K^ur = K_f inside SeparableClosure K. The proof followed step by step (fixingSubgroup_unramifiedExtension, relfinrank_mul_intermediateMean, subgroupDiscriminantExponent_sub_eq_mul, isLowerHullVertices_subgroupMeanPoints, subgroupMeanOrdinate_sub_mul, subgroupMeanAbscissa_sup_succ, the invariant's Herbrand function), with no hypothesis beyond L finite separable inside K-bar; independent example Q_3(3^(1/6)): points (1,0), (2,0), (3,3), (6,6), m_0 = 0, m_1 = 1 = m, H = 6, (p - 1) s_1 = 3 = p m_1 - m_0. - `lf.packet` [Fields › Local fields]: Formalised by the user's ruling of 2026-11-24 ('Yeah (b) is fine.'): residual polynomials equivalent up to the action of Gal(K_f/K) on the coefficients for f > 1 (they lie in a common subfamily), with the text fix recorded in the LMFDB issues. Round AP (AP2_transport), 2026-11-23. Partial by the doubt rule only (the f > 1 reading of 'their residual polynomials are equivalent', as for lf.subfamily); everything else the knowl states is proved. Defined (ExtensionPacket.lean): Algebra.GaloisPermIsomorphic K E1 E2, isomorphism as permutation groups of the Galois groups of the Galois closures, for any two extensions of a field: an isomorphism psi of the Galois groups and a bijection beta of the K-embeddings into the Galois closures with beta(g o iota) = psi(g) o beta(iota); reflexive, symmetric, transitive, and implied by K-isomorphism (galoisPermIsomorphic_of_algEquiv); HerbrandInvariant.SamePacket I K c1 c2: members E1, E2 inside K-bar of c1, c2 such that c1, c2 lie in a common subfamily (an element of HerbrandInvariant.subfamilies), the Galois permutation groups are isomorphic, the Galois closures have the same residue field degree (galoisUnramifiedDegree) and the same ramification index, and E1, E2 have the same hidden Swan slopes (equivalently hidden Artin slopes, hiddenArtinSlopes_eq_iff); HerbrandInvariant.packets: its classes on I/K. Proved: each condition is invariant under K-isomorphism (galoisPermIsomorphic_of_algEquiv, galoisUnramifiedDegree_eq_of_algEquiv, ramificationIndex_galoisClosure_eq_of_algEquiv, hiddenSwanSlopes_eq_of_algEquiv, hiddenArtinSlopes_eq_of_algEquiv), so the relation does not depend on the members (samePacket_mk_iff); it is an equivalence relation on I/K (samePacket_refl, SamePacket.symm, SamePacket.trans) and 'Thus the family I/K is partitioned into packets' (isPartition_packets). Equivalent residual polynomials, read as lying in a common subfamily: for members E1, E2 with uniformisers, iff their classes read over the residue field of K_f differ by an element of Gal(K_f/K), a power of Frobenius (exists_mem_subfamilies_iff), and for f = 1 iff they are equal (exists_mem_subfamilies_iff_of_f_eq_one); this uses the transport and partition of lf.subfamily (ResidualPolynomialTransportFamily.lean). Hypothesis: ringChar of the residue field of K is p, as for lf.subfamily. LMFDB checked: packets are recorded inside subfamilies (local_fields/main.py:1964, 'we don't record packets unless all hidden info known for that subfamily'); family.py compares Galois groups by transitive labels (fields grouped by (gal, galois_label), gal_slope_tables with cols 'hidden', 'galois_label'), and equal labels nTj mean conjugate transitive subgroups of S_n, which is GaloisPermIsomorphic; the packet column (main.py:574) and the family page's table 'Galois groups and Hidden Artin slopes' (lf-family.html:69) are shown only for n0 = 1 (families over Q_p), which include families with f > 1. Text error (fixable, with the lf.subfamily fix): old 'are equivalent and they have the same' (once in knowls_live.json) new 'are equivalent (they lie in a common {{KNOWL('lf.subfamily', 'subfamily')}} of $I/K$) and they have the same'. Not proved (not stated by the knowl): that the permutation representation is faithful and transitive, and a comparison with Tau Ceti's HasGaloisLabel for polynomials. Blocked by: the user's ruling on the f > 1 reading of equivalent residual polynomials (in a common subfamily, proved to mean classes up to Gal(K_f/K)); an 'every member' reading would not give a reflexive relation for the review's example, and the partition would fail. Difficulty: none left in Lean (ruling only). Stale blockers: AO1's (1) the transport of the class of residual polynomials, (2) permutation-group isomorphism for subfields of K-bar and its invariance, (3) the invariance of the hidden slopes under K-isomorphism, all proved here. Review (AP2 reviewer, 2026-11-24; review/AP2_transport.md): partial kept, pending the same ruling; the reviewer recommends formalised with the two text fixes. Every sentence of the live text (2025-06-26) checked: the setting (family, hp as for lf.subfamily), the definition and its five conditions, the Galois closures (Algebra.galoisClosure, the normal closure in K-bar), 'isomorphic as permutation groups' (Algebra.GaloisPermIsomorphic is the permutation isomorphism of the actions of the Galois groups on the K-embeddings, the action of nf.galois_group; equal labels nTj give and are given by it for the LMFDB's fields, whose actions are faithful and transitive, facts of nf.galois_group that lf.packet does not state), the residue field degree and ramification index of the closures, the hidden slopes (Swan, equivalently Artin) and 'Thus the family I/K is partitioned into packets' (isPartition_packets). Nothing the knowl states is left out. The families paper (arXiv:2507.02360, section 4.1) defines packets by the Galois group and the hidden slope content alone; in its Table 4.1 each packet lies in one subfamily, and the LMFDB records packets per subfamily, so the knowl's added condition changes nothing there (not recorded). Text pair checked (old string once in the live text; a clarification that depends on the lf.subfamily fix). - `lf.padic_field` [Fields › Local fields]: The gap is closed: nonempty_finitePadicExtension_ringChar proves that a nonarchimedean local field K (Mathlib's IsNonarchimedeanLocalField) of characteristic zero is a TauCeti.FinitePadicExtension K p for p its residue characteristic, i.e. a finite extension of ℚ_p whose valuation extends the p-adic one; the structure is the def finitePadicExtension, for any prime p in the maximal ideal (natCast_ringChar_mem_maximalIdeal for the residue characteristic). Construction: the reductions ℤ_p → ℤ/p^n → 𝒪_K/𝓂^n are compatible, so Mathlib's IsAdicComplete.liftRingHom gives ℤ_p → 𝒪_K (padicIntToIntegerRing), injective since p^n ≠ 0 in K; IsFractionRing.lift extends it to ℚ_p → K (padicToField); an element of ℚ_p is integral exactly when its image is (the inverse of a non-integral element lies in pℤ_p, which maps into 𝓂_K), which is ValuativeExtension; finiteness is Tau Ceti's finite_of_valuativeExtension. The other direction was already proved: a finite extension of ℚ_p, with Tau Ceti's (unique) spectral-norm structure, is a nonarchimedean local field (TauCeti.finiteExtension_isNonarchimedeanLocalField, compatible by algebraicExtension_valuativeExtension) of characteristic zero (FinitePadicExtension.charZero). Every sentence is proved; no text error found. Review (ZZ3): formalised confirmed; TauCeti.FinitePadicExtension K p bundles the ℚ_p-algebra with Module.Finite and ValuativeExtension ℚ_[p] K, so nonempty_finitePadicExtension_ringChar gives the finite ℚ_p-structure with the valuation of K restricting to the p-adic one, as the knowl's 'equivalently' needs.

Formalised at the pin, with two corrections of the text (the degree of L_i, the boundary of R_1^z), both proved in the corrected form. Setting: K a nonarchimedean local field, L/K finite separable inside K-bar; the possible rams over K are for K of characteristic 0 (the knowl's p-adic fields), with p the residue characteristic and e_0 = v_K(p) = e_K. Sentence by sentence. (1) The rams, small rams and tiny rams and the two relations: committed (visibleRams, ramsOfSubgroup, visibleRams_eq_ramsOfIsGalois; smallRam, tinyRam, smallRam_eq_mean_sub_mean, tinyRam_eq_swanSlope_sub_mean). (2) 'When L/K is Galois a ram is any number of the form v_L(sigma(pi_L) - pi_L) - 1 for some sigma != 1 in the wild inertia group ... Thus the rams of a Galois extension are positive integers': GaloisRamsUniformizer.lean, mem_ramsOfIsGalois_iff_exists_addVal (for a uniformiser pi of L, n is a ram iff v_L(sigma pi - pi) = n + 1 for some sigma != 1 in G_1, the wild inertia group), with lowerIndex_eq_addVal_smul_sub (i_G(sigma) = v_L(sigma pi - pi) for sigma in G_0) and mem_ramsOfIsGalois_iff (n is a ram iff n >= 1 and G_(n+1) != G_n). (5) 'The possible rams r_1 = ... = r_w for totally wildly ramified extensions of degree p^w over K are then just given by R_w^(e_K)': mem_possibleRamSet_iff_exists_visibleRams_eq_replicate (for w >= 1, alpha lies in the corrected R_w^(e_0) iff some totally ramified extension E/K of degree p^w inside K-bar has visibleRams E = w copies of alpha), both directions; exists_visibleRams_eq_singleton_arithmetic (the boundary value p e_0/(p - 1) is the ram of a totally ramified extension of degree p, so the correction is needed). Checks: lake build of the five modules, #lint clean, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Unproved: only the counterexample of (a), by hand. Review (AN2 reviewer, 2026-11-18; review/AN2_heights_rams.md): formalised, confirmed, with the two corrections, both fixable errors (ruling of 2026-11-11): each replaces a false statement by the true one, which is proved in full, and drops no true claim. Every sentence of the live text (2025-05-28) checked against the Lean, those proved in earlier rounds included. The existence theorem followed step by step: IsCompatible.isAdmissible (induction over the vertices; a geometric block gives e m_k = p^(w-k)(p^d B + N) with p not dividing N, an arithmetic one the small ram e_0) and the committed hasSameRams_of_specialisation, whose hypotheses are met for every compatible invariant, every f and every eps (all coefficients 1 over the unramified extension of degree f); no nonemptiness hypothesis enters, so there is no circularity. Non-vacuity (scratch AN2_heights_rams-review/Probe.lean): (2)_1^1 at p = 2, (3)_2^1 at p = 3 and (15/4, 75/4)_3^2 at p = 5 are compatible with e_K = 1, and their families are not empty over every K of that residue characteristic with v_K(p) = 1. (b) The boundary, checked in Lean and by hand: over Q_2 the totally ramified quartic fields have c in {4, 6, 8} for one block (rams 1/3, 1, 5/3; the pair (2, 2) does not occur) and c in {8, 9, 10, 11} for two ((1, 3), (1, 4), (2, 3), (2, 4)), and over Q_3 the totally ramified cubic fields have rams 1/2, 1, 3/2 (c = 3, 4, 5); without the boundary value Q_2(sqrt 2), Q_3(cuberoot 3) and Q_2(2^(1/4)) would be missing. (a) The degree: the counterexample checked step by step for p = 5 mod 6, with a second argument for its key step (Q_(p^2)(cuberoot(up)) is not Galois over Q_p, as Frob(u)/u is not a cube, while Q_(p^2)(cuberoot p) is, so the former has no cubic subfield); for p = 5 the invariant is (15/4, 75/4)_3^2 and every member has [L_1 : K] = 30, not 15 (Probe.lean). The committed ramSet: keep its body (the knowl's literal set, on which the three comparison theorems rest) and change its docstring to say so and to point to possibleRamSet; exact texts in the review. decls changed by the review: IsInvariantOf.den_dvd_pow_ramMultiplicity_sub_one (the denominator sentence) is linked and possibleRamSet no longer is (it is named in the statements of the two linked theorems on possible rams); the author's list is the alternative. Otherwise style fixes only (review, section Changes): no statement of a linked declaration changed.
- `lf.residual_polynomials` [Fields › Local fields]: Round AO (AO1_residual_polynomials), 2026-11-23. Formalised, with one fixable text issue (the order of S_1, ..., S_l). Every statement of the knowl is proved for a totally ramified extension L/K of p-adic fields (more generally of nonarchimedean local fields with L/K separable; the CharZero corollary covers p-adic fields), alpha a uniformiser, phi its minimal polynomial over K, v_alpha = addValuation L (v(alpha) = 1), rho = ramificationPolynomial phi alpha (committed). (1) rho in O_L[x]: mem_integer_coeff_ramificationPolynomial. (2) The segments S with endpoints (-k-l, v(rho_{k+l})), (-k, v(rho_k)) and slope h/m are exactly the segments of the ramification polygon (mem_polygonEdges_ramificationPolygonOf_iff, on residualSegments, read off Tau Ceti's lowerConvexEnvelope; the ends are points by EdgeOfSlopeEnds.lean). (3) A(x) = sum_{j=0}^{l/m} red(rho_{jm+k} alpha^{jh - v(rho_k)}) x^j exactly as written (residualPolynomial; the reduced elements lie in O_L: mem_integer_residualPolynomial; degree l/m and nonzero constant term: natDegree_residualPolynomial, coeff_zero_residualPolynomial_ne_zero). (4) For S of positive slope, x^k A(x^m) is additive: its coefficients vanish away from the powers of p (coeff_X_pow_mul_comp_residualPolynomial_eq_zero, through Monge's binomial argument v(rho_s) <= v(rho_i) for s = p^{v_p(i)}, coeffVal_pow_padicValNat_le) and B(x+y) = B(x)+B(y) in every commutative algebra over the residue field, polynomial rings included (aeval_add_X_pow_mul_comp_residualPolynomial); no separability needed. (5) The list residualPolynomials, S_1 at the right. (6) 'The list ... is not an invariant': Q_3(3^(1/3)) (the lead's example, LeanBridge.PadicRadical 3 3 = AdjoinRoot (X^3 - 3), its lemmas in the namespace PadicCbrtThree): the single segment (k,l) = (1,2) of slope 3/2 (residualSegments_eq), lists [1 + x] at alpha and [2 + x] at -alpha (residualPolynomials_cbrtThree, residualPolynomials_neg_cbrtThree), which differ (residualPolynomials_neg_cbrtThree_ne). (7) The class A = {(gamma_{d,1} A_1(d^{h_1} x), ..., gamma_{d,l} A_l(d^{h_l} x)) : d in K_^x} with the knowl's recursion gamma_{d,l} = d^(-h_l deg A_l), gamma_{d,i} = gamma_{d,i+1} d^(-h_i deg A_i) (residualGammas, residualAct, residualPolynomialClass, d mapped into the residue field of L), and 'A is an invariant of K[x]/(phi)': the class does not depend on the uniformiser (residualPolynomialClass_eq_of_irreducible, separable; residualPolynomialClass_eq_of_irreducible_of_charZero for p-adic fields), with the list at alpha' inside the class at alpha (residualPolynomials_mem_residualPolynomialClass) and the explicit change A'_S(x) = u_^(-v(rho_k)) A_S(u_^h x) for alpha' = u alpha (residualPolynomial_eq_of_irreducible, Pauli-Sinclair Lemma 4.7); the knowl's gamma_{d,i} is d^(-v(rho_{k_i})) (residualAct_residualPairs). Route (Monge's invariance proof, MongeInvariance.lean): in the normal closure M of L/K inside an algebraic closure (Tau Ceti's finite intermediate field structures), phi(alpha + alpha x) = prod over Gal(M/K)/Gal(M/L) of (alpha - s alpha + alpha x) (committed map_eq_prod_quotient, map_mongeShift_eq_prod); each factor of phi'(alpha' + alpha' x) differs from u times the factor of phi by s(alpha)(u - s u), divisible by alpha(s alpha - alpha) (committed smul_sub_dvd_smul_algebraMap_sub); Mathlib's Gauss norm (multiplicative for a nonarchimedean absolute value, any real c > 0) gives ||F' - F|| < ||F|| for the products (Polynomial.gaussNorm_prod_sub_prod_lt), i.e. every point of rho' - rho lies strictly above every supporting line of rho at every real slope (exists_coeffVal_sub_lt); so the Newton polygons agree (coeffEnvelope_eq_of_forall) and on each segment the coefficients agree to first order (residualPolynomial_mul_eq). Monge's comparison only covers the integer slopes m; rational slopes h/m need the real Gauss norm, hence the new addValAbs (x -> 2^(-v(x))). Numerical tests before writing (scratch/AO1_residual_polynomials/residual_test.py): five examples, the lead's first and Pauli-Sinclair's Example 4.9, whose class is reproduced exactly (their base list is ours at -alpha). TEXT (fixable, ambiguous order): the knowl never says how S_1, ..., S_l are numbered, and the gamma recursion depends on it: it is right with S_1 the rightmost segment (Pauli-Sinclair's numbering, S_l ending at (-n, 0)), where gamma_{d,i} = d^(-v(rho_{k_i})) by telescoping (consecutive segments share ends, the last ends at height 0); numbered from the left, gamma_{d,l} would be d^(-(v(rho_1) - v(rho_{1+l}))) instead of the d^(-v(rho_1)) of the change of uniformiser. Old (live text of 2025-05-15, occurs once): `The **residual polynomials** of $\varphi$ are the residual polynomials associated to the segments $S_1, \dots, S_\ell$ of the {{KNOWL('lf.ramification_polygon', 'ramification polygon')}} of $\varphi$.` New: `The **residual polynomials** of $\varphi$ are the residual polynomials associated to the segments $S_1, \dots, S_\ell$ of the {{KNOWL('lf.ramification_polygon', 'ramification polygon')}} of $\varphi$, numbered from right to left: $S_1$ has right endpoint $(-1,v_\alpha(\rho_1))$ and $S_\ell$ has left endpoint $(-\deg\varphi,0)$.` (The LMFDB stores and displays the list in the opposite order, S_l first: main.py's plot_ramification_polygon reverses it.) Stale blockers: AN9z_lead's 'nothing is formalised yet' and the round of 28 October's needs_main. Fold notes (done by fold AP1, 2026-11-23): the example is built on LeanBridge.PadicRadical 3 3, whose general part is now in ForMathlib/NumberTheory/LocalField/PadicRadical.lean; gaussNorm_neg and gaussNorm_add_eq_of_lt gave way to Mathlib's absolute-value facts; coe_units_zpow is Subring.coe_units_zpow (Algebra/Ring/Subring/Units.lean); addValAbs stays (Tau Ceti's toRealAbsoluteValue is for fields). Review (AO1 reviewer, 2026-11-23; review/AO1_residual_polynomials.md): formalised, confirmed. The invariance theorem was followed step by step (factor comparison, Gauss norm of products at every real radius through addValAbs, rational slopes, the knowl's gamma telescoping to d^(-v(rho_{k_i}))) and the tests recomputed with independent code, including residue fields F_4 and F_25 (the author's were all F_p). Order: Pauli-Sinclair number S_1 at (1, J_0) (Figure 1, Lemma 4.3(b), Example 4.9), the rightmost segment after reflection; with the left-to-right numbering the knowl's class is not an invariant (Pauli-Sinclair's Example 4.9 at -alpha and the F_4 example at zeta*alpha fall outside it), so the numbering is a fixable text, not an ambiguity; the author's strings were the blueprint's LaTeX conversion and did not occur in the live text, now given in the live text's form (with -deg(phi) for the undefined n). Pauli-Sinclair's printed residual polynomials (1 + 2x, 2 + x^3) are the list at -alpha; the class agrees. Style: Option.some.injEq and Valuation.integer.integers (two namespace components) replaced, redeclared variables k, l, i made explicit with variable ... in (argument order of num_mul_div_den now k, hl), duplicated proof terms in exists_coeffVal_sub_lt replaced by the lemmas coe_coeff_mongeShift_minpoly, coeff_mongeShift_eq_zero_iff, toNat_addVal_coeff_mongeShift (moved from ResidualPolynomialAdditive), monic_ramificationPolynomial_minpoly and residualAct_one_residualPairs freed of an unneeded [Algebra.IsSeparable K L], layout fixes, four unnecessary simp lemmas removed.

- `lf.slopes` [Fields › Local fields] (#64): Round AM (AM1_slopes), 2026-11-17. Formalised at the pin. Every definition and claim of the knowl is proved, for every finite separable extension L/K of nonarchimedean local fields with L an intermediate field of K-bar/K. The knowl's p-adic fields are the characteristic-0 case. The subextensions of an abstract L/K are those of its image in K-bar, and the points (n_E, c_E) are invariant under K-isomorphism. This closes the tracker v60c note ('Missing: The lower convex hull of (n_E, c_E) over the subextensions E/K, the Artin slopes (segment slopes repeated log_p(n2/n1) times), the Swan and wild slopes and the Artin and Swan slope contents; that the Swan slopes are the upper ramification breaks is a theorem (Deligne)'). Definitions (VisibleSlopes): subextensionPoints (n_E = [E:K], c_E = discriminantExponent K E, for Tau Ceti's local-field structure on finite intermediate fields); slopesPolygon (B, round AJ's lowerConvexHull); hullArtinSlopes (the segmentSlopes of B); hullWildArtinSlopes (the slopes > 1, each repeated slopeMultiplicity = log_p(n2/n1) times, through wildSegmentSlopes of LowerHullVertices); hullSwanSlopes (the Artin slopes minus 1); hullWildSwanSlopes (the wild Artin slopes minus 1, with multiplicities); visibleArtinSlopeContent and visibleSwanSlopeContent ([a_1..a_w]_eps^f and [s_1..s_w]_eps^f, as (multiset, tameDegree, inertiaDegree)). Claims: div_eq_pow_slopeMultiplicity (a segment of B of slope > 1 from (n1, c1) to (n2, c2) has n2/n1 = p^m, m the multiplicity of its slope); mem_hullWildSwanSlopes_iff (the wild Swan slopes are exactly the positive Swan slopes); hullWildArtinSlopes_eq_visibleArtinSlopes and hullWildSwanSlopes_eq_visibleSwanSlopes (the wild Swan slopes, with multiplicities, are Deligne's positive upper ramification breaks of L/K, the committed visibleSwanSlopes); hullWildSwanSlopes_eq_swanSlopesOfIsGalois (for L/K Galois, Serre's positive upper breaks of Gal(L/K), the committed swanSlopesOfIsGalois); visibleArtinSlopeContent_eq and visibleSwanSlopeContent_eq (the two contents through the upper breaks). Route: the vertex theorem is proved once and shared with lf.means. (1) LowerHullVertices: if the lines of slopes tau_t through points (n_t, y_t) of a set S lie below S, then the lower convex hull of S is the graph of the maximum of these lines over [n_0, n_(k+1)], with its segments, slopes and log_p multiplicities (IsLowerHullVertices.lowerConvexHull_eq, segmentSlopes_lowerConvexHull, mem_polygonEdges_lowerConvexHull, wildSegmentSlopes_lowerConvexHull). (2) SubgroupSlopePolygon applies it to the subgroups J of the Galois group G of the Galois closure M that contain H = Gal(M/L). The points ([G:J], c(J)), with c(J) = [G:J] sum_i (#G_i - #(J meet G_i))/#G_0, have their vertices at G and at the H G_t, with slopes tau_t = sum_(i<t) #G_i/#G_0 = 1 + phi_(M/K)(t - 1) (isLowerHullVertices_subgroupSlopePoints, natCast_subgroupSlope_succ). c(J) is the discriminant exponent of M^J/K (natCast_discriminantExponent_eq_subgroupDiscriminantExponent, through the different in the tower M/M^J/K). (3) VisibleSlopes carries this over through the Galois correspondence inside K-bar (subextensionPoints_eq). Text error (fixable, ruling of 2026-11-11): 'The Swan slopes are the same as the positive upper ramification jumps of $L/K$.' is false as written whenever f > 1 or eps > 1. The knowl's own Swan slopes (all Artin slopes minus 1) then include -1 (the unramified segment, Artin slope 0) or 0 (the tame segment, Artin slope 1). Corrected: 'The wild Swan slopes are the same as the positive upper ramification jumps of $L/K$, with multiplicities.' The LMFDB's pages also use 'Swan slopes' this way, listing only the wild ones. The corrected statement is proved in full, multiplicities included, and no true claim is dropped. Bump: no longer needed. Nothing from Tau Ceti's main is used. TauCeti.lowerConvexEnvelope, IntermediateField.discriminantExponent and FiniteCompressedSlopeData.segmentSlope (the needs_main of the the round of 28 October record) are replaced by round AJ's lowerConvexHull, segmentSlopes and polygonEdges and by the pin's discriminantExponent on finite intermediate fields. Main has no hull of subextension points to rebase on: its convex-sequence files treat envelopes of height sequences (Newton polygons). Consistent with lf.means: both are formalised through the same vertex theorem, so the tracker's medium rating no longer applies. No category field (LeanBridge declarations). Review (AM1 reviewer, 2026-11-17; review/AM1_slopes.md): formalised, confirmed. Every sentence of the live text (2025-05-28) checked against the Lean; the vertex theorem (IsLowerHullVertices.lowerConvexHull_eq, isLowerHullVertices_subgroupSlopePoints, natCast_discriminantExponent_eq_subgroupDiscriminantExponent, sum_filter_replicate_eq_map_swanSlopesOfSubgroup) followed step by step; independent example Q_3(3^(1/6)): points (1,0), (2,1), (3,5), (6,11), Artin slopes {1, 5/2}, wild [5/2], Swan slopes {0, 3/2}, wild [3/2], Deligne's break 3/2. The text error is real (a fixable error, not a typo; it changes no outcome), but the old string as recorded above does not occur in the live text, which breaks the line after 'jumps of': the exact old string is 'The Swan slopes are the same as the positive upper ramification jumps of' followed by a line break and '$L/K$.' (once), the new 'The wild Swan slopes are the same as the positive upper ramification jumps of' followed by a line break and '$L/K$, with multiplicities.'. The bump is not needed: nothing of Tau Ceti's main is used or restated beyond two short lemmas (fold items). Style fixes only: 58 untyped local haves typed or removed, 14 headers that rebound variables, two names qualified through two namespaces, HerbrandInvariant.monotone_swanSlope deleted (a restatement of the committed HerbrandInvariant.swanSlope_mono), three repeated proof terms factored into helpers, layout; no statement or name of a decls entry changed. Leads for lf.visible_slopes, lf.heights and lf.rams in the review.
- `lf.subfamily` [Fields › Local fields]: Formalised by the user's ruling of 2026-11-24 ('Yeah (b) is fine.'): residual polynomial classes compared up to the action of Gal(K_f/K) on the coefficients for f > 1, with the text fix recorded in the LMFDB issues. Round AP (AP2_transport), 2026-11-23. Partial by the doubt rule only: every fact and definition of the knowl is proved under the reading 'some member of the K-isomorphism class and some uniformiser' (the committed HerbrandInvariant.subfamily) and under reading (b), 'in A up to the action of Gal(K_f/K) on the coefficients' (new galoisSubfamily), and the two readings give the same subfamily for every A and every f (subfamily_eq_galoisSubfamily); only an 'every member' reading differs, for f > 1. Transport (ResidualPolynomialTransport.lean): along a K-isomorphism sigma : L = L' of finite extensions of a nonarchimedean local field, valuations, coefficient heights, envelopes, segments and slopes are preserved and the residual polynomials of sigma(phi) at sigma(alpha) are those of phi at alpha with the residue map of sigma on the coefficients; the ramification polynomial of the minimal polynomial over L'^un of sigma(alpha) is the image of that over L^un of alpha, and the class of residual polynomials is the image under the residue map of sigma (residualPolynomialClass_minpoly_algEquiv); the action of the residue units composes (residualAct_residualAct) and the class over a field onto whose residue field the base surjects is an orbit (residualPolynomialClass_eq_residualActOrbit). Family (ResidualPolynomialTransportFamily.lean): for a member E of I/K the residue map of K_f <= E is an isomorphism (IsInvariantOf.residueFieldEquiv); the class of E at alpha read over the residue field of K_f (IsInvariantOf.residualClass) is an orbit of the residue units (residualClass_eq_residualActOrbit) and independent of the uniformiser (residualClass_eq_of_irreducible); for a K-isomorphism sigma : E = E' of members it changes by the automorphism of the residue field induced by the restriction of sigma to K_f (residualClass_algEquiv, pairs: residualPairsOver_algEquiv), a power of Frobenius x -> x^(q^n) (exists_residueFieldHom_eq_pow), and every element of Gal(K_f/K) arises from a K-isomorphism onto another member (exists_restrictUnramifiedExtension_eq). Consequences: E lies in the subfamily of the class A0 of a member E0 iff its class is the image of A0 under an element of Gal(K_f/K) (mk_mem_subfamily_residualClass_iff); (a) for f = 1 the literal condition holds at any member and any uniformiser (mk_mem_subfamily_residualClass_iff_of_f_eq_one); (b) for every f the condition up to Gal(K_f/K) holds at any member and any uniformiser (mk_mem_galoisSubfamily_residualClass_iff); the subfamily of the image of A under any element of Gal(K_f/K) is the subfamily of A (subfamily_image_map_residueFieldHom); the subfamilies of the classes of the members partition I/K, for every f (isPartition_subfamilies). Hypothesis throughout the family results: ringChar of the residue field of K is p (I at the residue characteristic, as for the LMFDB's families); it gives equal slopes to all members. Finding against the AO1 review: under 'some member, some uniformiser' the review's example does not lie in two subfamilies; the subfamilies of a class and of its Frobenius image are the same set (subfamily_image_map_residueFieldHom) and the subfamilies partition I/K (isPartition_subfamilies); 'some member' and 'up to Gal(K_f/K)' coincide, and only 'every member' fails (the example would lie in no subfamily). LMFDB checked: lf.field.label gives each field one code i 'shared among fields in the same family with equivalent residual polynomials'; ctr_subfamily is data; rcs.cande.lf: all extensions of Q_p of degree n < 24 with p < 200, so the review's octic example (Q_2, f = 2, e = 4) is in the database; residual polynomials are stored data. Text error (fixable, reading (b); the reviewer's wording, which names the extension L/K_f whose residual polynomials are meant): old 'whose list of residual polynomials is in $\mathcal{A}$.' (once in knowls_live.json) new 'whose list of residual polynomials over the unramified extension $K_f$ of $K$ of degree $f$ is in $\mathcal{A}$ up to the action of $\Gal(K_f/K)$ on the coefficients.' Not formalised: the review's octic example over Q_2(zeta_3) (not cheap; it shows that a class need not be Frobenius-stable, which only the 'every member' reading needs). Blocked by: the user's ruling on the f > 1 reading of 'whose list of residual polynomials is in A' (some member, equivalently up to Gal(K_f/K): proved; every member: not the LMFDB's partition); with the text fix accepted, formalised. Difficulty: none left in Lean (ruling only). Stale blockers: AO1's (1) the transport along K-isomorphisms inside K-bar and (2) the independence of the uniformiser within I/K, both proved here. Review (AP2 reviewer, 2026-11-24; review/AP2_transport.md): partial kept, pending the user's ruling; the reviewer recommends formalised with the text fix (question in the review). Checked: the transport (residualPolynomialClass_minpoly_algEquiv, for every K-isomorphism of finite extensions of a nonarchimedean local field; its redundant FiniteDimensional hypothesis on the target removed), the twist (IsInvariantOf.residualClass_algEquiv, any element alpha, no hypothesis on p), Frobenius (exists_residueFieldHom_eq_pow), every element of Gal(K_f/K) arising (exists_restrictUnramifiedExtension_eq), the orbit algebra (residualAct_residualAct, residualClass_eq_residualActOrbit) and the consequences. hp : ringChar k_K = p is the LMFDB's setting (I is a Herbrand invariant at the residue characteristic of K: lf.herbrand_invariant, lf.family_polynomial; committed precedent IsInvariantOf.ramificationPolygonOf_minpoly and round AI6's review), used only to give two members the same slopes; the transport, the twist, subfamily_eq_galoisSubfamily and subfamily_image_map_residueFieldHom do not use it. The finding against the AO1 review is right: the octic's two classes (recomputed with AO1's resid_check.py: list (zeta + x, 1 + x^2); the Frobenius-conjugate polynomial's list (zeta^2 + x, 1 + x^2) is outside the class) give one subfamily as a set; for f > 1 only the injectivity of A -> subfamily(A) and the 'every member' reading fail. LMFDB: its code computes no subfamily (ctr_subfamily is stored and used in sort orders only); stored residual polynomials have coefficients in Z[t] (main.py, plot_ramification_polygon: R = ZZ['t']['z']), t the residue generator of the stored K_f, so for f > 1 a stored list depends on the chosen K_f-structure of the field; the families paper (arXiv:2507.02360) works with f = 1 (section 3) and defers f > 1. Decls trimmed to the eight to link; also relevant: subfamilies, mk_mem_subfamily_residualClass_iff, IsInvariantOf.residualClass_algEquiv, exists_residueFieldHom_eq_pow, residualPolynomialClass_minpoly_algEquiv (ResidualPolynomialTransport), subfamily_subset_family (ExtensionSubfamily), family, residualPolynomialClass, residualPolynomialClass_eq_of_irreducible.
- `lf.swan_slopes` [Fields › Local fields] (#64): Formalised on the user's ruling of 2026-11-11 ("Something that has a different but fixable definition isn't partial. Something that is strictly weaker is partial."): corrected. The text as written admits the tame break. For ℚ₃(√3)/ℚ₃ (e = 2, tame), G^0 = G ≠ G^{0+} = 1, so 0 is a nonnegative upper break and 1 a positive Artin slope, giving the Swan slopes [0]. 'The number of wild segments of I/K is the number of segments of the ramification polygon of L/K with positive slope': the segments of a subset P of the plane are its maximal straight pieces, polygonEdges P (the segments [q, q'], q.1 < q'.1, contained in P and in no larger such segment contained in P), polygonEdgesWithSlope P T those of slope in T; wildSegmentCount I := ncard of the segments of positive slope of reflectedPolygon I, and IsInvariantOf.ncard_polygonEdgesWithSlope_eq: for every extension E inside K-bar with Herbrand invariant I at the residue characteristic (every member of I/K, AI6's mk_mem_family_iff) and every uniformiser pi of E, the number of segments of positive slope of the ramification polygon of E/K at pi (ramificationPolygonOf, lf.ramification_polygon above) is wildSegmentCount I; so 'does not depend on the choice of L/K in I/K' (nor on pi). 'This is equal to the number of distinct positive Swan slopes of L/K': IsInvariantOf.ncard_setOf_mem_visibleSwanSlopes ({s | 0 < s and s in visibleSwanSlopes E}.ncard = wildSegmentCount I, Swan slopes = Deligne's upper breaks by the ruling of 2026-11-13) and, without I, ncard_polygonEdgesWithSlope_ramificationPolygonOf_minpoly (number of segments of positive slope of the polygon of E/K = number of distinct positive Swan slopes of E/K, for every finite E inside K-bar and every uniformiser). Route: the segments of the polygon of a convex height sequence with finitely many finite heights are the segments edgeOfSlope h s of the slopes s of its unit edges, from the first to the last index of slope s (TauCeti.mem_polygonEdges_polygonGraph_iff; a segment contained in the graph has the slope of every unit edge it overlaps and lies in the segment of its slope), distinct slopes giving distinct segments (TauCeti.ncard_polygonEdgesWithSlope_polygonGraph); the reflection through the vertical axis maps segments to segments and negates slopes (polygonEdgesWithSlope_image_reflectVertical); AI7's polygon of I is convex with unit slopes -r_k and 0 (isConvexSeq_ramificationPolygon), so wildSegmentCount I is the number of distinct rams (wildSegmentCount_eq_ncard_image_ram), which is the number of distinct Swan slopes, s_j = s_k exactly when r_j = r_k (swanSlope_eq_swanSlope_iff, ncard_image_swanSlope_eq_wildSegmentCount). - `lfunction.functional_equation` [L-functions]: Round AE (AE1), on the user's request to prove the sentence 'The axioms of the Selberg class are less restrictive than given above' instead of reading it as a cross-reference (AD6). Reading, from the knowl, lfunction.selberg_class, lfunction.selberg_class.axioms and lfunction: the sentence compares the functional equation given above (Lambda(s) = N^{s/2} prod Gamma_R(s + mu_j) prod Gamma_C(s + nu_k) L(s) = epsilon conj Lambda(1 - conj s), N a positive integer, Re mu_j in {0, 1}, 2 Re nu_k a positive integer, sum mu_j + 2 sum nu_k real) with Selberg's axiom 3 (gamma(s) = omega Q^s prod_i Gamma(lambda_i s + mu_i) with |omega| = 1, Q > 0, lambda_i > 0, Re mu_i >= 0, and gamma(s) F(s) = conj(gamma(1 - conj s) F(1 - conj s))): inclusion of the first in the second, and strictly more admissible gamma factors. It is not about the four axioms as a whole (the Ramanujan hypothesis and the bound theta < 1/2 on the coefficients of log F are extra restrictions, only expected for analytic L-functions by lfunction.euler_product and not assumed by AnalyticLFunction). 'Less restrictive' weighs the restrictions on the data of the equation, which the knowl lists just before ('With those restrictions on the spectral parameters'), so the strictness proved is about the admissible gamma factors. The author's further reason, that a strictness among Dirichlet series would contradict lfunction's conjecture, is wrong (AE1 review): the shifts L(s + i theta, chi), theta != 0 and chi primitive and non-principal, lie in the Selberg class, and their gamma factor is a constant times q^{s/2} Gamma_R(s + a + i theta), whose poles force any equation of the LMFDB's form to have mu = {a + i theta}, with sum mu not real. That Dirichlet-series strictness is not formalised; asked of the user. Proved in SelbergFunctionalEquation.lean. Inclusion: Gamma_R(s + mu) = pi^{-mu/2} pi^{-s/2} Gamma(s/2 + mu/2) and Gamma_C(s + nu) = 2 (2 pi)^{-nu} (2 pi)^{-s} Gamma(s + nu) give N^{s/2} L_inf(s) = C Q^s prod Gamma(lambda_i s + mu_i) with Q = sqrt(N) pi^{-J/2} (2 pi)^{-K}, pairs (1/2, mu_j/2) and (1, nu_k), C = prod pi^{-mu_j/2} prod 2 (2 pi)^{-nu_k} (SelbergData.conductor_cpow_mul_gammaFactor, SelbergData.gammaConst). The Selberg gamma factor SelbergData.selbergGammaFactor takes epsilon' = omega C / |C|, with omega = exp(-i arg epsilon / 2) a square root of conj epsilon; for |epsilon| = 1 any function satisfies the LMFDB equation at s iff it satisfies Selberg's there (SelbergData.toFun_selbergGammaFactor_mul_eq_conj_iff, which uses no axiom of AnalyticLFunction). Hence every analytic L-function satisfies LSeries.SelbergFunctionalEquation, the committed formalisation of axiom 3 (AnalyticLFunction.selbergFunctionalEquation_coeff, with completed_eq_of_notMem_gammaPoles on the strip and norm_sign); this is a statement about the class the knowl describes, as allowed by lfunction's AD4 record. Strictness: Gamma(s/3) (LSeries.SelbergGammaFactor.gammaDivThree: epsilon = 1, Q = 1, (lambda, mu) = (1/3, 0)) is admissible for Selberg but is not c N^{s/2} L_inf(s) on re s > 0 for any Selberg data and any constant c (SelbergData.not_eqOn_gammaDivThree). The inverses are entire, so they would agree on C; 1/Gamma(s/3) vanishes exactly at 0, -3, -6, ..., while a zero of 1/L_inf at 0 forces one at -2 (factor Gamma_R) or -1 (factor Gamma_C). The proof uses none of the LMFDB's restrictions on N, mu, nu. No nonzero element of the extended Selberg class has the gamma factor Gamma(s/3) (Kaczorowski-Perelli: no degree in (0, 1)); the witness is about the form of the equation, which is what the sentence compares. All other claims as in AD6: the form and restrictions (SelbergData, gammaFactor, completed_eq, completed_eq_sign_mul_conj), degree d = J + 2K (SelbergData.degree), central point 1/2 and s <-> 1 - s (centralPoint, one_sub_eq_self_iff), arithmetic normalisation (completed_sub_eq_sign_mul_conj, arithmeticCentralPoint, isIntegral_arithmeticCoeff_motivicWeight), uniqueness waived by the ruling of 2026-11-12, typo 'positive integer w' (should be nonnegative) already recorded. Links: AD6's six, with SelbergData.degree and completed_sub_eq_sign_mul_conj restored by the review (the author had dropped them for a limit of six; the limit of rounds AC and AD is eight), and the two new theorems. New file 256 lines after the review, lake build clean, #lint 0 errors in 10 declarations (slow linters included), every simp-list entry needed (30 deletions), axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, dup_decls 0 clashes. Non-vacuous: the hypothesis |epsilon| = 1 of the iff holds for the Selberg data of every analytic L-function (norm_sign), e.g. zeta, and the inclusion and the strictness both apply to zeta. Side finding, an LMFDB issue that does not count: lfunction.selberg_class has an href without its opening quote.

One new file (349 lines as written, 361 after the review), Mathlib imports only. The text, sentence by sentence. (1) 'Dirichlet ... used L-functions to prove that there are infinitely many primes in any (primitive) arithmetic progression': Mathlib's Nat.infinite_setOfPred_prime_and_modEq (q != 0, a coprime to q). (2) 'series of the form L(s, chi) = sum chi(n)/n^s where chi is a (Dirichlet) character, which is the extension to the integers of a character of the group (Z/qZ)^*': Mathlib's DirichletCharacter (a MulChar on ZMod q, with MulChar.equivToUnitHom / MulChar.ofUnitHom for the extension by zero of a character of the units), LSeries and its continuation DirichletCharacter.LFunction (LFunction_eq_LSeries for re s > 1). (3) 'the arithmetic function chi defined by chi(n) = 1, -1, 0 for n = 1, 2, 0 mod 3 is a Dirichlet character modulo 3': new, DirichletCharacter.χ₃ : DirichletCharacter C 3 (the quadratic character of the field Z/3Z with complex values; no declaration for the modulus 3 existed in the three trees, see the review below for the Kronecker characters) and χ₃_intCast: for every integer m, χ₃ m = if m % 3 = 1 then 1 else if m % 3 = 2 then -1 else 0 (also χ₃_natCast for the positive integers). Further: χ₃ is quadratic, odd, nontrivial and primitive (isQuadratic_χ₃, inv_χ₃, odd_χ₃, χ₃_ne_one, isPrimitive_χ₃). (4) 'The above L-function has an Euler product L(s, chi) = prod_p (1 - chi(p)/p^s)^{-1}': Mathlib's DirichletCharacter.LSeries_eulerProduct_hasProd (and _tprod) for the series; new, LFunction_eulerProduct_hasProd: HasProd (fun p : Nat.Primes => (1 - chi p * p^(-s))^{-1}) (LFunction chi s) for re s > 1, for every Dirichlet character chi, in particular χ₃. (5) 'satisfies a functional equation that (3/pi)^{s/2} Gamma((s+1)/2) L(s, chi) is invariant under s -> 1 - s': new. gaussSum_χ₃: the Gauss sum for ZMod.stdAddChar is sqrt(3) i (e(1/3) - e(2/3), from cos and sin of pi/3); rootNumber_χ₃: Mathlib's root number is 1; completedLFunction_χ₃_one_sub: Mathlib's functional equation becomes Lambda(1 - s) = 3^(s - 1/2) Lambda(s) for Lambda = DirichletCharacter.completedLFunction χ₃ (= Gamma_R(s+1) L(s, χ₃)). The knowl's function is the entire function completedLFunctionModThree s := sqrt(pi) * 3^(s/2) * Lambda(s) (differentiable_completedLFunctionModThree): completedLFunctionModThree_eq proves completedLFunctionModThree s = (3/pi)^(s/2) * Gamma((s+1)/2) * LFunction χ₃ s for every s that is not a pole -1, -3, -5, ... of Gamma((s+1)/2), and completedLFunctionModThree_one_sub proves completedLFunctionModThree (1 - s) = completedLFunctionModThree s for every s. For the expression itself, Gamma_mul_LFunction_χ₃_one_sub: (3/pi)^((1-s)/2) * Gamma((1-s+1)/2) * LFunction χ₃ (1-s) = (3/pi)^(s/2) * Gamma((s+1)/2) * LFunction χ₃ s for s outside {-1, -3, ...} and {2, 4, ...}. (6) 'the special value L(1, chi) = pi/(3 sqrt 3)': new, LFunction_χ₃_apply_one : LFunction χ₃ 1 = pi / (3 * sqrt 3). Not available from Mathlib's Hurwitz values (hurwitzZeta_neg_nat, sinZeta_two_mul_nat_add_one and hurwitzZetaOdd_neg_two_mul_nat all need k != 0) nor from Tau Ceti at the pin (gaussSum_mul_tsum_inv_pow_eq_generalizedBernoulli needs k >= 2); on Tau Ceti's main, see the review below. Proof: hasSum_LFunction_χ₃ (for re s > 1, L(s, χ₃) is the sum over k >= 0 of 1/(3k+1)^s - 1/(3k+2)^s, by grouping the Dirichlet series in blocks of three with Nat.divModEquiv); for real 1 <= sigma <= 2 the k-th term has norm at most 2/(3k+1)^2 (Bernoulli's inequality one_add_mul_self_le_rpow_one_add); Tannery's theorem tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence along sigma -> 1+ and the continuity of LFunction χ₃ at 1 (differentiable_LFunction, χ₃ != 1) give hasSum_LFunction_χ₃_one: HasSum (fun k => 1/(3k+1) - 1/(3k+2)) (LFunction χ₃ 1), i.e. L(1, χ₃) = 1 - 1/2 + 1/4 - 1/5 + ...; the partial sums are one third of those of Mathlib's cotangent partial fractions at x = 1/3 (tendsto_logDeriv_euler_cot_sub) plus 1 - 1/(3n+1), so the sum is (pi/3) cot(pi/3) = pi/(3 sqrt 3). (7) 'Dirichlet needed to know that his L-functions did not vanish at 1 and he used special values to prove this fact': Mathlib's DirichletCharacter.LFunction_apply_one_ne_zero (every chi != 1); for the example, LFunction_χ₃_apply_one_ne_zero is read off the special value. The functional equation is the knowl's statement, not a weaker one: the knowl's function is the meromorphic function (3/pi)^(s/2) Gamma((s+1)/2) L(s, chi), entire because the simple poles of Gamma((s+1)/2) at s = -1, -3, ... meet the trivial zeros of L(s, χ₃) (Mathlib's DirichletCharacter.Odd.LFunction_neg_two_mul_nat_sub_one); completedLFunctionModThree is that function (entire, and equal to the expression at every s that is not one of these poles) and it is invariant at every s. The exclusions of the literal version are sharp: for the Lean expression E s := (3/pi)^(s/2) * Gamma((s+1)/2) * LFunction χ₃ s, the review's scratch Check.lean proves E s = completedLFunctionModThree s if and only if s is none of -1, -3, ... (E_eq_iff) and E (1 - s) = E s if and only if s is none of -1, -3, ... and none of 2, 4, ... (E_one_sub_iff): at the excluded points one side is 0 only because Complex.Gamma is 0 at its poles. Nothing that is true is left unproved. The history sentences state two facts, both in Mathlib at the pin with the knowl's meaning (Dirichlet's theorem for every modulus q != 0 and every a coprime to q; L(1, chi) != 0 for every chi != 1 of every modulus); the first use of the letter L, the prime moduli of the original proof and the class number formula (named, not stated) are history. - `lfunction.history.hecke_operators` [L-functions]: Round AI (AI5_mf_history), reviewed (review/AI5_mf_history.md). Audit record N3.json: 'Partially in Tau Ceti', easy, the sentence being an unstated composite. The one mathematical sentence is 'The forms which were simultaneous eigenvalues of these operators have multiplicative Fourier coefficients so that their associated Dirichlet series have Euler products and functional equations.' The rest is history: Hecke and Mordell introduced the operators (Tau Ceti's heckeTNat on M_k(Gamma_1(N))), Hecke mainly worked in level 1, and the Atkin-Lehner-Li theory is only named. TEXT ERROR, fixable (ruling of 2026-11-11): 'eigenvalues' is a slip for 'eigenforms', and without 'normalized' the coefficients are not multiplicative (2 Delta: a_2 a_3 = -24192, a_6 = -12096). Old: 'The forms which were simultaneous eigenvalues'; new: 'The normalized forms which were simultaneous eigenforms' (the old string occurs once in the live text). READING (ruling of 2026-11-12, the LMFDB's setting): the forms are cusp forms, at every level. The eigenforms are Tau Ceti's HeckeRing.GL2.Eigenform N k: nonzero cusp forms on Gamma_1(N) with a nebentypus that are eigenforms of every T_n, n >= 1 (every newform is one, Newform.toEigenform). The Eisenstein series, the non-cuspidal eigenforms of level 1, are not covered: no tree proves that they are Hecke eigenforms. Sentence by sentence, for f : Eigenform N k with a_1 = 1. (1) Multiplicative coefficients: Tau Ceti's Eigenform.qExpansion_coeff_mul. (2) Euler product of the Dirichlet series itself: Tau Ceti's Eigenform.LSeries_eulerProduct_hasProd, on Re s > k/2 + 1 (linked by the review in place of L_eulerProduct_hasProd, which is about Mathlib's ModularForm.L). (3) Functional equation. The review found that the author's three lemmas used only f.toCuspForm and that Eigenform.frickeCompletedL_sub_eq restated Tau Ceti's CuspForm.frickeCompletedL_functional_equation_gamma1: the restatement is removed and the other two are now stated for every cusp form on Gamma_1(N), in particular for eigenforms. CuspForm.frickeCompletedL_eq_mul_LSeries (new): on Re s > k/2 + 1 the entire function Lambda_M(s, f) (Tau Ceti's frickeCompletedL, entire by differentiable_frickeCompletedL) is M^{s/2} (2 pi)^{-s} Gamma(s) sum a_n n^{-s}, for every M (M = N at level N, M = 1 at level 1). Tau Ceti's frickeCompletedL_functional_equation_gamma1: Hecke's equation Lambda_N(k - s, f) = i^k Lambda_N(s, W_N f) for every k > 0. CuspForm.frickeCompletedL_sub_eq_of_level_one (new): at level 1, Lambda(k - s, f) = i^k Lambda(s, f), because W_1 is the identity (CuspForm.normalizedFrickeOperatorCusp_eq_self, new: frickeGL R 1 is the image of S and the normalizer is sqrt(1)^{2-k} = 1). For the LMFDB's newforms at every level the equation Lambda(s, f) = eps conj(Lambda(1 - conj s, f)) is the committed HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.analyticCompletedL_eq_rootNumber_mul (linked). Not vacuous: Tau Ceti's discriminantEigenform : Eigenform 1 12 with a_1 = 1 (checked in the review's Check.lean). Not linked (eight-declaration cap): CuspForm.normalizedFrickeOperatorCusp_eq_self, CuspForm.differentiable_frickeCompletedL. Checks by the review: lake build through the guard; #lint: 0 errors; #print axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; dup_decls: 0 clashes.

- `lfunction.primitive` [L-functions]: Formalised on the user's ruling of 2026-11-11 ("Something that has a different but fixable definition isn't partial. Something that is strictly weaker is partial."): convention. Two readings: literally (a product of at least two nontrivial L-functions, else nothing would be primitive) the trivial L-function 1 is primitive, since degrees add and nontrivial means degree >= 1; under the irreducible-element (Selberg class) convention it is not. The knowl does not fix the case, and AnalyticLFunction.IsPrimitive adds the conjunct 'not trivial', so 1 is not primitive (not_isPrimitive_one), as its docstring concedes. The wording is in the LMFDB issues.
- `lfunction.rational` [L-functions]: Round AF (AF2): the missing equivalence is proved in Rational.lean. IsRational is the knowl's definition: L is arithmetic with a motivic weight (a_n n^{w/2} algebraic integers for some w, which makes the a_n algebraic) and its coefficient field, IntermediateField.adjoin Q {a_n n^{w/2} : n != 0} for w = motivicWeight, is Q. The Euler factor in the arithmetic normalisation of weight w is arithmeticEulerPolynomial w p = F_p(p^{w/2} T), F_p the analytic one (eulerPolynomial), and L_p(T) sum_k a_{p^k} p^{kw/2} T^k = 1 (arithmeticEulerPolynomial_mul_mk), so L(s - w/2) = prod_p L_p(p^{-s})^{-1}. isRational_iff: L is rational if and only if every L_p of the arithmetic normalisation of the motivic weight is the image of a polynomial in Z[T]. Forward: the a_n n^{w/2} are rational algebraic integers, hence integers, and the inverse of a power series with integer coefficients and constant term 1 has integer coefficients (PowerSeries.invOfUnit over Z). Backward: the inverse series sum_k a_{p^k} p^{kw/2} T^k then has integer coefficients, by multiplicativity every a_n n^{w/2} is an integer, so w is a motivic weight and the coefficient field is Q. Non-vacuous: zeta is rational (isRational_zeta). No wrong text; 'the arithmetic normalization' is read with the motivic weight, as lfunction.normalization and lfunction.coefficient_field fix it. AF2 review: IsRational asks for a motivic weight instead of algebraic coefficients, since the coefficient field is only defined when one exists; that this implies the knowl's 'arithmetic' was claimed in the docstring without proof and is now proved (IsRational.isAlgebraic_coeff: a_n = (a_n n^{w/2}) / n^{w/2}, a quotient of an algebraic integer by a square root of n^w).

The recorded gap was only that 'its root number' is the epsilon of the bundled Selberg data; by the ruling it is AnalyticLFunction.sign. The root angle is the composite alpha = arg(epsilon) / (2 pi). It lies in (-1/2, 1/2] since -pi < arg <= pi (neg_pi_lt_arg, arg_le_pi), and it determines epsilon = exp(2 pi i alpha) since |epsilon| = 1 (norm_sign). No new Lean.
- `lfunction.root_number` [L-functions]: Formalised on the user's ruling of 2026-11-12 (the Selberg data of an L-function need not be unique), with the missing claims proved in round AD6. The definition (the epsilon of the bundled functional equation, fourth component of the Selberg data) is accepted by the ruling. The recorded gap was that 'real coefficients => epsilon = ±1' and 'real coefficients and epsilon = -1 => L(1/2) = 0' were proved only under the extra hypothesis that the gamma factor is real at 1/2 (sign_eq_neg_one_pow_analyticRank, hypothesis hγ). That hypothesis is now proved for the bundled data, without uniqueness, in RootNumber.lean. Write the gamma factor as prod_a Gamma_R(s + a) over the shifts mu_j, nu_k, nu_k + 1 (SelbergData.gammaℝShifts). With real coefficients, the functional equation and its conjugate give, on 0 < re s < 1 and then everywhere by the identity theorem, the identity of entire functions 1/L*_inf(s) * 1/L*_inf(1-s) = epsilon^2 / (L_inf(s) L_inf(1-s)), where L*_inf(s) = conj L_inf(conj s) is the gamma factor of the dual data SelbergData.dual. Poles in re s <= 0 then force equal pole orders. Since 1/Gamma_R(s) = s/(2 pi) * 1/Gamma_R(s + 2), the multiplicity of a shift a is the order at -a minus the order at -a + 2 (Complex.eq_of_forall_analyticOrderAt_prod_inv_Gammaℝ_eq). So the shifts are closed under conjugation (gammaFactor_dual_eq), L_inf is real on the real line (conj_gammaFactor_conj), and epsilon = (-1)^r (sign_eq_neg_one_pow_analyticRank_of_selfDual). Hence sign_eq_one_or_eq_neg_one and toFun_one_half_eq_zero_of_sign_eq_neg_one. New file: 395 lines after the review (which factored a repeated proof term into the helper Complex.differentiable_prod_add_div_two_pi), lake build clean, #lint 0 errors in 27 declarations, axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Non-vacuous: zeta satisfies the real-coefficient hypothesis. No AnalyticLFunction instance of sign -1 exists in the trees; the hypothesis epsilon = -1 is the knowl's own condition.

- `lfunction.zeros` [L-functions]: Round AJ (AJ7). The one gap of the sweep of 2026-11-06 ('No lemma relates RiemannHypothesis to trivialZeros'; tracker blocker: non-trivial zeros have positive real part under RH, via Lambda = N^{s/2} L_inf L on re s <= 0) is closed; the blocker was stale, since AF2's TrivialZeroOrder.lean already gives ord_s L = ord_s Lambda + ord_s (1/L_inf) at every s. Proved, for every AnalyticLFunction L: RiemannHypothesis.zeros_diff_trivialZeros_subset_criticalLine, under L.RiemannHypothesis (lfunction.rh: zeros with re rho > 0 have re rho = 1/2) every zero of L that is not a trivial zero (L.zeros \ L.trivialZeros; trivialZeros = the zeros at the poles of the gamma factor, as lfunction.trivial_zero defines them) lies on criticalLine (re s = 1/2, analytic normalisation); conversely and unconditionally riemannHypothesis_iff_zeros_diff_trivialZeros_subset_criticalLine (a zero with re > 0 is never a gamma pole); also RiemannHypothesis.mem_arithmeticCriticalLine (arithmetic normalisation of weight w: re s = (1 + w)/2) and generalizedRiemannHypothesis_iff_zeros_diff_trivialZeros_subset_criticalLine. Route: one_sub_conj_mem_zeros, the reflection 1 - conj rho of a nontrivial zero rho is a zero: at rho the order of 1/L_inf is 0, so ord Lambda = ord L > 0 (this covers rho = 0, where the field completed is unconstrained, because it works with orders, not values); the functional equation Lambda(s) = eps conj Lambda(1 - conj s) off {0, 1} transfers positive order to 1 - conj rho (tendsto_zero_iff_meromorphicOrderAt_pos along the punctured-neighbourhood map s -> 1 - conj s); and ord L >= ord Lambda everywhere since 1/L_inf is entire. If re rho <= 0 the reflected zero has re >= 1 > 0, so RH gives re(1 - conj rho) = 1/2, i.e. re rho = 1/2. Reading: the knowl's claim is the implication 'under RH, every non-trivial zero lies on the critical line', and that implication is proved outright; RH itself is not claimed. The rest of the knowl was already formalised (S1): zeros as positive meromorphic order (= vanishing of the continuation away from s = 1, mem_zeros_iff); lowestZero, the least gamma > 0 with 1/2 + i gamma a zero, attained and positive whenever such a gamma exists (it takes the junk value 0 when none exists, but no claim of the knowl rests on that value). Also linkable: RiemannHypothesis.mem_arithmeticCriticalLine. No text error. Review (AJ7): formalised, confirmed. RiemannHypothesis is lfunction.rh's definition literally (zeros with re rho > 0 have re rho = 1/2, analytic normalisation, per L; GeneralizedRiemannHypothesis for all L), and the knowl's sentence is the implication RH => every non-trivial zero on the critical line, a theorem that needs the functional equation (RH constrains only re rho > 0; a non-trivial zero with re rho = 0 is excluded by its reflection 1 - conj rho, of real part 1), not a restatement of the definition. Nothing conjectural is asserted, so the ruling 'the conjectural objects stay partial' (2026-11-12) does not apply; the tracker treats the conditional theorems of nf.serre_odlyzko_bound and g2c.has_square_sha the same way (their blockers are those theorems). one_sub_conj_mem_zeros checked at rho = 0 and rho = 1 (orders on punctured neighbourhoods; the field completed is used only off 0 and 1). Non-vacuous: the trivial L-function 1 satisfies RH (no zeros), and for zeta RH is Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis.
- `lfunction.zfunction` [L-functions]: Round AF (AF2), on item 2 of the brief (a claim about every analytic L-function counts when proved for every AnalyticLFunction). The three recorded gaps are proved for every AnalyticLFunction in ZFunctionZeros.lean: Z is real analytic (analyticAt_zFunction), hence smooth, ContDiff R infinity (contDiff_zFunction); the order of vanishing of Z at t is the order of vanishing of L at 1/2 + it (analyticOrderAt_zFunction), so the multisets of zeros of Z(t) and L(1/2 + it) agree; and if that order is odd, Z(t) Z(u) < 0 for t < t0 < u close to t0 (eventually_zFunction_mul_zFunction_neg), the sign change. Proof: t -> |gamma(1/2 + it)| is real analytic since gamma = N^{s/2} L_inf is holomorphic and nonzero on the critical line (norm = exp(log(normSq)/2)); near t0, with L(s) = (s - s0)^m g(s), g(s0) != 0, Z(t) = (t - t0)^m Q(t) with Q : R -> C real analytic and Q(t0) != 0, and Q is real for t != t0 because Z is, hence at t0 by continuity, so Z(t) = (t - t0)^m re Q(t). Everything else was proved before (S1, ZX2): the definition with the root of conj epsilon chosen so that Z > 0 for small t > 0 (ofReal_zFunction, eventually_zFunction_pos), realness and |Z(t)| = |L(1/2 + it)| (abs_zFunction), and Hardy's Z with theta (riemannSiegelTheta, exp_riemannSiegelTheta_mul_I, ofReal_hardyZ_eq_exp_mul_riemannZeta; the bijection of zeros follows as |exp(i theta)| = 1). The recorded inconsistency stands (S1): for zeta the general normalisation gives -hardyZ, as zeta(1/2) < 0. AF2 review: the knowl defines the Riemann-Siegel theta function, so riemannSiegelTheta is linked again (abs_zFunction, cited in zFunction's docstring, dropped for the limit of eight); the bijection of zeros for zeta is also Mathlib's hardyZ_eq_zero_iff. - `mf.bianchi.bianchicongruencesubgroup` [Modular forms › Bianchi]: Γ(𝔑) ≤ PSL₂(R) is the image of the kernel of SL₂(R) → SL₂(R/𝔑) (any commutative ring R), and for a domain such as 𝒪_K it is proved to be exactly {γ ≡ ±1 mod 𝔑} (mk_mem_gammaPSL_iff, the knowl's definition); a congruence subgroup of PSL₂(R) contains Γ(𝔑) for some 𝔑 ≠ 0. - `mf.gl2.history.new` [Modular forms › Miscellaneous]: Round AI follow-up (AI9c_rankin_cohen). This record overrides the record of AI9b_history_new for this knowl (from 'Nothing to formalise'; audit N4: formalisable, medium, 'Partially in LeanBridge'). Reviewed on 2026-11-13: review/AI9b_history_new.md for DerivativeLaw.lean and ChangeOfGroup.lean, review/AI9c_rankin_cohen.md for the two RankinCohen.lean files (written by the first reviewer, checked by a second, independent one); this record is the second review's, and sections 1, 3 and 4 below are taken from the first review's record. OUTCOME: formalised. Every mathematical sentence of the knowl is proved, three of them after a text correction (TEXT ERRORS 1 to 3 below, fixable errors), in four files: Multiplier/DerivativeLaw.lean (437 lines), Multiplier/ChangeOfGroup.lean (492 lines), RingTheory/Derivation/RankinCohen.lean (177 lines) and Multiplier/RankinCohen.lean (239 lines). AI9b's record was partial pending a question on sentence (8), the Rankin-Cohen sentence (does it only name the family, or assert that the family sends modular forms to modular forms?). Cohen's theorem is now proved for every n, so the knowl is formalised under either reading and the question needs no answer. Setting: the modular forms of weight k in Z and multiplier system v on a subgroup Gamma of SL(2, R) are LeanBridge's ModularForm.multiplierSpace k v (holomorphic, f|_k gamma = v(gamma) f, bounded at every cusp); for v = 1 they are Mathlib's ModularForm Gamma k (mem_multiplierSpace_one_iff). f' is ModularForm.derivOfComplex f, the derivative on H (Mathlib's D f is f'/(2 pi i)). SECTION 1, vector space and graded ring. (1) 'lambda f + mu g': multiplierSpace k v is a Submodule over C (existing), for every subgroup of SL(2, R) and every homomorphism v to the unit circle. (2) 'graded ring' for trivial multiplier: Mathlib's ModularForm.instGCommRing (every subgroup of GL(2, R) with determinants 1 or -1). (3) Product: mul_mem_multiplierSpace, f g is in multiplierSpace (k + l) (v * w); it is also the case n = 0 of Cohen's theorem below (rankinCohenBracket_zero: [f, g]_0 = f g). SECTION 2, differentiation. (4) The modular identity f(gamma z) = v(gamma)(cz+d)^k f(z) is apply_smul_of_mem_multiplierSpace; (gamma z)' = (cz+d)^-2 for det gamma = 1 is hasDerivAt_smul_coe; the law is derivOfComplex_smul, f'(gamma z) = v(gamma)((cz+d)^{k+2} f'(z) + k c (cz+d)^{k+1} f(z)). TEXT ERROR 1: the factor c is missing. Proved: eq_zero_of_derivOfComplex_smul, the LMFDB's formula at gamma and z forces k = 0 or c = 1 or f(z) = 0, so it fails already for translations. Old: '\[f'(\gamma z)=v(\gamma)((cz+d)^{k+2}f'(z)+k(cz+d)^{k+1}f(z))\;.\]'; new: '\[f'(\gamma z)=v(\gamma)((cz+d)^{k+2}f'(z)+kc(cz+d)^{k+1}f(z))\;.\]'. (5) 'f' is a quasi-modular form of weight k+2': isQuasiModularForm_derivOfComplex (LeanBridge's IsQuasiModularForm Gamma (k+2) 1 v, depth at most 1, P(z, X) = f'(z) + k f(z) X, with holomorphy and boundedness at every cusp); 'exactly modular if k = 0': derivOfComplex_mem_multiplierSpace (a modular form of weight 2 in the full sense). The tool is derivOfComplex_slash, (f|_k gamma)' = f'|_{k+2} gamma - k (c/(cz+d)) f|_k gamma for det gamma = 1, from Mathlib's normalizedDerivOfComplex_slash. (6) The two repairs. By 1/y: ModularForm.maassShimura k f = f' + k f/(2 i y), and maassShimura_slash (the transformation law of weight k+2 and multiplier v; the function is not holomorphic). By E_2: serreDerivative_mem_multiplierSpace, Mathlib's Serre derivative D f - (k/12) E_2 f is in multiplierSpace (k+2) v for Gamma inside SL(2, Z), the groups on which E_2 is quasi-modular (Mathlib's serreDerivativeMF is the case v = 1). (7) Combinations: zpow_div_zpow_slash (f^l/g^k satisfies the transformation law of weight 0 and multiplier v^l/w^k; integer powers, no hypothesis on zeros: the quotient is only meromorphic, so the law is all the sentence can mean); derivOfComplex_slash_of_slash_eq and derivOfComplex_zpow_div_zpow_slash ('its derivative is really modular of weight 2': the transformation law of weight 2, with no differentiability hypothesis); derivOfComplex_zpow_div_zpow ('expanding': (f^l/g^k)' = f^{l-1} g^{-k-1} (l f' g - k f g') where f and g do not vanish); rankinCohen_mem_multiplierSpace: l f' g - k f g' (ModularForm.rankinCohen k l f g) is a modular form in the full sense, in multiplierSpace (k + l + 2) (v * w), and rankinCohen_slash is its equivariance under matrices of determinant 1. (8) 'This is a special case of a series of bilinear operators called the Rankin-Cohen operators'. The operators: ModularForm.rankinCohenBracket k l f g n = sum over r + s = n of (-1)^r C(k+n-1, s) C(l+n-1, r) f^(r) g^(s), with generalised binomial coefficients over Z (Ring.choose, so any integers k and l are allowed) and derivatives in z. It is the standard bracket of Cohen 1975 and Zagier 1994 (the same signs and binomial coefficients: compared with the formula on Wikipedia's page 'Rankin-Cohen bracket', which cites both, and with the two computed examples below; the papers themselves could not be read) with d/dz in place of D = (2 pi i)^-1 d/dz, so (2 pi i)^n times the bracket in Zagier's normalisation. The special case: rankinCohenBracket_one, [f, g]_1 = -(l f' g - k f g'), the knowl's operator up to sign (and rankinCohenBracket_zero, [f, g]_0 = f g). Cohen's theorem, ModularForm.rankinCohenBracket_mem_multiplierSpace (file Multiplier/RankinCohen.lean): for every subgroup Gamma of SL(2, R), all integers k and l (negative ones included), all homomorphisms v and w from Gamma to the unit circle and every n, if f is in multiplierSpace k v and g in multiplierSpace l w, then [f, g]_n is in multiplierSpace (k + l + 2n) (v * w): a modular form in the full sense (holomorphic, the functional equation with multiplier v w, bounded at every cusp of Gamma). It follows from ModularForm.rankinCohenBracket_slash, [f, g]_n |_{k+l+2n} gamma = [f|_k gamma, g|_l gamma]_n for holomorphic f and g and det gamma = 1, which is proved by an algebraic identity in a differential ring (file RingTheory/Derivation/RankinCohen.lean, on Mathlib's class Differential): in A[X] with the derivation extending that of A by X' = -X^2 (Mathlib's Differential.implicitDeriv), the iterated covariant derivatives of u of weight k are polynomials Differential.weightDerivPoly k u r with d/dX of the (r+1)-st equal to (r+1)(k+r) times the r-th (derivative_weightDerivPoly_succ); so the bracket of these polynomials, Differential.rankinCohenPoly, has derivative 0 in X (derivative_rankinCohenPoly, the terms cancel in pairs) and, when A has no additive torsion, takes the same value at every x as at 0, where it is the bracket Differential.rankinCohenBracket of u and v (aeval_rankinCohenPoly). The holomorphic functions on H form such a ring (ModularForm.holomorphicSubalgebra with f -> f', an instance of Differential; a C-algebra, so without torsion), x = c/(cz+d) (ModularForm.slashDefect) satisfies x' = -x^2, and by derivOfComplex_slash the slashes f^(r)|_{k+2r} gamma are the values at x of the polynomials of f|_k gamma. Non-vacuity (scratch/AI9c_rankin_cohen/Check.lean and Examples.lean): the theorem applies to any two Mathlib modular forms on any Gamma, with a Mathlib modular form of weight k + l + 2n as result, in particular to E_4 and E_6 on SL(2, Z) for every n; and from Mathlib's formulas of Ramanujan and Delta = (E_4^3 - E_6^2)/1728, [E_4, E_6]_1 = -(2 pi i) 3456 Delta and [E_4, E_4]_2 = (2 pi i)^2 4800 Delta, which vanish nowhere (in Zagier's normalisation these are -3456 Delta and 4800 Delta, the values that the first q-coefficients give). SECTION 3, changing the group. (9) f(mz): slash_mem_multiplierSpace (for det alpha > 0, f|_k alpha is in multiplierSpace k (conjMultiplier v alpha) on alpha^-1 Gamma alpha, with multiplier delta -> v(alpha delta alpha^-1)); for alpha = dilationGL m = diag(m, 1) with m in Q positive, comp_dilationGL_smul_mem_multiplierSpace (z -> f(mz) is in that space; coe_dilationGL_smul: the point is mz), and alpha^-1 Gamma alpha is arithmetic if Gamma is (instance, from Mathlib's IsArithmetic.conj). TEXT ERROR 2: mz is in the upper half-plane only for m > 0. Old: 'for any $m\in\Q^{\times}$'; new: 'for any $m\in\Q_{>0}$'. (10) Sub-series and twists, for a Mathlib modular form f on Gamma (determinant 1, trivial multiplier), N a strict period of Gamma (so that f = sum a_n q^{n/N} with q^{1/N} = e^{2 pi i z/N}) and psi a function modulo M: ModularForm.twistOfWidth N psi f = M^-1 sum over a mod M of (DFT psi)(a) f(z + aN/M), a modular form on twistLevel Gamma M N, the intersection of the conjugates of Gamma by the translations by aN/M (a subgroup of Gamma; it has determinant 1, has N as a strict period, and is arithmetic if Gamma is); qExpansion_twistOfWidth_coeff: its n-th coefficient in q^{1/N} is psi(n) a_n; qExpansion_twistOfWidth_single_coeff: for the indicator function of r mod M the coefficients are a_n for n = r mod M and 0 otherwise, the sub-series. Readings: 'modular' with trivial multiplier (for a multiplier of infinite order the claim is false, see review/AI9b_history_new.md; for one of finite order restrict to its kernel; on Gamma_1(N), Tau Ceti's ModularForm.twist_mem_modFormCharSpace gives the nebentypus of the twist); for a modular form in the LMFDB's sense n_0 >= 0; meromorphy at the other cusps of a form with poles is not stated (no notion at the pins). For Gamma_1(N) and q = e^{2 pi i z}, Tau Ceti's ModularForm.twist and qExpansion_twist_coeff give the same on the explicit group Gamma_1(L). SECTION 4, enlarging the group. At level 1 (Tau Ceti's Gamma_1(1), which is SL(2, Z) by TauCeti.Gamma1_one_map_eq_SL), p prime: heckeTNat_apply_of_level_one, T_p f (z) = (sum over 0 <= j < p of f((z+j)/p) + p^k f(pz))/p for Tau Ceti's heckeTNat, the standard normalisation, so g = p T_p f is modular on Gamma. f(pz) is TauCeti.ModularForm.levelRaise p on Gamma_0(p), through Gamma0_map_le_conjAct_scaleGL_one. f((z+j)/p) is HeckeRing.GL2.upperTriTranslate f j (upperTriTranslate_apply), a modular form on the conjugate (S T^j)^-1 Gamma_0(p) S T^j: it is p^k times the translate of f(pz) by S T^j. TEXT ERROR 3: f((z+j)/p) is not modular on Gamma_0(p). Proved for every j: qExpansion_coeff_one_eq_zero_of_slash_upperTriTranslate (if z -> f((z+j)/p) is invariant under T, which lies in Gamma_0(p), then a_1(f) = 0) and not_forall_slash_upperTriTranslate_discriminant (so Delta((z+j)/p) is not modular on Gamma_0(p), nor on Gamma).
