- `mf.gl2.history.poincare` [Modular forms › Miscellaneous]: Round AI (AI5_mf_history), reviewed (review/AI5_mf_history.md). Audit record N4.json: 'Partially in LeanBridge', medium. All of the knowl's mathematics is proved for Gamma = SL_2(Z) (link group.sl2z) and integral weight k, sentence by sentence. (1) 'We can define a function which has the modular transformation property of modular forms by averaging over the group action: f(z) = sum over <T>\Gamma of h(gamma z)(cz+d)^-k, whenever this makes sense'. ModularForm.averageSeries is the tsum (0 when not summable) over the right cosets <T> gamma, with chosen representatives; for 1-periodic h the terms depend only on the coset (averageTerm_eq_of_rightRel). averageSeries_smul is the transformation property f(gamma z) = (cz+d)^k f(z) for every gamma in SL_2(Z) and every 1-periodic h; it holds for the tsum, so wherever the series converges absolutely, and trivially (0 = 0) elsewhere. 'Makes sense': summable_norm_averageTerm (added by the review) proves absolute convergence in weight k >= 3 whenever h is bounded on the orbit of z, in particular for bounded h. averageSeries_eq_zero_of_odd (added by the review): in odd weight the average is 0, the terms at gamma and -gamma cancelling; the trivial multiplier is a multiplier system only for even k. (2) 'If h = 1 we recover the Eisenstein series'. averageSeries_one: the bottom row identifies <T>\Gamma with the coprime pairs, so the average is Mathlib's level-1 eisensteinSeries, the sum over coprime (c, d) of (cz+d)^-k. averageSeries_one_eq_E: that is 2 E_k (Mathlib's normalised E, k >= 3). NORMALISATION, a question for the editors and not an error of substance: <T> does not contain -I, while cmf.eisenstein sums over Gamma_infty = +-<T>, so h = 1 gives twice the linked E_k. Old: 'If $h=1$ we recover the {{KNOWL('cmf.eisenstein', "Eisenstein series")}}.'; new: 'If $h=1$ we recover twice the {{KNOWL('cmf.eisenstein', "Eisenstein series")}} $E_k$.' (3) 'If h(z) = exp(2 pi i n z) with n in Z, which is indeed 1-periodic, we produce what are called Poincare series'. cexp_smul_T: e^{2 pi i n z} is invariant under T for every n in Z. averageSeries_cexp: in even weight k >= 3 and for every n in Z, the average is twice the Poincare series P_k^n(Gamma, 1; z; infinity) of specialfunction.poincare, i.e. LeanBridge's poincareSeries with G = top, gamma_s = 1, v = 1, w = 1; absolute convergence for every n in Z from summable_norm_averageTerm and Mathlib's exists_max_im. The factor 2 is the same normalisation; for odd k, specialfunction.poincare's condition v(-I) = (-1)^k excludes v = 1. (4) 'A special case for which it is not necessary to divide by the left-action of T is the function f(z) = sum over gamma in Gamma of (gamma z)^-n (cz+d)^-k, for suitable values of n'. fullAverageSeries is that sum over all of SL_2(Z). summable_norm_averageTerm_zpow gives absolute convergence for 2 <= n <= k - 2, the full range of absolute convergence and the range of the knowl's source (H. Cohen, An introduction to modular forms, arXiv:1809.10907, the exercise on phi(tau) = tau^-m: 2 <= m <= k - 2). The author proved 3 <= n <= k - 3 only (empty for k = 4, 5); the review replaced the proof: where |az+b| <= |cz+d|, gamma is determined by its top row and the integer m nearest to Re((cz+d)/(az+b)), and |cz+d| >= |az+b| |m+i| / 3, so the term is at most 3^{k-n} |az+b|^-k |m+i|^-(k-n); elsewhere the same for S gamma. fullAverageSeries_smul is the transformation property (it also follows from the next two and averageSeries_smul). tsum_zpow_smul_T shows w -> sum over m in Z of (w+m)^-n is 1-periodic. fullAverageSeries_eq_averageSeries (now for 2 <= n <= k - 2): the sum over Gamma is the average of that function over <T>\Gamma, via the bijection (<T>\Gamma) x Z = SL_2(Z), (q, m) -> T^m q.out. So it is a special case of the construction. not_summable_averageTerm_one (renamed from not_summable_denom_zpow): for h = 1 the sum over all of Gamma diverges (the terms at T^m are 1), which is why dividing by T is necessary in general. Not linked (eight-declaration cap; the review linked summable_norm_averageTerm in place of fullAverageSeries_smul): averageTerm, averageSeries_one, averageSeries_eq_zero_of_odd, fullAverageSeries, fullAverageSeries_smul, tsum_zpow_smul_T, not_summable_averageTerm_one, and the existing ModularForm.poincareSeries and Mathlib eisensteinSeries/E. - `mf.hilbert` [Modular forms › Hilbert]: Round AL (AL5_hilbert_koecher). Both parts of the tracker v59 blocker are closed ('the knowl's Gamma_0(N)_b corrected (a, d in Z_F), and the Koecher principle for Hilbert modular forms of degree n > 1'). (1) The corrected group, a fixable text (recorded in lmfdb-knowl-edits.md, section mf.hilbert: Old 'c \in \mathfrak{Nb}, \ b \in \mathfrak{b}^{-1},' New 'a, d \in \Z_F,\ c \in \mathfrak{Nb}, \ b \in \mathfrak{b}^{-1},'; without a, d in Z_F the set contains diag(1/2, 2) and the law forces f = 0): HilbertModularGroup.mem_gammaZero_glPlus_iff proves that gammaZero b (glPlus b) N, for every invertible fractional ideal b (the knowl's integral representatives included) and every ideal N, is exactly the set of the matrices (a, b; c, d) of GL_2(F) with a, d in O_F, b in b^-1, c in Nb, and det a totally positive unit of O_F (det and det^-1 in O_F, det totally positive): the corrected knowl's Gamma_0(N)_b, membership by entries in both directions (the forward direction from the committed lattice lemmas apply_zero_zero_mem, apply_zero_one_mul_mem, apply_one_one_mul_mem, mem_one_of_forall_mul_mem, det_mem_one and mem_gammaZero_iff, the converse is the committed mem_gammaZero_of_apply_mem). (2) The cusp condition: HilbertModularForm imposes isBoundedAtCusps (f|alpha bounded as all Im z_w tend to infinity, for every alpha in SL_2(F), so that degree 1 is right); the knowl imposes nothing. In the knowl's setting (F totally real of degree n > 1, N nonzero) it is automatic: isBoundedAtCusps_of_mem_slashInvariants. Hence HilbertModularForm.mem_space_iff: HilbertModularForm.space k N b is exactly the set of tuples (f_c) of holomorphic functions with f_c(gamma z) = automorphyFactor k gamma z * f_c(z) for gamma in Gamma_0(N)_{b_c}, the knowl's definition word for word; and HilbertModularForm.ofSmulEq builds a HilbertModularForm from the knowl's data alone. Proof. (i) FourierExistence.lean, hasHilbertFourierExpansion_fourierCoeff: for F totally real, a holomorphic phi on H^n invariant under z -> z + b, b in b^-1 (IsTranslationInvariant), is the sum of its Fourier series over the trace dual (b^-1)^v = b d^-1 (the committed HasHilbertFourierExpansion, with the committed fourierCoeff as the coefficients): with a Z-basis (e_j) of b^-1, the vectors (w(e_j))_w form an R-basis of R^n (Mathlib's fractionalIdealLatticeBasis), so x -> (sum_j x_j w(e_j))_w maps C^n onto C^n and the tube over the open convex cone {y : sum_j y_j w(e_j) > 0} onto H^n; x -> phi(sum_j x_j e_j) is holomorphic and Z^n-periodic there, hence the sum of its Fourier series (the committed hasSum_tubeFourierCoeff_mul_cexp, TubeFourierSeries.lean); nu -> (Tr(nu e_j))_j is a bijection from (b^-1)^v onto Z^n (inverse k -> sum_j k_j e_j^v, Mathlib's Basis.traceDual), and k.x = Tr(nu z). (ii) KoecherPrinciple.lean, HasHilbertFourierExpansion.eq_zero_or_isTotallyPositive: if moreover phi|_k diag(1, eps^M) = phi for every totally positive unit eps of O_F (some M != 0), then a(nu) != 0 only for nu = 0 or nu totally positive: a(eps nu) = C a(nu) by uniqueness (apply_mulUnit, any weight k); if w0(nu) < 0, Dirichlet's unit theorem (Mathlib's dirichletUnitTheorem.exists_unit and the product formula Units.sum_mult_mul_log, with a second real place as n > 1) gives a unit u with |w0(u)| > 1 and |w(u)| < 1 at the other places; with eps = u^(2M), the terms of the series at (i, ..., i) along eps^s nu have absolute value |C|^s |a(nu)| exp(-2 pi Tr(eps^s nu)), and -Tr(eps^s nu) >= |w0(nu)| w0(eps)^s - sum_w |w(nu)| beats s log|C|, against their convergence to 0. (iii) HasHilbertFourierExpansion.boundedAtFilter: such a series is bounded on {Im z_w >= 1 for all w}. (iv) BoundedAtCusps.lean: for alpha in SL_2(F), Gamma cap alpha^-1 Gamma alpha has finite index in Gamma = Gamma_0(N)_b (the committed isFiniteRelIndex_conj_smul_gammaZero, behind mem_commensurator_gammaZero, needs N != 0), so alpha gamma^M alpha^-1 is in Gamma for M the factorial of that index (cuspExponent, mul_pow_cuspExponent_mul_inv_mem); f|alpha is invariant under the translations by M b^-1, the inverse of cuspIdeal b N alpha (as (1, b; 0, 1)^M = (1, Mb; 0, 1)), and under diag(1, eps^M); (i)-(iii) apply (hasHilbertFourierExpansion_slash, eq_zero_or_isTotallyPositive_slash, isBoundedAtCusps_of_mem_slashInvariants). Also proved: the statement HilbertModularForm.KoecherPrinciple of FourierExpansion.lean (koecherPrinciple, for every number field), and the cusp-form half read as usual: HasHilbertFourierExpansion.tendsto_atImInfty (the limit at infinity is the constant term, Tannery's theorem), vanishesAtCusps_iff and isCuspForm_iff (a Hilbert modular form is a cusp form, IsCuspForm = VanishesAtCusps at every component, exactly when the constant terms of its Fourier expansions at all cusps vanish). Setting: the definitions are for any number field, real places, integer weights, any ideal N and any invertible fractional representatives; the knowl's restrictions (totally real, n > 1, k_i >= 2 of the same parity, N nonzero, integral representatives) are generalised, and the equality of the spaces is proved exactly in the knowl's setting (totally real, n > 1, N nonzero; no condition on the weights). - `mf.maass.mwf` [Modular forms › Maass]: Round AL (AL1_multiplier_systems), from partial (tracker v59: medium, theory; bk: the classification of the multiplier systems of real weight k on SL_2(Z), the knowl's '6 conjugates'; x: square-integrability imposed in weight k though the knowl lists it only for weight 0). Reviewed 2026-11-16 (review/AL1_multiplier_systems.md): outcome confirmed; style fixes only (two redeclared variables, five statement layouts, a two-component name, two hoisted binders, the scattered opens) and two docstrings made precise, no statement changed. Every sentence of the live text (2020-07-24) is proved or is no mathematical claim, with two fixable texts (one recorded) and one wording question for the editors. Source: F. Stromberg, Computation of Maass waveforms with nontrivial multiplier systems, Math. Comp. 77 (2008), 2375-2416 (arXiv:math/0611146: Definition 2.2, Remark 2.6, Section 3), and Hecke operators for Maass waveforms on PSL(2,Z) with integer weight and eta multiplier (arXiv:math/0611148: Lemma 2.1, Section 2.1); the LMFDB's former weight-k Maass forms (character 'eta' in mwf_main.py, removed in lmfdb 93942a217) were his. (1) Weight 0: UpperHalfPlane.IsMaassForm (committed). (2) Weight k with multiplier system v: UpperHalfPlane.IsMaassFormOfWeight (committed; maassSlash, maassLaplacian) with v a multiplier system of real weight k, the new ModularForm.IsMultiplierSystemOfWeight (Multiplier/RealWeight.lean): v : Gamma -> S^1 with v(gamma delta) j(gamma delta, z)^k = v(gamma) v(delta) j(gamma, delta z)^k j(delta, z)^k for all z (principal powers, j = cz + d) and v(-I) = e^{-pi i k} when -I is in Gamma; this is Stromberg's Definition 2.2 (v(AB) = sigma_k(A,B) v(A) v(B) with j_A(z;k) = e^{ik Arg(cz+d)}, Arg in (-pi, pi]), as |j(gamma delta, z)| = |j(gamma, delta z)| |j(delta, z)|. The eta multiplier satisfies it for every real k (isMultiplierSystemOfWeight_etaMultiplier); in integral weight on subgroups of SL(2,R) it is the LMFDB's mf.multipliersystem (isMultiplierSystemOfWeight_intCast_iff, IsMultiplierSystemOfWeight.map_mul); algebra: .mul, .inv, divMonoidHom with divMonoidHom_neg_one, isMultiplierSystemOfWeight_add_two_mul_iff (weights k and k + 2m, Stromberg's remark after Definition 2.2). The multiplier of a Maass form not identically zero, on a group with some multiplier system of weight k (SL(2,Z): the eta multiplier), is a multiplier system (IsMultiplierSystemOfWeight.of_maassSlash, IsMaassFormOfWeight.isMultiplierSystemOfWeight). Square-integrability in weight k is the knowl's notion: its weight-0 paragraph, with which the weight-k definition must agree at k = 0, v = 1 (isMaassFormOfWeight_zero_iff); Stromberg's condition 3 (Math. Comp., Section 3) and arXiv:math/0611148, Section 2.1; the ruling of 2026-11-12 (Maass knowls read for the cusp forms the LMFDB stores). Its omission is a fixable text (pair 2). (3) 'If the level is equal to 1, the only possible multiplier systems are given by the Dedekind eta function. A compatible multiplier system for weight k is given by [v_eta^{2k}] or one of its 6 conjugates': Stromberg's Remark 2.6 (exactly six multiplier systems of each real weight k on PSL(2,Z), v_eta^{2(k+r)}, r in {0,2,4,6,8,10}) and Lemma 2.1 of arXiv:math/0611148 (v(T) = xi_6 e^{pi i k/6}, 'exactly 6 different multiplier systems'); 'its 6 conjugates' are these six, v_eta^{2k} among them (the six roots xi_6 e^{pi i k/6} of x^6 = e^{pi i k}); the literal seven is false (at most six exist), so six in all is the LMFDB's reading (ruling of 2026-11-14), with a wording question for the editors (pair 3). Proved in Multiplier/RealWeightLevelOne.lean on the image of SL(2,Z) (level 1), for every real k: isMultiplierSystemOfWeight_iff_exists_etaMultiplier (v is a multiplier system of weight k iff v = v_eta^{2(k+2m)} for some m : Fin 6), injective_etaMultiplier_add_two_mul and ncard_setOf_isMultiplierSystemOfWeight (exactly six), IsMultiplierSystemOfWeight.ext_T and pow_six_apply_T (Lemma 2.1's form), UpperHalfPlane.IsMaassFormOfWeight.exists_eq_etaMultiplier (the multiplier of a Maass form of weight k on SL(2,Z) not identically zero is one of the six; only the transformation law is used). Route: the characters of SL(2,Z) (ModularGroup.map_S_mul_map_T_pow_three, map_T_pow_twelve, map_neg_one_eq_map_T_pow_six, monoidHom_ext_T) are the powers of ModularForm.etaCharacter = v_eta^2, with v_eta^2(T) = e^{pi i/6} (exists_eq_etaCharacter_zpow), those trivial at -I the v_eta^{4m}; v / v_eta^{2k} is one (divMonoidHom); v_eta^{24} = 1. Not claimed and not proved: that each of the five other systems carries a nonzero Maass form. (4) 'One can show that v(A) is well-defined and independent of the point z in the upper half-plane': coe_etaMultiplier, coe_etaMultiplier_of_cexp_eq (round AI), for the corrected formula (pair 1). (5) The remark, in Maass/HolomorphicSlashConvention.lean: holomorphicSlash ((cz+d)^{-k} F(gamma z), principal power) and holomorphicMaassLaplacian (the remark's y^2(d_xx + d_yy) - iky(d_x + i d_y); Bruinier-Funke's weight k Laplacian up to sign); maassSlash_im_rpow_mul_eq (det 1: the unitary slash of y^{k/2} F is y^{k/2} times the holomorphic slash of F), maassLaplacian_im_rpow_mul_eq (Delta_k(y^{k/2} F) = y^{k/2}(Delta^hol_k F + (k/2)(k/2 - 1) F) for F of class C^2; recomputed by hand, and with the committed maassLaplacian_im_rpow_mul it gives Delta^hol_k F = 0 for holomorphic F, as Cauchy-Riemann predicts), maassSlash_im_rpow_mul_eq_mul_iff and maassLaplacian_im_rpow_mul_add_mul_eq_zero_iff (the transformation laws and the Laplace equations correspond, the eigenvalue shifted by (k/2)(k/2 - 1); not vacuous: eta^{2k} with v_eta^{2k}); 'This convention is usually used in the context of Harmonic weak Maass forms' is a remark on the literature. The tracker v59 gap ('PSL(2, ℤ[i]) as a subgroup of PSL(2, ℂ) acting on ℋ₃ by isometries, discrete, of finite covolume and not cocompact') is closed, so every claim of the knowl is proved for the formalisation's objects, under either reading of 'the group of isometries PSL(2, ℂ)' (see (7)). (1) Subgroup: picardToPSL : PSL(2, ℤ[i]) →* PSL(2, ℂ) is Tau Ceti's TauCeti.SpecialLinear.projectiveMap 2 GaussianInt.toComplex (the review replaced the author's pslMap and center_le_comap_center, duplicates of Tau Ceti's projectiveMap and map_center_le_comap_center at the pin, equal to them by rfl). It is injective (picardToPSL_injective, from the general HyperbolicThreeSpace.projectiveMap_injective: for an injective ring hom, a matrix whose image is scalar is scalar). The committed SMul of PicardGroup on ℋ₃ factors through it (picardToPSL_smul), and picardSubgroup is its range. (2) PSL(2, ℂ) is a group of isometries acting by linear fractional transformations. pslToIsom : PSL(2, ℂ) →* Isom(ℋ₃) maps into Tau Ceti's group of smooth Riemannian isometries (C^∞ diffeomorphisms preserving the metric tensor) of TauCeti.UpperHalfSpace ℂ, whose metric (‖dx‖² + dy²)/y² is the knowl's ds = |dz|/y (TauCeti.UpperHalfSpace.norm_def). Its value is the LMFDB coordinate formula moebius (pslToIsom_apply: pslToIsom γ z = γ • z), and it is injective (pslToIsom_injective: the fixed points of g ≠ ±1 are null, by hyperbolicVolume_setOf_smul_eq_self). Proof: an upper triangular matrix acts by a Tau Ceti similarity, (0,-1;1,0) acts by (x, y) ↦ (-x̄, y) after Tau Ceti's inversion in the unit sphere, and g = (c⁻¹, a; 0, c)(0,-1;1,0)(1, d/c; 0, 1) when c ≠ 0. Riemannian isometries also preserve the Riemannian distance (Tau Ceti's RiemannianIsometry.riemannianEDist_eq), so each element of PSL(2, ℂ) is a metric isometry as well. The formula z ↦ (az + b)(cz + d)⁻¹ holds in Mathlib's quaternions ℍ[ℝ] with z = x + yj (toQuaternion_smul, for a representative of determinant 1). (3) Discrete: discreteTopology_picardSubgroup, for Mathlib's quotient topology of PSL(2, ℂ) = SL(2, ℂ)/{±1}, SL(2, ℂ) with the subspace topology of M₂(ℂ). It comes from the general criterion discreteTopology_of_finite: only finitely many elements have a representative with entries of absolute value at most C (finite_setOf_mem_picardSubgroup). (4) Cofinite: exists_isFundamentalDomain_picardSubgroup gives a measurable fundamental domain (proper discontinuity, countability, null fixed-point sets). Every fundamental domain has finite hyperbolic volume (hyperbolicVolume_lt_top_picardSubgroup), so Mathlib's covolume is finite (covolume_picardSubgroup_lt_top); Mathlib's covolume is 0 when no fundamental domain exists, which is excluded here by the existence theorem (the docstring says so; Tau Ceti's Subgroup.IsCofinite for Fuchsian groups uses the same covolume). The measure is the committed hyperbolicVolume dx₁ dx₂ dy / y³, the volume element of ds² = (dx₁² + dx₂² + dy²)/y², invariant under PSL(2, ℂ). The volume bound comes from reduction theory, proved directly for ℤ[i] (exists_norm_le_one_and_le_height): every point is moved by SL(2, ℤ[i]) into {|x| ≤ 1, y ≥ 1/2}, using a point of maximal height in the orbit, a Gaussian-integer translation and S. The brief's suggested transfer from bianchiPSLGroup σ (bianchiGammaZero 1) was not used: no tree identifies ℤ[i] with 𝒪_K for a number field K (Tau Ceti's GaussianRationals.adjoin_eq_top gives 𝒪_K = ℤ[θ] only), and the direct proof is short. The SL₂ image for general K is in BianchiGroupKleinian.lean (record mf.bianchi.bianchigroup), so the GL₂-against-SL₂ index never arises. (5) Not cocompact: Γ \ ℋ₃ is not compact (not_compactSpace_quotient_picardSubgroup), and neither is PSL(2, ℂ)/Γ, so Γ is not a cocompact subgroup of PSL(2, ℂ) in the group sense either (not_compactSpace_quotientGroup_picardSubgroup). These come from the general not_compactSpace_quotient_of_height (an element sends height y to y, or to at most 1/y) and compactSpace_quotient_of_compactSpace_quotientGroup. (6) The committed definition IsPicardMaassForm now has a non-vacuous, well-posed L²(Γ \ ℋ₃) clause. The Picard group itself has a measurable fundamental domain (exists_isFundamentalDomain_picardGroup, via isFundamentalDomain_picardGroup_iff). Integrability of an invariant function, such as |f|², does not depend on the fundamental domain (integrableOn_iff_of_isFundamentalDomain_picardGroup). These are the two facts the R4 record called 'not proved here'. The review checked that the constant function 1 satisfies IsPicardMaassForm with eigenvalue 0 (scratch AL2_picard_group-review/Probe.lean), so the definition is inhabited. Bases: mf.maass.picard.laplacian is formalised (tracker v59). (7) READING, no longer a judgement call: 'a ... subgroup of the group of isometries PSL(2, ℂ), where the isometries are given by linear fractional transformations' is proved under both readings. (i) 'PSL(2, ℂ), a group of isometries of ℋ₃ acting by linear fractional transformations', the brief's reading: pslToIsom is injective, with pslToIsom_apply and toQuaternion_smul. (ii) 'PSL(2, ℂ) is the group of orientation-preserving isometries' (follow-up, OrientationPreservingIsometry.lean): an isometry is orientation-preserving (IsOrientationPreserving) when the Jacobian determinant of its differential in the chart ℂ × ℝ = ℝ³ (jacobianDet; the chart of the open subset ℋ₃ is the inclusion and tangentSpaceCastModel is the identity, so this is the Euclidean Jacobian) is positive; its sign is the same at every point (isOrientationPreserving_iff_jacobianDet_pos). isOrientationPreserving_iff_mem_range shows, for every element of Tau Ceti's Isom (all four cases of Tau Ceti's classification exists_eq_similarity_or_exists_eq_inversion_mul_similarity with Mathlib's linear_isometry_complex), that these are exactly the elements of the image of pslToIsom, so pslEquivOrientationPreservingIsom : PSL(2, ℂ) ≃* Isom⁺(ℋ₃) (orientationPreservingIsom, whose carrier is {Φ | IsOrientationPreserving Φ}). Proof: the Jacobian determinants are c³ det A for a similarity (jacobianDet_similarity) and negative for an inversion (jacobianDet_inversion_neg); a similarity with a rotation is the action of an upper triangular matrix (similarity_rotation_mem_range); the inversion in the sphere of radius |R| about (a, 0) is the action of (a, |a|² − R²; 1, ā)/R after (x, y) ↦ (−x̄, y) (inversion_eq_pslToIsom_mul_negConjIsom). The literal 'PSL(2, ℂ) is the group of all isometries' is false: (x, y) ↦ (−x̄, y) is an isometry that reverses orientation (not_isOrientationPreserving_negConjIsom); this is recorded as an optional fixable wording. pslToIsom stays the underlying map and is no longer in decls. TEXT ERRORS. New, fixable (changes the mathematics), old string once in the live text: '$ad-bc\not=0$' → '$ad-bc=1$'. For a matrix of determinant δ, the quaternion (az + b)(cz + d)⁻¹ has j-coefficient yδ/(|cx + d|² + |c|²y²), which lies in ℋ₃ only for real δ > 0: diag(i, 1) sends j to k. Optional, fixable (the literal reading is false), once: 'the group of isometries' → 'the group of orientation-preserving isometries' (no overlap with the recorded comma fix). Already recorded in lmfdb-knowl-edits.md, each old string once in the live text: 'z=x+iy' → 'z=x+yj' (in the quaternions) and ' ,where' → ', where'. Sp(2g, R) is made a topological group (new instance, inverse -J A^t J continuous), so Gamma is closed (Mathlib's Subgroup.isClosed_of_discreteTopology); its elements with entries bounded by M form a compact discrete set, hence finite, and the committed exists_abs_apply_le_of_isCompact bounds the entries of every element moving a compact K to meet a compact L. not_free_integral: Gamma_g = Sp(2g, Z) (SymplecticGroup.integral, acting through Sp(2g, Q) -> Sp(2g, R)) does not act freely, since -1 lies in it, is not 1, and fixes every point (negOne_smul: (-tau)(-1)^-1 = tau). This last statement assumes g >= 1 ([Nonempty l]); for g = 0 Sp(0, Z) is trivial and acts freely on the one-point H_0, but the LMFDB's Siegel degrees are positive and other committed Siegel files make the same assumption. - `modlgal.top_slope` [Representations › Mod-ℓ Galois] (#64): Round AF: gaps (0)-(2) of the round-AA record (AA2_local_fields; the prompt's 'AD2' is a typo) are closed, for every number field L (Galois over Q or not), so for mod-l representations over any number field K; gap (3), the lf.slopes reading, is closed by the ruling of 2026-11-11 under which lf.top_slope is formalised on the Galois reading. (0) Local, GaloisClosureRamification: the Galois closure of a finite separable E/K of nonarchimedean local fields is unramified (tamely ramified) iff E is (isUnramified_galoisClosure_iff, isTamelyRamified_galoisClosure_iff: E embeds in its Galois closure, tower_bot; conversely the normal closure is a compositum of conjugates, isUnramified_normalClosure mirrors Tau Ceti's IsTamelyRamified.normalClosure through a new isUnramified_sup), so topArtinSlope K E = 0 iff E/K unramified, <= 1 iff tame, = 1 iff tame and ramified (topArtinSlope_eq_zero_iff_isUnramified, _le_one_iff_isTamelyRamified, _eq_one_iff_isTamelyRamified), for any local-field structure on E. (1) Global, TopSlopeRamification: localAlgebraToCompletion, Q_l (x) L -> L_w, a (x) x |-> e(a)x, is onto (from Tau Ceti's semilocalHom_surjective), and every maximal ideal of Q_l (x) L is the kernel of one of them (exists_eq_ker_localAlgebraToCompletion: the product map to prod_w L_w is onto between Q_l-spaces of dimension [L:Q], by Tau Ceti's sum_finrank_adicCompletion_eq_finrank, hence injective); the factor (Q_l (x) L)/ker = L_w has ramification index over Q_l the global e(w) (ramificationIndex_quotient_eq: Q_l -> Q_v is a continuous field isomorphism, hence a ValuativeExtension by Tau Ceti's of_continuous_algebraMap, with e(Q_v/Q_l) = 1, then Tau Ceti's ramificationIndex_adicCompletion; new ramificationIndex_eq_of_algEquiv). Hence topArtinSlopeAt L l = 0 iff every prime P of O_L containing l has P.ramificationIdx Z = 1, <= 1 iff l divides none of them, = 1 iff tame but not unramified (NumberField.topArtinSlopeAt_eq_zero_iff, _le_one_iff, _eq_one_iff; MonoidHom.topArtinSlope_eq_zero_iff, _eq_one_iff for the splitting field of rho). Glue proved: P lies over the place of Q at l iff l in P, and ramificationIdx over O_Q equals that over Z. (2) TopArtinSlopeCompositum + TopSlopeCompositum: top slope is monotone in Galois towers and the top slope of a compositum of finitely many Galois extensions is the largest of theirs (topArtinSlopeOfIsGalois_iSup, from Tau Ceti's Herbrand theorem map_restrictNormalHom_upperRamificationGroup and the triviality of the intersection of the restriction kernels); the Galois closure of Q_l (x) L is the compositum of the Galois closures of its factors (galoisClosure_localAlgebra_eq_iSup), so topArtinSlopeAt L l = top Artin slope of the compositum (topArtinSlopeAt_eq_topArtinSlopeOfIsGalois), and the definition's supremum is attained, 'the largest' (isGreatest_topArtinSlopeAt); when the top slope is neither 0 nor 1 it is the largest wild Artin slope of the compositum (isGreatest_wildArtinSlopesOfIsGalois_topArtinSlopeAt). The product decomposition of Q_l (x) L into l-adic fields is localAlgebraEquivPi (round ZZ). Alternatives to link: NumberField.topArtinSlopeAt_eq_zero_iff, _le_one_iff, _eq_one_iff, NumberField.topArtinSlopeAt_eq (L Galois), IsNonarchimedeanLocalField.topArtinSlopeOfIsGalois_iSup, NumberField.ramificationIndex_quotient_eq, IsNonarchimedeanLocalField.topArtinSlope_eq_zero_iff_isUnramified, IsNonarchimedeanLocalField.isGreatest_topArtinSlope. Side finding: for K = Q, Tau Ceti's semilocal tensor product and Mathlib's Padic.adicCompletionEquiv use the Q-algebra structure of Q_v as a completion of Q (HeightOneSpectrum.instAlgebraAdicCompletion), not the DivisionRing.toRatAlgebra found by instance search, and the two are not defeq at instance transparency; worked around by Padic.ringEquivAdicCompletion and one explicit instance argument. No text error. Review (AF4): formalised, confirmed. Gaps (0)-(2) checked against their statements: no hidden hypothesis (the hypotheses of the intermediate lemmas, a continuous ring isomorphism e : Q_l = Q_v and 𝔪 = ker of the map to L_w, are met in the main proofs by Padic.ringEquivAdicCompletion and rfl, and every maximal ideal is such a kernel). The Q-algebra diamond on Q_v only enters proofs: no linked statement mentions Q_v, the linked iff statements are about topArtinSlopeAt and the primes of O_L, and ramificationIndex depends only on the valuations. The compositum is represented by its Galois closure, galoisClosure Q_l (Q_l (x) L), which is the Galois closure of every compositum of the factors, so its top slope is lf.top_slope of the compositum. LMFDB setting: the statements hold for every number field K; the LMFDB's codomains GL(1,3), GL(1,5), GL(2,2), GL(2,3), GL(2,5) and GSp(4,2) in GL(4,2) are GL_n-valued, and the top slope depends only on ker rho (the NumberField statements apply to the kernel field kerSplittingField of a representation into any group), so this is not a GL_n-only formalisation in the sense of the ruling of 2026-11-07. - `nf.algebraic_closure` [Fields › Number fields]: The reading is removed: isAlgClosure_iff_forall_isAlgClosed_eq_top proves that an algebraically closed extension L of K satisfies Mathlib's IsAlgClosure K L (algebraic over K) exactly when it is the knowl's minimal algebraically closed extension, i.e. every algebraically closed intermediate field of L/K is L (one way: L is algebraic over E, so algebraMap E L is onto; the other: the relative algebraic closure algebraicClosure K L is algebraically closed, hence all of L). Uniqueness up to isomorphism is IsAlgClosure.equiv. NumberField.ringEquivAlgebraicClosure is an isomorphism from any algebraic closure of a number field (an algebraic closure of ℚ, hence written ℚ̄) onto algebraicClosure ℚ ℂ, the field of algebraic numbers in ℂ; it applies to Mathlib's AlgebraicClosure K. The remark '(non-canonical)' is proved in the form 'not unique': nontrivial_algEquiv_of_not_isSepClosed shows that an algebraic closure of any field K that is not separably closed has a nontrivial automorphism over K (a separable element outside K is moved to another root of its minimal polynomial, by Normal.minpoly_eq_iff_mem_orbit), so two algebraic closures are isomorphic in more than one way, and NumberField.not_isSepClosed shows this applies to every number field (a root of the cyclotomic polynomial of a prime p > [K:ℚ] + 1, separable over ℚ, would have degree p - 1). The review generalised this from 'characteristic zero and not algebraically closed' to 'not separably closed', so that finite fields and other fields of characteristic p are covered too; for a separably closed K the isomorphism is unique, so this is the full range where the remark can hold, and the remark is read as the usual 'not canonical in general' (not formalised: uniqueness for separably closed K, which the knowl does not claim). 'Usually denoted' is notation. No text error found.

The sentence 'There are four basic types, I-IV, which describe the structure of the units U modulo roots of unity', read (the user's ruling of 2026-11-14) as Mazur and Ullom's Theorem 1 and Remark 1, is proved in the form 'up to an automorphism of V4' that the paper's Remark 2 gives the types: V4 = ℤˣ × ℤˣ (new instance IsKleinFour (ℤˣ × ℤˣ)), the four ℤ[V4]-modules MazurUllomBasicType.rep T (Representation ℤ (ℤˣ × ℤˣ) T.lattice: sublattices of A0 ⊕ A1 ⊕ A2 = ℤ³ with the three nontrivial characters acting on the coordinates; type I all of ℤ³, II {v0 ≡ v1}, III {v0 + v1 + v2 even}, IV {v0 ≡ v1 ≡ v2} mod 2), the Galois module of K as Mathlib's Representation.ofMulDistribMulAction of a new instance MulDistribMulAction Gal(K/ℚ) ((𝓞 K)ˣ ⧸ torsion K) (modTorsionRep K, through round AJ's modTorsionMap), and the basic type IsMazurUllomBasicType K T (some subtype with roman numeral T). Proved: Theorem 1, IsMazurUllomBasicType.exists_equiv (K of basic type T has U/{±1} ≅ T.rep along some Gal(K/ℚ) ≃* V4, as a Representation.Equiv), in the paper's labelled form QuadraticUnitFrame.galoisModuleEquiv (along f.kleinEquiv, which sends the automorphism fixing the i-th quadratic subfield of the frame to σi; type II gives B2 ⊕ A2 in the frame's labelling, the paper's A_k ⊕ B_k); Remark 1, MazurUllomBasicType.eq_of_equiv (the four modules are pairwise non-isomorphic even after an automorphism of V4) and eq_of_equiv_comp (pulled back along two isomorphisms G ≃* V4); existsUnique_isMazurUllomBasicType; isMazurUllomBasicType_iff (the basic type is the isomorphism class: K has basic type T iff U/{±1} ≅ T.rep along some Gal(K/ℚ) ≃* V4); exists_equiv_iff (two real biquadratic fields have isomorphic Galois modules, along an isomorphism of their Galois groups, iff they have the same basic type: the invariant and its converse). The four modules are the paper's (MazurUllomModuleGroupRing): type I is A0 ⊕ A1 ⊕ A2 by definition, type II has the basis (1,1,0), (1,-1,0), (0,0,1) with the relations of B2 and A2 (MazurUllomBasicType.typeIIBasis, rep_typeIIBasis_zero, rep_typeIIBasis_two), type III is the augmentation ideal J of ℤ[V4] (augmentationEquiv, J being Tau Ceti's TauCeti.augmentationSubrepresentation of ℤ[V4] under Mathlib's left regular representation, the kernel of the coefficient sum), type IV is ℤ[V4]/(ν) (traceQuotientEquiv, (ν) = ℤν being Tau Ceti's TauCeti.invariantLine, ν = TauCeti.permutationSum). Route: the square-exponent isomorphism x ↦ v with x² = ∏ (ēi^(scale i))^(vi) of a frame of subtype t (MazurUllomType.IsSquareBasis.sqVecEquiv, uniform over the seven subtypes, using round AJ's isSquareBasis_unitClass and isTypeOf_iff), and for Remark 1 the lattices fixed by σ0, σ1, σ2, whose generators have the parity pattern of I (i), II (i), III or IV, compared up to permutation by round AJ's decide lemma eq_of_forall_parity_iff. Not proved, and not stated by the knowls (the user's ruling reads the types up to automorphisms of V4): the paper's finer fixed-Γ statement that A_i ⊕ B_i and A_j ⊕ B_j are non-isomorphic for i ≠ j; that each type occurs (Kubota's examples) is not claimed by the texts either. - `nf.galois_group.name` [Fields › Number fields]: Round AI (AI2), reviewed. Formalised by an example in the LMFDB's setting, following the ruling of 2026-11-13 on nf.sextic_twin: a mathematical remark is a stated fact, to be proved by an example. The 'nTt' search syntax, the short names (Cj, Dj, Sj, Aj, the alias table), what a label encodes and the search behaviour are site conventions; that a Galois group is a faithful transitive permutation group belongs to gg.galois_group (Mathlib's galActionHom_injective and galAction_isPretransitive, linked there). The remark is 'An abstract group may have more than one representation as a Galois group. Correspondingly, the familiar symbol for a group may represent several Galois groups.' The Galois group of a number field is formalised as the blueprint does for nf.galois_group: the Galois group of a defining polynomial (Mathlib's Polynomial.Gal, the automorphism group of its splitting field, the Galois closure) acting on its roots (Polynomial.Gal.galActionHom). The example is S3, the LMFDB's own (its alias S3 stands for 3T2 and its sibling representations, lmfdb/galois_groups/transitive_group.py), and the smallest, since no abstract group repeats among the transitive groups of degree <= 5. (1) The cubic field Q(cbrt 2), LMFDB 3.1.108.1, defined by the irreducible X^3 - 2: its Galois group is S3 acting on its 3 complex roots, the group 3T2. Tau Ceti's TauCeti.hasGaloisLabel_X_pow_three_sub_two gives the label; Polynomial.card_rootSet_X_pow_three_sub_two (3 roots), Polynomial.bijective_galActionHom_X_pow_three_sub_two (the action is the full symmetric group, from faithfulness and Tau Ceti's TauCeti.natCard_gal_X_pow_three_sub_two = 6) and Polynomial.galXPowThreeSubTwoMulEquiv : Gal(X^3 - 2) ≃* Perm (Fin 3). (2) Its Galois closure L = SplittingField (X^3 - 2), a sextic field (Polynomial.finrank_splittingField_X_pow_three_sub_two). For every primitive element y of L (hypothesis Q⟮y⟯ = ⊤), that is for every defining polynomial g = minpoly Q y of L: Polynomial.galMinpolySplittingFieldXPowThreeSubTwoMulEquiv : Gal(g) ≃* Perm (Fin 3), through Tau Ceti's TauCeti.galEquivNormalClosure (Gal(g) is the automorphism group of the normal closure of Q(y) = L, which is Gal(X^3 - 2) by definition), and Polynomial.card_rootSet_minpoly_splittingField_X_pow_three_sub_two (Gal(g) acts on 6 complex roots, the group 6T2). (3) Added by the review, the remark as one unconditional statement, Polynomial.exists_card_rootSet_eq_six_and_nonempty_gal_mulEquiv: there is an irreducible g in Q[X] with 6 complex roots and Gal(g) ≃* Perm (Fin 3) (a primitive element exists by Mathlib's Field.exists_primitive_element). So the abstract group S3 is the Galois group of a cubic and of a sextic number field, with faithful transitive permutation representations of degrees 3 and 6, which differ. The label 6T2 itself is not formalised (T-numbers in degree >= 6 are gg.tnumber's gap, issue #49); the remark does not need it, the degrees already telling the two representations apart. Doubtful reading, flagged by the audit: a minor 'may' remark inside a search knowl, formalised on the ruling above. No error of mathematics in the text; two pure typos recorded (a missing word 'representation', a missing comma). Review: three declarations renamed after what they are about (natDegree_minpoly_eq_six, galMinpolyMulEquiv, card_rootSet_minpoly_eq_six: now ..._splittingField_X_pow_three_sub_two), no statement changed; the degree lemma now uses Mathlib's Field.primitive_element_iff_minpoly_natDegree_eq. lake build through the guard; #lint (15 linters) clean; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; the eight public names are new in Mathlib, Tau Ceti and LeanBridge.
- `nf.ideal_labels` [Fields › Number fields]: Formalised the Cremona-Page-Sutherland order (arXiv:2005.09491, sections 2-3; conventions checked against psort.py of github.com/JohnCremona/Sorting) for an integral primitive element alpha: primes by norm, ramification index and the lexicographic order of the p-adic digit vector (a_{0,0}, a_{1,0}, ..., a_{0,1}, ...) of their p-adic factor (the minimal polynomial over Q_p of alpha in K_P, proved irreducible, dividing g, of degree e*f and with Z_p coefficients), and the ideals of norm N lexicographically on their p-parts, each compared by weight and then by the reverse lexicographic order of the exponents. Proved that distinct primes above p have distinct p-adic factors (via Tau Ceti's semilocal decomposition Q_p (x) K = prod K_P), that the order is a strict total order on primes and on ideals, that the label N.i (the existing Ideal.normLabel) is injective with values exactly N.1, ..., N.m, and that prime ideals come first among the ideals of their norm and are ordered as the primes. The LMFDB's alpha is the class of X in Q[X]/(g), g = NumberField.polredabs K (nf.polredabs, formalised), proved integral and primitive, which gives NumberField.lmfdbIdealLabel (injective); for an abstract K the labels depend on the isomorphism Q[X]/(g) = K only up to an automorphism of K, as the knowl's 'canonical alpha' presupposes K = Q[X]/(g).

- `nf.nickname` [Fields › Number fields]: Round AI (AI2), reviewed. Formalised. The nicknames themselves (Q, Qi, QsqrtN, QzetaN, QzetaN+, Q(s1, ..., sk), and the sqrt, root, cbrt, zetaN, phi syntax with its examples) are a site convention: 'Q(sqrt N)', 'zeta_N is a primitive Nth root of unity' and 'phi (for (1 + sqrt 5)/2)' only say what the names denote and assert nothing. The one mathematical statement is in 'QzetaN+, for Q(zeta_N)^+; i.e. the maximal real subfield of Q(zeta_N) (equivalently, the field Q(zeta_N + zeta_N^{-1}))': the maximal real subfield of Q(zeta_N) is Q(zeta_N + zeta_N^{-1}). Q(zeta_N) is any K with Mathlib's IsCyclotomicExtension {N} Q K, a number field, for example Mathlib's CyclotomicField N Q or the subfield of C generated by the N-th roots of unity. Its maximal real subfield is Mathlib's NumberField.maximalRealSubfield, the elements real under every complex embedding, which is the largest totally real subfield (Mathlib's isTotallyReal_iff_le_maximalRealSubfield). New, IsPrimitiveRoot.maximalRealSubfield_eq_adjoin_add_inv: for every primitive N-th root of unity zeta in K, every N >= 1 (N = 1 and N = 2, where both sides are K = Q, included), maximalRealSubfield K = (Q⟮zeta + zeta⁻¹⟯).toSubfield. Proof, without galEquivZMod: (i) zeta + zeta^{-1} is real under every embedding phi, as |phi zeta| = 1 makes (phi zeta)^{-1} its conjugate (IsPrimitiveRoot.add_inv_mem_maximalRealSubfield); (ii) K/Q is Galois (Mathlib's IsCyclotomicExtension.isGalois), so Q(zeta + zeta^{-1}) is the fixed field of its fixing subgroup (IsGalois.fixedField_fixingSubgroup). An automorphism sigma fixing zeta + zeta^{-1} satisfies (sigma zeta - zeta)(sigma zeta - zeta^{-1}) = 0. Either sigma = 1 (it agrees with the identity on the generator zeta), or sigma zeta = zeta^{-1}, and then phi o sigma = conj o phi for every complex embedding phi, so sigma fixes the maximal real subfield. Tau Ceti's TauCeti.IsCyclotomicExtension.Rat.toSubfield_fixedField_zpowers_galEquivZMod_symm_neg_one (the maximal real subfield is the fixed field of zeta -> zeta^{-1}) is linked as the companion description. No text error. Review: statement and proof checked; no statement changed (two inline extensionality proofs shortened with Set.eqOn_singleton). Non-vacuity (scratch Probe.lean): the theorem applies to CyclotomicField n Q for every n >= 1 and for n = 1, 2 (Mathlib's instance CyclotomicField.isCyclotomicExtension n Q given explicitly; inferInstance does not find it at this pin), and to IntermediateField.adjoin Q {b : C | b ^ n = 1} through the committed instances of MulChar/GaloisAction.lean. lake build through the guard; #lint (15 linters) clean; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; both simp lemmas needed (deletion test); the three public names are new in Mathlib, Tau Ceti and LeanBridge.

- `nf.picture` [Fields › Number fields]: Round AI (AI2), reviewed. Formalised under either reading of its one ambiguous sentence; no confirmed text error, one question for the editors. The drawing conventions (points, colours, radii, connecting lines, where Spec Z is drawn) are display. Two mathematical remarks. (1) 'points on a curve over $\mathbb{C}$ are in bijection with prime ideals of its coordinate ring'. Review's reading: the knowl is written in the language of schemes (the prime spectrum of O_F 'visualized as a curve over Spec Z', 'Each prime ideal in Spec O_F is drawn as a point', the fibres of Spec O_F -> Spec Z), and the LMFDB's picture marks the generic point (0) on Spec O_F and on Spec Z (lmfdb/number_fields/draw_spectrum.py). For the points of an affine curve as a scheme the sentence is true and is Mathlib's definition of Spec: the points of Spec A are the prime ideals of A (PrimeSpectrum; (Spec A : Type) = PrimeSpectrum A by rfl), and an affine scheme is the spectrum of its coordinate ring (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.isoSpec). For the points of the curve in C^n (the LMFDB's own ag.variety is classical) the sentence is false as written: the zero ideal of the coordinate ring of an irreducible curve is prime and is no point; the true statement is with the maximal ideals, old 'are in bijection with prime ideals of its coordinate ring', new 'are in bijection with maximal ideals of its coordinate ring'. That statement is proved for every affine variety over every algebraically closed field (curves over C included): MvPolynomial.bijective_zeroLocusToMaximalSpectrum. For an ideal I of K[X_s : s in sigma], sigma finite, the map MvPolynomial.zeroLocusToMaximalSpectrum, sending a point x of V(I) to the kernel of the evaluation at x on K[X] / I, is a bijection onto MaximalSpectrum (K[X] / I); with I the defining ideal of a variety, K[X] / I is its coordinate ring. The proof uses Mathlib's Nullstellensatz MvPolynomial.isMaximal_iff_eq_vanishingIdeal_singleton and comaps along K[X] -> K[X] / I. So both readings are formalised; which wording the editors want is recorded as a question for them, not as an error. (2) 'the fibers of the map Spec O_F -> Spec Z, where the fiber above a rational prime p is the set of primes of O_F lying above p': PrimeSpectrum.preimage_comap_singleton_eq_primesOver, for any R -> S the preimage of a point P of Spec R under Spec S -> Spec R is {Q | Q in P.primesOver S} (Mathlib's Ideal.primesOver, the primes lying over P). NumberField.range_fiberι_spec_map_algebraMap_int: for the ring of integers O_F (any field F : Type) and the point (p) of Spec Z (p a prime number, or p = 0 for the generic point), the underlying set of the scheme-theoretic fibre (Mathlib's AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.fiber, embedded by fiberι, through Scheme.Hom.range_fiberι) is that set. (3) The twin itself, Algebra.IsSexticTwin.nonempty_algEquiv_seventhCyclotomicTwin: every finite separable (etale) twin of K is isomorphic to Q x Q(sqrt(-7)) x Q(zeta_7 + zeta_7^-1), written Q x Q⟮seventhCyclotomicSqrtNegSeven⟯ x Q⟮zeta 7 Q K + (zeta 7 Q K)^-1⟯ (Tau Ceti's Gaussian period 1 + 2(z + z^2 + z^4), square -7). The factors correspond to the orbits {2}, {1, 3}, {0, 4, 5} of (0 4 5)(1 3). False as written: in the irreducible Sym²(ℂ²), diag(a₁,a₂) acts on e₁², e₁e₂ by a₁², a₁a₂, so two lines carry dominant integer weights (2,0) and (1,1); and A ↦ |det A| is irreducible with no such tuple. Something that is strictly weaker is partial."): corrected. False as written: the 1-dimensional (so irreducible) representations g ↦ |det g|^s, s ∈ ℂ, are uncountably many and have no integer highest weight, so there is no such bijection over all finite-dimensional irreducibles. - `specialfunction.poincare` [Modular forms › Classical]: Round AF. The only gap left by the sweep of 2026-11-06 was the generation claim for multipliers of infinite order (mf.multipliersystem allows any character G -> S^1), which rested on the named hypotheses of span_poincareSeries_eq_multiplierCuspSpace (finite dimension of S_k(G, v), expansions without constant term at s, integrable Petersson integrands). All three are now proved for every multiplier v on a subgroup G of finite index. (1) S_k(G, v) is finite-dimensional (finiteDimensional_multiplierCuspSpace, also registered as an instance): for f0 != 0 in S_k(G, v), the norm F0 = prod over the cosets q of f0|_k q.out^-1 transforms under all of SL(2, Z) by a character c of absolute value 1 (exists_prod_slash), and c^12 = 1 by S^4 = 1 and S^3 T S T S = T^-1 (pow_twelve_eq_one); the partial product g0 over the cosets other than G transforms under G by c / v, so H = g0 F0^11 transforms by 1 / v, and f -> f H is an injective linear map (identity theorem, H != 0) into cusp forms of trivial multiplier on G, finite-dimensional by Tau Ceti's finiteDimensional_cuspForm_finiteIndex. (2) y^k |f(z)|^2 is bounded on H for f in S_k(G, v) (exists_norm_petersson_le): the translates f|_k gamma are quasi-periodic, F(z + h) = c F(z) with |c| = 1 (exists_slash_vadd_eq_mul), hence O(e^(-2 pi kappa y / h)) at i infinity (isBigO_exp_of_vadd_eq_mul, through the removable singularity isBoundedAtImInfty_of_tendsto_mul_qParam of GrowthCondition.lean, the mf.growth_condition file, which CuspDecay.lean imports), and Mathlib's ModularGroup.exists_bound_of_subgroup_invariant applies; so the Petersson integrands are integrable on sets of finite measure (integrableOn_petersson_of_mem_multiplierCuspSpace) and against e^(2 pi i m z / w) on the strip. (3) The expansion at s without constant term is Mathlib's q-expansion of f|_k gamma_s (period w). Hence span_poincareSeries_eq_multiplierCuspSpace_of_finiteIndex (named ..._of_finiteIndex_subgroup until the fold of 2026-11-12): for G of finite index, k >= 3, s = gamma_s(oo) of width w and v(h) = (+-1)^k on G_s, the P_m (m >= 1) span S_k(G, v), with no hypothesis on the order of v. Every other sentence was proved before (the round of 31 October: independence of the representatives, dependence on gamma_s via poincareTerm_mul_T_zpow and poincareTerm_neg; the round of 31 October: cusp forms for n >= 1; the round of 1 November: convergence and holomorphy for every n). The three recorded corrections stand (v(h) = (+-1)^k on G_s for 'v trivial on G_s'; the factor (+-1)^k e^(-2 pi i n m / w) for the choice of gamma_s, so a sign ambiguity for odd k; only the P^n with n >= 1 are cusp forms and generate), fixable texts under the ruling of 2026-11-11, so the knowl is formalised. Superseded and removed by the fold of 2026-11-12: the committed finite-order theorem that had the name span_poincareSeries_eq_multiplierCuspSpace_of_finiteIndex, and its FiniteDimensional instance (PoincareSpanFiniteOrder.lean); the new instance, spelt Module.Finite in round AF because its generated name clashed with that one's, is now spelt FiniteDimensional. Review AF3 (2026-11-12): checked the finite dimension (c is a character of SL(2, Z) with c^12 = 1, H = g0 F0^11 has multiplier 1/v, and f -> f H is injective into the cusp forms of weight 12 k [SL(2, Z) : G] and trivial multiplier on G), the bound on y^k |f|^2, the integrability, and the hypotheses: every cusp of a finite-index G has a width, and hv holds for v = 1 in even weight, for a nebentypus with chi(-1) = (-1)^k at the cusp oo of Gamma_0(N), and for characters of infinite order (Gamma(2) = {+-1} x F_2 with F_2 free on (1 2; 0 1) and (1 0; 2 1): v(-1) = (-1)^k, v = 1 on the first generator, an irrational angle on the second). The theorem has the knowl's generality (any G of finite index, any multiplier, k >= 3, any cusp). Added by the review, PoincareCuspRepresentative.lean: the recorded correction of the last sentence also states that replacing s by g s multiplies the series by conj(v(g)) (the round of 31 October's review: 'not formalised'), and the dependence on gamma_s was proved only for the terms. Now proved for the series: poincareSeries_mul_T_zpow, poincareSeries_neg, exists_poincareSeries_eq_of_smul_infty_eq (any gamma'_s with gamma'_s(oo) = gamma_s(oo) gives (+-1)^k e^(-2 pi i n m / w) times the series), poincareSeries_eq_of_smul_infty_eq (equal for w | n and even k) and poincareSeries_coe_mul (P(z; g gamma_s) = conj(v(g)) P(z; gamma_s) for g in G). Links: finiteDimensional_multiplierCuspSpace (an input, not a claim of the knowl), span_range_poincareCuspForm_eq_top (the trivial multiplier) and the term-level poincareTerm_mul_T_zpow were replaced by hasSum_poincareSeries_of_three_le (the series converges for every n, so the tsum is never a junk value) and the two series-level dependence theorems.
- `st_group.components` [Groups › Sato–Tate groups]: Every sentence is now proved. A Sato-Tate group is a compact Lie group: its image in GL_d(C) under Unitary.toUnits is closed, hence an embedded Lie subgroup by Tau Ceti's closed-subgroup theorem (isEmbeddedLieSubgroup); it is therefore locally path-connected (an instance, transported along the homeomorphism onto that image), so G0 is open of finite index. The components are the cosets g G0 (connectedComponent_eq_smul, from Mathlib's smul_connectedComponent; connectedComponentsEquivQuotient is the bijection ConnectedComponents G = G / G0), G0 is normal (Tau Ceti), there are finitely many (finite_connectedComponents) and their number is the order of the component group, numComponents = Nat.card (G / G0) (card_connectedComponents; also numComponents_pos). 'Need not be connected' is proved for the LMFDB group N(U(1)) (not_connectedSpace_satoTateNU1: its diagonal matrices form a clopen set containing 1 but not J). No Tau Ceti main overlap found (checkout of 10-28 and a code search).
- `st_group.embedding` [Groups › Sato–Tate groups]: Round AO (AO3_sato_tate_lie), 2026-11-23; reviewed (review/AO3_sato_tate_lie.md): formalised, confirmed. Formalised at the pin; nothing of Tau Ceti's main is used. Was partial (AI9z, the user's ruling of 2026-11-13: 'isomorphic as real Lie groups' needs Lie groups; tracker v63, medium): 'a Lie group structure on Sato-Tate groups (a manifold structure on the subgroup itself; LeanBridge has only the predicate that they are embedded Lie subgroups of GL_d(C)), so that the two example groups, isomorphic as topological groups, are isomorphic as real Lie groups'. Partly stale: Cartan's closed-subgroup theorem and automatic smoothness are at the pin, and LeanBridge proves isEmbeddedLieSubgroup; what was missing, a manifold structure on the subgroup itself, is built here (RealLieGroup.lean). Every Sato-Tate group G is a real Lie group, by instances for its own topology (the subspace topology of U(d), the one of haarProb and of the connected components; checked in the default context): ChartedSpace G.LieModel G.toSubgroup and LieGroup 𝓘(ℝ, G.LieModel) ∞ G.toSubgroup, modelled on its Lie algebra SatoTateGroup.LieModel (Tau Ceti's lieSubalgebraOfSubgroup of its image K in GL_d(C)), of dimension G.realDimension (finrank_lieModel, by rfl: LMFDB st_group.real_dimension). The charts are those of Cartan's embedded-Lie-subgroup structure on K (embeddedLieSubgroupData, from nonempty_embeddedLieSubgroupData_lieSubalgebraOfSubgroup_of_isClosed: a Lie group for the subspace topology of K, with smooth immersive inclusion into GL_d(C)) pulled back along the homeomorphism G -> K (isLocalHomeomorph_toUnits, Tau Ceti's IsLocalHomeomorph.chartedSpaceComap, as Tau Ceti does for universal covers); multiplication and inversion are smooth as they lie over those of K (lieGroupAux). No other ChartedSpace or LieGroup instance on these types exists in Mathlib, Tau Ceti or LeanBridge. Automatic smoothness (Tau Ceti's TauCeti.Lie.contMDiff_of_continuous_monoidHom) makes every isomorphism of topological groups between Sato-Tate groups a diffeomorphism (diffeomorphOfContinuousMulEquiv, coe_diffeomorphOfContinuousMulEquiv: smooth both ways, and its underlying map is the group isomorphism). The knowl's example, from round AI: the Sato-Tate groups {(u, u zeta, u zeta^2)} (regularCubeRoots) and {(u, u, u zeta)} (reflectionCubeRoots) of weight 1 and degree 6 in USp(6), both U(1) x C_3 with identity component U(1)_3 (LMFDB identity component 1.6.N.1.1a, lmfdb/sato_tate_groups/main.py), are isomorphic as real Lie groups (regularCubeRootsDiffeomorph, a diffeomorphism whose underlying map is the group isomorphism regularCubeRootsEquiv: coe_regularCubeRootsDiffeomorph) and have different distributions of characteristic polynomials (charpolyDistribution_regularCubeRoots_ne). The rest as in AI4: charpolyDistribution, conj, charpolyDistribution_conj, moment_charpolyCoeff_conj ('(up to conjugacy)'). Not checked, as before: the labels 1.6.N.3.* of the two groups in the LMFDB's database (only 1.6.N.1.1a = U(1)_3 is in the LMFDB source). No text error. Checks (review): lake build; #lint clean; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; dup_decls 0 clashes; names new in the three trees.
- `st_group.identity_component` [Groups › Sato–Tate groups]: The gap is closed: finiteIndex_connectedComponentOfOne proves that G0 has finite index in every Sato-Tate group. The route: the image of G in GL_d(C) (units of the matrix algebra with the L-infinity operator norm, as in realDimension) is closed, so an embedded Lie subgroup by Tau Ceti's closed-subgroup theorem (isEmbeddedLieSubgroup, 'as a compact Lie group'); a closed subgroup of a Lie group is locally path-connected (Subgroup.locallyPathConnectedSpace_of_isClosed, from the charts of the closed-subgroup data); G is homeomorphic to its image (a continuous bijection from a compact space), so G0 is open (isOpen_connectedComponentOfOne) and of finite index in the compact G. G0 is Mathlib's connectedComponentOfOne (also packaged as the Sato-Tate group identityComponent, itself a compact Lie group), normal by Tau Ceti's instance, and G/G0 is componentGroup. The operator-norm topology equals the entrywise one only by unfolding (Tau Ceti's warning), so all statements about G use the entrywise topology and the other is selected inside proofs.
- `st_group.index` [Groups › Sato–Tate groups]: Proved that the identity component of a compact real Lie group (Mathlib's LieGroup I n G for any real model with corners I and any n, with CompactSpace G) has finite index: the model space is homeomorphic to the convex range of I, hence locally path-connected, so G is, its identity component is open (Subgroup.isOpen_connectedComponentOfOne, for any topological group charted on a real model), and an open subgroup of a compact group has finite index. Normality is Tau Ceti's instance, and 'index = cardinality of G/G^0' is the definition of Subgroup.index (Subgroup.index_eq_card); every sentence of the knowl is covered.
- `st_group.moment_matrix` [Groups › Sato–Tate groups]: Formalised on the user's ruling of 2026-11-11 ("Something that has a different but fixable definition isn't partial. Something that is strictly weaker is partial."): convention. The order of the irreducible characters of O(d) in even weight is not fixed by the knowl (its highest weight does not separate χ from χ ⊗ det); LeanBridge orders them by Weyl's partitions, with Weyl's classification proved in full. The question is in the LMFDB issues.
- `st_group.moment_simplex` [Groups › Sato–Tate groups]: Formalised on the user's ruling of 2026-11-11 ("Something that has a different but fixable definition isn't partial. Something that is strictly weaker is partial."): convention. momentSimplexRow is the set of exponent vectors of weighted degree 2k with nonzero mixed moment; the order within a row is not recorded, and the knowl gives it two inconsistent ways (with the true vectors (0,1), (2,0) the example is ascending lexicographic, not reverse lexicographic). Contrary to the sweep, the vanishing of the moments of odd weighted degree is proved, but only under the extra hypothesis −1 ∈ G (mixedMoment_eq_zero_of_odd), which a SatoTateGroup need not satisfy. The literal claim that a moment with an odd term i·eᵢ vanishes is false for g ≥ 3: E[a₁a₃] = 1 on USp(6), as Λ³V contains V. The wording is in the LMFDB issues.
- `st_group.moments` [Groups › Sato–Tate groups]: Formalised on the user's ruling of 2026-11-11 ("Something that has a different but fixable definition isn't partial. Something that is strictly weaker is partial."), with the missing claim proved in round AC: convention. aᵢ is the coefficient of x^(d − i), as in the data. The missing claim, that the moment sequences are integer sequences, is proved for every Sato–Tate group: E[aᵢⁿ] = (−1)^(in) dim((⋀ⁱℂ^d)^(⊗n))^G (moment_charpolyCoeff_eq_finrank_invariants), likewise for the eᵢ, for the power sums sᵢ through Newton's identities (exists_moment_powerSum_eq_intCast), and for every integer polynomial in the aᵢ (exists_expectation_aeval_eq_intCast). 'Or any random variable' is false (E|a₁| = 8/(3π) on SU(2)), and binomial convolutions compute moments of sums, not products. The wording is in the LMFDB issues.
- `st_group.probabilities` [Groups › Sato–Tate groups]: Round AO (AO3_sato_tate_lie), 2026-11-23; reviewed (review/AO3_sato_tate_lie.md): formalised, confirmed. Formalised at the pin; nothing of Tau Ceti's main is used. Was partial (tracker v63, hard): 'Serre's Proposition 8.4.3.3 (a real-analytic function on a connected component of a compact Lie group is constant or has null level sets) and the finiteness of the components'. The finiteness half of that blocker was stale (SatoTateGroup.finite_connectedComponents, Components.lean; finiteIndex_connectedComponentOfOne, LieGroup.lean). Serre's proposition is now proved, for every LeanBridge SatoTateGroup (so every LMFDB group) with its normalised Haar measure TauCeti.haarProb, and every random variable that is a polynomial in the matrix entries (SatoTateGroup.IsEntryPolynomial: the a_i in either indexing, isEntryPolynomial_charpolyCoeff and isEntryPolynomial_coeff_charpoly, and the trace). Route, which needs neither the zero set of a several-variable analytic function nor Haar measure in charts (the pin has neither; Tau Ceti's MvPolynomial.volume_setOfPred_eval_eq_zero is for polynomials, and exponential coordinates are transcendental): (1) Cartan's closed-subgroup theorem at the pin, read in GL_d(C) (Subgroup.exists_mem_nhds_one_forall_exists_expUnit_eq, ClosedSubgroupExp.lean, from exists_mem_nhds_one_iff_exists_mem_lieSubalgebraOfSubgroup_and_lieExp_eq_of_isClosed, lieExp_eq_expUnit and unitsLieAlgebraLieEquiv_symm_mem_lieSubalgebraOfSubgroup_iff): the one-parameter subgroups t -> exp(tX) of G (SatoTateGroup.expOneParameter, for X in SatoTateGroup.matrixLieAlgebra) generate an open subgroup, which contains G^0 (SatoTateGroup.connectedComponentOfOne_le_closure_iUnion_range_expOneParameter, OneParameter.lean; the review replaced the author's existential exists_expOneParameter by these named objects); (2) along them a polynomial in the entries is real-analytic in t (Matrix.analyticAt_eval_mul_exp_smul_mul, from NormedSpace.exp_analytic); (3) a real-analytic function on R vanishes identically or at finitely many points of [0,1] (AnalyticOnNhd.forall_eq_zero_or_volume_eq_zero, AnalyticLevelSet.lean); (4) Fubini/Tonelli on [0,1] x K and left invariance: saturating a closed set along a curve does not decrease its measure when every line meets it everywhere or in a null set (measure_le_measure_setOf_forall_mul_mem), iterated over words in the curves, plus Lindeloef (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable) for countably many words: almost every g with F g = z has F(hg) = z for all h in the generated subgroup (MeasureTheory.measure_setOf_eq_sdiff_setOf_forall_mem_closure_eq_zero; for Sato-Tate groups SatoTateGroup.IsEntryPolynomial.measure_setOf_eq_sdiff_eq_zero); (5) on each connected component F is identically z or = z on a null set (MeasureTheory.forall_eq_or_measure_inter_connectedComponent_eq_zero, SatoTateGroup.IsEntryPolynomial.forall_eq_or_measure_eq_zero), and, the components being finitely many cosets of G^0 of measure 1/#components (Subgroup.index_mul_measure), mu{F = z} is the proportion of the connected components on which F is identically z (MeasureTheory.measureReal_setOf_eq_eq_card_div_card, SatoTateGroup.IsEntryPolynomial.measureReal_setOf_eq). Knowl claims: Pr[a_i = n] := mu{a_i = n} (SatoTateGroup.probability, committed); 'a rational number equal to the proportion of connected components of G on which a_i is identically equal to n' (probability_eq_card_div_card, stated as the cast of a rational number, the ratio of Nat.card of the components ConnectedComponents G on which a_i is identically n to Nat.card of all); 'necessarily zero unless n is one of a finite set of integers' (finite_setOf_probability_ne_zero); 'Pr[a_i = n] = 0 implies that {g : a_i(g) = n} has measure zero' (probability_eq_zero_iff); 'this set need not be empty' (on U(1) = LMFDB 1.2.B.1.1a, SatoTateGroup.torusU1: probability_torusU1_one_zero and nonempty_setOf_charpolyCoeff_torusU1_one_eq_zero, a_1 = 0 at diag(i, -i)); '(unless G is finite)' (probability_eq_zero_iff_of_finite). Text: the knowl writes the characteristic polynomial as sum a_i x^i, while SatoTateGroup.probability uses the LMFDB's a_i = coefficient of x^(d-i); this correction is already recorded (lmfdb-knowl-edits-ai0b.md, for the editors to decide, with the typo 'Lecture's'), so the author's variant wording is not a new record. The general results hold for every coefficient of the characteristic polynomial and for the trace (isEntryPolynomial_coeff_charpoly, isEntryPolynomial_trace with IsEntryPolynomial.measureReal_setOf_eq), so the proportion formula holds in the literal reading and in the convention of the LMFDB's pages of mu(n), n odd, which use a_1 = +tr (recorded in ai0/ai0b). The LMFDB computes every probability it displays as a number of components over the number of components (lmfdb/sato_tate_groups/main.py: zvector[k]/n in degrees 4 and 6, counts/n in degrees 1 and 2), the formula proved here; tested by hand on 1.2.B.1.1a (U(1): all 0), 1.2.B.2.1a (N(U(1)): Pr[a_1 = 0] = 1/2), 0.1.2 (Pr[a_1 = 1] = Pr[a_1 = -1] = 1/2) and 0.1.1 (Pr[a_1 = -1] = 1 here, the page shows Pr[a_1 = 1] = 1, the recorded sign convention). Checks (review): lake build; #lint clean; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; dup_decls 0 clashes; names new in Mathlib, Tau Ceti (pin and main) and LeanBridge; every simp-list entry needed.
- `st_group.real_dimension` [Groups › Sato–Tate groups]: `SatoTateGroup.realDimension`, `TauCeti.Lie.nonempty_embeddedLieSubgroupData_lieSubalgebraOfSubgroup_of_isClosed`
- `st_group.subgroups` [Groups › Sato–Tate groups]: IsMaximalSubgroup is the knowl's definition word for word: H < G, H of finite index in G (relIndex not 0), and no K with H < K < G; H is any subgroup of the abstract group, not assumed closed. H0 = G0 is proved for every finite-index subgroup, closed or not (map_connectedComponentOfOne_eq_of_relIndex_ne_zero), so for maximal ones. The non-closed case uses the new general theorem LieGroup.connectedComponentOfOne_le_of_finiteIndex: a finite-index subgroup of a finite-dimensional real Lie group contains G0, since G0 is generated by exponentials (Tau Ceti) and exp X = exp(X/n)^n lies in the normal core of index n; it is applied to the image of G in GL_d(C), a Lie group by the closed-subgroup theorem (Subgroup.connectedComponentOfOne_le_of_isClosed), and transported to G (connectedComponentOfOne_le_of_finiteIndex). Concrete instance: U(1) is a maximal subgroup of N(U(1)) (index 2), as the LMFDB lists it.

'Or equivalently a nondegenerate alternating pairing': rootsOfUnity.exteriorSquareEquivPairing is a bijection between isomorphisms α : ⋀²M ≃ μ_N and nondegenerate alternating pairings M × M → μ_N (α ↦ (x, y) ↦ α(x ∧ y)), for M free of rank 2 over ℤ/N and μ_N in a separably (e.g. algebraically) closed field of characteristic prime to N; its core is LinearMap.injective_iff_separatingLeft (any commutative ring, through the trivialisation Module.Basis.exteriorSquareEquiv : ⋀²M ≃ R, x ∧ y ↦ det(x, y)) and bijective_iff_nondegenerate (|μ_N| = N). The L-function attached to a newform f in S_k^new(Gamma_0(N)) is now an AnalyticLFunction (see lfunction.conductor) whose sign is rootNumber = i^k lambda_N(f) (sign_analyticLFunction); for trivial nebentypus the weight is even (Tau Ceti's parity lemma) and lambda_N(f) is the Fricke eigenvalue, so the sign is i^{-k} times the eigenvalue of w_N (rootNumber_eq_I_zpow_neg_mul_frickeSign). As f is self-dual, the sign is (-1)^r with r the analytic rank (IsSelfDual.rootNumber_eq_neg_one_pow_analyticRank), so in weight 2, where i^{-2} = -1, the analytic rank is even exactly when w_N f = -f (even_analyticRank_iff_frickeSign_eq_neg_one), and odd exactly when w_N f = +f (odd_analyticRank_iff_frickeSign_eq_one, added by the AF2 review: the author left it as a composite with frickeSign_eq_one_or_neg_one; it replaces IsSelfDual.rootNumber_eq_neg_one_pow_analyticRank in the links, which stays linked under cmf.analytic_rank). Remaining gap, unchanged: '(induced by the corresponding involution on the modular curve X_0(N))' needs the involution w_N of X_0(N) and the action it induces on S_k(Gamma_0(N)); X_0(N) is partial (ag.modcurve.x0: no algebraic curve, and the compact Riemann surface Gamma_0(N)\H* of CompactRiemannSurface.lean has no w_N), so this is the same gap as cmf.atkin-lehner's last sentence. Previous category: Partially in Tau Ceti; the new links are LeanBridge's. 'omega_N' for w_N is a pure typo. No weight-2 newform is constructed in the trees; the general-weight statements apply to deltaNewform. AF2 review: the parenthetical is a claim, not an explanatory remark (ruling of 2026-11-06: an unproved fact the text states, remarks included, keeps a knowl partial; it is not a 'special case of' cross-reference): it says that the operator w_N on S_k(Gamma_0(N)) is induced by the involution of X_0(N), i.e. that f(z) (dz)^{k/2} pulls back to (f |_k W_N)(z) (dz)^{k/2} under z -> -1/(Nz) with the normalised W_N. AF3's ModularCurve/AtkinLehner.lean builds the involution of Gamma_0(N)\H* (atkinLehnerX0), not its action on forms. Blocked by: the involution w_N of the modular curve X_0(N) (ag.modcurve.x0; AF3 has it on the Riemann surface Gamma_0(N)\H*) and the identification of the action it induces on S_k(Gamma_0(N)) (holomorphic differentials for k = 2) with the Fricke operator. Not formalised: “(induced by the corresponding involution on the modular curve $X_0(N)$)”.

- `group.min_faithful_linear` [Groups › Abstract groups] (hard): Done: Round AG (AG1); partial, three of the four round-AF blockers closed and the fourth half closed. (i) 'there may be no faithful irreducible representations of G' (AF blocker i): closed. A finite abelian group with a faithful irreducible complex representation is cyclic (isCyclic_of_injective_of_isIrreducible: the representation is one-dimensional, Mathlib's IsIrreducible.finrank_eq_one_of_isMulCommutative, so G embeds in C^x, isCyclic_of_injective_ringHom), so a non-cyclic finite abelian group has irr_C(G) = -1 (irreducibleDegree_complex_eq_neg_one_of_not_isCyclic), in particular every Klein four-group, Mathlib's IsKleinFour class, e.g. Multiplicative (ZMod 2 x ZMod 2) (IsKleinFour.irreducibleDegree_complex_eq_neg_one); faithful representations exist (AF's toHomUnits_permMatrixHom_comp_injective). (ii) 'computing lin_C(G) requires finding linear combinations of characters that are faithful' (AF blocker ii): closed. G has a faithful matrix representation of degree n over C exactly when some N-combination psi = sum m_i chi_i of the rows of Tau Ceti's character table with sum m_i chi_i(1) = n is faithful, psi(g) = n only at g = 1 (exists_injective_iff_exists_nsmul_sum: forward by Tau Ceti's character_eq_sum_nsmul_irreducibleCharacter, backward by direct sums of the row representations, FDRep.exists_character_eq_sum_nsmul, and a basis, FDRep.exists_representation_character_eq; faithfulness by AF's Representation.injective_iff_character_eq_character_one), so lin_C(G) is the least degree of a faithful N-combination (linearDegree_complex_eq). (iii) the Galois-orbit sentence for k = R (AF blocker iii): closed. FDRep.realGaloisConjugates (sigma o chi, sigma in Gal(C/R)) = {chi, conj o chi} (realGaloisConjugates_eq); FDRep.realCharacter, their sum, is chi when chi is real valued and chi + conj chi otherwise (realCharacter_eq_of_conj_comp_eq, realCharacter_eq_add); for irreducible chi it is a real valued character, of a direct sum (exists_real_character_eq_realCharacter), faithful iff chi is (realCharacter_faithful_iff, from the new FDRep.sum_faithful_iff for any set s of Aut(C)-conjugates of chi containing chi, s a subset of FDRep.galoisConjugates and hence finite, through FDRep.realGaloisConjugates_subset_galoisConjugates; the argument of AF's rationalCharacter_faithful_iff, which is the case s = galoisConjugates), and each summand is faithful iff chi is (faithful_iff_of_mem_realGaloisConjugates); k = Q was AF's (FDRep.rationalCharacter_faithful_iff, FDRep.algEquiv_comp_faithful_iff). (iv) the Schur-index sentence (AF blocker iv): half closed. Upper bound, in general over Q: for an irreducible complex representation with character chi and Schur index m = FDRep.schurIndex Q (the LMFDB's least [E : Q(chi)]), m times the irreducible rational character psi = sum of the distinct Galois conjugates is the character of a representation over Q (FDRep.exists_character_eq_schurIndex_mul_rationalCharacter): restriction of scalars of a realisation over E with [E : Q(chi)] = m (FDRep.exists_character_eq_trace, Tau Ceti's LinearMap.trace_restrictScalars), Tr_{E/Q}(x) = [E : K] Tr_{K/Q}(x) for x in K (IntermediateField.trace_inclusion, by sums of roots of the minimal polynomial), and Tr_{Q(chi)/Q}(chi(g)) = psi(g) (FDRep.sum_algHom_characterField_eq_rationalCharacter: embeddings of Q(chi) extend to Aut(C), LeanBridge's exists_algEquiv_apply_eq_of_countable). The knowl's example completed (AF's 'or at least'): the two-dimensional character chi of Q8 is rational (AF's isRational_two), faithful (AF's injective_twoDimHom), not the character of any representation with matrix entries in Q (QuaternionGroup.not_exists_trace_eq_twoDimHom: it would be faithful of degree 2, against AF's not_injective_rat_two), while 2 chi is, by left multiplication on the rational quaternions Q^4 (QuaternionGroup.ratQuaternionHom, trace_ratQuaternionHom). Blocked by (exact): (1) the lower bound of the Schur-index sentence over Q: if c psi is the character of a representation over Q then m <= c (indeed m | c; Isaacs, Character Theory of Finite Groups, Cor. 10.2), so that m is the least number of copies; missing theory: the simple component of Q[G] at the Galois orbit of chi as M_r(D), D a division algebra with centre Q(chi) and index m, whose maximal subfields are splitting fields of degree m realising chi (Tau Ceti has central simple algebras, maximal subfields and splitting, TauCeti.Algebra.CentralSimple and BrauerGroup, but nothing linking them to group algebras and characters); (2) the same sentence over k = R, which the LMFDB also tabulates (irrR_degree, linR_degree): m_R(chi) copies of the real orbit sum afforded over R and no fewer; route clear but not done: positivity of FDRep.schurIndex R (realisation over the top intermediate field C), restriction of scalars C -> R with Tr_{C/R}(z) = z + conj z for the upper bound, and for the lower bound a real representation with character chi realises V (FDRep.nonempty_iso_of_character_eq; Tau Ceti's frobeniusSchurIndicator_eq_one_iff_isRealizableOverReal). Judgement call (author): read as a possibility claim ('may be needed', exemplified) plus the role of the Schur index (m copies always suffice, proved), the sentence would be covered, as the AF review's 'or at least the knowl's example completed' allows, and the knowl would be formalised; left partial under the ruling of 2026-11-04 (when in doubt, partial) because 'the Schur index plays a role' most naturally means 'exactly m copies are needed'. Review (AG1): partial, confirmed. Blockers i-iii of round AF are closed as stated there (i: concrete instances checked, Multiplicative (ZMod 2 x ZMod 2) and DihedralGroup 2; iii: k = R as tabulated by the LMFDB); iv is half closed. FDRep.schurIndex is the LMFDB's (group.representation.schur_index: least [E : Q(chi)] over Q(chi) <= E <= C realising V), equal to the classical multiplicity form only by the missing lower bound, and the upper bound is a genuine restriction-of-scalars theorem, not true by definition. The Schur-index sentence is read with the knowl's 'For fields R of characteristic 0, these values can be characterized in terms of the character table of G': over k = Q and R that characterisation needs the characters afforded over k to be exactly the N-combinations of the m_k(chi) psi_chi, so the sentence states that exactly m copies are needed (the lower bound), over both fields the LMFDB tabulates. Blocked by: the lower bound, that m_k(chi) divides the multiplicity of chi in every character afforded over k (Isaacs, Cor. 10.2), for k = Q (missing theory: the simple components of Q[G] as matrix algebras over division algebras of index m) and for k = R, where the upper bound (m_R(chi) copies of the real orbit sum afforded over R) is missing too. Whether the upper bound and the example are enough is question 1 of review/AG1_linear_groups.md; under either answer the knowl stays partial for now (the real case). Review changes: FDRep.sum_faithful_iff restated for any set s of conjugates inside galoisConjugates (realCharacter_faithful_iff is then a one-line application, and so would be AF's rationalCharacter_faithful_iff); FDRep.exists_character_eq_zero became FDRep.character_trivial_fin_zero (witness named); layout and simp-only fixes. Not done either (optional): the Schur index of the example, m_Q(chi) = 2 for Q8 (route: irreducibility of twoDimHom, Brauer's realisation over Q(zeta_4) of degree 2, and the new upper bound with not_exists_trace_eq_twoDimHom for m >= 2). Supporting declarations not linked (limit of eight): AF's toHomUnits_permMatrixHom_comp_injective, Representation.injective_iff_character_eq_character_one, FDRep.rationalCharacter_faithful_iff, FDRep.algEquiv_comp_faithful_iff, QuaternionGroup.three_le_linearDegree_rat, QuaternionGroup.isRational_two, QuaternionGroup.injective_twoDimHom; new exists_injective_iff_exists_nsmul_sum, irreducibleDegree_complex_eq_neg_one_of_not_isCyclic, FDRep.exists_real_character_eq_realCharacter, FDRep.faithful_iff_of_mem_realGaloisConjugates, FDRep.sum_faithful_iff, QuaternionGroup.not_exists_trace_eq_twoDimHom, FDRep.exists_character_eq_trace, IntermediateField.trace_inclusion. Recorded text errors unchanged (finite G; 'k-values' typo).

- `lattice.additively_indecomposable` [Groups › Lattices] (hard): Done: Round AO (AO2_lattices), 2026-11-23; reviewed (review/AO2_lattices.md): partial, confirmed; no new Lean (the optional claim of the round was not attempted). Proved (round S2): IsAdditivelyIndecomposable (positive definite, nonzero, the form not a sum of two nonzero symmetric positive semidefinite integral forms) and IsAdditivelyIndecomposable.isOrthogonallyIndecomposable. Nothing in the three trees or Tau Ceti's main (checkout 62bbc05) proves the rest; the tracker's blocker is not stale. Route for the unimodular converse, checked: if B = B_1 + B_2 on a unimodular L, B_i integral, positive semidefinite and nonzero, then f = B^-1 B_1 is an integral endomorphism of L (unimodularity), self-adjoint for B, with 0 <= B(fx, x) <= B(x, x); its eigenvalues are real and in [0, 1] and its characteristic polynomial lies in Z[t], so a monic factor without the roots 0 and 1 would have a nonzero integer constant term of absolute value < 1; hence f^2 = f and L = f(L) + (1 - f)(L) is an orthogonal splitting with both summands nonzero. The converse fails for A_2: (2,1;1,2) = (1,1;1,1) + (1,0;0,1), and A_2 is orthogonally indecomposable since a splitting <a> + <b> would have ab = 3 with a, b >= 2. Blocked by: (1) the unimodular converse (route above; Mathlib has the spectral theorem for symmetric operators, the transfer from the lattice and the integrality argument are missing); (2) the A_2 counterexample to the converse (short, not done); (3) the Mordell-Ko classification of the additively indecomposable lattices of rank <= 8 (Z, E_6, E_7, E_8), out of scope. Difficulty: hard.

- `lfunction.central_character` [L-functions] (hard): Done: Round AF (AF2). The gap is unchanged by item 2 of the brief: the knowl asserts that every L-function has Euler factors 1 + a_p x + ... + (-1)^d chi(p) x^d for a Dirichlet character chi mod N, so with lfunction read as AnalyticLFunction this must hold for every AnalyticLFunction, and it is not among the axioms and not known to follow from them (they only fix the degrees of the Euler factors, d exactly for p not dividing N, with nothing tying the top coefficients at different primes). The predicate, its uniqueness by Dirichlet's theorem and the vanishing at p | N are proved (CentralCharacter.lean). New: for the analytic L-function of a newform (built in this round, see lfunction.conductor) the nebentypus is the central character, isCentralCharacter_analyticLFunction: the T^2 coefficient of the Euler factor 1 - a_p T + chi(p) T^2 is (-1)^2 chi(p). AF2 review: confirmed partial; the existence for every analytic L-function is not a consequence of the axioms and is not known (it follows from the expected automorphy of every L-function), so it stays partial as a conjecture would. Side finding for the editors: 'L_p(x) = 1 + a_p x + ...' has the opposite sign to the Dirichlet coefficient a_p (cmf.lfunction writes 1 - a_p p^{-s}; for d = 1 the term a_p x is -chi(p) x); it does not affect the central character. Blocked by: the existence, for every analytic L-function of degree d and conductor N, of a Dirichlet character chi mod N with top Euler coefficients (-1)^d chi(p) (not implied by the class's axioms; open). Not formalised: “An L-function has an Euler product of the form $L(s) = \prod_p L_p(p^{-s})^{-1}$ where $L_p(x) = 1 + a_p x + \ldots + (-1)^d \chi(p) x^d$. The character $\chi$ is a Dirichlet character mod $N$”.
