Even corrected it is a claim about every arithmetic L-function (algebraic Dirichlet coefficients) that is not known: a Maass cusp form of eigenvalue 1/4 + r^2, r != 0, with algebraic Hecke eigenvalues would give an AnalyticLFunction with algebraic coefficients and poles at -2n -+ ir, and that none exists is open; it holds for motivic L-functions, of which LeanBridge has no general notion. Also recorded (AF2 review): 'the L-function must have zeros at poles of the gamma factors' fails for zeta at s = 0; the corrected 'at the poles of the gamma factors at which the completed L-function has no pole' is what mem_trivialZeros_of_mem_gammaPoles and gammaPoles_diff_zero_subset_trivialZeros prove (fixable text, ruling of 2026-11-11). '(except possibly from Riemann zeta-function factors)' is read as the class's axiom that Lambda is holomorphic off {0, 1}, as for lfunction.completed. Blocked by: the last sentence, corrected to integers in the arithmetic normalization, for every arithmetic L-function (open in general: it excludes algebraic Maass eigenvalues; true for motivic L-functions, which have no notion in the trees). Not formalised: “For arithmetic L-functions, the poles are at certain negative integers.”

The review asked which reading 'Let K be an imaginary quadratic field' and 'hyperbolic 3-fold' should get (review/AL2_picard_group.md); the lead settled it on the standing rulings and reported it to the user: finite volume is true for every K and proved only for class number one (a claim proved on part of the range where it is true is partial), and reading '3-fold' as 'the quotient' would drop the true orbifold structure (a correction must keep every true claim), so both stay blockers. Earlier record: Satake's theorem for Sp(2g, Z) at p is proved in every degree g >= 1, sorry-free: every double coset of the local Hecke algebra H_p is some T(delta; a) = Gamma diag(p^a, p^(delta - a)) Gamma with a_0 <= ... <= a_(g-1), 2 a_j <= delta (exists_eq_elementaryCoset, symplectic elementary divisors); the universal Satake map Omega (whose evaluations are the committed satakeMap) is invariant under the Weyl group W_g (satakeMapUniv_mem_weylInvariants, by a rank-one count on the parabolic subgroups of the simple roots), triangular for the dominance order (minors of the elementary divisors and of the Borel representatives), injective (satakeMapUniv_injective), with image the W_g-invariant Laurent polynomials supported on the cone 0 <= d_j <= delta (exists_satakeMapUniv_eq_iff), so that H_p is isomorphic to those invariants (satakeInvariantsHom_bijective). The cone algebra is integral over its invariants (the spinor monomials are roots of a W_g-invariant monic polynomial), so a character extends by lying over: every C-linear character of H_p not vanishing at T_0(p^2) is a Satake map (exists_satakeMap_eq_of_ne_zero), and an eigenform's eigenvalue at T_0(p^2) is nonzero. Hence the committed SatakeParametersExist and EulerFactorsWellDefined hold in every degree (satakeParametersExist, eulerFactorsWellDefined): every Siegel eigenform has Euler factors of both kinds at every prime, and they are unique (SiegelEigenform.isEulerFactor_unique; the coefficients of the spinor factor and of t^g times the standard factor, t = x_0^2 prod x_i, are W_g-invariant cone polynomials). So IsLift is a predicate on well-defined Euler factors, with the constant of degree 2 as a lift (isLift_const_two). Every Satake map value was checked against a brute-force enumeration of right cosets for g = 1, 2, 3 (W_g-invariance, triangularity, leading coefficient, scalar, rank-one counts, parabolic fibres); the review re-checked it with an independent enumeration (up to the 810,135 cosets of multiplier 8 in degree 3), including that the double cosets are indexed exactly by the dominant data, the integral structure constants of T(p)^2 and the committed degree-2 formulas. The interpretation stays as before: the knowl names neither the spinor nor the standard factor and says only products, so IsLift takes one kind of factor with shifts X -> p^a X and zeta factors, as the LMFDB's lift knowls need, at level Sp(2g, Z) (knowl imprecise, recorded in the ZV2 review). Not proved, and not needed here: that the Satake parameters of an eigenform form a single W_g-orbit. Matrix.det_mul_eq_sum_det_submatrix is a short helper (Cauchy-Binet expansion): Tau Ceti's main has the Cauchy-Binet formula TauCeti.det_mul_transpose_eq_sum_plucker_mul, which is not at the pin.

The Fourier-support clause (coefficients supported on positive definite T) is gone. The transport rests on new reindexing along an equivalence e of index types (UpperHalfSpaceReindex.lean): SiegelUpperHalfSpace.reindex for the half-space, SymplecticGroup.reindex for Sp(2g, R), Tau Ceti's Equiv.reindexGL for GL(g, C); reindex_smul and slash_comp_reindex make them compatible with the action and the slash operator. Nothing at the pins (Mathlib, Tau Ceti, LeanBridge; Tau Ceti main checked with one narrow GitHub query) reindexes Matrix.symplecticGroup or the half-space. isSiegelCuspForm_comp_reindex_iff proves that the clause says Phi(F |_k gamma) = 0 for every gamma in Sp(6, Q) in the Fin 3 coordinates, and val_reindex_finSumUnitEquiv_phiPoint shows that diag(tau, it) is the matrix with tau in its upper left 2 x 2 block and it in its last diagonal entry, as in mf.siegel.phi. isSiegelCuspForm_comp_reindex_congr shows the condition does not depend on the identification of Fin 3 with Fin 2 + Unit: two identifications differ by a permutation, which acts through the symplectic permutation matrix SymplecticGroup.ofPerm (ofPerm_smul). The clause order is unchanged, so IsMiyawakiLiftTypeII.standardEulerFactor_eq and .spinorEulerFactor_eq (SatakeEigenform) build as they were: the knowl's Euler factors hold at every Satake parameter of F, by Satake's theorem (round ZW). Every notion of the knowl is now captured: k even; f, g level-1 newforms; F a Siegel Hecke cusp eigenform of weight k on Sp(6, Z), that is a modular form, a cusp form and at every prime an eigenform with Satake parameters; and the standard and spinor Euler factors with the knowl's factorisations, which are those of one Satake point. The L-function identities are those of the Euler products. So the knowl is formalised as a predicate. The lift is conjectural, so no F is known to satisfy the predicate and no existence is asked. Not proved, and not needed for the predicate: the classical equivalence between the cusp condition and the earlier Fourier-support condition, in either direction. The definition is formalised (LinearMap.IsDualPairOfAlgebras), but no declaration relates dual pairs to Hopf algebras or group schemes. Tau Ceti's Cartier duality is an anti-equivalence of finite locally free bicommutative Hopf algebras with themselves, not of dual pairs with group schemes. As written the claim is also false: identities 1–4 give no antipode, and the functions on the monoid {0, 1} with its monoid algebra form a dual pair whose spectrum is a monoid scheme, not a group scheme (LMFDB issue). The extreme cases are not proved even for the model; only Σ h^{p,w−p} = d is (sum_hodgeVector). [...] For $t \in \Q$ with $t \neq 0,1$, the {{ KNOWL('hgm.motive', 'motive') }} $H(A,B,t)$ has the same Hodge vector as the family. For $t=1$, the motive $H(A,B,t)$ has degree $d-1$ or $d-2$, according to whether $w$ is even or odd: if $w$ is even, then the middle Hodge number $h^{w/2,w/2}$ drops by $1$, whereas if $w$ is odd, then the two middle Hodge numbers drop by $1$.”.

- `portrait.maass` [Modular forms › Maass] (hard): Done: Round AI (AI3_cmf_pictures, reviewed in review/AI3_cmf_pictures.md), made partial by the user's ruling of 2026-11-13: for 'If the Maass form f has squarefree level, then f takes only real values', the dichotomy that every Maass cusp newform is even or odd must be proved first; a statement that holds for the other forms only through a junk value does not count as the LMFDB's setting. Proved: the Moebius map mu(z) = (1 - iz)/(z - i) from the disc onto the upper half-plane and its values at -i, 0 and i (PortraitMoebius.lean); Maass cusp forms tend to 0 at the cusp, uniformly in x, that is on small discs tangent to the unit circle at the top (CuspDecay.lean, with the lower bound e^(-2x) <= |K_nu(x)| for large x of BesselKLowerBound.lean); the literal 'vanish near the top of the disk' is false for every nonzero form invariant under z -> z + 1, and the decay on horodiscs is the correct statement; and the normalised newform (first coefficient 1 in the cosine or sine expansion) of an even or odd Maass cusp newform is real-valued, at every level (IsMaassCuspNewform.conj_maassNormalisedNewform, where for a newform that is neither even nor odd the normalised newform is the junk value 0). Missing: every Maass cusp newform of weight 0 on Gamma_0(N) with trivial character is even or odd. The wording 'vanish near the top of the disk' is recorded for the editors.

- `sh.level` [Varieties › Shimura curves] (hard): Done: Round AJ (AJ3): still partial. 'The level of a Shimura curve is the level of the associated Eichler order': the level of an Eichler order is now unique when it exists (IsEichlerOrderOfLevel.unique) and exists exactly when every ramified prime divides discrd(O) exactly once (exists_isEichlerOrderOfLevel_iff), so the level is a well-defined function on the Eichler orders that have one; that every Eichler order has one is shimcurve.eichler's open claim (for the curves X(D,M;1) = X_0(D;M) of shimcurve.xdm1 the order is Eichler of level M by hypothesis, in Standard.lean's StandardShimuraCurve.eichler). The other blockers are stale: discrd(O) and disc(B) are formalised (shimcurve.disco and shimcurve.discb, round ZZ7), and 'Shimura curves themselves' is the modcurve.level case, as for sh.disc: the knowl defines an invariant of the curve through its data (the order O), with no theorem about the curve. Blocked by: shimcurve.eichler (for every prime p at which B ramifies and every Eichler order O of B, p divides discrd(O) exactly once). Difficulty: hard. Review (AJ3): partial confirmed. 'The associated Eichler order' is data of the curve (X(D,M;1) = X_0(D;M)), not a fact about it; the sentence needs the level of every Eichler order to exist, which is shimcurve.eichler's open claim (whose local-global half is on Tau Ceti main only, so it also waits for the bump).

- `shimcurve.eichler` [Varieties › Shimura curves] (hard): Done: Round AJ (AJ3): partial progress; the knowl's claim is not proved in general. New file EichlerOrderLevel.lean, for a quaternion algebra B over Q (central simple of dimension 4): (1) the index formula discrd(O) = [O' : O] discrd(O') for orders O <= O' (quaternionDiscrd_eq_relIndex_mul, from disc(O) = [O' : O]^2 disc(O') by Mathlib's AddSubgroup.relIndex_eq_abs_det and Tau Ceti's IsLattice.toAddSubgroup_eq_closure_range_extendOfIsLattice); (2) every order lies in a maximal order (exists_isMaximalQuaternionOrder_le: an order of least reduced discriminant above it), so Eichler orders exist (exists_isEichlerOrder_matrix for M_2(Q)); (3) an Eichler order is an order (IsEichlerOrder.isQuaternionOrder); (4) the level is unique when it exists (IsEichlerOrderOfLevel.unique); (5) the exact reduction of the knowl's claim: an Eichler order O has a level iff every prime at which B ramifies divides discrd(O) exactly once (exists_isEichlerOrderOfLevel_iff, as disc(B) is the product of the ramified primes); (6) so the claim holds whenever no prime ramifies (exists_isEichlerOrderOfLevel_of_discriminant_eq_one), for instance for M_2(Q) (QuaternionAlgebra.discriminant_matrix, exists_isEichlerOrderOfLevel_matrix), which also shows that the committed IsEichlerOrderOfLevel is not vacuous. By (1), for O = O_1 ∩ O_2 the claim is equivalent to discrd(O_1) = disc(B) together with [O_1 : O] prime to disc(B); the split primes play no role. Not proved: the claim for B ramified somewhere, the case of the LMFDB's Shimura curves (indefinite division algebras). Overlap with Tau Ceti main (not at the pin): TauCeti.IntegralOrder.IsOrder.exists_le_isMaximalOrder (TauCeti/RingTheory/IntegralOrder/Maximal.lean) proves the existence of maximal orders in general; (2) here is a short corollary of (1), to rebase at the bump. Main has nothing on Eichler orders, quaternion orders or their discriminants (searched: Eichler, quaternion order, discrd, reduced discriminant, type number). Text error, a reading the formalisation already uses: the knowl writes the reduced discriminant as disc(O), which shimcurve.disco uses for the discriminant (= discrd(O)^2), and does not define D. Old: "is of the form $\mathrm{disc}(O)=D\cdot M$ with $\gcd(D,M)=1$"; new: "is of the form $\operatorname{discrd}(O)=D\cdot M$ with $D=\operatorname{disc}(B)$ and $\gcd(D,M)=1$". Blocked by: for every prime p at which B ramifies and every Eichler order O of B, p divides discrd(O) exactly once; that is, the local theory at a ramified prime: the elements of the division algebra B ⊗ Q_p with integral reduced norm form its unique maximal Z_p-order (v_p ∘ nrd is an ultrametric valuation there), of reduced discriminant p, with the local-global correspondence for orders (O is maximal iff O ⊗ Z_p is maximal for every p, and discrd(O) is read prime by prime). The local maximal order is in neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti (pin or main); Tau Ceti main, not the pin, has the local-global dictionary for lattices (TauCeti.glueCompletions, TauCeti.eq_glueCompletions_iff, RingTheory/DedekindDomain/AdicValuation/Gluing.lean) and the uniqueness of the quaternion division algebra over a local field (TauCeti.QuaternionAlgebra.nonempty_algEquiv_of_hilbertSymbol_eq_neg_one), so a proof through them waits for the bump. Difficulty: hard. Review (AJ3): partial confirmed. The reduction is exact (exists_isEichlerOrderOfLevel_iff, both directions checked), the index formula and the existence of maximal orders are right, and the M_2(Q) case is proved; the claim for ramified B, the LMFDB's case, is open. Correction to the author's blocker, which said none of the local theory is on Tau Ceti main: its local-global half is there (above). The text error is new to the LMFDB issues: round T8's review noted it in review/T8_mix.md and the 11-06 sweep used it as a reading, but neither lmfdb-knowl-edits*.md nor the tracker's issues record it; the old text occurs once in the live text.

- `shimcurve.order` [Varieties › Shimura curves] (hard): Done: Round AM (AM2_quaternion_orders), progress; stays partial. Of the three gaps of round AJ's record, (a) is closed, (c) is proved by the example M2(Q), which does not settle it in the LMFDB's setting (the lead, on the 2026-11-13 nf.sextic_twin ruling: the example must be among the LMFDB's indefinite division algebras), and (b) remains a missing theory. Setting: B any central simple Q-algebra of dimension 4 ([Algebra.IsCentral Q B] [IsSimpleRing B], finrank Q B = 4), the knowl's 'quaternion algebra over Q' (shimcurve.quaternion_algebra); orders and maximal orders are the committed IsQuaternionOrder (a Z-subalgebra that is a Z-lattice) and IsMaximalQuaternionOrder (Maximal IsQuaternionOrder); the conjugate gamma O gamma^-1 by a unit gamma of B is O.map (MulSemiringAction.toAlgHom Z B (ConjAct.toConjAct gamma)), Mathlib's idiom for inner automorphisms; 'the number of B^x-conjugacy classes' is read, from the clause before it, as that of maximal orders (as in round AJ's review; the orders of all indices fall into infinitely many classes). (a) 'there is never a unique maximal order in a rational quaternion algebra': QuaternionAlgebra.not_existsUnique_isMaximalQuaternionOrder (not exists-unique maximal order, for every quaternion algebra over Q) and the stronger QuaternionAlgebra.exists_isMaximalQuaternionOrder_ne (every quaternion algebra over Q has two different maximal orders), so both readings of 'never unique' are proved. Proof (MaximalOrderConjugate.lean, 224 lines after the review): an isomorphism of Q-algebras maps orders to orders and maximal orders to maximal orders (IsQuaternionOrder.map, IsMaximalQuaternionOrder.map), so conjugates of maximal orders are maximal; no order is normalised by every unit (Subalgebra.exists_map_conj_ne): for gamma in the normaliser of O, conjugation maps O onto itself, so trd(gamma)^2/nrd(gamma), its trace on B, is an integer (the committed exists_sq_reducedTrace_div_eq_intCast), while in B = (a, b / Q) (the committed exists_nonempty_algEquiv_of_finrank_eq_four) the unit gamma = 1 + s i, s = 3 den(a), has trd(gamma)^2/nrd(gamma) = 4/(1 - a s^2) with a s^2 = 9 num(a) den(a) a nonzero integer, so 4 = z (1 - 9w), w != 0, is impossible (exists_units_forall_sq_reducedTrace_div_ne); hence a maximal order has a different conjugate, again maximal (IsMaximalQuaternionOrder.exists_ne). Maximal orders exist: every quaternion algebra over Q has an order (QuaternionAlgebra.exists_isQuaternionOrder: in (a, b / Q) the Z-span of 1, d1 i, d2 j, d1 d2 ij, d1, d2 the denominators of a, b, the range of the liftHom of a quaternion basis with integral structure constants, QuaternionAlgebra.Basis.isQuaternionOrder_range_liftHom), and every order lies in a maximal order (committed exists_isMaximalQuaternionOrder_le). This replaces round AJ's suggested route (conjugation by 1 + y/n and a limit) by a direct trace computation. (c) 'in many cases, there is exactly one B^x-conjugacy class' (a stated fact, ruling of 2026-11-13: proved by an example): M2(Q), a quaternion algebra over Q (indefinite, discriminant 1), has exactly one class (MatrixMaximalOrder.lean, 164 lines after the review): M2(Z) (the range of the entrywise map) is a maximal order (isMaximalQuaternionOrder_range_mapMatrix: for x in an order containing M2(Z), x_ij = tr(E_ji x) = trd(E_ji x) is an integer, reducedTrace_matrix: trd = tr on M2(Q)); every order O of M2(Q) lies in a conjugate of M2(Z) (exists_le_map_conj_range_mapMatrix: the Z-span L of the columns of the elements of O is a lattice of Q^2 stable under O, and for gamma with columns a Z-basis of L, gamma^-1 O gamma is integral, via Module.Basis.extendOfIsLattice_repr); so the maximal orders of M2(Q) are exactly the conjugates gamma M2(Z) gamma^-1 (isMaximalQuaternionOrder_iff_exists_eq_map_conj), and any two are conjugate (exists_eq_map_conj_of_isMaximalQuaternionOrder). Caveat on (c), kept from round AJ's review: M2(Q) is a rational quaternion algebra, as the sentence says, but the LMFDB uses this knowl for its Shimura curves, whose algebras are indefinite division algebras (disc(B) > 1); there the fact is Eichler's theorem (every indefinite quaternion algebra over Q has type number 1, by strong approximation), in no tree. On 2026-11-13 the user asked for nf.sextic_twin's remark to be proved by an example in the LMFDB's setting (a sextic number field) although the knowl's text allowed any field; the lead applied that ruling here on 2026-11-17 (review AM2 had put it as a question), so (c) stays a blocker. It does not change the outcome, which (b) keeps partial. (b) 'the number of B^x-conjugacy classes is finite': not proved; for M2(Q) it follows from (c) (one class). Searched: no tree has the class set or the type number of an order; Tau Ceti's main (checkout-62bbc05) has IntegralOrder.IsOrder, IsMaximalOrder, IsOrder.exists_le_isMaximalOrder, Submodule.leftOrder_isOrder (the left order of a lattice is an order) and the finite ideles of an order with their lattices (IntegralOrder/Ideles), but no finiteness (its classSet is about permutation-triple passports); Mathlib has Minkowski's convex body theorem (MeasureTheory.exists_ne_zero_mem_lattice_of_measure_mul_two_pow_lt_measure), not its use for quaternion orders. Route: finiteness of the left class set of a maximal order O (Minkowski's theorem on B tensor R for an invertible left O-ideal I, with a positive definite majorant of |nrd|, gives a nonzero alpha in I with |nrd(alpha)| bounded by a constant times N(I), so I alpha^-1 is integral of bounded norm, finitely many), and connecting ideals (for maximal O, O', the lattice O O' is an invertible left O-ideal with right order O', and O' is conjugate to O exactly when it is principal), so the type number is at most the class number; this needs the ideal theory of quaternion orders (norms of lattices, invertibility over maximal orders, right orders), none of which is in any tree. Blocked by: the finiteness of the type number of a quaternion algebra over Q, the number of B^x-conjugacy classes of its maximal orders (missing theory: the ideal theory of quaternion orders, that is invertible lattices, left and right orders, the reduced norm of a lattice and connecting ideals, with the finiteness of the class set of a maximal order by Minkowski's theorem on B tensor R or by reduction theory; proved only for M2(Q), where there is one class); and, since 'in many cases there is exactly one class' needs an example among the LMFDB's indefinite division algebras (2026-11-13 ruling), Eichler's theorem that their type number is 1 (strong approximation), missing. Difficulty: hard. No text error in the knowl. Overlap with Tau Ceti's main, to fold at the bump: exists_isQuaternionOrder could come from main's Submodule.leftOrder_isOrder applied to the Z-span of a Q-basis; the committed IsQuaternionOrder and IsMaximalQuaternionOrder are main's IsOrder Q and IsMaximalOrder Q (round AJ's fold item 1); reducedTrace_matrix is one line from main's Matrix.trace_mulLeft. No new axioms, no sorry; lake build of the modules, #lint clean, #print axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Non-vacuity (scratch NonVacuity.lean): not_existsUnique_isMaximalQuaternionOrder and exists_isMaximalQuaternionOrder_ne applied to H[Q,-1,3] and to M2(Q); exists_isMaximalQuaternionOrder_le applied to the order of PolarizedQuaternionOrder.negOneThree. Review (AM2): partial confirmed. (a) checked step by step for every quaternion algebra over Q, with no hypothesis beyond finrank Q B = 4 and the instances; (c) checked for M2(Q), which is not the LMFDB's setting; (b) and its search confirmed. Review changes, no statement changed: Module.Finite.fg_top (two namespace components) to Finite.fg_top; the isomorphism e of IsQuaternionOrder.map and IsMaximalQuaternionOrder.map hoisted into the namespace variable (explicit arguments now e then hO; every use is dot notation hO.map e); hO.2 to hO.le_of_ge (twice); in exists_units_forall_sq_reducedTrace_div_ne the untyped have h1, h2 typed, the divisibility built once (hd, Dvd.intro), the known value 4 on the right; the leading fragment of isMaximalQuaternionOrder_iff_exists_eq_map_conj on the colon line. Checks after the review: lake build and lake env lean silent, #lint 0 errors in the 31 declarations of the three modules, the simp deletion test (43 entries in 23 lists, all needed), dup_decls 0 clashes over 16362 modules.

- `st_group.ambient` [Groups › Sato–Tate groups] (hard): Done: Round AF (AF5), kept partial, no new Lean. The reading of O(d) as the compact real orthogonal group is a fixable text (recorded) and is formalised (ambientGroup, mem_ambientGroup_iff_of_even), as is USp(d) (satoTateForm, reindex_J_eq_satoTateForm). Not formalised: the claim that a Sato–Tate group of weight w and degree d lies in USp(d) (w odd) or O(d) (w even). For Sato–Tate groups of motives (st_group.definition, partial: ℓ-adic realisations, Zariski closure, maximal compact subgroup) it is a theorem about motives, which LeanBridge builds into the bundled SatoTateGroup (field le_ambientGroup), a model. In the setting the LMFDB uses, its database of groups, it is false for weight 0: LMFDB/lmfdb lmfdb/sato_tate_groups/main.py gives the groups μ(n) (labels 0.1.n, mu_data) weight 0 and degree 1, and st_ambient returns O(d) for every even weight, so the page of μ(n), n ≥ 3, says 'Contained in O(1)' although μ(3) ⊄ O(1) = {±1} (the code's comment: 'only list supgroups with the same ambient (i.e. if mu(n) lies in O(1) don't list supgroups that are not)'). This is the recorded editors' item for st_group.definition and st_group.ambient; a fixed text must treat weight 0 apart (U(d), or self-dual motives only). Blocked by st_group.definition (very hard: motives). Review (AF5): confirmed partial, and the error is wider than weight 0. It is a knowl text error that changes the mathematics, which the display repeats (st_ambient implements the knowl's parity rule; the data, weight and degree, are right). main.py also generates, for every weight w ≥ 1, the degree-2 groups SU(2) × μ(n) and N(U(1)) × μ(n) (labels w.2.3.cn and w.2.1.dn, su2_mu_data and nu1_mu_data, 'of any wt > 0'), the Sato–Tate groups of newforms with a character of order n; for n ≥ 3 they contain the scalar ζI, ζ a primitive n-th root of unity, which lies in no conjugate of USp(2) (det ζI = ζ² ≠ 1) or of O(2) (its eigenvalues ζ, ζ are not closed under complex conjugation), although st_ambient gives them USp(2) (w odd) or O(2) (w even) as ambient. The dichotomy holds for motives with rational coefficients (a (−1)^w-symmetric polarization), such as abelian varieties; μ(n) and these groups come from motives with coefficients in Q(ζ_n) or a Hecke field. Proposed text: '$d$ is a subgroup of either:' → '$d$ is a subgroup of the unitary group $\mathrm{U}(d)$. When it is the Sato-Tate group of a motive with rational coefficients, such as an abelian variety, it is a subgroup of either:', with a third case for the ambient group (U(d)) and the matching change to st_ambient left to the editors. Blocked by: st_group.definition (Sato–Tate groups of motives), and the LMFDB's text.

- `st_group.supgroups` [Groups › Sato–Tate groups] (very hard): Done: The gap is closed: H^0 = G^0 is proved for every proper finite-index supergroup H of a Sato-Tate group G (closed, in the ambient group), so for the minimal and the minimal rational supergroups, through the general Subgroup.map_connectedComponentOfOne_eq_of_le (a closed finite-index subgroup K of L is open in L, so L^0 lies in K and is the identity component of K). Still partial, by the ruling of 11-04 on readings: 'A rational Sato-Tate group is maximal if it has no supergroups' is formalised (SatoTateGroup.IsMaximal) as 'has no rational proper finite-index supergroup', and the readings differ: in weight 0 the dihedral group D_6 of order 12 in O(2) is rational (its character values are integers, 2cos(pi/3) = 1) and its finite-index supergroups D_12, D_18, ... are all irrational (trace 2cos(pi/3k) of a generating rotation of D_6k, k >= 2), so it is maximal on the formalised reading but not on the literal one. The knowl's previous sentence ('we list only rational minimal supergroups') and the LMFDB code (a stored 'maximal' column, set in code only for mu(n), SU(2) x mu(n), N(U(1)) x mu(n), where both readings agree) do not decide it. Review: a second gap, not found by the author, keeps the knowl partial even if the reading is accepted: IsMinimalRationalSupergroup and IsMaximal rest on IsRational/IsRationalSubgroup, whose characters are those of Tau Ceti's rational Weyl modules, taken as all the irreducible characters of GL_d(C) although that they exhaust them is unproved; st_group.rational is partial for exactly this (sweep of 11-06), and its two rational notions inherit it. Blocked by: the reading of 'maximal' (question recorded for the editors) and the highest-weight classification behind st_group.rational.
- `st_group.trace_moments` [Groups › Sato–Tate groups] (hard): Done: Integrality is now proved: traceMoment_eq_finrank_invariants gives E[t^n] = dim of the G-invariants in the n-th tensor power of C^d (tensorPowerRep, the restriction of LeanBridge's ambientTensorRep, whose character is t^n by trace_tensorRep), through Tau Ceti's integral_character_eq_finrank_invariants: a nonnegative integer. The distribution of t is now explicit (traceDistribution, the pushforward of Haar measure under the trace) and M_n[t] is its n-th moment; t = -a_1 holds in every weight and degree (charpolyCoeff_one_eq_neg_trace, degree 0 included). Still partial: 'the moment sequences of t and a_1 coincide because their distributions are symmetric about zero' in odd weight is proved only when -1 lies in G (traceDistribution_map_neg, moment_charpolyCoeff_one_eq_traceMoment; odd moments vanish by traceMoment_eq_zero_of_odd). It is false for LeanBridge's SatoTateGroup, which has no Hodge circle or rationality axiom: the trivial subgroup of USp(2) in weight 1 has E[t] = 2 and E[a_1] = -2. It holds for Sato-Tate groups of motives (-1 is the image of -1 under a Hodge circle with p + q = w odd), and the committed IsHodgeCircle does not even force p + q = w, so it cannot supply -1 either.
- `st_group.trace_zero_density` [Groups › Sato–Tate groups] (hard): Done: Round AO (AO3_sato_tate_lie), 2026-11-23; the author proposed formalised, the review (review/AO3_sato_tate_lie.md) keeps it partial, hard. Blocked by: the Sato-Tate axioms on LeanBridge's SatoTateGroup (a Hodge circle in G^0 whose Hodge numbers h^{p,q} vanish off p + q = w, the gap of st_group.hodge_circle and st_group.definition): the true part of the wrong clause, 'constant and then equal to zero when the weight is odd', is proved only under that hypothesis (eq_zero_of_trace_eq_of_hasHodgeEigenvalues) and is false for SatoTateGroup without it (the trivial subgroup of USp(2), weight 1, has the constant trace 2), exactly as for st_group.trace_moments; dropping the clause instead (the shorter correction recorded on 11-07) drops a claim true for every Sato-Tate group of a motive of odd weight (the GL_2 precedent). Question put to the user in the review. Proved, for every SatoTateGroup with its normalised Haar measure: the trace zero density (SatoTateGroup.traceZeroDensity, committed); 'on each component the trace is either constant [...] or varies continuously taking each particular value with probability zero' (trace_const_or_forall_measure_eq_zero, from IsEntryPolynomial.forall_eq_or_measure_eq_zero, Serre's Proposition 8.4.3.3 proved as for st_group.probabilities; the trace is continuous, IsEntryPolynomial.continuous with isEntryPolynomial_trace); 'so this probability is simply the ratio of the number of components on which the trace is identically zero to the total number of components' (traceZeroDensity_eq_card_div_card; it gives the LMFDB's displayed values 0 for mu(n), SU(2) and U(1), 1/2 for N(U(1))). The stale half of the old blocker: the finiteness of the components (Components.lean). Text error, recorded on 11-07 (lmfdb-knowl-edits-2026-11-07.md, the shorter correction): 'constant and equal to zero' is false for the LMFDB's weight-0 groups mu(n), e.g. 0.1.1 with trace 1. The author's correction, which keeps the true part: old 'On each component of a Sato-Tate group, the trace is either constant and equal to zero, or varies continuously taking each particular value with probability zero;', new 'On each component of a Sato-Tate group, the trace is either constant (and then equal to zero when the weight is odd), or varies continuously taking each particular value with probability zero;' (it should replace the 11-07 one). Proved towards it: a constant trace is zero when -1 lies in the identity component (eq_zero_of_trace_eq_of_neg_one_mem, for every SatoTateGroup); a Hodge circle h with Hodge numbers vanishing off p + q = w, w odd, has h(-1) = -1 (matrix_eq_neg_one_of_hasHodgeEigenvalues, the inner step of the committed neg_one_mem_of_hasHodgeEigenvalues), so then a constant trace is zero (eq_zero_of_trace_eq_of_hasHodgeEigenvalues); the hypotheses are met by U(1) (torusU1HodgeCircle, torusU1HodgeCircle_mem, hasHodgeEigenvalues_torusU1HodgeCircle: h^{1,0} = h^{0,1} = 1). Checks (review): as for st_group.probabilities.

## LMFDB issues (598)

Problems in the LMFDB knowls, by kind: errors in their text, found while formalising them, with the proposed new text; wrong labels, whose id puts a knowl in the wrong category; duplicates, conflicting definitions, broken links and wrong titles; and suggested recategorisations. LeanBridge's blueprint follows the LMFDB's categories, so a knowl in the wrong category can only be moved in the LMFDB itself; the suggestions come from reading every knowl in the blueprint. Tick an item once it is fixed on beta.lmfdb.org.

- `ag.bielliptic_curve` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): Over a field k that is not algebraically closed the three conditions are not equivalent: the first asks for a double cover of an elliptic curve over k̄, the second for an involution defined over k whose quotient has a k-point, and the third for an involution defined over k whose quotient (of genus 1 by Riemann–Hurwitz, in characteristic ≠ 2) may have no k-point. For example, for f of degree 6 with x⁶f(2/x) = 8f(x) and otherwise generic, the genus-2 curve y² = f(x) over ℚ has exactly two bielliptic involutions, (x, y) ↦ (2/x, ±2√2·y/x³), conjugate over ℚ(√2), so it satisfies the first condition and neither of the others; read as a disjunction, the last two conditions are redundant and "the involution above" need not be defined over k. If the notion is geometric, the involutions in the second and third conditions should be taken in Aut(X_k̄) and the k-point dropped; if it is over k, the map and E in the first condition should be defined over k and the third condition should also ask for a k-point on the quotient.
- `ag.cohen_macaulay_type` (Error or typo; Suggested category: nf): A canonical module of a non-local ring is determined only up to an invertible module, so its global number of generators depends on the choice: ℤ[√−5] is Gorenstein, of type 1 by the knowl's formula, with canonical modules R and (2, 1 + √−5), minimally generated by 1 and 2 elements. The Gorenstein criterion lacks "= R", without which it fails for every non-maximal Gorenstein order (for ℤ[2i], ℤ[i] is a fractional ideal that is not invertible); `av.fq.singular_dimensions` has it right. Also: Pure typo: the bold covers half the term, and a stray comma separates subject and verb (round AM). — Suggested recategorisation: Commutative algebra of orders in étale ℚ-algebras (canonical module, Gorenstein orders), with nothing geometric; it belongs with the other knowls on orders, such as `nf.order`, although only `av.fq` knowls cite it. Another possible category: `av.fq`. Confidence: medium.
- `ag.complex_multiplication` (Error found while formalising; Suggested category: av): The definition uses the endomorphism algebra over the base field, which goes with simplicity over the base field (`ag.simple`, as in `ec.complex_multiplication`), but "simple" links to the knowl for geometrically simple. If geometric simplicity is meant instead, the text should say "geometrically simple" and use the geometric endomorphism algebra. — Suggested recategorisation: Complex multiplication of a simple abelian variety (endomorphism algebra a CM field of degree 2g).
- `ag.gonality` (Error or typo): False for curves that are not normal: the nodal cubic y² = x²(x + 1) has k(X) = k(y/x), so the field description gives 1, but its gonality is 2.
- `ag.hyperelliptic_curve` (Error found while formalising): For g ≥ 2 the equation w² = f(x,y,z) is not homogeneous in ℙ³ (w² has degree 2, f has degree g + 1); the model lives in the weighted projective space ℙ(1,1,1,(g+1)/2), which needs g odd. When g is even, Y has a k-rational divisor of odd degree g − 1 (a hyperplane section), so Y ≅ ℙ¹ and X has a Weierstrass model over k.
- `ag.kodaira_dimension` (Error or typo; Duplicate): For a nonempty connected proper variety P₀ = h⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = 1, so "P_d = 0 for all d" with d ≥ 0 never holds; the condition is for d ≥ 1. X must also be projective (or proper): otherwise H⁰(X, K^{⊗d}) can be infinite-dimensional, for example for X = 𝔸¹, and P_d is not defined. — Duplicate: Duplicates `hmsurface.kodaira_dimension`: same notion.
- `ag.modcurve.xnsp` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide); Conflict; Suggested category: modcurve): For N with r distinct prime factors, a Cartan subgroup C of GL₂(ℤ/Nℤ) = ∏_ℓ GL₂(ℤ/ℓ^e) that is nonsplit at every ℓ | N is ∏_ℓ C_ℓ, and its normalizer ∏_ℓ N(C_ℓ) contains C with index 2^r, while the extended Cartan subgroup E (C and the canonical involution, gl2.cartan), which modcurve.xns_plus uses for the same curve X_ns⁺(N), contains C with index 2. By brute force [N(C) : C] = [E : C] = 2 for N = 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, but [N(C) : C] = 4 and [E : C] = 2 for N = 6, 10, 12, 14, 15, so the two knowls define different curves unless N is a prime power. Also, gl2.nonsplit_cartan defines non-split Cartan subgroups of GL₂(𝔽_p) only. The replacement follows modcurve.xns_plus; if the database's X_ns⁺(N) is the curve of the full normalizer, keep "normalizer" here, of a Cartan subgroup of GL₂(ℤ/Nℤ) that is nonsplit at every prime dividing N, and change modcurve.xns_plus instead. — Conflicting definition: Conflicts with `modcurve.xns_plus`: normaliser vs extended Cartan: different groups when N has two or more prime factors. — Suggested recategorisation: The modular curve X_ns^+(N); duplicates modcurve.xns_plus.
- `ag.quotient_curve` (Error found while formalising): The last sentence lacks its full stop.
- `ag.shimura_variety` (Error or typo): Without arithmeticity the quotient need not be Hausdorff (an irrational rotation of the disc generates a torsion-free group that is not discrete) or algebraic, and non-arithmetic Fuchsian groups give compact Riemann surfaces that are not Shimura curves. The involutions are holomorphic ones.
- `ag.variety` (Error found while formalising): ℙⁿ has the n + 1 homogeneous coordinates x₀, …, xₙ (`ag.projective_space`).
- `alg.bezout_matrix` (Error or typo): The Bézoutian has degree at most n − 1 in each variable, so the exponents run from 0 to n − 1. Also: For n = 2, f = x² and g = 1 the Bézout matrix is (0, 1; 1, 0), of determinant −1, while the resultant is 1; LeanBridge proves det = (−1)^(n(n−1)/2) Res(f, g) (`Polynomial.det_bezoutMatrix`). The exponent error in the displayed sum is in section 3.
- `alg.binary_operation` (Typo): Stray comma and double space.
- `alg.binary_operation.associative` (Typo): Stray HTML fragment "/div>" after the display.
- `artin.galois_orbit` (Error or typo): Galois automorphisms act on the values of a representation (composition with σ on matrix entries), not by pre-composition.
- `artin.projective_image_type` (Error or typo): The projective image of a reducible two-dimensional Artin representation χ₁ ⊕ χ₂ is cyclic (it is the image of χ₁/χ₂), for example trivial for 1 ⊕ 1, which is none of A₄, S₄, A₅ or D_n with n ≥ 2; that list is the one for irreducible representations, whose projective image is never cyclic. The dihedral index is renamed m, since n is already the dimension.
- `av.deligne_module` (Typo; Suggested category: av.fq): Three typos: "than", "in in" and "abelian variety". — Suggested recategorisation: Deligne modules describe abelian varieties over finite fields through the Frobenius order and the Weil polynomial.
- `av.fq.class_number_1` (Error or typo): Every curve of genus 0 over a finite field is the projective line, whose class group is trivial, so the count needs 'positive genus', as in the sources (Shen and Shi, arXiv:1412.3505: 'with positive genus and class number one'). The second DOI lacks its first digit: Leitzel, Madan and Queen, Algebraic function fields with small class number, J. Number Theory 7 (1975), is 10.1016/0022-314X(75)90004-9 (checked on Crossref).
- `av.fq.endomorphism_ring_notation` (Error or typo): Every nonzero x gives an invertible fractional ideal xS, so there are infinitely many invertible fractional S-ideals; #Pic counts their isomorphism classes, the order of Pic(S) (av.fq.picard_group: invertible fractional S-ideals modulo S-linear isomorphism). The link on $S$ points to the Frobenius order ℤ[F, V], which S is not in general. The vertices of the graph are endomorphism rings, not endomorphisms, and "Picard groups" and "correspond" (twice) are typos.
- `av.fq.honda_tate` (Typo): Missing word: "if and only" should read "if and only if".
- `av.fq.initial_coefficients` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): 'leading constant term' reads oddly: the constant term is the first one in the increasing order the knowl fixes, not the leading coefficient.
- `av.fq.lmfdb_label` (Error or typo): The displayed polynomial is the L-polynomial, not the Weil polynomial (which is its reverse). Also: The displayed polynomial, with constant term 1 and leading coefficient q^g, is the L-polynomial (av.fq.l-polynomial); the Weil q-polynomial is monic, its reverse (av.fq.weil_polynomial). The a_i are the same. The display also lacks a + between x^{g+1} and the following ⋯. ℚ[F] is an étale algebra, a product of fields, and a field only for an isotypic isogeny class (compare av.fq.endomorphism_ring_notation). The rest are typos: "Each polarizations", "weak equivalence class class" (the link text already ends in "class") and "all the with".
- `av.fq.max_cohen_macaulay_type` (Error or typo): The link labelled 'Frobenius order' points to av.fq.bass_zfv (the knowl defining Bass); the Frobenius order is av.fq.frobenius_order, which av.fq.bass_zfv itself links for the same words. The title "Maximum Cohen-Macaulay" also lacks "type".
- `av.fq.singular_primes` (Error or typo): The conductor of a non-maximal order is not invertible, and then 'divides' (𝔣_R = 𝔓J for an ideal J of R) is stronger than 'contains': for R = ℤ[9i], 𝔣_R = 9ℤ[i] and the only maximal ideal containing it is 𝔓 = 3ℤ + 9ℤ[i], but (𝔣_R : 𝔓) = 𝔓 and 𝔓² = 9ℤ + 27ℤi does not contain 9i, so 𝔓 does not divide 𝔣_R and R would have no singular prime. The singular primes are the maximal ideals containing the conductor (those at which R is not integrally closed). Also, "a singular primes" should be singular.
- `av.fq.weak_equivalence_class` (Typo; Suggested category: nf): Weak equivalence classes are also called local isomorphism classes or genera (compare `av.weak_equivalence_class`: "locally isomorphic or in the same genus"). — Suggested recategorisation: Weak equivalence of fractional ideals of an order: general order theory, duplicating av.weak_equivalence_class. Another possible category: `av.fq`. Confidence: medium.
- `av.fq.zfv_real_index` (Error or typo): K⁺ = ℚ[F + V] is a field only when the Weil polynomial is a power of an irreducible polynomial; in general it is a product of totally real fields.
- `av.fq.zfv_rel_disc_norm` (Error or typo): The Frobenius order is ℤ[F, V]; K = ℚ[F, V] is its fraction field. Also: A real root ±√q of the Weil polynomial gives a factor of K on which F = V, so N(F − V) = 0, while discriminants of orders are non-zero: for 1.4.ae (h = (x − 2)², q = 4), K = ℚ and F = V = 2, but R = R⁺ = ℤ gives |Δ_R|/Δ_{R⁺}² = 1. Without real roots R = R⁺ ⊕ R⁺F and the identity holds; the typo ℚ[F, V] in the same sentence is in section 3.
- `av.galois_rep` (Error or typo): The Weil pairing is a pairing A[m] × A^∨[m] → μ_m; it gives a non-degenerate alternating pairing on A[m] only after composing with a polarization A → A^∨ of degree prime to m, for example a principal one, as for Jacobians. In the ℓ-adic representation, T_ℓ(E) should be T_ℓ(A), and Aut(T_ℓ(A)) ≅ GL_{2g}(ℤ_ℓ), not GSp_{2g}(ℤ_ℓ): it is the image of ρ_{A,ℓ} that lies in GSp_{2g}(ℤ_ℓ).
- `av.simple` (Error found while formalising): "Isogenous" links to the knowl on isogeny factors instead of `av.isogeny`, which defines it.
- `belyi.primitivization` (Error or typo): The minimal-degree primitive subcover is not unique up to isomorphism: a degree-9 Belyi map with monodromy group C₃ × C₃ acting regularly (for example (u,v) ↦ u³ on the Fermat cubic u³ + v³ = 1) has one block system for each of the four subgroups of order 3, giving four degree-3 subcovers with primitive monodromy group C₃. Three of them have genus 0 (branched over two of 0, 1, ∞) and one has genus 1 (branched over all three), so they are not isomorphic even after permuting 0, 1, ∞. Similarly, the degree-4 map with group C₂ × C₂ has three degree-2 subcovers branched over different pairs of points.
- `character.dirichlet` (Error or typo): As written the definition asks only that χ be completely multiplicative and q-periodic, and the next sentence reads as a consequence, which is false: χ ≡ 1 with q = 2 is completely multiplicative and 2-periodic but χ(2) = 1, and χ ≡ 0 has χ(1) = 0, which is not a root of unity. The vanishing exactly at the n with (n,q) > 1 must be part of the definition; the values at the other n are then roots of unity.
- `character.dirichlet.conrey.orbit_label` (Error or typo): A modulus with more than 26 Galois orbits has orbit labels of several letters (the 27th orbit is q.ba, as character.dirichlet.galois_orbit_label says), so A is not always a single letter. The last entry of the vector also lacks a closing parenthesis.
- `character.dirichlet.galois_orbit_index` (Error found while formalising): The orbits being ordered are those of modulus q, and the first is the orbit of the principal character of modulus q, the only character of order 1 (LeanBridge proves this: `DirichletCharacter.galoisOrbitIndex_one`). The tuple has q entries, as "∈ ℤ^q" and the later "q-tuple" say.
- `character.dirichlet.group.structure` (Error or typo): Without n₁ > 1 the expression is not unique, since factors C₁ can be added (C₂ ≅ C₁ × C₂ with 1 | 2); the trivial group is then the empty product. The product also lacks a × before the dots.
- `character.dirichlet.minimal` (Error found while formalising; Typo): Condition 1 excludes the trivial character when the 2-part of N is 2ᵉ with e ≥ 4 even: for N = 16 it requires cond(χ) ∈ {4, 16}, but the trivial character has conductor 1. LeanBridge proves the claim false for these moduli: `DirichletCharacter.isMinimalOfPrimePowerModulus_one_iff` (for a prime power N, the trivial character satisfies the conditions exactly when N is not a square divisible by 16). Also: "characters", plural.
- `character.dirichlet.modulus` (Error or typo): As written the definition asks only that χ be completely multiplicative and q-periodic, and the last sentence reads as a consequence, which is false: χ ≡ 1 with q = 2 is completely multiplicative and 2-periodic but χ(2) = 1, and χ ≡ 0 has χ(1) = 0, which is not a root of unity. The vanishing exactly at the n with (n,q) > 1 must be part of the definition (as in the fix proposed for character.dirichlet); the values at the other n are then roots of unity.
- `character.dirichlet.values` (Error or typo; Typo): The listed values include χ(q) = 0, and χ(n) = 0 whenever gcd(n, q) > 1, so they are not all roots of unity; the corrected statement is proved in LeanBridge (round AI). Also: The math mode closes before the parenthesis.
- `character.hecke` (Error or typo): An arbitrary homomorphism χ_∞ imposes essentially no condition, and triviality on ℚˣ excludes e.g. |N(·)|^s. The standard condition is that χ_∞ is the restriction to Kˣ of a continuous character of (K ⊗ ℝ)ˣ.
- `cmf.atkin-lehner` (Error or typo): The claim fails for oldforms: Δ ∈ S₁₂(Γ₀(2)) is an eigenform of every T_p with p odd, but w₂ maps it to a nonzero multiple of Δ(2z), so it is not an eigenform of w₂. It holds in the new subspace, by multiplicity one, since w_Q preserves it and commutes with the T_p with p ∤ N.
- `cmf.atkin_lehner_dims` (Error or typo): For a nontrivial character χ the Atkin–Lehner operator W_Q maps S_k(Γ₀(N), χ) to the space of character χ̄_Q·χ_{N/Q} and need not square to 1: if χ is not real-valued, W_N sends a newform of character χ to a multiple of a newform of character χ̄, so it does not scale it by ±1, and S_k^new(Γ₀(N), χ) has no subspaces with prescribed signs. The signs and these subspaces are those of the newforms of trivial character, in S_k^new(Γ₀(N)); the LMFDB records Atkin–Lehner signs only for trivial character.
- `cmf.character` (Error or typo): The law does not define the character for every Γ ⊇ Γ(N): for Γ = Γ₁(N) or Γ(N) every γ ∈ Γ has d ≡ 1 mod N, so every character mod N satisfies it, and for Γ = SL₂(ℤ) and N > 1 the law at γ = (0 −1; 1 0), where χ(0) = 0, forces f = 0. The character is determined by the law on Γ₀(N), the setting of the spaces M_k(N, χ).
- `cmf.coefficient_field` (Error or typo; Typo): Found in round ZS. The knowl defines the coefficient field as a subfield of ℂ, and 1.36.a.a has field x³ - 12422194 x - 2645665785 of non-square discriminant 7478532150925922921461, so it is not normal and the three conjugates have three different fields in ℂ. Conjugates do have isomorphic fields (IsGaloisConjugateBy.coefficientFieldEquiv in LeanBridge). Also: A full stop is missing.
- `cmf.decomposition.new.gamma0chi` (Error or typo): Within a single S_k^new(N, χ) with χ not rational-valued, a piece has dimension [ℚ(f) : ℚ(χ)], not [ℚ(f) : ℚ]: for 13.2.e.a, S₂(Γ₁(13)) is 2-dimensional, split between χ and χ̄ of order 6, so the piece in S₂^new(13, χ) is 1-dimensional while ℚ(f) = ℚ(√−3) has degree 2. Alternatively, take the space S_k^new(N, [χ]).
- `cmf.defining_polynomial` (Error or typo): By cmf.coefficient_field the coefficient field is the subfield of ℂ generated by the a_n, which for an arbitrary modular form need not be a number field: πΔ ∈ S₁₂(SL₂(ℤ)) has coefficient field ℚ(π). It is a number field for a newform, whose coefficient field is the one whose defining polynomial the LMFDB records.
- `cmf.dimension` (Error or typo): S_k^new(N,χ) is a complex vector space, so as a ℚ(χ)-vector space it is infinite-dimensional whenever it is nonzero, and so is every newform subspace: as written the relative dimension is infinite for every nonzero space. The LMFDB's relative dimension is the dimension divided by [ℚ(χ):ℚ], for the newspace S_k^new(N,[χ]) of the Galois orbit of χ (where it equals the dimension of S_k^new(N,χ)) and for newform subspaces (where it is [ℚ(f):ℚ(χ)], as in cmf.relative_dimension).
- `cmf.distinguishing_primes` (Error found while formalising; Error or typo): With i < m, c₁ = 1 and p_n enters no c_m, so any prime can be appended: the sequence is not unique, and its length can reach the number of newforms (two newforms distinguished by p₁ give (p₁, p₂) with c₁ = 1 < c₂ = 2). Uniqueness also needs each p_m to be the least prime that increases the count. The knowl breaks the line on each side of the display, hence three replacements; the third also fixes "less then". Also: The bound on the length fails for the zero space, which has no newforms and the empty sequence (0 is not less than 0).
- `cmf.eisenstein_newspace` (Error found while formalising): The exception is false when N = m² with m > 1 the conductor of a primitive character ψ: then E₂^(ψ,ψ̄) is holomorphic of weight 2, level N and trivial character, and new by the knowl's own rule (N₁N₂ = N). For example, E₂(Γ₀(9)) has dimension 3 and its old part, spanned by E₂(τ) − 3E₂(3τ) and E₂(3τ) − 3E₂(9τ), has dimension 2, so E₂^new(9) is spanned by E₂^(ψ,ψ) for the quadratic character ψ modulo 3.
- `cmf.eisenstein_series` (Error or typo): Without the parity condition χ₁(−1)χ₂(−1) = (−1)^k the series is not a modular form of weight k: for k = 3 and χ₁ = χ₂ = 1 it is Σσ₂(n)qⁿ ≠ 0, while M₃(SL₂(ℤ)) = 0. With it the series is a modular form of level N₁N₂ and character χ₁χ₂, except E₂^{1,1} = −1/24 + Σσ₁(n)qⁿ, which is only quasimodular and which cmf.eisenstein_form already treats separately.
- `cmf.embedding_format` (Error or typo): a_n is the n-th coefficient of f, that is the eigenvalue of T_n on f, an element of the coefficient field with embeddings iota(a_n). The trace of T_n, on the span of the conjugates of f or on the newspace, is a rational integer, the same for every embedding (the site's tr(a_n)). Also 'be newform' lacks 'a' (found while checking).
- `cmf.fouriercoefficients` (Error or typo): As written the expansion at γ∞ is one of f itself, which does not depend on the cusp: f has period 1, so f(z) = g(e^{2πiz/w}) with g(t) = Σ a_n t^{nw}, and a_γ(n) = a_{n/w} (zero unless w ∣ n). The expansion at the cusp γ∞ is that of (f|_kγ)(z) = (cz + d)^{−k} f(γz). Also, "is it understood" should read "it is understood".
- `cmf.fricke` (Typo): The Fricke involution is w_N; omega_N here is a typo.
- `cmf.galois_orbit` (Error found while formalising): The newform subspace is a complex vector space, which has no finite ℚ-basis, and when its dimension d is greater than 1 the conjugates σ(f) do not have rational coefficients. They form a basis over ℂ; for a rational statement, the traces Tr(αf), α running over a ℚ-basis of ℚ(f), form a ℚ-basis of the forms in the subspace with rational coefficients.
- `cmf.hecke_galois_orbit` (Error or typo): The LMFDB's letter code is base 26 with a = 0, so z is followed by ba and bb, and "aa" never occurs (as in character.dirichlet.galois_orbit_label: "the index 27 is written as ba"). The third trace is missing the slash of K/ℚ.
- `cmf.hecke_kernels` (Error or typo): Distinguishing primes compare characteristic polynomials on the orbit subspaces, which separate orbits of different dimensions even when their a_p are conjugate, while ker g_p(T_p) sees only the roots. In S_2^new(Γ₀(187)) the LMFDB's sequence is just (2), since T_2 has characteristic polynomials x, x−2, x²+2x−2, (x−2)², a cubic and a quartic on the six orbits; yet 187.2.a.b (dimension 1) and 187.2.a.d (dimension 2) both have a_2 = 2, so ker(T_2 − 2) is 3-dimensional and contains both orbits (S_2^new(Γ₀(203)) fails the same way with 203.2.a.b, 203.2.a.d and a_2 = −1). Separately, the q-expansion is written ∑ a_n^n instead of ∑ a_n q^n.
- `cmf.hecke_operator` (Error or typo): The T_n with gcd(n,N) > 1 need not be normal: in S₁₂(Γ₀(8)), where the formula gives T₂ = U₂, the span of Δ(z), Δ(2z), Δ(4z), Δ(8z) is T₂-stable with characteristic polynomial x²(x² + 24x + 2048) but a one-dimensional kernel, so T₂ is not diagonalizable and S₁₂(Γ₀(8)) has no basis of eigenforms for all the Hecke operators. A common eigenbasis of S_k(N,χ) exists for the T_n with gcd(n,N) = 1 (not canonical on the oldforms, whose eigenspaces can have dimension > 1), and one for all the T_n exists in the newspace: the newforms.
- `cmf.hecke_orbit` (Error or typo): As written, for an eigenform f the space generated by the T_p(f) is the line ℂf, since T_p f = a_p f, while cmf.dimension_galois_orbit gives the Hecke orbit of a newform the dimension of its Galois orbit, which exceeds 1 whenever the coefficient field is not ℚ (the newform 23.2.a.a, with coefficient field ℚ(√5), and its conjugate span a two-dimensional space). The intended notion is the span of the Galois conjugates of a newform, its newform subspace.
- `cmf.inner_twist` (Error found while formalising): Two repeated words.
- `cmf.lfunction` (Error or typo): The root number of a newform with nontrivial character has absolute value 1 but need not be a root of unity: the twist of 11.2.a.a by a cubic character χ of conductor 7 is a newform in S_2^new(539, χ²) with ε = χ(11)τ(χ)²/7 ≈ 0.3865 + 0.9223i (Iwaniec–Kowalski, Prop. 14.20; checked numerically from the functional equation). Its cube ε³ = (−13 − 3√−3)/14 is a root of 7x² + 13x + 7, so ε is not an algebraic integer and hence not a root of unity.
- `cmf.maximal` (Error or typo): The Galois conjugates σ(f) of a newform f of character χ have the characters σ(χ), which differ from χ unless χ is rational-valued, so the Galois orbit of f does not lie in the newspace S_k^new(N,χ) of cmf.newspace and, as written, no newform of non-rational character is maximal; the ambient space is S_k^new(N,[χ]), the sum over the Galois conjugates of χ. Likewise the Galois conjugates of f lie in its ambient subspace and have its dimension, so as written no newform of dimension > 1 is largest, contradicting "(this includes newforms that are maximal)".
- `cmf.newform_subspace` (Error or typo): The Galois conjugates σ(f) of a newform f of character χ have the characters σ(χ), which differ from χ unless χ is rational-valued (the two conjugates in 13.2.e.a have the characters χ and χ̄), so the newform subspace of f does not lie in the newspace S_k^new(N,χ) of cmf.newspace, which therefore has no decomposition into newform subspaces. The decomposition is that of S_k^new(N,[χ]), the sum over the Galois conjugates of χ.
- `cmf.newspaces` (Error or typo): An automorphism σ maps S_k^new(N, χ) to S_k^new(N, σ∘χ), so the absolute Galois group of ℚ acts on the newforms of S_k^new(N, [χ]), and on those of S_k^new(N, χ) only when χ is rational-valued (the two conjugate newforms of 13.2.e.a have the characters χ and χ̄). Also "acts the set" is missing "on". Also: Found in round ZS. A typo: "the space of S_k^new(N, χ) of".
- `cmf.projective_image` (Error found while formalising): ρ is the linear representation in `cmf.artin_image`; the projective one is ρ̄, as in `cmf.projective_field`.
- `cmf.relative_dimension` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide); Typo): Writes $S_k^{\mathrm{new}}(\Gamma_0(N),\chi)$; the other cmf knowls write $S_k^{\mathrm{new}}(N,\chi)$. Notation only. Also: Suggested text, drafted 2026-11-01.
- `cmf.satake_parameters` (Error found while formalising; Typo): For the Hecke operator T_p on S_k(N, chi), det(1 - tT_p) has degree dim S_k(N, chi), never this quadratic. The identity holds for the Hecke operator of level Np (that is U_p, since p divides Np) on the 2-dimensional space V_p(f) spanned by f(z) and f(pz), which it preserves and on which its trace is a_p (proved in LeanBridge: HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.det_one_sub_smul_pOldSpaceHeckeT and trace_pOldSpaceHeckeT). This correction replaces the earlier one through a Frobenius element on the Galois representation attached to f, at the user's choice of 2026-11-12. Also 'be a newform'.
- `cmf.sato_tate` (Error found while formalising): The determinant of the Artin representation of a weight one newform is its nebentypus, which is odd, so complex conjugation maps to a matrix of determinant −1.
- `cmf.shimura_correspondence` (Error found while formalising; Error or typo): Shimura's character is χ(m)((−1)^λ t/m) = χ(m)(−1/m)^λ (t/m) (Shimura 1973; Koblitz IV.3), so the knowl's version is wrong for even λ. For k = 3 the image lies only in M₂(N/2, χ²), as the knowl's last sentence implies by saying that cusp forms go to cusp forms only for k ≥ 5. Also: Found in round ZT. The Dirichlet series uses a_{tn^2}, and g = sum_{n >= 1} a_n q^n has no coefficient of negative index, so t must be positive, as in Shimura's theorem.
- `cmf.sort_order` (Error or typo): Out of date: the default sort of the newform search is by analytic conductor first, then level, character orbit and Hecke orbit (CMFSearchArray._sort in lmfdb/classical_modular_forms/main.py). Analytic conductor and level determine the weight, so the corrected sentence still describes a complete ordering.
- `cmf.space_trace_form` (Error or typo): S_k(N,χ) is the whole space of cusp forms, which the newforms do not span when there are oldforms. The LMFDB's newspace trace forms, with integer coefficients, are the sums of the newforms of S_k^new(N,[χ]), the sum over the Galois conjugates of χ; summing those of S_k^new(N,χ) alone gives non-rational coefficients when χ is not rational-valued (for 13.2.e, a single newform with coefficients in ℚ(√−3)).
- `cmf.trace_bound` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): Found in round ZS: a mismatch of knowl and data. The database stores trace_bound = 0 for a space with one orbit (11.2.a, 1.24.a), with 2 for 37.2.a and 1 for 43.2.a (dims [1,2]). LeanBridge's traceBound follows the knowl as written and is 1 there.
- `cmf.trace_form` (Error found while formalising): Typo: k for χ.
- `cmf.twist_multiplicity` (Error found while formalising; Error or typo): For [g] = [f] the multiplicity counts only the inner twists of f by characters in [ψ], which is the inner twist multiplicity for [ψ]; the inner twist count is the sum of these over all character orbits. A CM newform with no other inner twist, such as 27.2.a.a, has inner twist count 2 but multiplicity 1 as a twist of itself by the orbit of its CM character. LeanBridge proves "multiplicity ≤ inner twist multiplicity": `HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.twistMultiplicity_self_le_innerTwistMultiplicity`. Also: Found in round ZT. The multiplicity is the inner twist multiplicity for [ψ], and the inner twist count is the sum of these over the orbits. On 361.2.e.d the LMFDB itself lists Mult 1, 2, 3 with count 6, and 13.2.e.a has Mult 1, 1 with count 2.
- `cmf.weight` (Error found while formalising (for the editors to decide); Error or typo): The transformation law as written holds only for integral k, but the knowl allows half-integral weight, where the law carries Shimura's theta multiplier: f(γz) = χ(d)(c/d)ε_d^(−2k)(cz + d)^k f(z) for γ ∈ Γ₀(4N). State the law for integral k and give the half-integral law separately. Also: Suggested text, drafted 2026-11-01.
- `crystals.crystal` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): As written a crystal is any nonempty set with arbitrary maps wt, eᵢ and fᵢ, with no axiom relating them, so the definition is degenerate. Kashiwara's definition adds maps εᵢ, φᵢ : B → ℤ ⊔ {−∞} with φᵢ(b) = εᵢ(b) + ⟨hᵢ, wt(b)⟩, and requires, among other axioms, that fᵢ(b) = b′ if and only if eᵢ(b′) = b, in which case wt(b′) = wt(b) − αᵢ, εᵢ(b′) = εᵢ(b) + 1 and φᵢ(b′) = φᵢ(b) − 1. The editors should state these axioms, or those of the narrower seminormal crystals, in which εᵢ(b) and φᵢ(b) are the largest k with eᵢᵏ(b) ≠ 0, respectively fᵢᵏ(b) ≠ 0.
- `crystals.highest_weight` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): With only "has a highest weight element", the knowl's labelling by the weight of the highest weight element is ill-defined (e.g. for B(λ) ⊔ B(μ), which has two highest weight elements of different weights); the standard notion requires the crystal to be generated by its highest weight element (the round of 31 October review).
- `crystals.littelmann_path` (Error or typo): Garbled: π(0) = 0 is a condition, and what is required of the endpoint is that π(1) is a weight, an element of P (the path takes values in P ⊗ ℚ).
- `curve.highergenus.aut.braid_equivalence` (Error or typo): Subscript typo.
- `curve.highergenus.aut.branchpoints` (Error or typo): X/G is then called compact, and the finiteness claim fails for non-compact X: the involution (x, y) ↦ (x, −y) of the smooth connected curve y² = sin x in ℂ² fixes the infinitely many points (kπ, 0).
- `curve.highergenus.aut.conjugacyclasses` (Typo): Spelling: "clases".
- `curve.highergenus.aut.generators` (Error or typo): The class of a loop going once around b depends on the path joining it to y₀, and independently chosen loops need not satisfy the product relation: for B = {b₁, b₂, b₃} ⊂ ℙ¹, with π₁ free on standard loops x₁, x₂ and x₃ = (x₁x₂)⁻¹, the loops x₁, x₂, x₁x₃x₁⁻¹ each go once around one point of B, but no ordering of them has product 1. `curve.highergenus.aut.generatingvector` relies on the coherent choice.
- `curve.highergenus.aut.signature` (Error or typo): The signature uses standard generators of π₁(Y − B, y₀) for a quotient Y = X/G of any genus g₀, but curve.highergenus.aut.generators defines them only for Y of genus 0. For g₀ > 0 the loops around the branch points are the elements c₁, …, c_r of a canonical system of generators a₁, b₁, …, a_{g₀}, b_{g₀}, c₁, …, c_r with ∏[a_j, b_j]∏c_i = 1, which the replacement says (alternatively, extend curve.highergenus.aut.generators to any genus).
- `dq.curve.highergenus.aut.label` (Error or typo): The first field of the label is the genus g, which is 3 here: the text says 'genus 3', and Riemann-Hurwitz gives 2g - 2 = 168 (-2 + 1/2 + 2/3 + 6/7) = 4. The site's label is 3.168-42.0.2-3-7, as in curve.highergenus.hurwitz_bound, in modcurve.xarith.remarks and in the search example of lmfdb/higher_genus_w_automorphisms/main.py.
- `dq.ecnf.reliability` (Typo): 'critial' for 'critical', the same sentence as in rcs.rigor.ec (found while checking the audit's typos).
- `dq.ecnf.source` (Typo): 'we computed' for 'were computed', the same sentence as in rcs.source.ec (found while checking the audit's typos).
- `dq.mf.bianchi.source` (Typo): A doubled 'http://' in two links.
- `ec.analytic_sha_order` (Error found while formalising): r is the analytic rank, but the link goes to the Mordell-Weil rank.
- `ec.bad_reduction` (Error or typo): The linked discriminant is that of a Weierstrass equation, and for an equation that is not minimal at 𝔭 the criterion fails: y² = x³ − 81x (Δ = 2⁶·3¹²) is an equation of the curve y² = x³ − x (conductor 32), which has good reduction at 3. The criterion holds for the discriminant of a local minimal model at 𝔭, equivalently for the minimal discriminant ideal.
- `ec.bsdconjecture` (Error found while formalising): The legend describes Reg(E/K), but the formula uses Reg_NT(E/K) = [K:ℚ]ʳ Reg(E/K) (`ec.regulator`), and the two differ when K ≠ ℚ and the rank is positive. Also "of vanishing" is repeated.
- `ec.canonical_height` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): The definition uses the Weil height h(x) of nf.weil_height, which is the absolute height (already divided by [K:Q]); with it, lim n^{-2} h(x(nP)) is already invariant under base change, so "This definition gives the non-normalised height" and the normalised height (1/[K:Q]) ĥ(P) are inconsistent with the link. Either say that h is the height relative to K, i.e. [K:Q] times the absolute Weil height, or drop the division by [K:Q].
- `ec.congruent_number_curve` (Error or typo): For y² = x(x² + ax + b) the quotient by (0, 0) is y² = x(x² − 2ax + a² − 4b). The kernel (0, 0) gives [0,0,0,4n²,0], and moving (∓n, 0) to the origin gives a = ∓3n, b = 2n², hence [0,±6n,0,n²,0]; for n = 1, x = X ∓ 2 turns [0,±6,0,1,0] into [0,0,0,−11,±14], the other two curves of the isogeny class of conductor 32. The stated [0,12n,0,n²,0] has Δ = 2240n⁶ = 2⁶·5·7·n⁶, so for n = 1 it has bad reduction at 5 and 7 and is not isogenous to E₁.
- `ec.congruent_number_problem` (Error or typo): If a = A², a + n = B² and a − n = C², then (B + C)² + (B − C)² = 2(a + n) + 2(a − n) = 4a = (2A)² and (B + C)(B − C) = 2n, so the hypotenuse 2A comes last. The knowl's order fails X² + Y² = Z² and XY = 2n: for n = 6 and a = 25/4 it gives (5, 4, 3), and 25 + 16 ≠ 9.
- `ec.discriminant` (Error or typo): Link error: "Weierstrass coefficients" links to ec.q.minimal_weierstrass_equation (minimal equations of curves over ℚ), while the knowl is about a Weierstrass equation over any field, whose coefficients ec.weierstrass_coeffs defines.
- `ec.galois_rep_elladic_image` (Error or typo): For an elliptic curve E over a number field K the ℓ-adic Galois representation is a representation of G_K = Gal(K̄/K); G_ℚ does not act on E[ℓ^∞] unless K = ℚ. "by by" is a typo.
- `ec.galois_rep_modell_image` (Error or typo): Sutherland's integers a, b, c are nonnegative (arXiv:1504.07618, §6.4: "(optional) nonnegative integers"), and a = 0 occurs: 5Cn.0.1, with surjective determinant (Table 5), and 7Nn.0.1.1[2]. G is listed among the classes of the subgroups that do not contain SL(2, 𝔽_ℓ) but is never defined: in the paper G is the class of the subgroups that contain SL₂ (labels ℓG and ℓG[d]), and the knowl's later list of possibilities rightly omits it (checked against the paper in the round of 1 November).
- `ec.intrinsic_torsion` (Error found while formalising; Error found while formalising (for the editors to decide)): X is not defined (the divisors are on E), and n must be nonzero since the value involves 1/n. The choice of D is in the list below. Also: The pairing is defined using a choice of D as well as of n and f, so the statement that it "is independent of n and f" should also cover D; check how the cited paper states it.
- `ec.isogeny` (Error found while formalising): Typo.
- `ec.isogeny_graph` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): Read literally, every isogeny of prime degree is an edge, so φ and −φ give separate edges, as do φ and its dual. The text should say which isogenies give the same edge (for instance isogenies up to automorphisms of source and target, with or without identifying an isogeny with its dual, or one edge for each pair of vertices and each prime ℓ for which an ℓ-isogeny between them exists) and whether endomorphisms of prime degree give loops. The readings differ under CM over the base field: on y² = x³ − x over ℚ(i), 2 + i and 2 − i are endomorphisms of degree 5 with different kernels, not related by automorphisms and each the dual of the other, giving two 5-loops if edges are isogenies up to automorphisms, and one if duals are identified or edges are counted per pair of vertices and prime.
- `ec.local_minimal_model` (Wrong Mathlib link): `WeierstrassCurve.minimal` is a chosen minimal model (`Classical.choose`); the property of being a local minimal model is `WeierstrassCurve.IsMinimal`.
- `ec.maximal_galois_rep` (Error or typo): When ℓ ramifies in O, the absolute Galois group of the CM field acts on E[ℓ] through Aut_O(E[ℓ]) ≅ (O/ℓO)^×, of order ℓ(ℓ − 1), so the image of Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) has order at most 2ℓ(ℓ − 1), less than the order ℓ(ℓ − 1)² of a Borel subgroup once ℓ ≥ 5 (for example ℓ = 7 for CM by ℤ[(1+√−7)/2]). For maximal ρ̄ the image is generated by Aut_O(E[ℓ]) and complex conjugation, a conjugate of the group of matrices (a b; 0 ±a), which is the whole Borel subgroup only for ℓ ≤ 3.
- `ec.mordell_weil_group` (Error or typo): E(K) is finitely generated when K is a number field (the Mordell–Weil theorem, as the knowl says below), but not over every field: E(ℝ) is uncountable, and E(ℚ̄) is divisible with torsion subgroup (ℚ/ℤ)².
- `ec.mw_generators` (Error found while formalising): A ℤ-basis and a minimal set of generators are not the same: in ℤ/2 × ℤ/4 the points (1,1) and (0,1) generate but are not independent, and ℤ/6 = ℤ/2 ⊕ ℤ/3 has a basis of two elements but is cyclic. The generators meant are a basis with one torsion element for each invariant factor of the torsion subgroup.
- `ec.period` (Error found while formalising): The integrals use ω_E, which is not defined; the differential defined is ω_v. When Δ(E_v) > 0, E_v(ℝ) has two components and |∫ ω| depends on how they are oriented (the two integrals can cancel); the value 2x given next is ∫ |ω_v|.
- `ec.q` (Error or typo): A minimal Weierstrass equation is unique only up to the changes of variables with u = ±1 and r, s, t ∈ ℤ: 37.a1, y² + y = x³ − x, and its translate by x ↦ x + 1, y² + y = x³ + 3x² + 2x, are both minimal, with Δ = 37. As `ec.q.minimal_weierstrass_equation` says, the reduced minimal equation is unique.
- `ec.q.abc_quality` (Error or typo): The abc conjecture omits a + b = c and is false as written: the triples (2^n, 1, 1) are relatively prime, of quality n.
- `ec.q.analytic_sha_order` (Error found while formalising): Spelling, as in the other knowls (the section 5 row for this knowl repeats the misspelling).
- `ec.q.analytic_sha_value` (Typo): 'can been computed' for 'can be computed'.
- `ec.q.bsd_invariants` (Typo; Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): Word order: 'an elliptic $E$ curve' (found while checking the audit's note on this knowl). Also: The analytic order of Sha is defined by the BSD formula (ec.analytic_sha_order), so with it in the list the leading-coefficient half of the conjecture holds by definition; the conjecture is about the order of the Tate-Shafarevich group itself, as ec.q.bsdconjecture states. The editors may instead list #Sha.
- `ec.q.canonical_height` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): Over a number field K the last sentence computes ĥ with the Weil height h of nf.weil_height, the absolute height (divided by [K:ℚ]), which gives the normalised canonical height, invariant under base change; ec.canonical_height calls the value of the same formula the non-normalised height. The editors should say which h is meant (the height relative to K, [K:ℚ] times the absolute one, or the absolute height), consistently with ec.canonical_height. Over ℚ the two readings agree.
- `ec.q.cremona_label` (Error or typo): False for class 990h, whose optimal curve is 990h3 (ec.q.optimal); and that curve number 1 is optimal has been proved for all conductors up to 400000 and in many other cases, but not in general (ec.q.optimal).
- `ec.q.frey` (Error or typo): The roots 0, A and −B of x(x − A)(x + B) are distinct exactly when A, B and C = A + B are nonzero (the discriminant is 16A²B²C²). For A = 0 and B = C = 1 the equation is y² = x²(x + 1), a nodal cubic, not an elliptic curve.
- `ec.q.minimal_twist` (Error found while formalising): The two values are swapped: 32.a3 is Y² = X³ − X, the equation the knowl gives, with Δ = 2⁶, and 32.a4 is Y² = X³ + 4X, with Δ = −2¹² (also checked in Lean with `norm_num` on Mathlib's `WeierstrassCurve.Δ`). With the correction, "smaller discriminant" holds in absolute value, as in the 27.a paragraph.
- `ec.q.minimal_weierstrass_equation` (Error or typo): Over all Weierstrass models, rational ones included, |Δ| has no minimum: the change of variables x = u²x′, y = u³y′ divides Δ by u¹², so as written no equation is minimal. The minimum is meant over the integral models introduced in the first sentence.
- `ec.q.naive_height` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): As a quantity of the curve, max(4|a₄|³, 27|a₆|²) depends on the short equation: the change of variables x = u²x′, y = u³y′ replaces (a₄, a₆) by (u⁻⁴a₄, u⁻⁶a₆) and divides it by u¹², so every curve has rational short equations of arbitrarily small height. The knowl should say which equation is meant; the usual one (as in Balakrishnan, Ho, Kaplan, Spicer, Stein and Weigandt) is the unique short equation with a₄, a₆ ∈ ℤ and no prime p such that p⁴ | a₄ and p⁶ | a₆.
- `ec.q.reduction_type` (Error or typo): Typo: "a curves" should read "a curve".
- `ec.q.serre_invariants` (Error or typo): Multiplying by the Hasse invariant E_{l-1} (and Deligne-Serre lifting) gives eigenforms of weight k + l - 1 at level M with the same mod-l representation, so the weight is not unique; the Serre weight is the minimal one. Also: Two errors besides the uniqueness claim recorded in an earlier check. (1) Weight 1 occurs for ℓ = 2: for E: y² = x³ − x − 1, ρ̄_{E,2} is the S₃-representation cut out by the Hilbert class field of ℚ(√−23), unramified at 2 and of conductor 23, and the weight-1 newform η(τ)η(23τ) of level 23 has the same mod-2 representation, so the least weight at the least level is 1, against "the Serre weight k is divisible by 2". Serre's convention takes newforms of weight k ≥ 2 (his invariants here are (2, 23)), so the minimal weight in the in an earlier check correction must be taken among k ≥ 2. (2) The exceptional primes include primes ℓ > 7 of good reduction: E: y² = x(x − 3¹³)(x + 1) has Δ = 16·3²⁶·(3¹³ + 1)² and c₄ = 16(3²⁶ + 3¹³ + 1), so it has good reduction at 13 (3¹³ + 1 ≡ 4 mod 13) and minimal multiplicative reduction at 3 with v₃(Δ) = 26. ρ̄_{E,13} is irreducible (a rational 13-isogeny together with the rational 2-isogenies would give a cyclic 26-isogeny, which Mazur and Kenku exclude) and unramified at 3 as 13 | 26, so by Ribet's level lowering (3 ≢ 1 mod 13) it arises at level N/3 and its Serre conductor is not N.
- `ec.q.szpiro_ratio` (Error found while formalising): The ratio depends on the model (c₄³ and c₆² both scale by u⁻¹²), so c₄ and c₆ must come from a minimal model; and Δ can be negative, so the second ratio needs log |Δ|.
- `ec.rank` (Wrong Mathlib link): The Mordell-Weil group is additive in Mathlib, so the rank is the additive twin `AddCommGroup.freeRank` (generated on the same page).
- `ec.reduction_type` (Error or typo): The knowl does not say which equation is reduced, and the type depends on it: modulo a prime p ∤ 62, y² = x³ + p⁴x + p⁶ reduces to the cusp y² = x³, while the same curve, y² = x³ + x + 1 after scaling, has good reduction at p. As in `ec.q.reduction_type`, the reduction is that of an equation minimal at 𝔭. Also "are as follows" has a stray "are".
- `ec.scheme` (Error or typo): An elliptic scheme (an elliptic curve over S in the sense of Katz and Mazur) comes with a zero section, which fibres that are elliptic curves do not provide. Over two copies of ℙ¹ glued at two points, glue E × U₁ and E × U₂ (Uᵢ the complement of the i-th node) by the identity over one component of the overlap and by a translation by a point P ≠ 0 over the other: every fibre is E, but there is no section, since each Uᵢ maps constantly to E.
- `ec.simple_equation` (Error or typo): Typo: "have" is missing.
- `ec.tamagawa_number` (Error found while formalising): K is never introduced, and the reduction of a point depends on the model: E⁰ is defined using a minimal model at 𝔭.
- `ec.torsion_subgroup` (Error or typo): Over an arbitrary field the torsion subgroup can be infinite, and is then not a product of two cyclic groups: E(ℚ̄)_tor ≅ (ℚ/ℤ)², and E(ℝ)_tor is ℚ/ℤ or ℚ/ℤ × ℤ/2. When it is finite it lies in some E[N], so it is generated by two elements. Also, as [n] is used only for n > 1, Mazur's list should include the trivial structure [].
- `ec.twists` (Error found while formalising; Error or typo): Typo. Also: The automorphism group over K̄ of such a curve is nonabelian (of order 24 in characteristic 2 and 12 in characteristic 3), but over K it need not be: over 𝔽₂, y² + y = x³ has only the automorphisms (x, y) ↦ (x, y) and (x, y) ↦ (x, y + 1). The H¹ that follows also takes Aut(E) over K̄.
- `g2c.aut_grp` (Error found while formalising; Suggested category: ag): For y² + h(x)y = f(x) the hyperelliptic involution is (x, y) ↦ (x, −y − h(x)). On 169.a.169.1, y² + (x³ + x + 1)y = x⁵ + x⁴, the map as written sends the point (0, −1) to (0, 1), which is not on the curve. — Suggested recategorisation: Covers the automorphism group of any algebraic curve (its title, its current Background chapter, and ec.twists links to it); only a remark on the hyperelliptic involution is specific to genus 2. Another possible category: `g2c`. Confidence: medium.
- `g2c.conditional_mw_group` (Typo; Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): 'In cases were' for 'In cases where' (in the audit's quote); the first paragraph ends with a comma. Also: The hypotheses do not give the conclusion. Let r be the Mordell-Weil rank, l <= r a known lower bound and u an upper bound on the analytic rank with l = u - 1, where u has the parity given by the root number. The parity conjecture gives r = u mod 2, hence r >= u, but no upper bound on r: that needs BSD (r is the analytic rank, at most u) or an upper bound on r itself, for example from a Selmer group. With a lower bound that is one less than an upper bound on the Mordell-Weil rank, the parity conjecture does determine r, which is what the suggested text says. Also a lower bound 'on the Mordell-Weil group' should be on its rank.
- `g2c.conductor` (Typo): Malformed HTML: both rows of the table end with "</td</tr>" instead of "</td></tr>".
- `g2c.discriminant` (Error or typo; Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): Rechecked in round AI0; the pair is unchanged and the reason corrected. The substitution y -> y + t(x) changes (f, h) to (f - t^2 - ht, h + 2t), which fixes f + h^2/4 but not f, so the leading coefficient must be that of f + h^2/4. For example 3125.a.3125.1, y^2 + y = x^5, has Delta = 3125, but its equation y^2 + (4x^3 + 1)y = -4x^6 + x^5 - 2x^3 (from t = 2x^3) gets 50000 from the formula as written. The two readings agree on the LMFDB's reduced equations, whose h has coefficients 0 and 1, but not because deg h <= 2, as the earlier entry said: 169.a.169.1 has h = x^3 + x + 1 (lmfdb/genus2_curves/test_genus2_curves.py, line 312). When deg h = 3 the x^6 coefficient of f + h^2/4 is f_6 + 1/4, never 0, so the even case applies, which has no lc factor; when deg h <= 2, f and f + h^2/4 have the same leading coefficient, as deg f >= 5. Also: The two cases should read 'degree 5' and 'degree 6', with Delta = 0 when f + h^2/4 has lower degree (the discriminant of the binary sextic, which then has a double root at infinity).
