As written, degenerate equations get nonzero values, such as 65536 for y^2 = x^4 + 1 and 256 for y^2 + 2x^3y = -x^6 + x (genus 0 although deg h = 3). Recorded without pairs on the old page; the pairs are new in round AI0, so that the point stays with the editors when the entry is replaced. The editors may add the case Delta = 0.
- `g2c.galois_rep.non_maximal_primes` (Typo): The knowl refers to "the Jacobian of C" without introducing C.
- `g2c.galois_rep_image` (Error or typo): The knowl fixes a prime p but then works mod ℓ, with values in GSp(4, 𝔽_ℓ), and calls the representation ρ_{J,p}: one prime, ℓ, is meant. The link for the Galois representation goes to ec.galois_rep, the knowl for elliptic curves, instead of g2c.galois_rep.
- `g2c.galois_rep_modell_image` (Typo): "an genus 2 curve" should be "a genus 2 curve".
- `g2c.igusa_clebsch_invariants` (Error or typo): Multiplying I_{2k} by (−i)^k makes I_2 non-real; the sign change is by (−1)^k = i^{2k}.
- `g2c.igusa_invariants` (Error or typo): This knowl defines J₂, …, J₁₀, but the normalisation paragraphs use the Igusa–Clebsch names I₂ₖ, in the second paragraph and (for J₁₀) in the fourth. Also: Same (−i)^k error as g2c.igusa_clebsch_invariants; also the Igusa invariants are J_{2k} (weights 1..5), not I_{2k}, and "nonnegative" should be "positive". Also: With I₂, …, I₁₀ computed from f as in `g2c.igusa_clebsch_invariants`, J₁₀ = I₁₀/4096 = disc(f)/4096, which for the integral sextic f = x⁶ − 1 is 46656/4096 = 729/64. Integrality holds for the sextic 4f₀ + h₀² of an integral equation y² + h₀(x)y = f₀(x) (for y² = x⁶ − 1 that is 4x⁶ − 4, with J₁₀ = 2⁸·46656).
- `g2c.label` (Typo): The last sentence lacks its full stop.
- `g2c.minimal_equation` (Error found while formalising; Error or typo): y has weight g + 1, so y² and f(x,z) have weighted degree 2g + 2; 6 is the case g = 2. Also: With `ag.hyperelliptic_curve`'s definition (a 2-to-1 map to ℙ¹ over the algebraic closure), a hyperelliptic curve over ℚ has a Weierstrass equation over ℚ only if its canonical conic has a rational point. For odd g this can fail: the genus 3 curve w² = q(x, y, z) on the conic x² + y² + z² = 0 (q a general quartic form) has no Weierstrass equation over ℚ. For even g, in particular g = 2, the conic always has a rational point.
- `g2c.mw_generator` (Error or typo): On y² − yz³ = x⁵z (with weights 1, 3, 1), z = 0 forces y = 0, so (0:1:0) is not on the curve (y² = 1 ≠ 0); the only point at infinity is (1:0:0).
- `g2c.num_rat_wpts` (Error or typo; Suggested category: ag): In characteristic 2 a hyperelliptic curve has at most g + 1 Weierstrass points, not 2g + 2. A model y² = f(x) with deg f = 2g + 2 needs a rational point of ℙ¹ that is not a branch point, which a finite field may lack (all four points of ℙ¹(𝔽₃) are branch points of y² = x⁵ − x), and over ℚ a curve of odd genus whose canonical conic has no rational point has no model y² = f(x) at all. Exactly 2g + 1 rational Weierstrass points never occur, since if 2g + 1 roots of f are rational so is the last; over other fields fewer counts occur (over ℝ only even ones). — Suggested recategorisation: Weierstrass points of hyperelliptic curves of any genus; it belongs next to ag.hyperelliptic_curve.
- `g2c.st_group` (Error or typo): USp(4) occurs exactly when the geometric endomorphism ring End(J_ℚ̄) is ℤ. A Jacobian with End(J) = ℤ over ℚ but extra endomorphisms over ℚ̄ has a smaller identity component, so its Sato–Tate group is not USp(4): for example, real multiplication defined only over a quadratic field gives ST⁰ = SU(2) × SU(2). g2c.galois_rep.non_maximal_primes itself says "geometric endomorphism ring ℤ, equivalently, curves with Sato-Tate group USp(4)".
- `g2c.st_group_identity_component` (Typo; Duplicate): Typo: "ellliptic". — Duplicate: Duplicates `st_group.identity_component`: repeats it for abelian surfaces.
- `gg.concentrated` (Error or typo): By `gg.index`, ind(σ) = n − (number of cycles), so the identity has index 0 and is the only element of minimal index; it generates the trivial subgroup, so as written every nontrivial transitive group is concentrated. The minimum must be taken over the non-identity elements, as in `gg.malle_a` (e ≠ g).
- `gg.degree` (Error or typo): For an inseparable irreducible polynomial the Galois group permutes fewer than deg(f) roots: f = X^p − t over 𝔽_p(t) has a single root and trivial Galois group, a transitive group of degree 1, not p. `gg.galois_group` and `gg.group_action_invariants` already say "irreducible separable".
- `gg.group_action_invariants` (Error or typo): A transitive action need not be faithful, and then it is not isomorphic to the action of a subgroup of S_n: S₃ acts transitively on two points through the sign, but S₃ is isomorphic to no subgroup of S₂. The Galois action on the roots described next is faithful.
- `gg.malle_b` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): gg.malle_a gives a(G) = 0 for the trivial group, so the formula b(G) = #{C : ind(C) = a(G)⁻¹} asks for 0⁻¹ there; the second description (the non-identity rational classes of minimal index) gives b(G) = 0.
- `gg.resolvents` (Typo): Grammatical slips: "Let K/F is finite", "let let", "the other fields are in a collection are", "reputation" for representation, and "has is".
- `gg.semiconcentrated` (Error or typo): By `gg.index` the identity is the unique element of minimal index 0, and its normal closure {e} is proper, so as written every nontrivial transitive group is semiconcentrated, including S₃ on 3 points, whose non-identity elements of least index (the transpositions) have normal closure S₃. The minimum must be taken over the non-identity elements, as in `gg.malle_a`.
- `gl2.borel` (Error found while formalising; Error or typo): A non-diagonal subgroup of the upper triangular group need not contain an element of order p: for p = 3, the matrix with rows (1, 1) and (0, 2) generates a group of order 2. A subgroup of order prime to p is conjugate into the diagonal subgroup, but need not lie in it. Also: The sentence on the label B has no full stop.
- `gl2.cartan` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): For R = 0 the algebra A is 0 and both groups are trivial, so the index is 1; the claim needs R nonzero (proved in LeanBridge for every nonzero ring).
- `gl2.label` (Error or typo): The subgroups are ordered inside GL₂(ℤ/Nℤ), N being the level; n is the label's last component.
- `gl2.nonsplit_cartan` (Error or typo): Sutherland's labels Cn.a.b allow a = 0: 5Cn.0.1 (arXiv:1504.07618, Table 5, with surjective determinant) is the subgroup generated by the matrix with rows (0, 2) and (1, 0), as ε = 2. Found in round ZR. "minimally chosen": the LMFDB has 23Cn.1.11, while 23Cn.1.5 names the same group. The code of Sutherland's script first restricts to generators g with (tr g)²/det g − 2 the trace of a fixed primitive root of unity; the paper and the script's comment say lexicographically minimal. Suggested: "chosen by Sutherland's algorithm, minimal among the generators g with (tr g)²/det g − 2 the trace of a fixed primitive root of unity".
- `gl2.normalizer_cartan` (Error found while formalising): The normalizer of a split Cartan subgroup is not maximal for p = 3, where it has order 8 and lies in a Sylow 2-subgroup of order 16, nor for p = 5, where its image in PGL₂(𝔽₅) ≅ S₅ is a dihedral group of order 8 inside an S₄, so that it lies in a subgroup of order 96. A brute-force check finds it maximal for 7 ≤ p ≤ 13, and the non-split normalizer maximal for 3 ≤ p ≤ 13.
- `gl2.normalizer_nonsplit_cartan` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): The knowl describes only the labels Nn and Nn.a.b, but Sutherland also uses labels Nn.a.b.c with three integers (arXiv:1504.07618, §6.4 and Corollary 3.17: the subgroup generated by the matrix with rows (a, εb) and (b, a) and by diag(1, −1)·δ^c, for a generator δ of Cn), already for subgroups with surjective determinant (5Nn.1.1.1, Table 5). Found in round ZR. "minimally chosen": the LMFDB has 17Nn.3.7.1, while 17Nn.1.1.1 names a conjugate for the same c. The code of Sutherland's script first restricts to generators g with (tr g)²/det g − 2 the trace of a fixed primitive root of unity; the paper and the script's comment say lexicographically minimal. Suggested: "chosen by Sutherland's algorithm, minimal among the generators g with (tr g)²/det g − 2 the trace of a fixed primitive root of unity". Also: Suggested text, drafted 2026-11-01.
- `gl2.normalizer_split_cartan` (Error found while formalising; Error or typo): Not maximal for p = 3 or p = 5; see `gl2.normalizer_cartan`. Also: Found in round ZR. The clause of Ns.a.b.c says "where a and b are minimally chosen" and leaves out c, one of the integers of the label. "where a and b are minimally chosen positive integers": the stored labels do not minimise b. The LMFDB has 13Ns.5.2, while 13Ns.5.1 names a conjugate of the same group (also 17Ns.2.3, 19Ns.8.4, 31Ns.15.5, 37Ns.8.2). Suggested: "where a, b (and c) are positive integers chosen by Sutherland's algorithm, in the conjugate of the group containing the matrix with rows (0, 1), (1, 0) (or the corresponding matrix of [Corollary 3.18])".
- `gl2.open` (Error or typo): Typo: a doubled "a".
- `group.abelian_invariants` (Error or typo): An infinite abelian group such as ℤ or ℚ is not isomorphic to a finite product of finite cyclic groups, so it has neither list of invariants. For finitely generated groups one could instead add the free rank.
- `group.affine_linear_automorphism` (Error or typo): A semi-direct product depends on the action of A, which the knowl does not give (`group.linear_automorphism` does: entry-wise on GL(n,q)), and the choice matters: for n = 1 and q = 4 the entry-wise action gives AΓL(1,4) ≅ S₄, while the trivial action gives A₄ × C₂.
- `group.almost_simple` (Error or typo): The sentence says that quasisimple groups need not be almost simple, but the link lists the converse, almost simple groups that are not quasisimple (group.quasisimple has the mirror error).
- `group.autjugate_subgroup` (Error or typo): The automorphism must send H₁ to H₂.
- `group.chief_series` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): That each factor N_{i+1}/N_i is a product of copies of a single simple group holds for finite groups, the LMFDB's setting, but the knowl starts "If G is a group"; whether it can fail for an infinite group with a chief series was left open, so the replacement only makes the finiteness assumption explicit. The infinite case is settled: in Q^2 ⋊ SL(2, Q) the chief series 1 < Q^2 < Q^2 ⋊ {±1} < G has the factor Q^2, which is not a power of a simple group, so the claim needs G finite.
- `group.complete` (Error or typo): The map from G onto Inn(G) is always surjective with kernel the centre, so this condition only says that the centre is trivial, as it is for A₄, A₅ and S₆, which are not complete. The equivalent condition is that the natural map to the full automorphism group is an isomorphism.
- `group.computing_subgroup_labels` (Typo): Spelling: "Gassman" for Gassmann. For the editors to decide: the 'permutation representation signatures' used to break ties are never defined, in this knowl or in a linked one.
- `group.dicyclic` (Wrong Mathlib link; Error or typo): DihedralGroup is the dihedral group; Mathlib's dicyclic group is QuaternionGroup (its docstring: "the (generalised) quaternion group of order 4n, also known as dicyclic group"). Also: The definition does not determine the group: C₄ₙ, and for n = 6 also C₃ ⋊ C₈, are non-split extensions of C₂ₙ by C₂ too. The action must be inversion.
- `group.dihedral` (Error or typo): LaTeX typo: the powers of g are written as subscripts.
- `group.direct_product` (Error or typo): Typo: "a direct factors".
- `group.elementary` (Error or typo): For the trivial group no prime divides |G|, so the parenthesis allows no elementary subgroup and the trivial character is no combination of induced characters.
- `group.fitting_subgroup` (Error or typo): The product of normal nilpotent subgroups is nilpotent only for finitely many of them (Fitting's theorem); for infinite groups the Fitting subgroup need not be nilpotent.
- `group.frobenius` (Error or typo): For q = p^k with k ≥ 2 the Sylow p-subgroup of F_q is the translation group (𝔽_q, +) ≅ C_p^k, which is not cyclic, so F_q is not a Z-group; it is not metacyclic either, since every nontrivial normal subgroup of F_q contains the translations (F_4 ≅ A_4, F_8 ≅ C_2^3 ⋊ C_7). F_q is solvable for every q, and is a Z-group, hence metacyclic, when q is prime.
- `group.fuchsian` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): The covolume integrates over 'the fundamental domain' of G, linked to group.fuchsian.fundamental_domain, which defines (closed) fundamental domains only for subgroups of the modular group, so 'first kind' is undefined for other Fuchsian groups, such as the cocompact ones; fundamental domains are also not unique. Either extend that knowl to all Fuchsian groups (e.g. Dirichlet domains, whose boundaries have measure zero), or define covol(G) here through any measurable set meeting almost every G-orbit exactly once, writing 'a fundamental domain' and noting that the integral does not depend on the choice.
- `group.fuchsian.cusps.width` (Error or typo; Suggested category: cmf): Since T^0 = I lies in Γ, and T^(−w) lies in Γ whenever T^w does, 'the smallest number w' is 0 or does not exist; the width is the smallest positive such integer. With γ ∈ Γ, γ⁻¹Γγ = Γ and γ∞ is Γ-equivalent to ∞, so only the cusps equivalent to ∞ would get a width, that of ∞; γ must be taken in SL₂(ℤ), which moves ∞ to any x ∈ ℙ¹(ℚ). — Suggested recategorisation: The width of a cusp of a subgroup of SL(2,Z) is used for Fourier expansions of classical modular forms (cmf.fouriercoefficients) and Poincare series and belongs next to the cusps knowl (modcurve.cusp_widths is its adelic analogue). Another possible category: `modcurve`. Confidence: medium.
- `group.fuchsian.fundamental_domain` (Error found while formalising; Suggested category: cmf): A fundamental domain is a subset of ℋ ∪ ℚ ∪ {∞}, not an element of it. — Suggested recategorisation: This defines a fundamental domain for a subgroup of the modular group acting on H (cited by cmf.petersson_scalar_product), part of the classical SL(2,Z) setup rather than abstract group theory. Another possible category: `mf`. Confidence: medium.
- `group.group_mathlib_defn` (Outdated Mathlib link): `Monoid` moved from `Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Defs.lean` to `Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Monoid.lean`.
- `group.haar_measure` (Error or typo): A left Haar measure is right-invariant only for unimodular groups (for example compact, abelian or discrete ones), and on a non-compact group it takes the value ∞. The proposed "Radon (finite on compact sets)" should also require the measure to be regular: on groups that are not sigma-compact, uniqueness up to a scalar needs regularity (the discrete reals times the reals carry two non-proportional Haar measures).
- `group.isoclinism` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): With group.derived_series' derived length (the index where the derived series becomes stationary, defined for every finite group), the claim fails: A₅ (length 0) and A₅ × C₂ (length 1) are isoclinic. It holds for solvable groups. More precisely (round AL, proved in LeanBridge): with group.derived_series' derived length, invariance holds between two isoclinic groups exactly when both are perfect or both are not (S₅ and S₅ × C₂ agree; A₅ and A₅ × C₂ do not). A wording that keeps that case, instead of the recorded one: replace "but {{KNOWL('group.nilpotent', 'nilpotency class')}} and {{KNOWL('group.derived_series', 'solvable length')}} are (except for the trivial group)." by "but {{KNOWL('group.nilpotent', 'nilpotency class')}} and {{KNOWL('group.derived_series', 'derived length')}} are (except for the trivial group), the latter between groups that are both {{KNOWL('group.perfect', 'perfect')}} or both not."
- `group.label_conjugacy_class` (Typo): "an enumeration of class" should be "an enumeration of the classes".
- `group.label_rational_group_char` (Error or typo): A rational character is not a class of elements, so "the order of elements in this class" (wording taken from group.label_conjugacy_class) means nothing here. In the database (table gps_qchar) o is cdim, the degree of the irreducible complex constituents of the rational character, not qdim, the degree of the rational character itself: 3.1.1b has qdim 2 and cdim 1, and 4.1.1c has qdim 2 and cdim 1.
- `group.lie_type` (Error or typo; Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): GU(n, q) preserves the standard hermitian form up to a scalar (the knowl's next sentence), so it is the conformal unitary group; the conformal symplectic group is GSp(n, q), the item before. Also: The knowl writes G for the conformal groups (GO, GSp, GU) and lists GSO among them two paragraphs below ('defined similarly for H = GO, GSO, ...'); CSO is Magma's name for the same group, and the site prints GSO (lmfdb/groups/abstract/main.py, FAMILY_NAME_ALIASES). Also: (a) Spin(n, q) is a finite group, not a manifold, and no double cover of SO(n, q): for q odd the two have the same order (the LMFDB has Spin(3, 5) = SL(2, 5) = 120.5 while SO(3, 5) = S_5 also has order 120, and Spin+(4, 3) = 576.5128 beside SO+(4, 3) = 576.8282). For q odd, Spin(n, q) is a double cover of Omega(n, q), the kernel of the spinor norm, of index 2 in SO(n, q); for q even it is isomorphic to Omega(n, q). (b) GO(n, q), Magma's CO, is the group of similitudes. It is the product of O(n, q) and the scalars when n is odd or q is even, but for n even and q odd the multiplier of a similitude can be a non-square and the index is 2: by enumeration |O+(4, 3)| = 1152 and |GO+(4, 3)| = 2304, |O-(4, 3)| = 1440 and |GO-(4, 3)| = 2880 (the LMFDB's 1152.157478, 2304.a, 1440.5842 and 2880.a), while the scalars +-1 lie in O. In the database plain GO(n, q) has n odd, but the knowl defines GO+ and GO- 'similarly'. The suggested sentence is the one the knowl uses for GSp and GU; it also repairs the grammar ('denotes ... consists of'). (c) The four groups are semilinear groups, as group.linear_automorphism says of the first two, not automorphism groups. Aut(PGL(n, q)) is larger than PGammaL(n, q) for n >= 3, by the inverse-transpose automorphism (|Aut(PGL(3, 2))| = 336, |PGammaL(3, 2)| = 168). Aut(PSL(n, q)) is PSigmaL(n, q) only for n = 2 and q even (PSigmaL(2, 5) = A_5 with Aut(A_5) = S_5; |PSigmaL(2, 9)| = 720 and |Aut(A_6)| = 1440). Aut(PSp(n, q)) is PSigmaSp(n, q) only for q even and n not 4 (the LMFDB has PSigmaSp(2, 5) = 60.5 = A_5). Aut(PGU(n, q)) = PGammaU(n, q) does hold for n >= 3, but not for n = 2 (|PGammaU(2, 2)| = 12, |Aut(PGU(2, 2))| = |Aut(S_3)| = 6). The orders of these automorphism groups were computed by brute force. The editors may also want another heading than 'Automorphism Groups'.
- `group.linear` (Error or typo): PGL(n, K) acts on the projective space of lines in Kⁿ, which has dimension n − 1; the automorphism group of projective n-space ℙⁿ(K) is PGL(n + 1, K).
- `group.maximal_quotient` (Error or typo): As written K = 1 satisfies the condition (the only H ≤ 1 is H = 1 = K), so G = G/1 would be a maximal quotient of G, and 1 a minimal normal subgroup; minimal normal subgroups are nontrivial by convention.
- `group.maximal_subgroup` (Error or typo): As written M = G satisfies the condition (the only H with G ⊆ H ⊆ G is H = G = M), so every group would be a maximal subgroup of itself; maximal subgroups are proper by convention.
- `group.metabelian` (Error or typo; Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): Groups of p-rank one need not be metabelian, or even solvable: A₅ has cyclic Sylow 3- and 5-subgroups, so its 3-rank and 5-rank are one, and SL(2, 5) has p-rank one for each prime p dividing its order, its Sylow subgroups being Q₈, C₃ and C₅. The claim holds for p-groups of p-rank one, which are cyclic or generalised quaternion. Also 'metacylic' is misspelt. Also: The text has a zero-width space (U+200B) inside 'extraspecial'; it may be a deliberate line-break hint.
- `group.min_faithful_linear` (Error or typo; Typo): Needs G finite: an infinite group need not be a matrix group of finite degree. Also: 'k-values character' should be 'k-valued character'.
- `group.minimal_normal` (Error or typo): As written the trivial subgroup satisfies the condition (the only H ≤ 1 is H = 1), so 1 would be a minimal normal subgroup of every group; minimal normal subgroups are nontrivial by convention.
- `group.name` (Error or typo; Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): The description of OD_n as 'the non-trivial semidirect product C_{2^{k-1}} : C_2 which is not isomorphic to either SD_n or D_{2^{k-1}}' fails for k = 3: C_4 has one non-trivial automorphism, so the only non-trivial C_4 : C_2 is D_4, and OD_8 is isomorphic to it; for k ≤ 2 there is no non-trivial product. For k ≥ 4 it is proved in LeanBridge (round AI). The same range is recorded for group.other_dihedral. Also: For consistency with the corrected OD_n, the range of SD_n could be stated too: the line asserts nothing, but with the usual presentation SD_8 is abelian (recorded for group.semi_dihedral).
- `group.nonsplit_product` (Error or typo): Every surjection of groups has a set-theoretic section, so the existence of a section is no condition; the equivalence with a complement holds for a homomorphic section (a splitting). Also "a extension" should be "an extension".
- `group.omega` (Typo; Error or typo): Typo: in "The groups PΩ(n,q) are PΩ^±(n,q) are" the first "are" should be "and". Also: For n = 1 the group SO(1, q) is trivial, so Ω(1, q) = SO(1, q) has index 1, not 2. For odd n ≥ 3 and odd q the spinor norm is onto (𝔽_q^×)/(𝔽_q^×)², so the index is 2. Also: Typo: the first 'are' of the last paragraph should be 'and'. Also: For odd q every orthogonal g satisfies det g = (−1)^(n − dim Fix g), so for even n the quasideterminant g ↦ (−1)^(dim Fix g) equals det g and is identically 1 on SO^±(n,q): its kernel is all of SO^±(n,q), not the index-2 spinor-norm kernel Ω^±(n,q) (as group.lie_type says). For example, in SO^+(4,3) the element acting as −1 on one hyperbolic plane and as 1 on the other fixes a 2-dimensional subspace but has spinor norm −1, a nonsquare mod 3; enumerating O^+(4,3) gives |SO^+(4,3)| = 576 but |Ω^+(4,3)| = 288. The quasideterminant description is right only for even q (it is the Dickson invariant there), and "fixing an even-dimensional subspace" should read "whose fixed subspace has even dimension", since every g fixes the zero subspace.
- `group.orthogonal` (Error or typo): For q odd there are two isometry classes of nondegenerate quadratic forms in odd dimension, distinguished by the discriminant; scaling by a non-square swaps them, so they form one similarity class, which is what makes GO(n, q) unique. Also: The counts of classes (one for odd n, two for even n) and the uniqueness of GO(n, q) and GO^±(n, q) hold only for nondegenerate quadratic forms: the zero form, for instance, lies in a class of its own, and its orthogonal group is all of GL(n, q).
- `group.other_dihedral` (Error or typo): Needs k ≥ 4, as for group.semi_dihedral: OD₈ ≅ D₈.
- `group.perfect` (Error or typo): (ℚ, +) is abelian, hence not perfect, but has no non-trivial cyclic quotient, since every quotient of a divisible group is divisible. The abelian and soluble versions hold for all groups, the cyclic one for finite groups (a non-trivial finite abelian group has a quotient of prime order).
- `group.quasisimple` (Error or typo): The sentence says that almost simple groups need not be quasisimple, but the link lists the converse, quasisimple groups that are not almost simple (group.almost_simple has the mirror error).
- `group.radical` (Error or typo): For infinite groups a largest normal solvable subgroup need not exist: in the restricted direct product of solvable groups G_n of derived length n, each G_n is normal and solvable, but together they generate the whole group, which is not solvable. For finite groups the product of two normal solvable subgroups is normal and solvable, so the radical exists.
- `group.rank` (Imprecise (for the editors to decide)): "Often smaller" has no precise content. What holds is that the rank is at most the number of generators of a polycyclic presentation and can be smaller (S₄ has rank 2, while every polycyclic sequence of S₄ is longer).
- `group.representation.center` (Error or typo): For infinite groups the set need not be a subgroup: for ℤ acting on ℂ² by n ↦ diag((3/2)ⁿ, (1/2)ⁿ), the character χ(n) = (3/2)ⁿ + (1/2)ⁿ has absolute value 2, its value at the identity, only at n = 0 and n = 1. For finite G, |χ(g)| = χ(1) exactly when ρ(g) is scalar, and these g form a subgroup.
- `group.representation.character` (Typo): The character table consists of the character values χ(g), not the matrices ρ(g), and what ranges over the irreducible characters is χ, not the representation ρ; 'classees' should be 'classes'.
- `group.representation.cyclotomic_n` (Error or typo): For infinite groups ℚ(χ) need not be abelian, or even algebraic: ℤ acting on ℂ by n ↦ 2^(n/3) gives ℚ(χ) = ℚ(∛2), which is not Galois over ℚ, and n ↦ πⁿ gives a transcendental extension. For finite G the character values are sums of roots of unity, so ℚ(χ) lies in a cyclotomic field.
- `group.representation.irrep` (Error or typo): As written the zero representation (V = 0) has no nontrivial subspace and so is irreducible, and its zero character would be an irreducible character missing from the character table; irreducible representations are nonzero by convention. In the equivalence, σ⁻¹ρ(g)σ is not defined for σ : V → V′ (it applies ρ(g) to vectors of V′): the condition is ρ′(g) = σρ(g)σ⁻¹.
- `group.representation.kernel` (Error or typo): For groups with elements of infinite order the set need not be a subgroup: for ℤ acting on ℂ² by n ↦ diag((3/2)ⁿ, (1/2)ⁿ), the character χ(n) = (3/2)ⁿ + (1/2)ⁿ equals 2, its value at the identity, only at n = 0 and n = 1. For finite G, χ(g) = χ(1) exactly when ρ(g) = 1, so the set is the kernel of ρ.
- `group.representation.rational_character` (Error or typo): Rational characters are not closed under negation or under multiplication by rational numbers, so they do not form a ℚ-vector space; the irreducible rational characters are a ℚ-basis of their ℚ-span (the ℚ-valued class functions that are constant on the rational conjugacy classes). Also: For an irreducible character with rational values (the trivial character, say) the sum of its Galois conjugates is the character itself, which is irreducible, so irreducible rational characters need not be reducible as complex characters. Also 'is complex character' lacks an article, and 'each ... rational conjugacy classes' should be singular.
- `group.semi_dihedral` (Error or typo): Needs k ≥ 4: SD₈ is abelian (proved).
- `group.special_linear` (Error or typo): PSL(1, q) is trivial, hence not simple, so the range 'n > 2 or q > 3' is wrong for n = 1. PSL(n, q) is simple for n > 2, and for n = 2 when q > 3 (proved in LeanBridge: Matrix.ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup.isSimpleGroup_of_three_le_card and isSimpleGroup_fin).
- `group.spinor_norm` (Error or typo): For odd q a reflection has determinant −1, so it lies in GO(n, q), not SO(n, q). An element of SO(n, q) is a product of an even number k ≤ n of reflections (Cartan–Dieudonné), so k = n is impossible for odd n, and the spinor norm multiplies the values Q(v_i) of the vectors v_i defining the reflections r_i, not 'Q(r_i)'. For even q the target group is trivial and the factorisation can fail: the 6 reflections of GO⁺(4, 2), a group of order 72, generate a subgroup of order 36 (by enumeration).
- `group.stem_extension` (Error or typo; Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): K is a subgroup of C, so the center and commutator subgroup are those of C. Also: Clarification: the maximal size is taken among stem extensions of G, the extensions the sentence before bounds; among all central extensions the size of C is not bounded (round AM, where the maximal stem extensions are proved to have kernel H₂(G, ℤ)).
- `group.subgroup.diagram.lmfdb` (Typo): 'then' for 'than'.
- `group.subgroup_label` (Error or typo): Subgroups related by an automorphism of the ambient group share the part a but need not be Gassmann equivalent: in D₄ = ⟨r, s⟩ the automorphism r ↦ r, s ↦ rs swaps the Klein subgroups {1, r², s, r²s} and {1, r², rs, r³s}, which meet the conjugacy class {s, r²s} in 2 and 0 elements. So for a the letters order the Gassmann classes up to automorphism, in which conjugacy classes related by an automorphism are collected together (group.computing_subgroup_labels). The ordinal distinguishes subgroups, not groups, and the parenthesis "(in which case the first form is used, omitting the j." is not closed.
- `group.subgroup_properties_interdependencies` (Typo): A doubled word.
- `group.subgroups_beyond_bound` (Typo): 'or' for 'of', and a singular for a plural (found by the review of round AI). For the editors to decide: 'the same scheme described above' refers to nothing in the knowl; the labelling scheme it means is described in another knowl, which could be linked.
- `group.symplectic` (Error or typo): For even q a skew-symmetric matrix (Mᵀ = −M) is just a symmetric one, so Ω = I qualifies and {M : MᵀΩM = Ω} becomes an orthogonal group: over 𝔽₂ it has order 2 for n = 1 and 48 for n = 2 (by enumeration), against |Sp(2, 2)| = 6 and |Sp(4, 2)| = 720, which an alternating Ω gives. Ω must be alternating (zero diagonal), which for odd q is automatic. "for Ω is" is also ungrammatical.
- `group.type` (Error or typo): With $d_i>0$, factors $C_1$ can be added freely, so $n$ is not unique; the invariant factors must satisfy $d_i>1$. A group of prime order is both cyclic and simple, so both 'Cyclic' and 'Simple' apply to it: unlike the other items, 'If G is simple' does not exclude the earlier cases. If the database writes 'Cyclic' for groups of prime order, as the order of the items suggests, that item should read 'If G is non-abelian simple'; otherwise the first item must exclude them.
- `group.weight_function` (Error or typo): As written no non-trivial group has a weight function: n = 2·#G does not divide #G and g^n = 1, so w(g) = w(1) = 0 for every g, against condition 1 (in a group of order 6 already n = 4 gives w(g) = w(g⁴) = 0 for g of order 2). Invariance under invertible powering means n coprime to #G.
- `group.weyl_group` (Error or typo): For Lie groups that are not compact and connected, Z_G(T) = T fails: in G = ℝ × U(1), or in the compact but disconnected U(1) × C₂, the maximal torus T = U(1) is central, so Z_G(T) = G ≠ T. In a compact connected Lie group the maximal tori are conjugate, Z_G(T) = T, and N_G(T)/T is finite.
- `hgm.defining_parameters` (Error or typo): A pair g, −g in γ contributes (x^g − 1)/(x^g − 1) = 1, so the identity does not characterise γ: for A = [2], B = [1] both [−1, −1, 2] and [−3, −1, −1, 2, 3] give (x² − 1)/(x − 1)² = (x + 1)/(x − 1). Excluding such pairs makes γ unique, since x^g − 1 = ∏_{d | g} Φ_d(x) determines the exponents. Also M(ℚ(t), t) should read M(ℚ(t), ℚ): a hypergeometric family is a motive over ℚ(t) with coefficients in ℚ, as M(ℚ, ℚ) denotes the motives over ℚ.
- `hgm.familes` (Error or typo; Duplicate): With θ = t d/dt, the factors must be θ + α_i (Beukers–Heckman's operator t∏(θ + α_i) − ∏(θ + β_j − 1)); with θ − α_i the knowl's own series are not solutions. For (A, B) = ([2], [1]), so α = 1/2 and β = 1, the series is (1 − t)^(−1/2) = Σ (1/2)_n/n! tⁿ, which t(θ − 1/2) − θ sends to −t(1 − t)^(−1/2) and t(θ + 1/2) − θ kills. With + α_i every series of the knowl is a solution, since its coefficients satisfy c_n ∏_j(n + β_j − β_k) = c_{n−1} ∏_i(n + α_i − β_k). The equation is also written in t and the series in z. — Duplicate: Duplicates `hgm.families`: identical text.
- `hgm.families` (Error or typo): The same text as hgm.familes, with the same errors. With θ = t d/dt, the factors must be θ + α_i (Beukers–Heckman's operator t∏(θ + α_i) − ∏(θ + β_j − 1)); with θ − α_i the knowl's own series are not solutions. For (A, B) = ([2], [1]), so α = 1/2 and β = 1, the series is (1 − t)^(−1/2) = Σ (1/2)_n/n! tⁿ, which t(θ − 1/2) − θ sends to −t(1 − t)^(−1/2) and t(θ + 1/2) − θ kills. With + α_i every series of the knowl is a solution, since its coefficients satisfy c_n ∏_j(n + β_j − β_k) = c_{n−1} ∏_i(n + α_i − β_k). The equation is also written in t and the series in z.
- `hgm.levelt_matrices` (Error or typo): Fixing the characteristic polynomials does not determine the pair up to simultaneous conjugacy: for A = [3], B = [4] the commuting pair (diag(ω, ω²), diag(i, −i)) has the characteristic polynomials T² + T + 1 and T² + 1, as does Levelt's pair (C(Φ₃), C(Φ₄)⁻¹) = ((0, −1; 1, −1), (0, 1; −1, 0)), which does not commute, so the two pairs are not simultaneously conjugate. Levelt's theorem also needs h₁ = (h₀h_∞)⁻¹, the local monodromy around 1, to be a pseudo-reflection, i.e. h_∞ − h₀⁻¹ to have rank 1 (Beukers–Heckman, Def. 3.1 and Thm. 3.5).
- `hgm.motive` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): This cannot hold: E_{1728t} has j-invariant 1728²t, of degree 1 in t, but the function ₂F₁(1/3, 2/3; 1; ·) of H([3],[1,1],t) has projective monodromy the triangle group (∞, 3, ∞), of index 4 in PSL(2, ℤ), so the j-invariant of the family's elliptic curves is a rational function of degree 4 of the parameter: 27(1 + 8x)³/(x(1 − x)³) for ₂F₁(1/3, 2/3; 1; x) in Ramanujan's cubic theory, up to the LMFDB's normalisation of t. No degree-2 family with B = [1, 1] has j of degree 1 (for A = [2, 2], [3], [4], [6] the degrees are 6, 4, 3 and 2). The replacement states only what is certain; the editors should give the family's actual elliptic curves.
- `hmsurface.component_ideal` (Error or typo): A polarization module is a rank-one ℤ_F-module, isomorphic to a fractional ideal (hmsurface.polarization_module), and hmsurface.x0 gives (𝔡_F𝔟)⁻¹ for the component of 𝔟; ℤ_F ⊕ 𝔟 has rank two (it is the lattice of the surfaces). This also fits the last sentence: the surfaces are principally polarized exactly when (𝔡_F𝔟)⁻¹ is trivial in the narrow class group, that is when 𝔟 is the inverse different up to narrow equivalence. The link should go to hmsurface.polarization_module, not av.polarization. The endomorphism algebra is F only generically (for example a product of two elliptic curves has a larger one); the surfaces have real multiplication by ℤ_F. Also: The polarization module of an abelian surface with real multiplication by ℤ_F is a rank-one ℤ_F-module (hmsurface.polarization_module), whereas ℤ_F ⊕ 𝔟 has rank two: it is the lattice whose automorphism group is the Hilbert modular group of the component. hmsurface.x0 and hmsurface.x01 give (𝔡_F𝔟)⁻¹, and only this makes the last sentence true: the surfaces are principally polarizable if and only if (𝔡_F𝔟)⁻¹ ≅ ℤ_F with positivity, that is, [𝔟] = [𝔡_F⁻¹] in the narrow class group. A component corresponds to a narrow ideal class, not to one ideal, and the link should go to hmsurface.polarization_module.
- `hmsurface.congruence_subgroup` (Error or typo): In GL⁺ there need be no least such ideal: over ℚ(√2), with 𝔟 = ℤ_F and ε = 3 + 2√2 of order 4 modulo 3 and 6 modulo 5, the elements with determinant in ⟨ε²⟩ form a congruence subgroup containing Γ(3) and Γ(5) but not Γ(1), and least norm is no substitute, since for ⟨ε³⟩ the two primes above 7 are valid ideals of the same least norm. In SL the least ideal exists, since Γ(𝔐)Γ(𝔑) = Γ(𝔐 + 𝔑).
- `hmsurface.euler_number` (Error or typo; Suggested category: ag): The Euler number is the alternating sum of the ranks, not of the groups. — Suggested recategorisation: Topological Euler number of any smooth projective variety; nothing specific to Hilbert modular surfaces. Another possible category: `hmsurface`. Confidence: medium.
- `hmsurface.hmsurface` (Error or typo): The completed upper half-plane of mf.upper_half_plane is ℋ ∪ ℚ ∪ {∞}, and Γ does not preserve its square: every congruence subgroup contains some (1 b; 0 1) with b ∈ F ∖ ℚ, which moves (0, 0) to (σ₁(b), σ₂(b)) ∉ ℚ². Γ acts properly discontinuously on 𝔥²; the boundary to add is ℙ¹(F), embedded diagonally, where the action is not proper (cusp stabilisers are infinite). Γ∖𝔥² is not compact, so it is not the set of complex points of a projective surface; its Baily–Borel compactification Γ∖(𝔥² ∪ ℙ¹(F)) is.
- `hmsurface.kodaira_dimension` (Error or typo; Suggested category: ag): The limit need not exist when the plurigenera oscillate: for an Enriques surface dim H⁰(X, K^⊗m) is 1 for even m and 0 for odd m (bielliptic surfaces are similar), so no d qualifies and the knowl gives −1 instead of κ = 0. The standard definition asks for boundedness, with −1 (for −∞) when all plurigenera vanish, and agrees with the knowl's d whenever the limit exists and is non-zero; H⁰ also stood for its dimension. Also: For singular X the definition does not give the Kodaira dimension, a birational invariant computed on a smooth model: the projective cone X ⊂ ℙ³ over a smooth plane curve of degree d ≥ 5 is Gorenstein with K = O_X(d − 4) ample, so the knowl gives 2, although X is birational to a ruled surface and has Kodaira dimension −∞ (−1 in the knowl's convention). Hilbert modular surfaces are singular, and their Kodaira dimension is that of a smooth model. — Suggested recategorisation: Kodaira dimension of any projective variety; duplicates ag.kodaira_dimension. Another possible category: `hmsurface`. Confidence: medium.
- `hmsurface.label` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): Ideal labels (nf.ideal_labels) exist only for nonzero ideals of the ring of integers, while the component ideal is a fractional ideal (hmsurface.congruence_subgroup), for example the inverse different (hmsurface.component_ideal), which is not integral. The label must use an integral ideal in the narrow ideal class, as proposed, or the knowl must say how a fractional ideal is labelled; which the database does could not be checked.
- `hmsurface.x01` (Typo): Stray comma in the quadruple (A, ι, , λ, φ).
- `intro.features` (Error or typo): False for the imprimitive L-functions of the database: L(s, chi_-4) and the Dedekind zeta function of Q(i), which is zeta(s) L(s, chi_-4), have the same lowest zero, 6.0209489..., since the lowest zero of zeta is 14.1347251... (both computed). The belief concerns primitive L-functions (lfunction.primitive).
- `lattice.algebraic` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): The knowl says neither which bilinear form the number field K carries nor whether the ℤ-module must have rank [K : ℚ], and the choices give different notions: with the twisted trace forms Tr_{K/ℚ}(αxy), α totally positive, every ⟨a⟩ with a > 0 is algebraic (ℤ ⊂ ℚ with α = a), while with the trace form Tr_{K/ℚ}(xy), ⟨2⟩ is algebraic as ℤ·1 ⊂ ℚ(√2) if any rank is allowed but not if full rank is required. The editors should name the form (for example Tr_{K/ℚ}(αxy), or Tr_{K/ℚ}(xȳ) for CM fields) and say whether the module must have full rank.
- `lattice.density` (Error or typo): The minimum m(L) of `lattice.minimum` is a norm Q(v) (2 for E₈), so spheres of radius ρ centred at the lattice points touch when m(L) = 4ρ²; with m(L) = 2ρ, E₈ would get Δ = V₈ = π⁴/24 ≈ 4.06 > 1 instead of π⁴/384 ≈ 0.254. V_n is the volume of the unit ball.
- `lattice.discriminant` (Error or typo): In odd rank the even Clifford algebra is central simple (rank 1: C₀ = ℚ, while the Witt discriminant a gives ℚ(√a)); z = e₁⋯eₙ is central in C₀ for n even and in C for n odd. In rank 0 the even Clifford algebra is ℚ, not ℚ[X]/(X² − 1) = ℚ × ℚ (the zero lattice is nondegenerate, of Witt discriminant 1), so the corrected sentence needs positive rank; this supersedes the new text recorded in round ZZ. The corrected sentence is proved in LeanBridge for L ⊗ ℚ with the LMFDB's form Q(v) = ⟨v, v⟩ (round AL). Also a doubled "the".
- `lattice.dual` (Error or typo): If cB makes L^# primitive, so does −cB, so the rescaling is unique only up to sign; and for L = 0 no rescaling is primitive, while for degenerate L the set L^# is not a lattice.
- `lattice.eutactic` (Error or typo): Pure typo: there is one coefficient c_j for each of the m minimal vectors x_j, so the sum runs to m, not to the dimension n (found in review T7_mix, confirmed in round AL).
- `lattice.even_sublattice` (Error or typo): No lattice knowl defines the length of a vector, and read as Euclidean length the sentence is false: A₂ is even but has no nonzero vector of even length. The even sublattice is spanned by the vectors of even norm.
- `lattice.festi_veniani_index` (Error or typo): Festi and Veniani take the index of the image of O(L) in the isometry group of the discriminant form, not in the automorphism group of the abstract group L^∨/L.
- `lattice.genus_label` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): Text and example disagree, and the example is wrong: the LMFDB data and code (the knowl author's create_genus_label in k3s-lmfdb and the LMFDB test suite, checked in the round of 1 November) omit only the rank at valuation 0, so the ranks at valuations 1, …, 6 encode as 001a0B, not 01a0B (the same slip is in create_genus_label's docstring). Also "once" should be "one", and the knowl does not state the conventions the data use: in x, from the least significant bit, the type bits (1 = type I), each compartment oddity as 3 bits (least significant first), the train signs (1 = −1), then the signs at the odd primes (increasing primes and scales, 1 = −1), written in lowercase hexadecimal. To watch: s is n₊ − n₋ in the data, as the knowl says, but since June 2026 the k3s-lmfdb code writes n₊ there. Warning for the editors: since k3s-lmfdb commit dc4e0db (16 June 2026) the code that creates the labels writes n₊ in the slot s, while the knowl and the data now deployed use the signature n₊ − n₋. If the data are recomputed, the labels of all genera that are not positive definite will change. Decide which convention is intended and make the code, the data and the knowl agree.
- `lattice.gram` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): Found in round AO. lattice.successive_minima defines the successive minima through the unit ball, as lengths, while the diagonal entries B(v_j, v_j) of a Gram matrix are norms, their squares; the theorem holds with the minima measured as norms, which is also the LMFDB's own 'minimum'.
- `lattice.history` (Error or typo; Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): Hasse's theorem (Hasse-Minkowski) concerns rational representations and needs the real place: -1 is represented by x_1^2 + ... + x_5^2 over every Z_p but not over R; and for integral representations the local-global principle fails (x^2 + 11y^2 and 3x^2 + 2xy + 4y^2 form one genus, so x^2 + 11y^2 represents 3 locally everywhere, but not over Z), as the knowl's next sentences on integral analogues presuppose. Also: the authors of MR1604472 are Hsia, Shao and Xu, and 'does not exists' (found while checking). Also: The same reference, MR0332663, is cited for Siegel's work of the 1930s and for Shimura's lifting of 1973; one paper cannot be both, and the second citation is Shimura's 'On modular forms of half integral weight' (Ann. of Math. 97, 1973; the MR number itself could not be confirmed online, the MaRDI record gives DOI 10.2307/1970831). The editors should drop the first citation or replace it by Siegel's paper. Also: The theta series of a lattice of rank n has weight n/2 (lattice.theta), an integer when n is even, while 'half-integral weight' means k/2 with k odd (mf.half_integral_weight): the E_8 lattice of this knowl has theta series E_4, of weight 4. Also 'coefficients ... counts' and 'lattices theory'. All three were noticed in round AI0 and checked in round AI0b. Also: A theta series needs a positive definite lattice: in an indefinite one, such as the hyperbolic plane, infinitely many vectors have the same norm, and the series of lattice.theta diverges. lattice.definition and lattice.signature allow indefinite lattices ('signature (n_+, n_-) with n_+ >= n_-'), and this knowl itself speaks of them further down. Found while checking; the editors may want the same restriction in lattice.theta.
- `lattice.hyperbolic_plane` (Error or typo): Over ℚ, x² − 2y² is nondegenerate, indefinite and anisotropic, so it is neither definite nor the isotropic plane U, the only two-dimensional sums of the stated form; over a general field 'definite' has no meaning, and Witt's decomposition writes every nondegenerate quadratic space as an anisotropic one plus copies of U (over ℝ the anisotropic part is the definite one). The lattice statement holds only for indefinite lattices: D₁₆⁺ (whose roots form D₁₆, not E₈ + E₈) and the Leech lattice (which has no roots) are positive definite even unimodular lattices that are not sums E₈^{⊕s}. With 'in general', the last sentence no longer contradicts the one before it.
- `lattice.isometry` (Error or typo): As written σ is any map with Q(σ(v)) = Q(v), neither linear nor bijective, so being isometric is not symmetric: v ↦ (v, 0) maps ⟨1⟩ into ⟨1⟩ ⊕ ⟨1⟩, but no map back preserves Q, since (1, 1) has norm 2, which ⟨1⟩ does not represent; the isometry class is then not an equivalence class. Linearity alone is not enough either: x ↦ 2x maps ⟨4⟩ into ⟨1⟩, and no map goes back. The Gram matrix statement of the second paragraph also needs σ to be a linear bijection.
- `lattice.kissing` (Error or typo): Without equal radii the maximum is infinite, since arbitrarily small spheres can be added.
- `lattice.level` (Error or typo): No integer is smallest with this property, since N = 0 and every negative multiple of the level also satisfy it; the level is the smallest positive one. The parenthetical is false for odd lattices: ℤ with B(x, y) = xy has discriminant 1 and e = 1, but level 2, since N·B(1, 1) = N must be even. When 2 does not divide the discriminant the only 2-adic block is unimodular, of type I exactly when L is odd, so the level is e for even L and 2e for odd L, as the main rule gives.
- `lattice.minimal_vector` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide); Duplicate): The same text as `lattice.minimum`: m(L) is called a length, but minimal vectors are defined by Q(v) = m(L), so m(L) is a norm (2 for E₈, not √2). — Duplicate: Duplicates `lattice.minimum`: identical text.
- `lattice.minimum` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): m(L) is called the length of a shortest non-zero vector, but minimal vectors are defined by Q(v) = m(L), so m(L) is a norm, the square of the length (2 for E₈, not √2). Unless "length" is meant to mean norm throughout the lattice knowls (as in `lattice.root_sublattice`), it should say norm.
- `lattice.normalized_minimal_vector` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): The components depend on a basis, which the knowl does not name; the LMFDB uses the basis of the Gram matrix.
- `lattice.orthogonal_decomposition` (Error or typo): Uniqueness fails for indefinite lattices: U ⊕ ⟨−1⟩ ≅ ⟨1⟩ ⊕ ⟨−1⟩ ⊕ ⟨−1⟩ (with basis e + f + g, e + g, f + g of norms 1, −1, −1), where the hyperbolic plane U is indecomposable because it is even of rank 2, so the two decompositions do not even have the same number of summands. Existence holds for every lattice and uniqueness for definite ones (Eichler; Kneser). Also: As written the zero lattice is indecomposable (it has no non-trivial orthogonal decomposition), so zero summands can be added to any decomposition into indecomposable summands and none is unique, even for a definite lattice: L = L ⊕ 0 = L ⊕ 0 ⊕ 0. Indecomposable lattices must be nonzero, as indecomposable modules are; the uniqueness statement for definite lattices needs this too.
- `lattice.perfect` (Error or typo): Read literally (the minimal vectors determine the lattice), the sentence is false: D_12 and D_12^+ (also D_10 and D_10^+) are distinct integral perfect lattices with the same minimal vectors ±e_i±e_j and the same minimum 2, and they are not similar (determinants 4 and 1). Voronoi's statement is that the minimal vectors determine the form up to a positive scalar; proved in LeanBridge (round AJ).
- `lattice.pneighbor` (Error or typo): False as written when p divides 2 det(L): ℤ⁸ and E₈ are 2-neighbours in ℚ⁸ (ℤ⁸ ∩ E₈ = D₈ has index 2 in both) but lie in different genera, ℤ⁸ being odd and E₈ even; and for p = 3 the lattices with Gram matrices diag(1, 9) and [[2, 3], [3, 9]] (bases e, f and e + f/3, f) are 3-neighbours whose unimodular 3-adic Jordan components ⟨1⟩ and ⟨2⟩ are not isometric. For p ∤ 2 det(L), p-neighbours lie in the same genus. Also: "is not  reflexive nor transitive" has a double space and should read "is neither reflexive nor transitive".
- `lattice.quadratic_form` (Error or typo): A positive definite lattice has Q(L) ⊆ ℤ≥0, so as written it can be neither universal nor even universal, although these notions are mostly used for such lattices (the 15 and 290 theorems), where they mean representing every positive integer, resp. every positive even integer. The literal conditions are right for indefinite lattices.
- `lattice.root_lattice` (Error or typo): As written, 2α ∈ E is a scalar multiple of α other than ±α, so no root is allowed and the only root system is the empty one; the multiples must be taken in Φ.
- `lattice.root_sublattice` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): Read as Euclidean length, 'length at most 2' means norm at most 4, and then ⟨4⟩ (ℤ with Q(x) = 4x²) would be a root lattice, its generator having length 2; roots are the vectors of norm 1 and 2, so 'length' must mean the norm Q(v) here. As for lattice.minimum, unless 'length' is declared to mean the norm throughout the lattice knowls, it should say norm.
- `lattice.similarity` (Error or typo): The zero lattice, or ℤv with v isotropic, has only lattices with zero form in its similarity class, none of them primitive; and uniqueness holds only up to isometry (ℤ² and its rotations).
- `lattice.spherical_design` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): Found in round AO. The zero lattice of R^0 is vacuously strongly eutactic but its minimal vectors form no design (no point on a sphere of positive radius), and the knowl defines 'spherical t-design lattice': a lattice is not itself a design. Optional: rank 0 is outside the LMFDB's lattices. Also: Found in round AO. Pure typo, optional: the same shorthand for 'design lattice'.
- `lattice.sublattice` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): The root sublattice uses the vectors of norm 2 here but those of norm at most 2 in `lattice.root_sublattice`, which differ for odd lattices (for ℤⁿ with n ≥ 2, Dₙ against ℤⁿ); the proposal follows `lattice.root_sublattice`, but the editors may prefer to change that knowl instead. The max diag sublattice is not unique: in A₂ each pair of roots ±r, with the vector of norm 6 orthogonal to r, spans a maximal one, with Gram matrix diag(2, 6), so there are three; "vecotrs" is a typo.
- `lattice.tensor_decomposition` (Error or typo): As written every lattice is decomposable, since L ≅ L ⊗ ⟨1⟩; a factor of rank 1 only rescales the form, L ⊗ ⟨a⟩ being L with its form multiplied by a.
- `lattice.unimodular` (Error or typo): lattice.determinant is the signed determinant of a Gram matrix, and the database has indefinite lattices of signature (n₊, n₋), whose determinant has the sign (−1)^{n₋}. So the hyperbolic plane U (determinant −1) and ⟨1⟩ ⊕ ⟨−1⟩, which are self-dual and so unimodular in the sense of lattice.discriminant_group, are not unimodular by this definition, and neither are the even unimodular lattices U^{⊕r} ⊕ E₈^{⊕s} with r odd of lattice.hyperbolic_plane.
- `lf.associated_inertia` (Error or typo): Found in round AO. 'The inertia degree of phi' is defined nowhere, in this knowl or another, and the LMFDB's code computes nothing like it; the reading that makes the statement true and is the natural one is the inertia degree (residue degree) of the splitting field of phi over L^un, of which every other candidate is a multiple. Read as f(L/K) or f(L/L^un) the old sentence is false: Q_3(3^(1/4)) has associated inertia 2 and f = 1. Round AP proved the corrected sentence (Ore's theorem) and the other readings (the residue degree of the splitting field over K, the Galois unramified degree).
- `lf.eisenstein_diagram` (Error or typo): (a) The count of drawn points of index at most k in B_k fails for k not final in its segment: for I = (1/3, 1/3)_1^1 over Q_2, the invariant of Q_2[x]/(x^4 + 2x + 2), B_1 = {1/6 <= s < 1/3} contains only P_1 = (1, 1/4), of index 2, while ceil(r_1) = 1; in general the points counted are the multiples of p^(w-k) in an interval of length p^(w-k) r_k, so floor(r_k) or ceil(r_k) of them, and ceil(r_k) when k is final in its segment (checked on thousands of compatible invariants). (b) Monge's count is over K_f, per K_f-isomorphism class, with Aut(L/K_f): for f > 1 the knowl's Aut(L/K) fails, e.g. I = ()_1^2 over Q_p gives M(I/K) = 1/2 against 1, a count of 1/2 specialisations, and |Aut(K_2/Q_p)| = 2 in a rigid case. The editors should make M(I/K) agree with the mass of lf.family_mass.
- `lf.eisenstein_form` (Error or typo): lf.eisenstein_polynomial allows non-monic polynomials and constants, while Eisenstein form is defined for monic polynomials of positive degree (e.g. 2x² + px + p over ℤ_p, p odd, is Eisenstein but not monic).
- `lf.eisenstein_polynomial` (Error or typo; Suggested category: ring): False as written when D is not integrally closed: in D = k[t², t³] (k a field) with P = (t², t³), x² − t² is Eisenstein (t² ∉ P²) but equals (x − t)(x + t) in k(t)[x]. Integral closure is not enough for non-monic polynomials: in the normal domain D = k[u, v, w]/(uv − w²) with P = (u, w), vx² + 2wx + u is Eisenstein (v ∉ P, u ∉ P²) but equals (vx + w)²/v in F[x]. A nonzero constant a_0 ∉ P is also Eisenstein (n = 0) but a unit of F[x]. The classical criterion assumes D a unique factorization domain (it also holds for monic polynomials over an integrally closed D). — Suggested recategorisation: Defines Eisenstein polynomials over an arbitrary integral domain with respect to a prime ideal, and their irreducibility over the fraction field (Eisenstein's criterion), which is basic algebra; the characterisation of totally ramified extensions of p-adic fields is an application, though the knowl is mainly used by lf. Another possible category: `lf`. Confidence: medium.
- `lf.family_ambiguity` (Typo): Doubled 'be'.
- `lf.family_diagrams` (Error or typo): When the tame part ε of the ramification index is greater than 1 the ramification polygon has a horizontal segment, whose slope 0 is not a ram; the site's plot draws it and labels only the nonzero slopes. The corrected statement is proved in LeanBridge (round AI).
- `lf.family_invariants` (Typo): Punctuation of the list: a full stop for a comma, and a comma for the final full stop. For the editors to decide: for a relative family (base field other than Q_p) the family page labels the row 'Absolute Artin slopes' and shows those of L/Q_p, while the knowl's Artin slopes, written with the same w as the Swan slopes, are those of L/K.
- `lf.family_mass` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): The relation fails for the knowl's definition, a sum over K-isomorphism classes. Grouping the K_f-isomorphism classes of each L into Gal(K_f/K)-orbits shows that the sum of 1/|Aut(L/K_f)| over the K_f-classes is f times the absolute mass, while the knowl's mass has |S_L| in place of f, where S_L is the image of Aut(L/K) → Gal(K_f/K). Counterexample: p ≡ 2 mod 3 and I = ()_3^2. Over K₂ = ℚ_p(ζ₃) the totally tamely ramified cubic extensions are K₂((uⁱp)^{1/3}), i = 0, 1, 2, with u a non-cube unit, and Frobenius swaps i = 1 and 2, so I/ℚ_p = {K₂(p^{1/3}), K₂((up)^{1/3})}, with |Aut(L/ℚ_p)| = 6 and 3. The mass is 1/3 + 1/3 = 2/3 and the absolute mass 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2, but 2/3 ≠ 2 · 1/2. The proposed text states the relation that holds; if the database stores the K_f-class sum, the editors may prefer to define the mass as that sum.
- `lf.family_polynomial` (Error or typo): With σ(i, j) = ej + i the monomial attached to σ is π_K^{j+1}x^i, as in lf.eisenstein_diagram (x^e + π Σ f_σ π^j x^i with σ = je + i, 0 ≤ i < e). As written, terms with i = 0 are not divisible by π_K, so the specialisations would not be Eisenstein, and (i, j) = (0, 0) would give a constant term besides d₀π_K. Also: The subset S_{(i,j)} is not determined by (i, j): in Monge's construction (arXiv:1109.4617, Definition 1, p. 6) the quotient is λ/W with W = η^j S_m(λ) in Monge's indexing, where η = −d̄₀ and the additive polynomial S_m depends on the extension and on π mod 𝔭², so W depends on d₀ and the lower coefficients; in degree p the C-term is present only when the extension is Galois (p. 12). The correction of the monomials to π_K^{j+1}x^i is confirmed against Monge's terms f_{i,j}π_K^jT^i (Definition 1).
- `lf.field.label` (Error or typo; Conflict): The family label's f, e and c are defined as invariants "of K over ℚ_p", but K is only introduced in the next paragraph; they are the invariants shared by all fields K in the family. — Conflicting definition: Conflicts with `lf.field_label`: two different descriptions of the p-adic field label.
- `lf.galois_invariants` (Error or typo): The upper numbering filtration is decreasing, so the group just above j is the union (the intersection over all ε > 0 is trivial). `lf.slope_content` already uses the union. Also: The filtration is decreasing, so the intersection over ε > 0 is the trivial group; the group just above j is the union (as in lf.slope_content). Besides the recorded grammar fix ('Each jump in the filtration … gives a Swan slope of i'), the sentence must restrict to i > 0: the jumps at i = −1 (when the unramified degree u > 1, as G^{−1} = G ≠ G_0) and at i = 0 (when the tame degree t > 1) would otherwise give Swan slopes −1 and 0, against the next sentence, by which the Swan slopes are the wild Artin slopes minus 1, hence positive. Suggested: 'Each jump $G^{i}\neq G^{i+}$ with $i>0$ gives a **Swan slope** $i$, repeated $m$ times where $p^m=[G^i:G^{i+}]$.' (the same kind of error as the one recorded for lf.swan_slopes). Also: The last bullet has no subject: "For each jump in the filtration … gives a Swan slope of i".
- `lf.galois_mean_slope` (Error or typo): The weighted average is of the wild slopes and of (t − 1)/t, not of the tame degree t: every tamely ramified Galois K has mean slope (t − 1)/t ≠ t (for K = ℚ_p it is 0 while t = 1).
- `lf.heights` (Error or typo; Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): Residue degree f = 1 means totally ramified, not unramified. Also: The sentence is right for every ramified L/K (then K ⊆ K_f ⊊ L_1). For L/K unramified with L ≠ K the ramification polygon, which is that of L over its maximal unramified subextension K_f, has no segment, so r = 0 and L_r = L fails; starting the chain at K_f covers this case too. Proved in LeanBridge in both forms (round AN: ramificationTower, self_mem_ramificationTower_iff).
- `lf.hidden_slopes` (Error or typo): By lf.slopes the Swan slopes include −1 when f > 1 and 0 when the tame degree ε > 1, so with them the hidden slopes H would contain −1 when f = 1 < f^Gal and 0 when ε = 1 < ε^Gal (ℚ_3(3^{1/3}): the wild slopes give H = ∅, all the slopes give H = {0}). The LMFDB lists only the wild slopes as Galois, visible and hidden slopes (the tame and unramified degrees are separate). Proved in LeanBridge for the wild slopes, and for all the slopes too (round AN: hullWildSwanSlopes_add_hiddenSwanSlopes, hullSwanSlopeMultiset_galoisClosure_sub).
- `lf.jump_set` (Error or typo): The u_i = v_K(α_i − 1) are positive ("an increasing sequence of r + 1 positive integers"), so each α_i ≠ 1 is a 1-unit with v_K(α_i) = 0; then the first condition fails (p | 0) and the second is impossible, which would force every α_i = 1 and ζ_p = 1. The conditions must be on v_K(α_i − 1), which is positive for a 1-unit. The sequence is [u_0, u_1, …, u_r]. Also: The values u_i are not independent of the choice of the α_i under the knowl's conditions alone. For K = ℚ₂[x]/(x⁴+2x³+2x²+2) (2.1.4.6a2.1), −1 has factorisations meeting all the conditions with sequences [1,2,7] and [1,5,7], the second failing ρ(5) = 9 ≤ 7 (recomputed by exact arithmetic in round ZR; the LMFDB stores [1,2,7]). The missing condition is Pagano's (C.1), ρ(u_i) ≤ u_{i+1}, arXiv:1810.09975v1, §1.2 p. 3 and §1.4 p. 13. Separately, the jump set alone does not determine the filtered structure of the 1-units: Pagano §1.4 p. 13 says it does so together with p and the residue field degree, and ℚ₂ (2.1.1.0a1.1), its unramified quadratic extension (2.2.1.0a1.1) and ℚ₃(√−3) (3.1.2.1a1.1) all have jump set [1].
- `lf.local_height_function` (Error or typo): A weight function vanishes exactly at the identity (group.weight_function), so w(φ_p(τ_p)) = 0 whenever φ_p is unramified, for example when φ_p is trivial, and 0 is not in the stated codomain ℝ_{>0}. The local height is p^{w(φ_p(τ_p))}, as the radical-discriminant example of nf.inertial_height_function needs: with w = 1 off the identity, the product of the local heights is then the product of the ramified primes, while with w(φ_p(τ_p)) it would vanish.
- `lf.log` (Error or typo): log(1+z) = z − z²/2 + z³/3 − …, so the sign is (−1)^(n+1); with (−1)^n the series is −log(1+z). Also: The series is in z with |z|_p < 1, so log_p(1 + z) defines the logarithm on 1 + S = {x ∈ K : |x − 1|_p < 1}, not on S. The extension by log_p(p) = 0 and log_p(ζ) = 0 is a homomorphism on K^×, since 0 has no logarithm.
- `lf.packet` (Error or typo): Found in round AO, made precise in round AP. 'their residual polynomials are equivalent' needs the reading of lf.subfamily for residue degree f > 1 (the classes of two K-isomorphic copies of an extension can differ by a Frobenius twist of the residue field of K_f). With that reading round AP proved that the five conditions do not depend on the members of the K-isomorphism classes and that the packets partition I/K. A clarification, needed only together with the lf.subfamily fix:
- `lf.qp` (Error or typo): For r = 0 no such j, a, b exist and |0|_p is left undefined.
- `lf.ramification_polygon` (Error or typo; Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): The same error as in lf.family_diagrams: for ε > 1 the polygon has a segment of slope 0, which is not a ram. Also: The points are listed for ρ_i with 0 ≤ i ≤ n − 1, which omits the point (−n, 0) of the leading coefficient; the lower convex hull needs it.
- `lf.ramification_polygon_display` (Error or typo): When n = [L:K'] is not a power of p, the left end (-n, 0) is a vertex of the ramification polygon but not one of the points (-p^j, i_j): for Q_3(3^{1/6}) the vertices are (-6,0), (-3,0), (-1,6) and the points are (-1,6), (-3,0). The LMFDB's own vertex lists include (e, 0); if 'vertices' is meant to exclude the endpoints, the old sentence is true and the editors may prefer to say that instead.
- `lf.rams` (Error or typo): As written, 𝓡_1^z never contains its boundary value pz/(p − 1): in lowest terms its numerator is divisible by p, while 𝓡_1^∞ asks for a numerator prime to p, so the ≤ is a <. But the ram p e_K/(p − 1) occurs: it is the arithmetic ram of lf.herbrand_invariant (ℚ_2(√2) has ram 2 and ℚ_3(∛3) has ram 3/2, while the knowl's 𝓡_1^1 is {1} at p = 2). With the correction the sets are exactly the possible rams: the totally ramified quartic extensions of ℚ_2 get the discriminant exponents {4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11}, as known, and without it only {4, 6, 8}. Proved in LeanBridge (round AN: natCast_mul_div_notMem_ramSet, exists_visibleRams_eq_singleton_arithmetic, mem_possibleRamSet_iff_exists_visibleRams_eq_replicate). Also: For f > 1 the field L_i has degree f ε p^i over K, and no intermediate field of degree ε p^i over K need exist: for p ≡ 5 mod 6 and u a unit of ℚ_{p²} that is not a cube, L = ℚ_{p²}((up)^{1/(3p²)}) has f = 2, ε = 3, rams 3p/(p − 1) < 3p²/(p − 1), and no subfield of degree 3p over ℚ_p (such a subfield would be totally ramified, its tame cubic subfield would be ℚ_p(∛p) up to isomorphism, and ℚ_{p²}(∛p) is not the tame part ℚ_{p²}(∛(up)) of L). The corrected sentence is proved in LeanBridge for every L/K (round AN: finrank_ramSubextension_of_ram_lt); the counterexample is checked by hand.
- `lf.residual_polynomials` (Error or typo): Found in round AO. The knowl never numbers the segments S_1, ..., S_l, and its recursion for gamma_{delta,i} gives an invariant class only with S_1 the rightmost segment, as in its source (Pauli and Sinclair, Figure 1, Lemma 4.3(b), Example 4.9); numbered from the left, Pauli-Sinclair's example at -alpha and an example over F_4 fall outside the class. The LMFDB stores and prints the list from the left (local_fields/main.py) but never numbers it. The knowl does not define n, hence -deg(phi).
- `lf.ring_of_integers` (Error or typo): The linked lf.local_field includes the archimedean local fields ℝ and ℂ, for which {x : |x| ≤ 1} is not a subring (|1 + 1| = 2), let alone a discrete valuation ring; the definition is that of a nonarchimedean local field.
- `lf.slope_content` (Error or typo): False over K: for ℚ_3(ζ_8, √(3ζ_8)) one has e = f = t = 2, but the largest tamely totally ramified subextension over ℚ_3 is ℚ_3 itself. The statement holds over the maximal unramified subextension.
- `lf.slopes` (Error or typo): By the knowl's own definitions the Swan slopes include −1 when f > 1 and 0 when the tame degree ε > 1 (the unramified quadratic extension has Swan slopes {−1} and no positive jump), so they are not the positive upper ramification jumps; the wild (positive) Swan slopes are, counted with multiplicities. Proved in LeanBridge (round AM: hullWildSwanSlopes_eq_visibleSwanSlopes, Deligne's upper breaks, and Serre's in the Galois case). Also: This sentence calls all the Artin and Swan slopes visible, but lf.visible_slopes takes only the slopes greater than one, and so do the LMFDB's pages, which show "Visible Artin slopes" under this knowl with the wild slopes only: ℚ_3(3^{1/6}) has Artin slopes {1, 5/2} and visible Artin slopes [5/2]. The editors may prefer to change lf.visible_slopes instead; the data follow it (round AN).
- `lf.subfamily` (Error or typo): Found in round AO, made precise in round AP. For residue degree f > 1 an element of I/K is a K-isomorphism class, and the coefficients of the residual polynomials of a member are identified with the residue field of K_f only up to the Frobenius of K_f/K, so K-isomorphic copies can have Frobenius-conjugate classes: Q_2(zeta_3)(alpha) with alpha^4 + 2 alpha^2 + 4 zeta_3 alpha + 2 = 0, an octic in the LMFDB, has class {(delta zetabar + delta x, delta + x^2)} over F_4, and its conjugate copy has {(delta zetabar^2 + delta x, delta + x^2)}. The text does not say how such a class is compared with A. Round AP proved that 'some member has its list in A' and 'the list is in A up to the action of Gal(K_f/K)' give the same subfamily, that Frobenius-conjugate classes give the same subfamily, and that the subfamilies partition I/K, as the one-code-per-field labels need; only an 'every member' reading fails (the octic would lie in no subfamily). The LMFDB's source paper (arXiv:2507.02360) treats f = 1 only. The fix makes the reading explicit; LeanBridge formalises the knowl with it (the user's ruling of 2026-11-24). Data note: for families with f > 1 the stored residual polynomials depend on the stored K_f-structure (coefficients in Z[t]), so the subfamily codes (ctr_subfamily) should be checked to group fields whose stored lists differ by the Frobenius of K_f.
- `lf.swan_slopes` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): The knowl calls Swan slopes the "nonnegative" upper ramification breaks, but `lf.slopes` says positive, and its own last sentence subtracts 1 from the positive Artin slopes. Decide whether a tame break 0 counts and make the two knowls agree. Also: The tame break 0 is not a Swan slope (cf. lf.slopes and the same knowl's "positive Artin slopes"), so the Swan slopes are the positive upper breaks. Also: Subtracting 1 from every positive Artin slope also turns the Artin slope 1 of a tame segment into 0, which is not a Swan slope (lf.slopes: the Swan slopes are the positive upper ramification jumps; lf.herbrand_invariant has w = v_p(e) Swan slopes, all positive), so only the wild Artin slopes, those greater than 1, give Swan slopes. The link should go to lf.slopes, whose Artin slopes are those of L/K, rather than to lf.galois_invariants, whose slopes are those of the Galois closure, hidden slopes included.
- `lf.top_slope` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): The link goes to lf.slopes, whose Artin slope content of L/K is the visible [a_1, …, a_w]_ε^f, but the notation [s_1, …, s_k]_t^u is the Galois slope content of lf.slope_content. The three cases hold for both (the top break is visible), so the editors should pick one; the alternative is to keep lf.slopes, write [a_1, …, a_w]_ε^f and say that a_w is the largest visible wild slope.
- `lf.visible_slopes` (Error or typo): "The set" contradicts "(as multisets)": with a set, the Galois slopes [2, 2, 3] and the visible ones [2, 3] would leave nothing hidden instead of [2]. And "all slopes" are the wild slopes of the Galois closure, the list of the sentence before; in the wider sense of lf.slopes they would include its slopes 0 and 1, which are never visible. Proved in LeanBridge (round AN: hiddenArtinSlopes_eq_wildArtinSlopes_sub). Also: Pure typos: the first sentence is a fragment and "$c_E$ its" lacks a verb; the index k of [s_1,…,s_k] is already the multiplicity of one slope in the sentence before (round AN).
- `lfunction` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): 'A certain type of functional equation' (and of Euler product) leaves the class of L-functions open, while lfunction.functional_equation, lfunction.euler_product and lfunction.degree speak of a precise one. LeanBridge's AnalyticLFunction reads it as: a Dirichlet series converging absolutely for Re(s) > 1, with an Euler product whose factors at p are inverses of polynomials of degree at most d, of degree exactly d at the primes not dividing the conductor N; a continuation holomorphic off s = 1; and a completion Λ(s) = N^{s/2} ∏ Γ_ℝ(s + μ_j) ∏ Γ_ℂ(s + ν_k) L(s), holomorphic off {0, 1}, with Λ(s) = ε conj(Λ(1 − conj(s))) and Re(μ_j) ∈ {0, 1}. The editors should say which class is meant, in particular whether the degree of the Euler factors at the primes not dividing N is part of the definition (lfunction.degree says it holds 'in all known cases', lfunction.euler_product calls it expected).
- `lfunction.bad_prime` (Error or typo): Typo: "divided" should be "divide".
- `lfunction.central_character` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): Sign convention: with a_p the Dirichlet coefficient, the linear term of the Euler factor is -a_p x (zeta has 1 - x, and cmf.lfunction writes 1 - a_p p^{-s} + ...); for d = 1 the knowl's form makes a_p = -chi(p). It does not affect the knowl's status.
- `lfunction.completed` (Error or typo): The factor N^{s/2} is missing, so the sentence is false for conductor N > 1 (the same omission as the recorded error of lfunction.infinity_factor).
- `lfunction.degree` (Typo): The displayed functional equation has J + K Gamma factors, J of type Γ_ℝ and K of type Γ_ℂ; the degree J + 2K counts each Γ_ℂ(s) = Γ_ℝ(s)Γ_ℝ(s + 1) twice.
- `lfunction.dirichlet` (Error or typo): For odd χ the Gamma factor is Γ_ℝ(s + 1): for the primitive odd character χ mod 4, 4^{s/2}Γ_ℝ(s)L(s, χ) has a pole at s = 0, where L(0, χ) = 1/2, while the right-hand side is finite there. For imprimitive χ no equation of this form holds: for the trivial character mod 2, L(s, χ) = (1 − 2^{−s})ζ(s), and Riemann's functional equation leaves the factor 1 − 2^{−s}, which is not symmetric under s ↦ 1 − s.
- `lfunction.functional_equation` (Error found while formalising): The motivic weight is the least nonnegative integer with this property (`lfunction.motivic_weight`); it is 0 for ζ and for Dirichlet L-functions.
- `lfunction.history.artin` (Error or typo): As stated the conjecture is false: the Artin L-function of the trivial representation is the Riemann zeta function, which has a pole at s = 1. Artin's conjecture is about nontrivial irreducible representations.
- `lfunction.history.hecke_operators` (Error or typo): 'eigenvalues' is a slip for 'eigenforms', and without 'normalized' the coefficients are not multiplicative: for 2Δ, a_2 a_3 = −24192 but a_6 = −12096. The corrected statement is proved for cuspidal eigenforms (round AI).
- `lfunction.infinity_factor` (Error or typo): Without the factor N^{s/2} the equation is false whenever N > 1: for the even primitive character χ mod 5, Γ_ℝ(s)L(s, χ) = 5^{1/2−s}Γ_ℝ(1 − s)L(1 − s, χ), which is not a constant multiple of the reflection. With N the conductor, Λ(s) = N^{s/2}L_∞(s)L(s), as in lfunction.functional_equation.
- `lfunction.known_degree3` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): A symmetric square need not be primitive: for a CM form it factors. For the curve y^2 = x^3 - x, with CM by Z[i], the symmetric square is L(s - 1, chi_-4) L(s, g), where g = eta(4z)^6 is the CM newform of weight 3 and level 16 (checked on the Euler factors at the odd primes below 200). By Gelbart and Jacquet the symmetric square of a cuspidal representation of GL(2) is cuspidal exactly when the representation has no self-twist. The editors may instead restrict the first item, for example to newforms without self-twists.
- `lfunction.known_degree4` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): Several of the listed L-functions are not always primitive: the symmetric cube of a CM form; the spin L-function of a Saito-Kurokawa lift, L(s, f) zeta(s + 1/2) zeta(s - 1/2) (mf.siegel.lift.saito_kurokawa; by mf.siegel.automorphic_type only the forms of general type have primitive L-functions); and the L-functions of base changes from Q, of a Bianchi or Hilbert modular form or of an elliptic curve E over a quadratic field K that is defined over Q, where L(E/K, s) = L(E, s) L(E', s) with E' the twist of E by K. Also, in the LMFDB's Siegel knowls (mf.siegel.lift.miyawaki1) the standard L-function in degree n has degree 2n + 1, so 5 for Sp(4), and the L-function of degree 4 is the spin one; the fourth item presumably means the Maass forms for GSp(4) of the L-function pages.
- `lfunction.label` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): The rule does not determine the label: every N is the perfect power N¹, some N are perfect powers in several ways (64 = 2⁶ = 4³ = 8²), and conductors are normally written in decimal (1-1-1.1-r0-0-0 for the Riemann zeta function). The knowl should say which conductors are abbreviated and how m and n are chosen (for example n > 1 maximal). The rule the database follows could not be checked offline, so no replacement is proposed. Also: Suggested text, drafted 2026-11-01; the choice of m and n must be checked against the database.
- `lfunction.normalization` (Error found while formalising): s = (w + 1)/2 is the central point; the central value is the value of L there.
- `lfunction.primitive` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): Read literally, every nontrivial L-function is a product of nontrivial L-functions with one factor, so nothing would be primitive; with at least two factors, the trivial L-function 1 is primitive, since nontrivial L-functions have positive degree and degrees add. The usual convention, as for irreducible elements and in the Selberg class, excludes the trivial L-function; the editors should decide, and the proposed text follows that convention.
- `lfunction.selberg_class` (Error or typo): Malformed link: the href to Atle Selberg's Wikipedia page lacks its opening quote, so it points to a page ending in a quote mark, which does not exist.
- `lfunction.selberg_class.axioms` (Typo): Stray space inside the bold markup.
- `lfunction.spectral_label` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): The rule does not determine the label: when every multiplicity is divisible by 4, both e2 and e4 fit 'a multiple of an integer n > 1' (r0r0r0r0 could be r0r0e2 or r0e4); presumably n is the greatest common divisor of the multiplicities. The text also leaves open how ties are rounded, when an imaginary part counts as zero 'to the known precision' (p0) rather than as p0.00, and in which order p, m and c terms with the same real part and the same absolute value are listed. The rule the database follows could not be checked offline, so no replacement is proposed.
- `lfunction.symm` (Error or typo): A bad Euler factor of the symmetric power can have the full degree. If E is the quadratic twist of an elliptic curve E′ with good reduction at an odd prime p by a character ramified at p, then p is bad for L(E, s) (its Euler factor there is 1), yet sym² L(E) = sym² L(E′) has the full degree-3 factor at p. For n = 0, every Euler factor of sym⁰ L = ζ has degree 1.
- `lfunction.taxonomy` (Error or typo; Typo): With nu = (k - 1)/2 for a holomorphic form of weight k (section 1.5 of the knowl), min{0, max nu_k} is 0, against the knowl's next note (the motivic weight is k - 1) and lfunction.motivic_weight. The conjectural value is w = 2 max{0, nu_1, ..., nu_K}, the algebraic weight of Farmer, Pitale, Ryan and Schmidt (arXiv:1711.10375, Definition 4.1, conjecturally equal to the arithmetic weight). Found while checking, in section 4: F_p is a polynomial of degree d, so the Euler product is the product of the F_p(p^-s)^-1, as in lfunction.central_character (for zeta, F_p(x) = 1 - x); with a_p the Dirichlet coefficient, as everywhere else in the knowl, the linear term of F_p is -a_p x (the same formula in lfunction.central_character was recorded in round AF); and the Satake parameters, whose product is chi(p), are the reciprocal roots of F_p, as in cmf.satake_parameters. Also: 'paramaters' and '$L$-funciton' (in the audit's quote); 'a integer' and 'is in integer' (found while checking).
- `lfunction.trivial_zero` (Error or typo): The poles of the gamma factors, hence the trivial zeros, are not only at negative integers: 0 is one for even nontrivial Dirichlet characters and for newforms, and from motivic weight 2 on positive integers occur (L(Sym^3 E, s) has gamma factor Gamma_C(s) Gamma_C(s - 1) in the arithmetic normalization, so L(Sym^3 E, 1) = 0); in the analytic normalization the poles need not be integers. And the L-function vanishes only at those poles of the gamma factors where the completed L-function has no pole: Gamma_R(s) has a pole at 0, where the completed zeta function has one too, and zeta(0) = -1/2 (the corrected form is proved for every analytic L-function in LeanBridge).
- `lfunction.zfunction` (Error or typo (for the editors to decide)): For zeta the root number is 1 and the gamma factor Gamma_R, so the general Z is +-e^{i theta} zeta(1/2 + it); Hardy's Z is negative near 0 (Z(0) = zeta(1/2) = -1.46...), so the stated normalisation selects -Z. The editors may instead change the convention. Found in round S1 and never recorded until round AF.
- `mf` (Error or typo): Maass waveforms are eigenfunctions of the Laplacian (mf.maass.mwf: (Δ + λ)f = 0 for some λ), so the sum of two Maass forms of the same weight and multiplier system on the same group but with different eigenvalues is not an eigenfunction, hence not a Maass form. Only those with a fixed eigenvalue form a vector space.
- `mf.base_change` (Error or typo): Roots determine a polynomial only up to a scalar factor. The relation L_𝔮(g, T) = L_𝔭^{(r)}(f, T) between Euler factors with constant term 1 needs h^{(r)}(T) = ∏(1 − α_i^r T) for h(T) = ∏(1 − α_i T), that is the normalisation h^{(r)}(0) = h(0); the monic polynomial with these roots would be wrong.
